45_1_19: because that which is known about God is evident within them — for God made it evident to them.
45_1_20: For since the creation of the world His invisible attributes — His eternal power and divine nature — have been clearly seen, being understood through what has been made. So they are without excuse.
45_1_21: For even though they knew God, they did not honor Him as God, or give thanks. But they became futile in their thinking, and their foolish heart was darkened.
45_1_22: Professing to be wise, they became fools.
45_1_23: And exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God for an image in the form of corruptible man, and of birds, and four-footed animals, and crawling creatures.
45_1_24: Therefore God gave them over in the lusts of their hearts to impurity — that their bodies would be dishonored among them.
45_1_25: For they exchanged the truth of God for a lie — and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen.
45_1_26: For this reason God gave them over to degrading passions. For their women exchanged the natural function for that which is unnatural.
45_1_27: And in the same way also the men abandoned the natural function of the woman — and burned in their desire toward one another, men with men committing indecent acts, and receiving in their own persons the due penalty of their error.
45_1_28: And just as they did not see fit to acknowledge God any longer, God gave them over to a depraved mind — to do those things which are not proper.
45_1_29: Being filled with all unrighteousness, wickedness, greed, and evil — full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, malice. They are gossips,
45_1_30: slanderers, haters of God, insolent, arrogant, boastful, inventors of evil, disobedient to parents,
45_1_32: And although they know the ordinance of God — that those who practice such things are worthy of death — they not only do the same, but also give hearty approval to those who practice them.
45_2_1: Therefore you have no excuse, O man — every one of you who passes judgment. For in that which you judge another, you condemn yourself — for you who judge practice the same things.
45_2_2: And we know that the judgment of God rightly falls upon those who practice such things.
45_2_3: But do you suppose this, O man — when you pass judgment on those who practice such things, and yet do the same yourself — that you will escape the judgment of God?
45_2_4: Or do you think lightly of the riches of His kindness and tolerance and patience? — not knowing that the kindness of God leads you to repentance.
45_2_5: But because of your stubbornness and unrepentant heart, you are storing up wrath for yourself in the day of wrath — and the revelation of the righteous judgment of God,
45_2_6: who will render to each person according to his deeds:
45_2_7: to those who by perseverance in doing good seek for glory and honor and immortality — eternal life;
45_2_8: but to those who are selfishly ambitious — and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness — wrath and indignation.
45_2_9: There will be tribulation and distress for every soul of man who does evil — of the Jew first, and also of the Greek.
45_2_10: But glory and honor and peace to everyone who does good — to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.
45_2_11: For there is no partiality with God.
45_2_12: For all who have sinned without the Law will also perish without the Law — and all who have sinned under the Law will be judged by the Law.
45_2_13: For it is not the hearers of the Law who are righteous before God — but the doers of the Law will be justified.
45_2_14: For when Gentiles, who do not have the Law, instinctively do the things of the Law — these, not having the Law, are a law to themselves.
45_2_15: In that they show the work of the Law written in their hearts — their conscience also bearing witness, and their thoughts alternately accusing or defending them —
45_2_16: on the day when, according to my gospel, God will judge the secrets of men through Christ Jesus.
45_2_17: But if you bear the name "Jew" — and rely upon the Law, and boast in God,
45_2_18: and know His will, and approve the things that are essential, being instructed out of the Law,
45_2_19: and are confident that you yourself are a guide to the blind, a light to those in darkness,
45_2_20: a corrector of the foolish, a teacher of the immature — having in the Law the embodiment of knowledge and of the truth —
45_2_21: you, therefore, who teach another — do you not teach yourself? You who preach that one shall not steal — do you steal?
45_2_22: You who say that one should not commit adultery — do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols — do you rob temples?
45_2_23: You who boast in the Law — through your breaking the Law, do you dishonor God?
45_2_24: For "the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you" — just as it is written.
45_2_25: For circumcision is indeed of value if you practice the Law — but if you are a transgressor of the Law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.
45_2_26: So if the uncircumcised man keeps the requirements of the Law — will not his uncircumcision be regarded as circumcision?
45_2_27: And he who is physically uncircumcised, if he keeps the Law, will he not judge you — who though having the letter of the Law and circumcision are a transgressor of the Law?
45_2_28: For he is not a Jew who is one outwardly — nor is circumcision that which is outward in the flesh.
45_2_29: But he is a Jew who is one inwardly — and circumcision is that which is of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the letter; and his praise is not from men, but from God.
45_3_1: Then what advantage has the Jew? — or what is the benefit of circumcision?
45_3_2: Great in every respect. First of all, that they were entrusted with the oracles of God.
45_3_3: What then? If some did not believe, their unbelief will not nullify the faithfulness of God, will it?
45_3_4: May it never be! Rather, let God be found true, though every man be found a liar — as it is written: "That You may be justified in Your words, and prevail when You are judged."
45_3_5: But if our unrighteousness demonstrates the righteousness of God, what shall we say? The God who inflicts wrath is not unrighteous, is He? (I am speaking in human terms.)
45_3_6: May it never be! For otherwise, how will God judge the world?
45_3_7: But if through my lie the truth of God abounded to His glory, why am I also still being judged as a sinner?
45_3_8: And why not say (as we are slanderously reported and as some claim that we say), "Let us do evil that good may come"? Their condemnation is just.
45_3_9: What then? Are we better than they? Not at all! For we have already charged that both Jews and Greeks are all under sin.
45_3_10: As it is written: "There is none righteous — not even one.
45_3_11: There is none who understands; there is none who seeks for God.
45_3_12: All have turned aside; together they have become useless. There is none who does good — there is not even one."
45_3_13: "Their throat is an open grave; with their tongues they keep deceiving." "The poison of asps is under their lips."
45_3_14: "Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness."
45_3_15: "Their feet are swift to shed blood.
45_3_16: Destruction and misery are in their paths.
45_3_17: And the path of peace they have not known."
45_3_18: "There is no fear of God before their eyes."
45_3_19: Now we know that whatever the Law says, it speaks to those who are under the Law — so that every mouth may be closed, and all the world may become accountable to God.
45_3_20: Because by the works of the Law no flesh will be justified in His sight — for through the Law comes the knowledge of sin.
45_3_21: But now apart from the Law, the righteousness of God has been manifested — being witnessed by the Law and the Prophets;
45_3_22: even the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ — for all those who believe. For there is no distinction.
45_3_23: For all have sinned, and fall short of the glory of God —
45_3_24: being justified as a gift by His grace, through the redemption which is in Christ Jesus.
45_3_25: Whom God displayed publicly as a propitiation in His blood through faith — this was to demonstrate His righteousness, because in the forbearance of God, He passed over the sins previously committed.
45_3_26: For the demonstration, I say, of His righteousness at the present time — so that He would be just, and the justifier of the one who has faith in Jesus.
45_3_27: Where then is boasting? It is excluded. By what kind of law? Of works? No, but by a law of faith.
45_3_28: For we maintain that a man is justified by faith — apart from works of the Law.
45_3_29: Or is God the God of Jews only? Is He not the God of Gentiles also? Yes — of Gentiles also.
45_3_30: Since indeed God who will justify the circumcised by faith, and the uncircumcised through faith, is one.
45_3_31: Do we then nullify the Law through faith? May it never be! On the contrary — we establish the Law.
45_4_1: What then shall we say that Abraham, our forefather according to the flesh, has found?
45_4_2: For if Abraham was justified by works, he has something to boast about — but not before God.
45_4_3: For what does the Scripture say? "Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness."
45_4_4: Now to the one who works, his wage is not credited as a favor — but as what is due.
45_4_5: But to the one who does not work, but believes in Him who justifies the ungodly — his faith is credited as righteousness.
45_4_6: Just as David also speaks of the blessing on the man to whom God credits righteousness apart from works:
45_4_7: "Blessed are those whose lawless deeds have been forgiven, and whose sins have been covered.
45_4_8: Blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will not take into account."
45_4_9: Is this blessing then on the circumcised, or on the uncircumcised also? For we say, "Faith was credited to Abraham as righteousness."
45_4_10: How then was it credited? While he was circumcised, or uncircumcised? Not while circumcised — but while uncircumcised.
45_4_11: And he received the sign of circumcision — a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had while uncircumcised — so that he might be the father of all who believe without being circumcised, that righteousness might be credited to them,
45_4_12: and the father of circumcision to those who not only are of the circumcision, but who also follow in the steps of the faith of our father Abraham — which he had while uncircumcised.
45_4_13: For the promise to Abraham or to his descendants — that he would be heir of the world — was not through the Law, but through the righteousness of faith.
45_4_14: For if those who are of the Law are heirs, faith is made void, and the promise is nullified.
45_4_15: For the Law brings about wrath — but where there is no law, there also is no violation.
45_4_16: For this reason it is by faith — so that it may be in accordance with grace, in order that the promise may be guaranteed to all the descendants — not only to those who are of the Law, but also to those who are of the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all.
45_4_17: (As it is written, "A father of many nations have I made you.") In the presence of Him whom he believed — even God, who gives life to the dead and calls into being that which does not exist.
45_4_18: In hope against hope he believed — so that he might become a father of many nations, according to that which had been spoken: "So shall your descendants be."
45_4_19: And without becoming weak in faith, he contemplated his own body now as good as dead — since he was about a hundred years old — and the deadness of Sarah's womb.
45_4_20: Yet, with respect to the promise of God, he did not waver in unbelief — but grew strong in faith, giving glory to God.
45_4_21: And being fully assured that what God had promised, He was able also to perform.
45_4_22: Therefore it was also credited to him as righteousness.
45_4_23: Now not for his sake only was it written that it was credited to him —
45_4_24: but for our sake also, to whom it will be credited — to those who believe in Him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead.
45_4_25: He who was delivered over because of our transgressions — and was raised because of our justification.
45_5_1: Therefore, having been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.
45_5_2: Through Him also we have obtained our introduction by faith into this grace in which we stand. And we exult in hope of the glory of God.
45_5_3: And not only this — but we also exult in our tribulations, knowing that tribulation brings about perseverance.
45_5_4: And perseverance, proven character; and proven character, hope.
45_5_5: And hope does not disappoint — because the love of God has been poured out within our hearts through the Holy Spirit, who was given to us.
45_5_6: For while we were still helpless, at the right time Christ died for the ungodly.
45_5_7: For one will hardly die for a righteous man — though perhaps for the good man someone would dare even to die.
45_5_8: But God demonstrates His own love toward us — in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
45_5_9: Much more then, having now been justified by His blood — we shall be saved from the wrath of God through Him.
45_5_10: For if while we were enemies we were reconciled to God through the death of His Son — much more, having been reconciled, we shall be saved by His life.
45_5_11: And not only this — but we also exult in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received the reconciliation.
45_5_12: Therefore, just as through one man sin entered into the world — and death through sin, and so death spread to all men, because all sinned —
45_5_13: for until the Law sin was in the world — but sin is not imputed when there is no law.
45_5_14: Nevertheless, death reigned from Adam until Moses — even over those who had not sinned in the likeness of the offense of Adam, who is a type of Him who was to come.
45_5_15: But the free gift is not like the transgression. For if by the transgression of the one the many died, much more did the grace of God and the gift by the grace of the one Man, Jesus Christ, abound to the many.
45_5_16: And the gift is not like that which came through the one who sinned. For on the one hand the judgment arose from one transgression, resulting in condemnation — but on the other hand, the free gift arose from many transgressions, resulting in justification.
45_5_17: For if by the transgression of the one, death reigned through the one — much more those who receive the abundance of grace, and of the gift of righteousness, will reign in life through the One — Jesus Christ.
45_5_18: So then, as through one transgression there resulted condemnation to all men — even so through one act of righteousness, there resulted justification of life to all men.
45_5_19: For as through the one man's disobedience the many were made sinners — even so through the obedience of the One, the many will be made righteous.
45_5_20: And the Law came in so that the transgression would increase. But where sin increased, grace abounded all the more.
45_5_21: So that as sin reigned in death — even so grace would reign through righteousness to eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
45_6_1: What shall we say then? Are we to continue in sin so that grace may increase?
45_6_2: May it never be! How shall we who died to sin still live in it?
45_6_3: Or do you not know that all of us who have been baptized into Christ Jesus have been baptized into His death?
45_6_4: Therefore we have been buried with Him through baptism into death — so that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, so we too might walk in newness of life.
45_6_5: For if we have become united with Him in the likeness of His death — certainly we shall also be in the likeness of His resurrection.
45_6_6: Knowing this — that our old self was crucified with Him, in order that our body of sin might be done away with, so that we would no longer be slaves to sin.
45_6_7: For he who has died is freed from sin.
45_6_8: Now if we have died with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with Him.
45_6_9: Knowing that Christ, having been raised from the dead, is never to die again — death no longer is master over Him.
45_6_10: For the death that He died, He died to sin once for all — but the life that He lives, He lives to God.
45_6_11: Even so, consider yourselves to be dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus.
45_6_12: Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body — so that you obey its lusts.
45_6_13: And do not go on presenting the members of your body to sin as instruments of unrighteousness — but present yourselves to God as those alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness to God.
45_6_14: For sin shall not be master over you — for you are not under Law, but under grace.
45_6_15: What then? Shall we sin because we are not under Law but under grace? May it never be!
45_6_16: Do you not know that when you present yourselves to someone as slaves for obedience, you are slaves of the one whom you obey — either of sin, resulting in death, or of obedience, resulting in righteousness?
45_6_17: But thanks be to God that though you were slaves of sin — you became obedient from the heart to that form of teaching to which you were committed.
45_6_18: And having been freed from sin, you became slaves of righteousness.
45_6_19: I am speaking in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh. For just as you presented your members as slaves to impurity and to lawlessness, resulting in further lawlessness — so now present your members as slaves to righteousness, resulting in sanctification.
45_6_20: For when you were slaves of sin, you were free in regard to righteousness.
45_6_21: Therefore what benefit were you then deriving from the things of which you are now ashamed? For the outcome of those things is death.
45_6_22: But now, having been freed from sin, and enslaved to God — you derive your benefit, resulting in sanctification, and the outcome, eternal life.
45_6_23: For the wages of sin is death — but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
45_7_1: Or do you not know, brothers (for I am speaking to those who know the law), that the law has jurisdiction over a person as long as he lives?
45_7_2: For the married woman is bound by law to her husband while he is living — but if her husband dies, she is released from the law concerning the husband.
45_7_3: So then, if while her husband is living she is joined to another man, she shall be called an adulteress. But if her husband dies, she is free from the law — so that she is not an adulteress, though she is joined to another man.
45_7_4: Therefore, my brothers, you also were made to die to the Law through the body of Christ — so that you might be joined to another, to Him who was raised from the dead, that we might bear fruit for God.
45_7_5: For while we were in the flesh, the sinful passions, which were aroused by the Law, were at work in the members of our body to bear fruit for death.
45_7_6: But now we have been released from the Law — having died to that by which we were bound — so that we serve in newness of the Spirit, and not in oldness of the letter.
45_7_7: What shall we say then? Is the Law sin? May it never be! On the contrary, I would not have come to know sin except through the Law. For I would not have known about coveting if the Law had not said, "You shall not covet."
45_7_8: But sin, taking opportunity through the commandment, produced in me coveting of every kind. For apart from the Law sin is dead.
45_7_9: I was once alive apart from the Law — but when the commandment came, sin became alive, and I died.
45_7_10: And this commandment — which was to result in life — proved to result in death for me.
45_7_11: For sin, taking an opportunity through the commandment, deceived me — and through it killed me.
45_7_12: So then, the Law is holy, and the commandment is holy and righteous and good.
45_7_13: Therefore did that which is good become a cause of death for me? May it never be! Rather it was sin — in order that it might be shown to be sin by effecting my death through that which is good — so that through the commandment sin would become utterly sinful.
45_7_14: For we know that the Law is spiritual — but I am of flesh, sold into bondage to sin.
45_7_15: For what I am doing, I do not understand. For I am not practicing what I would like to do — but I am doing the very thing I hate.
45_7_16: But if I do the very thing I do not want to do, I agree with the Law — confessing that the Law is good.
45_7_17: So now, no longer am I the one doing it — but sin which dwells in me.
45_7_18: For I know that nothing good dwells in me — that is, in my flesh. For the wishing is present in me — but the doing of the good is not.
45_7_19: For the good that I want, I do not do — but I practice the very evil that I do not want.
45_7_20: But if I am doing the very thing I do not want, I am no longer the one doing it — but sin which dwells in me.
45_7_21: I find then the principle that evil is present in me — the one who wants to do good.
45_7_22: For I joyfully concur with the law of God in the inner man.
45_7_23: But I see a different law in the members of my body — waging war against the law of my mind, and making me a prisoner of the law of sin which is in my members.
45_7_24: Wretched man that I am! Who will set me free from the body of this death?
45_7_25: Thanks be to God — through Jesus Christ our Lord! So then, on the one hand I myself with my mind am serving the law of God — but on the other, with my flesh the law of sin.
45_8_1: Therefore there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.
45_8_2: For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set you free from the law of sin and of death.
45_8_3: For what the Law could not do — weak as it was through the flesh — God did. Sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and as an offering for sin, He condemned sin in the flesh —
45_8_4: so that the requirement of the Law might be fulfilled in us, who do not walk according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit.
45_8_5: For those who are according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh — but those who are according to the Spirit, the things of the Spirit.
45_8_6: For the mind set on the flesh is death — but the mind set on the Spirit is life and peace.
45_8_7: Because the mind set on the flesh is hostile toward God — for it does not subject itself to the law of God; for it is not even able to do so.
45_8_8: And those who are in the flesh cannot please God.
45_8_9: However, you are not in the flesh, but in the Spirit — if indeed the Spirit of God dwells in you. But if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he does not belong to Him.
45_8_10: And if Christ is in you, though the body is dead because of sin — yet the spirit is alive because of righteousness.
45_8_11: But if the Spirit of Him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you — He who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through His Spirit who dwells in you.
45_8_12: So then, brothers, we are under obligation — not to the flesh, to live according to the flesh.
45_8_13: For if you are living according to the flesh, you must die. But if by the Spirit you are putting to death the deeds of the body, you will live.
45_8_14: For all who are being led by the Spirit of God — these are sons of God.
45_8_15: For you have not received a spirit of slavery, leading to fear again — but you have received a spirit of adoption as sons, by which we cry out, "Abba! Father!"
45_8_16: The Spirit Himself testifies with our spirit that we are children of God.
45_8_17: And if children, then heirs also — heirs of God, and fellow heirs with Christ. If indeed we suffer with Him, so that we may also be glorified with Him.
45_8_18: For I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory that is to be revealed to us.
45_8_19: For the eager longing of the creation waits eagerly for the revealing of the sons of God.
45_8_20: For the creation was subjected to futility — not willingly, but because of Him who subjected it, in hope.
45_8_21: That the creation itself also will be set free from its slavery to corruption — into the freedom of the glory of the children of God.
45_8_22: For we know that the whole creation groans, and suffers the pains of childbirth together until now.
45_8_23: And not only this — but also we ourselves, having the firstfruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting eagerly for our adoption as sons — the redemption of our body.
45_8_24: For in hope we have been saved. But hope that is seen is not hope. For who hopes for what he already sees?
45_8_25: But if we hope for what we do not see, with perseverance we wait eagerly for it.
45_8_26: And in the same way the Spirit also helps our weakness. For we do not know how to pray as we should — but the Spirit Himself intercedes for us with groanings too deep for words.
45_8_27: And He who searches the hearts knows what the mind of the Spirit is — because He intercedes for the saints according to the will of God.
45_8_28: And we know that God causes all things to work together for good to those who love God — to those who are called according to His purpose.
45_8_29: For those whom He foreknew, He also predestined to become conformed to the image of His Son — so that He would be the firstborn among many brothers.
45_8_30: And these whom He predestined, He also called. And these whom He called, He also justified. And these whom He justified, He also glorified.
45_8_31: What then shall we say to these things? If God is for us, who is against us?
45_8_32: He who did not spare His own Son, but delivered Him over for us all — how will He not also with Him freely give us all things?
45_8_33: Who will bring a charge against God's elect? God is the One who justifies.
45_8_34: Who is the one who condemns? Christ Jesus is He who died — yes, rather who was raised, who is at the right hand of God, who also intercedes for us.
45_8_35: Who will separate us from the love of Christ? Will tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword?
45_8_36: Just as it is written: "For Your sake we are being put to death all day long; we were considered as sheep to be slaughtered."
45_8_37: But in all these things we overwhelmingly conquer through Him who loved us.
45_8_38: For I am convinced that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers,
45_8_39: nor height, nor depth, nor any other created thing, will be able to separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
45_9_1: I am telling the truth in Christ; I am not lying — my conscience testifies with me in the Holy Spirit —
45_9_2: that I have great sorrow and unceasing grief in my heart.
45_9_3: For I could wish that I myself were accursed, separated from Christ, for the sake of my brothers — my kinsmen according to the flesh.
45_9_4: Who are Israelites — to whom belongs the adoption as sons, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the Law, and the temple service, and the promises;
45_9_5: whose are the fathers — and from whom is the Christ according to the flesh, who is over all, God blessed forever. Amen.
45_9_6: But it is not as though the word of God has failed. For they are not all Israel who are descended from Israel.
45_9_7: Nor are they all children, because they are Abraham's descendants — but, "Through Isaac your descendants will be named."
45_9_8: That is — it is not the children of the flesh who are children of God. But the children of the promise are regarded as descendants.
45_9_9: For this is the word of promise: "At this time I will come, and Sarah shall have a son."
45_9_10: And not only this — but there was Rebekah also, when she had conceived twins by one man, our father Isaac.
45_9_11: For though the twins were not yet born, and had not done anything good or bad — so that God's purpose according to His choice would stand, not because of works, but because of Him who calls —
45_9_12: it was said to her: "The older will serve the younger."
45_9_13: Just as it is written: "Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated."
45_9_14: What shall we say then? There is no injustice with God, is there? May it never be!
45_9_15: For He says to Moses: "I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion."
45_9_16: So then it does not depend on the man who wills, or the man who runs — but on God who has mercy.
45_9_17: For the Scripture says to Pharaoh: "For this very purpose I raised you up — to demonstrate My power in you, and that My name might be proclaimed throughout the whole earth."
45_9_18: So then He has mercy on whom He desires — and He hardens whom He desires.
45_9_19: You will say to me then, "Why does He still find fault? For who resists His will?"
45_9_20: On the contrary, who are you, O man, who answers back to God? The thing molded will not say to the molder, "Why did you make me like this," will it?
45_9_21: Or does not the potter have a right over the clay — to make from the same lump one vessel for honorable use, and another for common use?
45_9_22: What if God — although willing to demonstrate His wrath, and to make His power known — endured with much patience vessels of wrath prepared for destruction?
45_9_23: And He did so to make known the riches of His glory upon vessels of mercy, which He prepared beforehand for glory.
45_9_24: Even us — whom He also called, not from among Jews only, but also from among Gentiles.
45_9_25: As He says also in Hosea: "I will call those who were not My people, 'My people' — and her who was not beloved, 'Beloved.'"
45_9_26: "And it shall be that in the place where it was said to them, 'You are not My people' — there they shall be called sons of the living God."
45_9_27: And Isaiah cries out concerning Israel: "Though the number of the sons of Israel be as the sand of the sea, only the remnant will be saved.
45_9_28: For the Lord will execute His word on the earth, completely and quickly."
45_9_29: And just as Isaiah foretold: "Unless the Lord of Sabaoth had left to us a posterity, we would have become like Sodom — and would have resembled Gomorrah."
45_9_30: What shall we say then? That Gentiles, who did not pursue righteousness, attained righteousness — even the righteousness which is by faith.
45_9_31: But Israel, pursuing a law of righteousness, did not arrive at that law.
45_9_32: Why? Because they did not pursue it by faith, but as though it were by works. They stumbled over the stumbling stone —
45_9_33: just as it is written: "Behold, I lay in Zion a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offense — and he who believes in Him will not be put to shame."
45_10_1: Brothers, my heart's desire and my prayer to God for them is for their salvation.
45_10_2: For I testify about them that they have a zeal for God — but not in accordance with knowledge.
45_10_3: For not knowing about God's righteousness — and seeking to establish their own — they did not subject themselves to the righteousness of God.
45_10_4: For Christ is the end of the Law for righteousness — to everyone who believes.
45_10_5: For Moses writes that the man who practices the righteousness which is based on Law shall live by that righteousness.
45_10_6: But the righteousness based on faith speaks like this: "Do not say in your heart, 'Who will ascend into heaven?'" (that is, to bring Christ down).
45_10_7: Or, "Who will descend into the abyss?" (that is, to bring Christ up from the dead).
45_10_8: But what does it say? "The word is near you — in your mouth and in your heart" — that is, the word of faith which we are preaching.
45_10_9: That if you confess with your mouth Jesus as Lord, and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead — you will be saved.
45_10_10: For with the heart a person believes, resulting in righteousness — and with the mouth he confesses, resulting in salvation.
45_10_11: For the Scripture says, "Whoever believes in Him will not be put to shame."
45_10_12: For there is no distinction between Jew and Greek — for the same Lord is Lord of all, abounding in riches for all who call on Him.
45_10_13: For "whoever will call on the name of the Lord will be saved."
45_10_14: How then will they call on Him in whom they have not believed? And how will they believe in Him whom they have not heard? And how will they hear without a preacher?
45_10_15: And how will they preach unless they are sent? Just as it is written: "How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news of good things!"
45_10_16: However, they did not all heed the good news. For Isaiah says, "Lord, who has believed our report?"
45_10_17: So faith comes from hearing — and hearing by the word of Christ.
45_10_18: But I say, surely they have never heard, have they? Indeed they have: "Their voice has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world."
45_10_19: But I say, surely Israel did not know, did they? At the first Moses says: "I will make you jealous by that which is not a nation; by a nation without understanding I will anger you."
45_10_20: And Isaiah is very bold, and says: "I was found by those who did not seek Me; I became manifest to those who did not ask for Me."
45_10_21: But as for Israel He says: "All the day long I have stretched out My hands to a disobedient and obstinate people."
45_11_1: I say then — God has not rejected His people, has He? May it never be! For I too am an Israelite, a descendant of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.
45_11_2: God has not rejected His people whom He foreknew. Or do you not know what the Scripture says in the passage about Elijah — how he pleads with God against Israel?
45_11_3: "Lord, they have killed Your prophets; they have torn down Your altars; and I alone am left, and they are seeking my life."
45_11_4: But what is the divine response to him? "I have kept for Myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal."
45_11_5: In the same way then, there has also come to be at the present time a remnant according to God's gracious choice.
45_11_6: But if it is by grace, it is no longer on the basis of works — otherwise grace is no longer grace.
45_11_7: What then? What Israel is seeking, it has not obtained. But those who were chosen obtained it — and the rest were hardened.
45_11_8: Just as it is written: "God gave them a spirit of stupor — eyes to see not, and ears to hear not, down to this very day."
45_11_9: And David says: "Let their table become a snare and a trap, and a stumbling block — and a retribution to them.
45_11_10: Let their eyes be darkened to see not, and bend their backs forever."
45_11_11: I say then — they did not stumble so as to fall, did they? May it never be! But by their transgression salvation has come to the Gentiles, to make them jealous.
45_11_12: Now if their transgression is riches for the world, and their failure is riches for the Gentiles — how much more will their fulfillment be?
45_11_13: But I am speaking to you who are Gentiles. Inasmuch then as I am an apostle of Gentiles, I magnify my ministry —
45_11_14: if somehow I might move to jealousy my fellow countrymen, and save some of them.
45_11_15: For if their rejection is the reconciliation of the world, what will their acceptance be but life from the dead?
45_11_16: And if the firstfruits is holy, the lump is also; and if the root is holy, the branches are too.
45_11_17: But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, being a wild olive, were grafted in among them, and became partaker with them of the rich root of the olive tree —
45_11_18: do not be arrogant toward the branches. But if you are arrogant — remember that it is not you who supports the root, but the root supports you.
45_11_19: You will say then, "Branches were broken off, so that I might be grafted in."
45_11_20: Quite right! They were broken off for their unbelief — but you stand by your faith. Do not be conceited, but fear.
45_11_21: For if God did not spare the natural branches, He will not spare you either.
45_11_22: Behold then the kindness and severity of God: to those who fell, severity; but to you, God's kindness — if you continue in His kindness; otherwise you also will be cut off.
45_11_23: And they also, if they do not continue in their unbelief, will be grafted in — for God is able to graft them in again.
45_11_24: For if you were cut off from what is by nature a wild olive tree, and were grafted contrary to nature into a cultivated olive tree — how much more will these who are the natural branches be grafted into their own olive tree?
45_11_25: For I do not want you, brothers, to be uninformed of this mystery — so that you will not be wise in your own estimation — that a partial hardening has happened to Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in.
45_11_26: And so all Israel will be saved. Just as it is written: "The Deliverer will come from Zion; He will remove ungodliness from Jacob.
45_11_27: And this is My covenant with them, when I take away their sins."
45_11_28: From the standpoint of the gospel they are enemies for your sake — but from the standpoint of God's choice, they are beloved for the sake of the fathers.
45_11_29: For the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.
45_11_30: For just as you once were disobedient to God, but now have been shown mercy because of their disobedience —
45_11_31: so these also now have been disobedient — that because of the mercy shown to you, they also may now be shown mercy.
45_11_32: For God has shut up all in disobedience — so that He may show mercy to all.
45_11_33: Oh, the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are His judgments — and unfathomable His ways!
45_11_34: For who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who became His counselor?
45_11_35: Or who has first given to Him, that it might be paid back to him?
45_11_36: For from Him, and through Him, and to Him are all things. To Him be the glory forever. Amen.
45_12_1: Therefore, I urge you, brothers, by the mercies of God — to present your bodies as a living and holy sacrifice, acceptable to God, which is your spiritual service of worship.
45_12_2: And do not be conformed to this world — but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may prove what the will of God is — that which is good and acceptable and perfect.
45_12_3: For through the grace given to me, I say to everyone among you not to think more highly of himself than he ought to think — but to think so as to have sound judgment, as God has allotted to each a measure of faith.
45_12_4: For just as we have many members in one body, and all the members do not have the same function —
45_12_5: so we, who are many, are one body in Christ — and individually members one of another.
45_12_6: Since we have gifts that differ according to the grace given to us, let each exercise them accordingly: if prophecy, according to the proportion of his faith;
45_12_7: if service, in his serving; or he who teaches, in his teaching;
45_12_8: or he who exhorts, in his exhortation; he who gives, with liberality; he who leads, with diligence; he who shows mercy, with cheerfulness.
45_12_9: Let love be without hypocrisy. Abhor what is evil; cling to what is good.
45_12_10: Be devoted to one another in brotherly love — give preference to one another in honor.
45_12_11: Not lagging behind in diligence — fervent in spirit, serving the Lord.
45_12_12: Rejoicing in hope, persevering in tribulation, devoted to prayer.
45_12_13: Contributing to the needs of the saints — practicing hospitality.
45_12_14: Bless those who persecute you. Bless and do not curse.
45_12_15: Rejoice with those who rejoice, and weep with those who weep.
45_12_16: Be of the same mind toward one another. Do not be haughty in mind — but associate with the lowly. Do not be wise in your own estimation.
45_12_17: Never pay back evil for evil to anyone. Respect what is right in the sight of all men.
45_12_18: If possible, so far as it depends on you — be at peace with all men.
45_12_19: Never take your own revenge, beloved — but leave room for the wrath of God. For it is written, "Vengeance is Mine; I will repay," says the Lord.
45_12_20: But "if your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink — for in so doing you will heap burning coals on his head."
45_12_21: Do not be overcome by evil — but overcome evil with good.
45_13_1: Every person is to be in subjection to the governing authorities. For there is no authority except from God — and those which exist are established by God.
45_13_2: Therefore he who resists authority has opposed the ordinance of God — and they who have opposed will receive condemnation upon themselves.
45_13_3: For rulers are not a cause of fear for good behavior, but for evil. Do you want to have no fear of authority? Do what is good — and you will have praise from the same.
45_13_4: For it is a minister of God to you for good. But if you do what is evil, be afraid — for it does not bear the sword for nothing. For it is a minister of God, an avenger who brings wrath on the one who practices evil.
45_13_5: Therefore it is necessary to be in subjection — not only because of wrath, but also for conscience' sake.
45_13_6: For because of this you also pay taxes — for rulers are servants of God, devoting themselves to this very thing.
45_13_7: Render to all what is due them: tax to whom tax is due; custom to whom custom is due; fear to whom fear is due; honor to whom honor is due.
45_13_8: Owe nothing to anyone — except to love one another. For he who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law.
45_13_9: For this — "You shall not commit adultery, you shall not murder, you shall not steal, you shall not covet," and if there is any other commandment — it is summed up in this saying: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself."
45_13_10: Love does no wrong to a neighbor. Therefore love is the fulfillment of the law.
45_13_11: And do this, knowing the time — that it is already the hour for you to wake from sleep. For now salvation is nearer to us than when we believed.
45_13_12: The night is almost gone, and the day is near. Therefore, let us lay aside the deeds of darkness — and put on the armor of light.
45_13_13: Let us behave properly as in the day — not in carousing and drunkenness, not in sexual promiscuity and sensuality, not in strife and jealousy.
45_13_14: But put on the Lord Jesus Christ — and make no provision for the flesh, in regard to its lusts.
45_14_1: Now accept the one who is weak in faith — but not for the purpose of passing judgment on his opinions.
45_14_2: One person has faith that he may eat all things — but he who is weak eats vegetables only.
45_14_3: The one who eats is not to regard with contempt the one who does not eat — and the one who does not eat is not to judge the one who eats. For God has accepted him.
45_14_4: Who are you to judge the servant of another? To his own master he stands or falls. And he will stand — for the Lord is able to make him stand.
45_14_5: One person regards one day above another, another regards every day alike. Each person must be fully convinced in his own mind.
45_14_6: He who observes the day, observes it for the Lord. And he who eats, does so for the Lord — for he gives thanks to God. And he who does not eat, for the Lord he does not eat — and gives thanks to God.
45_14_7: For not one of us lives for himself — and not one dies for himself.
45_14_8: For if we live, we live for the Lord; or if we die, we die for the Lord. Therefore whether we live or die, we are the Lord's.
45_14_9: For to this end Christ died and lived again — that He might be Lord both of the dead and of the living.
45_14_10: But you — why do you judge your brother? Or you again — why do you regard your brother with contempt? For we will all stand before the judgment seat of God.
45_14_11: For it is written: "As I live, says the Lord — every knee shall bow to Me, and every tongue shall give praise to God."
45_14_12: So then, each one of us will give an account of himself to God.
45_14_13: Therefore let us not judge one another anymore — but rather determine this: not to put an obstacle or a stumbling block in a brother's way.
45_14_14: I know and am convinced in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself — but to him who thinks anything to be unclean, to him it is unclean.
45_14_15: For if because of food your brother is hurt, you are no longer walking according to love. Do not destroy with your food him for whom Christ died.
45_14_16: Therefore do not let what is for you a good thing be spoken of as evil.
45_14_17: For the kingdom of God is not eating and drinking — but righteousness, and peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.
45_14_18: For the one who serves Christ in this way is acceptable to God — and approved by men.
45_14_19: So then, let us pursue the things which make for peace — and the building up of one another.
45_14_20: Do not tear down the work of God for the sake of food. All things indeed are clean — but they are evil for the man who eats and gives offense.
45_14_21: It is good not to eat meat or to drink wine — or to do anything by which your brother stumbles.
45_14_22: The faith which you have, have as your own conviction before God. Happy is he who does not condemn himself in what he approves.
45_14_23: But he who doubts is condemned if he eats — because his eating is not from faith. And whatever is not from faith is sin.
45_15_1: Now we who are strong ought to bear the weaknesses of those without strength — and not just please ourselves.
45_15_2: Each of us is to please his neighbor for his good — to his edification.
45_15_3: For even Christ did not please Himself — but as it is written: "The reproaches of those who reproached You fell on Me."
45_15_4: For whatever was written in earlier times was written for our instruction — so that through perseverance and the encouragement of the Scriptures we might have hope.
45_15_5: Now may the God who gives perseverance and encouragement grant you to be of the same mind with one another, according to Christ Jesus —
45_15_6: that with one accord, you may with one voice glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
45_15_7: Therefore, accept one another, just as Christ also accepted us — to the glory of God.
45_15_8: For I say that Christ has become a servant of the circumcision on behalf of the truth of God — to confirm the promises given to the fathers,
45_15_9: and that the Gentiles might glorify God for His mercy. Just as it is written: "Therefore I will give praise to You among the Gentiles, and I will sing to Your name."
45_15_10: And again he says: "Rejoice, O Gentiles, with His people."
45_15_11: And again: "Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles — and let all the peoples praise Him."
45_15_12: And again Isaiah says: "There shall come the root of Jesse, and He who arises to rule over the Gentiles — in Him shall the Gentiles hope."
45_15_13: Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing — so that you will abound in hope, by the power of the Holy Spirit.
45_15_14: And concerning you, my brothers, I myself also am convinced that you yourselves are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, and able also to admonish one another.
45_15_15: But I have written very boldly to you on some points — so as to remind you again, because of the grace that was given me from God,
45_15_16: to be a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles — ministering as a priest the gospel of God, so that my offering of the Gentiles may become acceptable, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.
45_15_17: Therefore in Christ Jesus I have found reason for boasting in things pertaining to God.
45_15_18: For I will not presume to speak of anything except what Christ has accomplished through me — resulting in the obedience of the Gentiles by word and deed,
45_15_19: in the power of signs and wonders, in the power of the Spirit. So that from Jerusalem and round about as far as Illyricum I have fully preached the gospel of Christ.
45_15_20: And thus I aspired to preach the gospel — not where Christ was already named — so that I would not build on another man's foundation.
45_15_21: But as it is written: "They who had no news of Him shall see — and they who have not heard shall understand."
45_15_22: For this reason I have often been hindered from coming to you.
45_15_23: But now, with no further place for me in these regions — and since I have had for many years a longing to come to you,
45_15_24: whenever I go to Spain — for I hope to see you in passing, and to be helped on my way there by you, when I have first enjoyed your company for a while.
45_15_25: But now, I am going to Jerusalem — serving the saints.
45_15_26: For Macedonia and Achaia have been pleased to make a contribution for the poor among the saints in Jerusalem.
45_15_27: Yes, they were pleased to do so — and they are indebted to them. For if the Gentiles have shared in their spiritual things, they are indebted to minister to them also in material things.
45_15_28: Therefore, when I have finished this — and have put my seal on this fruit of theirs — I will go on by way of you to Spain.
45_15_29: And I know that when I come to you, I will come in the fullness of the blessing of Christ.
45_15_30: Now I urge you, brothers, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Spirit, to strive together with me in your prayers to God for me —
45_15_31: that I may be rescued from those who are disobedient in Judea, and that my service for Jerusalem may prove acceptable to the saints.
45_15_32: So that I may come to you in joy by the will of God, and find refreshing rest in your company.
45_15_33: Now the God of peace be with you all. Amen.
45_16_1: I commend to you our sister Phoebe — who is a servant of the church which is at Cenchrea —
45_16_2: that you receive her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the saints, and that you help her in whatever matter she may have need of you. For she herself has also been a helper of many, and of myself as well.
45_16_3: Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus,
45_16_4: who for my life risked their own necks — to whom not only do I give thanks, but also all the churches of the Gentiles.
45_16_5: Also greet the church that is in their house. Greet Epaenetus, my beloved, who is the firstfruits to Christ from Asia.
45_16_6: Greet Mary, who has worked hard for you.
45_16_7: Greet Andronicus and Junia, my kinsmen and my fellow prisoners — who are outstanding among the apostles, who also were in Christ before me.
45_16_8: Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord.
45_16_9: Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ — and Stachys my beloved.
45_16_10: Greet Apelles, the approved in Christ. Greet those who are of the household of Aristobulus.
45_16_11: Greet Herodion, my kinsman. Greet those of the household of Narcissus, who are in the Lord.
45_16_12: Greet Tryphaena and Tryphosa, workers in the Lord. Greet Persis the beloved, who has worked hard in the Lord.
45_16_13: Greet Rufus, a choice man in the Lord — also his mother and mine.
45_16_14: Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers with them.
45_16_15: Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints who are with them.
45_16_16: Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the churches of Christ greet you.
45_16_17: Now I urge you, brothers, keep your eye on those who cause dissensions and hindrances contrary to the teaching which you learned — and turn away from them.
45_16_18: For such men are slaves not of our Lord Christ, but of their own appetites — and by their smooth and flattering speech they deceive the hearts of the unsuspecting.
45_16_19: For the report of your obedience has reached to all. Therefore I am rejoicing over you. But I want you to be wise in what is good — and innocent in what is evil.
45_16_20: And the God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus be with you.
45_16_21: Timothy, my fellow worker, greets you — and so do Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my kinsmen.
45_16_22: I, Tertius, who write this letter, greet you in the Lord.
45_16_23: Gaius, host to me and to the whole church, greets you. Erastus, the city treasurer, greets you — and Quartus, the brother.
45_16_24: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
45_16_25: Now to Him who is able to establish you, according to my gospel and the preaching of Jesus Christ — according to the revelation of the mystery which has been kept secret for long ages past,
45_16_26: but now is manifested — and by the Scriptures of the prophets, according to the commandment of the eternal God, has been made known to all the nations, leading to obedience of faith —
45_16_27: to the only wise God, through Jesus Christ — to Him be the glory forever. Amen.
48_1_1: Paul, an apostle — not from men nor through any man, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised Him from the dead —
48_1_2: and all the brothers who are with me, to the churches of Galatia:
48_1_3: Grace to you, and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ —
48_1_4: who gave Himself for our sins, so that He might rescue us from this present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father —
48_1_5: to whom be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
48_1_6: I am amazed that you are so quickly deserting Him who called you by the grace of Christ — for a different gospel,
48_1_7: which is really not another. There are some who are disturbing you, and want to distort the gospel of Christ.
48_1_8: But even if we, or an angel from heaven, should preach to you a gospel contrary to what we have preached to you — let him be accursed!
48_1_9: As we have said before, so I now say again: if anyone is preaching to you a gospel contrary to what you received — let him be accursed!
48_1_10: For am I now seeking the favor of men, or of God? Or am I striving to please men? If I were still trying to please men, I would not be a bondservant of Christ.
48_1_11: I would have you know, brothers, that the gospel which was preached by me is not according to man.
48_1_12: For I neither received it from man, nor was I taught it — but it came through a revelation of Jesus Christ.
48_1_13: For you have heard of my former manner of life in Judaism — how I used to persecute the church of God beyond measure, and tried to destroy it.
48_1_14: And I was advancing in Judaism beyond many of my contemporaries among my countrymen — being more extremely zealous for my ancestral traditions.
48_1_15: But when God — who had set me apart from my mother's womb, and called me through His grace — was pleased
48_1_16: to reveal His Son in me, so that I might preach Him among the Gentiles, I did not immediately consult with flesh and blood —
48_1_17: nor did I go up to Jerusalem to those who were apostles before me. But I went away to Arabia, and returned once more to Damascus.
48_1_18: Then three years later I went up to Jerusalem to become acquainted with Cephas — and I stayed with him fifteen days.
48_1_19: But I did not see any of the other apostles — except James, the Lord's brother.
48_1_20: (In what I am writing to you, behold — before God, I am not lying.)
48_1_21: Then I went into the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
48_1_22: I was still unknown by sight to the churches of Judea which were in Christ.
48_1_23: But only — they kept hearing, "He who once persecuted us is now preaching the faith which he once tried to destroy."
48_1_24: And they were glorifying God because of me.
48_2_1: Then after fourteen years, I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking Titus along also.
48_2_2: And I went up because of a revelation. And I submitted to them the gospel which I preach among the Gentiles — but I did so in private to those who were of reputation, for fear that I might be running, or had run, in vain.
48_2_3: But not even Titus, who was with me, was compelled to be circumcised — though he was a Greek.
48_2_4: But it was because of the false brothers who had been secretly brought in — who had sneaked in to spy on our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, in order to bring us into bondage.
48_2_5: We did not yield in submission to them, even for an hour — so that the truth of the gospel would remain with you.
48_2_6: But from those who were of high reputation (what they were makes no difference to me — God shows no partiality) — those of reputation contributed nothing to me.
48_2_7: But on the contrary — seeing that I had been entrusted with the gospel to the uncircumcised, just as Peter had been to the circumcised
48_2_8: (for He who effectively worked for Peter in his apostleship to the circumcised, also worked effectively for me to the Gentiles),
48_2_9: and recognizing the grace that had been given to me — James and Cephas and John, who were considered to be pillars, gave to Barnabas and me the right hand of fellowship — that we might go to the Gentiles, and they to the circumcised.
48_2_10: Only they asked us to remember the poor — the very thing I also was eager to do.
48_2_11: But when Cephas came to Antioch, I opposed him to his face — because he stood condemned.
48_2_12: For prior to the coming of certain men from James, he used to eat with the Gentiles. But when they came, he began to withdraw and hold himself aloof — fearing the party of the circumcision.
48_2_13: And the rest of the Jews joined him in hypocrisy — so that even Barnabas was carried away by their hypocrisy.
48_2_14: But when I saw that they were not straightforward about the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas in front of them all: "If you, being a Jew, live like the Gentiles, and not like the Jews — how is it that you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?"
48_2_15: We are Jews by nature, and not sinners from among the Gentiles —
48_2_16: knowing that a man is not justified by works of the Law, but through faith in Jesus Christ. Even we have believed in Christ Jesus — so that we may be justified by faith in Christ, and not by works of the Law. For by works of the Law no flesh will be justified.
48_2_17: But if, while seeking to be justified in Christ, we ourselves have also been found sinners — is Christ then a minister of sin? Absolutely not!
48_2_18: For if I rebuild what I once destroyed, I prove myself to be a transgressor.
48_2_19: For through the Law I died to the Law — so that I might live to God.
48_2_20: I have been crucified with Christ. And it is no longer I who live — but Christ lives in me. And the life which I now live in the flesh, I live by faith in the Son of God — who loved me and gave Himself up for me.
48_2_21: I do not nullify the grace of God — for if righteousness comes through the Law, then Christ died for nothing.
48_3_1: You foolish Galatians! Who has bewitched you — before whose eyes Jesus Christ was publicly portrayed as crucified?
48_3_2: This is the only thing I want to find out from you: did you receive the Spirit by the works of the Law, or by hearing with faith?
48_3_3: Are you so foolish? Having begun by the Spirit, are you now being perfected by the flesh?
48_3_4: Did you suffer so many things in vain — if indeed it was in vain?
48_3_5: So then, does He who supplies you with the Spirit and works miracles among you, do it by the works of the Law, or by hearing with faith?
48_3_6: Just as Abraham believed God — and it was reckoned to him as righteousness.
48_3_7: Therefore, recognize this: that those who are of faith are sons of Abraham.
48_3_8: And the Scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, preached the gospel beforehand to Abraham, saying, "All the nations will be blessed in you."
48_3_9: So then, those who are of faith are blessed with Abraham, the believer.
48_3_10: For all who are of the works of the Law are under a curse — for it is written, "Cursed is everyone who does not abide by all things written in the book of the Law, to perform them."
48_3_11: Now that no one is justified by the Law before God is evident — for, "The righteous one shall live by faith."
48_3_12: And the Law is not of faith. Rather, "The one who does these things will live by them."
48_3_13: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the Law — having become a curse for us. For it is written, "Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree" —
48_3_14: so that in Christ Jesus the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles, and that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.
48_3_15: Brothers, I speak in human terms: even with a man's covenant, when it has been ratified, no one sets it aside or adds conditions to it.
48_3_16: Now the promises were spoken to Abraham and to his Seed. He does not say, "And to seeds," as referring to many — but rather to one: "And to your Seed," who is Christ.
48_3_17: What I am saying is this: the Law, which came four hundred and thirty years later, does not invalidate a covenant previously ratified by God — so as to nullify the promise.
48_3_18: For if the inheritance is based on the Law, it is no longer based on a promise — but God has granted it to Abraham by means of a promise.
48_3_19: Why the Law then? It was added because of transgressions — until the Seed should come, to whom the promise had been made — and it was ordained through angels by the agency of a mediator.
48_3_20: Now a mediator is not for one party only — whereas God is one.
48_3_21: Is the Law then contrary to the promises of God? Absolutely not! For if a law had been given which was able to impart life, then righteousness would indeed have been based on law.
48_3_22: But the Scripture has shut up everyone under sin — so that the promise by faith in Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe.
48_3_23: But before faith came, we were kept in custody under the Law — being shut up to the faith which was later to be revealed.
48_3_24: Therefore the Law has become our tutor to lead us to Christ — so that we may be justified by faith.
48_3_25: But now that faith has come, we are no longer under a tutor.
48_3_26: For you are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus.
48_3_27: For all of you who were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ.
48_3_28: There is neither Jew nor Greek; there is neither slave nor free; there is neither male nor female — for you are all one in Christ Jesus.
48_3_29: And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham's offspring — heirs according to promise.
48_4_1: Now I say, as long as the heir is a child, he does not differ at all from a slave — although he is owner of everything,
48_4_2: but he is under guardians and managers until the date set by the father.
48_4_3: So we also, when we were children, were held in bondage under the elementary principles of the world.
48_4_4: But when the fullness of the time came, God sent forth His Son — born of a woman, born under the Law,
48_4_5: in order that He might redeem those who were under the Law — that we might receive the adoption as sons.
48_4_6: And because you are sons, God has sent forth the Spirit of His Son into our hearts — crying out, "Abba! Father!"
48_4_7: Therefore you are no longer a slave, but a son. And if a son, then an heir through God.
48_4_8: However at that time — when you did not know God — you were slaves to those which by nature are no gods.
48_4_9: But now that you have come to know God — or rather, to be known by God — how is it that you turn back again to the weak and worthless elementary principles, to which you desire to be enslaved all over again?
48_4_10: You observe days and months and seasons and years.
48_4_11: I fear for you — that perhaps I have labored over you in vain.
48_4_12: I beg of you, brothers, become as I am — for I also have become as you are. You have done me no wrong;
48_4_13: but you know that it was because of a bodily illness that I preached the gospel to you the first time.
48_4_14: And though my bodily condition was a trial to you, you did not despise or loathe me. But you received me as an angel of God — as Christ Jesus Himself.
48_4_15: Where then is that sense of blessing you had? For I bear you witness that, if possible, you would have plucked out your eyes and given them to me.
48_4_16: So have I become your enemy by telling you the truth?
48_4_17: They eagerly seek you — not commendably, but they want to shut you out, so that you will seek them.
48_4_18: But it is good always to be eagerly sought in a commendable manner — and not only when I am present with you.
48_4_19: My children, with whom I am again in labor pains until Christ is formed in you —
48_4_20: I would gladly be present with you now, and to change my tone — for I am perplexed about you.
48_4_21: Tell me, you who want to be under the Law — do you not listen to the Law?
48_4_22: For it is written that Abraham had two sons — one by the slave woman, and one by the free woman.
48_4_23: But the son by the slave woman was born according to the flesh — and the son by the free woman, through the promise.
48_4_24: These things are spoken allegorically — for these women are two covenants. One is from Mount Sinai, bearing children who are to be slaves — she is Hagar.
48_4_25: Now this Hagar represents Mount Sinai in Arabia — and corresponds to the present Jerusalem, for she is in slavery with her children.
48_4_26: But the Jerusalem above is free — she is our mother.
48_4_27: For it is written, "Rejoice, barren woman who does not bear; break forth and shout, you who are not in labor — for more numerous are the children of the desolate, than of the one who has a husband."
48_4_28: And we, brothers — like Isaac — are children of promise.
48_4_29: But just as at that time, the one who was born according to the flesh persecuted the one who was born according to the Spirit — so it is now also.
48_4_30: But what does the Scripture say? "Cast out the slave woman and her son — for the son of the slave woman shall not be an heir with the son of the free woman."
48_4_31: So then, brothers, we are not children of a slave woman, but of the free woman.
48_5_1: It was for freedom that Christ set us free. Therefore stand firm, and do not be subject again to a yoke of slavery.
48_5_2: Behold — I, Paul, say to you that if you receive circumcision, Christ will be of no benefit to you.
48_5_3: And I testify again to every man who receives circumcision, that he is under obligation to keep the whole Law.
48_5_4: You who are seeking to be justified by Law have been severed from Christ — you have fallen from grace.
48_5_5: For we, through the Spirit, by faith, are eagerly waiting for the hope of righteousness.
48_5_6: For in Christ Jesus, neither circumcision nor uncircumcision means anything — but only faith working through love.
48_5_7: You were running well; who hindered you from obeying the truth?
48_5_8: This persuasion did not come from the One who calls you.
48_5_9: A little leaven leavens the whole lump of dough.
48_5_10: I have confidence in you in the Lord, that you will adopt no other view. But the one who is disturbing you will bear his judgment, whoever he is.
48_5_11: But I, brothers — if I still preach circumcision, why am I still persecuted? Then the stumbling block of the cross has been abolished.
48_5_12: I wish that those who are troubling you would even mutilate themselves!
48_5_13: For you were called to freedom, brothers — only do not turn your freedom into an opportunity for the flesh, but through love serve one another.
48_5_14: For the whole Law is fulfilled in one word: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself."
48_5_15: But if you bite and devour one another, take care that you are not consumed by one another.
48_5_16: But I say, walk by the Spirit, and you will not carry out the desire of the flesh.
48_5_17: For the flesh sets its desire against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh — for these are in opposition to one another, so that you may not do the things you please.
48_5_18: But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the Law.
48_5_19: Now the deeds of the flesh are evident — sexual immorality, impurity, sensuality,
48_5_20: idolatry, sorcery, hostilities, strife, jealousy, outbursts of anger, selfish ambition, dissensions, factions,
48_5_21: envying, drunkenness, carousing, and things like these — of which I forewarn you, just as I have forewarned you, that those who practice such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.
48_5_22: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,
48_5_23: gentleness, self-control. Against such things there is no law.
48_5_24: Now those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires.
48_5_25: If we live by the Spirit, let us also walk by the Spirit.
48_5_26: Let us not become boastful, challenging one another, envying one another.
48_6_1: Brothers, even if anyone is caught in any trespass, you who are spiritual restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness — looking to yourself, so that you too will not be tempted.
48_6_2: Bear one another's burdens — and so fulfill the law of Christ.
48_6_3: For if anyone thinks he is something, when he is nothing — he deceives himself.
48_6_4: But each one must examine his own work — and then he will have reason for boasting in regard to himself alone, and not in regard to another.
48_6_5: For each one will bear his own load.
48_6_6: And the one who is taught the word is to share all good things with the one who teaches him.
48_6_7: Do not be deceived: God is not mocked. For whatever a man sows — this he will also reap.
48_6_8: For the one who sows to his own flesh will reap corruption from the flesh — but the one who sows to the Spirit will reap eternal life from the Spirit.
48_6_9: Let us not lose heart in doing good. For in due time we will reap, if we do not grow weary.
48_6_10: So then, while we have opportunity, let us do good to all people — and especially to those who are of the household of the faith.
48_6_11: See with what large letters I am writing to you with my own hand!
48_6_12: Those who desire to make a good showing in the flesh — they try to compel you to be circumcised, simply so that they will not be persecuted for the cross of Christ.
48_6_13: For those who are circumcised do not even keep the Law themselves — but they desire to have you circumcised, so that they may boast in your flesh.
48_6_14: But may it never be that I should boast — except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ — through which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
48_6_15: For neither is circumcision anything, nor uncircumcision — but a new creation.
48_6_16: And those who will walk by this rule — peace and mercy be upon them, and upon the Israel of God.
48_6_17: From now on, let no one cause trouble for me — for I bear on my body the brand-marks of Jesus.
48_6_18: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers. Amen.
50_1_1: Paul and Timothy, bondservants of Christ Jesus — to all the saints in Christ Jesus who are in Philippi, with the overseers and deacons:
50_1_2: Grace to you, and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
50_1_3: I thank my God in all my remembrance of you,
50_1_4: always — in every prayer of mine for you all — making my prayer with joy,
50_1_5: because of your partnership in the gospel from the first day until now.
50_1_6: I am confident of this very thing: that He who began a good work in you will bring it to completion at the day of Jesus Christ.
50_1_7: It is right for me to think this way about all of you — because I have you in my heart, since both in my chains and in the defense and confirmation of the gospel, all of you share with me in this grace.
50_1_8: For God is my witness — how I long for all of you with the affection of Christ Jesus.
50_1_9: And this is my prayer: that your love may abound still more and more, in full knowledge and all discernment,
50_1_10: so that you may approve the things that are excellent — that you may be sincere and blameless until the day of Christ,
50_1_11: filled with the fruit of righteousness which comes through Jesus Christ — to the glory and praise of God.
50_1_12: Now I want you to know, brothers, that what has happened to me has actually served to advance the gospel,
50_1_13: so that my chains in Christ have become known throughout the whole praetorian guard, and to all the rest;
50_1_14: and most of the brothers, having confidence in the Lord because of my chains, are much more bold to speak the word without fear.
50_1_15: Some, indeed, preach Christ even out of envy and rivalry — but others out of good will.
50_1_16: These do it out of love, knowing that I am put here for the defense of the gospel.
50_1_17: But the others proclaim Christ out of selfish ambition, not sincerely — supposing they will add affliction to my chains.
50_1_18: What then? Only that in every way, whether in pretense or in truth, Christ is proclaimed — and in this I rejoice. Yes, and I will continue to rejoice.
50_1_19: For I know that this will turn out for my deliverance through your prayer and the supply of the Spirit of Jesus Christ,
50_1_20: according to my eager expectation and hope — that I will not be put to shame in anything, but that with all boldness, as always, even now Christ will be magnified in my body, whether through life or through death.
50_1_21: For to me, to live is Christ — and to die is gain.
50_1_22: But if I am to live on in the flesh, this will mean fruitful labor for me. Yet what I shall choose, I cannot tell.
50_1_23: I am hard-pressed between the two — having the desire to depart and be with Christ, for that is far better.
50_1_24: But to remain in the flesh is more necessary for your sake.
50_1_25: And being convinced of this, I know that I will remain — and I will continue with you all for your progress and joy in the faith,
50_1_26: so that your boasting may abound in Christ Jesus on account of me, through my coming to you again.
50_1_27: Only let your conduct be worthy of the gospel of Christ — so that whether I come and see you, or am absent, I may hear of your circumstances: that you stand firm in one spirit, with one mind striving together for the faith of the gospel,
50_1_28: and not in any way frightened by your opponents. This is a sign of destruction to them, but of your salvation — and that from God.
50_1_29: For it has been granted to you for the sake of Christ — not only to believe in Him, but also to suffer for His sake,
50_1_30: having the same conflict that you saw in me, and now hear to be in me.
50_2_1: If, then, there is any encouragement in Christ, any comfort of love, any fellowship of the Spirit, any affection and compassion,
50_2_2: make my joy complete — by being of the same mind, having the same love, being united in spirit, intent on one purpose.
50_2_3: Do nothing from selfish ambition or empty conceit. Rather, in humility consider others as more important than yourselves.
50_2_4: Do not look out only for your own interests, but also for the interests of others.
50_2_5: Have this mind among yourselves, which was also in Christ Jesus —
50_2_6: who, although He existed in the form of God, did not regard equality with God a thing to be grasped,
50_2_7: but emptied Himself, taking the form of a bondservant, being made in the likeness of men.
50_2_8: And being found in appearance as a man, He humbled Himself by becoming obedient — to the point of death, even death on a cross.
50_2_9: For this reason God highly exalted Him, and bestowed on Him the name that is above every name —
50_2_10: so that at the name of Jesus every knee will bow — of those in heaven, and on earth, and under the earth —
50_2_11: and that every tongue will confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
50_2_12: Therefore, my beloved, just as you have always obeyed — not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence — work out your salvation with fear and trembling.
50_2_13: For it is God who is at work in you — both to will and to work for His good pleasure.
50_2_14: Do all things without grumbling and disputing,
50_2_15: so that you may be blameless and innocent — children of God without blemish, in the midst of a crooked and perverse generation, among whom you shine as lights in the world,
50_2_16: holding fast the word of life — so that I may have reason to boast on the day of Christ that I did not run in vain, nor labor in vain.
50_2_17: But even if I am being poured out as a drink offering on the sacrifice and service of your faith, I rejoice — and I rejoice with you all.
50_2_18: And in the same way, you also should rejoice — and rejoice with me.
50_2_19: But I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you shortly — so that I also may be encouraged when I learn of your circumstances.
50_2_20: For I have no one else of kindred spirit, who will genuinely care about your welfare.
50_2_21: For all of them seek their own interests — not those of Christ Jesus.
50_2_22: But you know of his proven worth — that as a child with a father, he served with me in the gospel.
50_2_23: Therefore I hope to send him at once, as soon as I see how things go with me.
50_2_24: And I trust in the Lord that I myself also will come shortly.
50_2_25: But I thought it necessary to send to you Epaphroditus — my brother and fellow worker and fellow soldier — your messenger and minister to my need.
50_2_26: For he was longing for all of you, and was distressed because you had heard that he was sick.
50_2_27: Indeed, he was sick to the point of death. But God had mercy on him — and not on him only, but also on me, lest I should have sorrow upon sorrow.
50_2_28: Therefore I have sent him all the more eagerly — that when you see him again, you may rejoice, and I may be less anxious.
50_2_29: Welcome him in the Lord with all joy, and hold men like him in honor —
50_2_30: because he came close to death for the work of Christ, risking his life to fill up what was lacking in your service to me.
50_3_1: Finally, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord. To write the same things again is no trouble to me — and is a safeguard for you.
50_3_2: Beware of the dogs. Beware of the evil workers. Beware of the false circumcision.
50_3_3: For we are the true circumcision — who worship in the Spirit of God, and glory in Christ Jesus, and put no confidence in the flesh —
50_3_4: though I myself might have confidence even in the flesh. If anyone else thinks he has reason to put confidence in the flesh, I have more:
50_3_5: circumcised the eighth day, of the people of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews; as to the law, a Pharisee;
50_3_6: as to zeal, persecuting the church; as to the righteousness which is in the law, found blameless.
50_3_7: But whatever things were gain to me, these I have counted as loss for the sake of Christ.
50_3_8: Indeed I count all things as loss for the surpassing worth of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord — for whose sake I have suffered the loss of all things, and count them but rubbish, that I may gain Christ —
50_3_9: and be found in Him, not having a righteousness of my own which is from the law, but that which is through faith in Christ — the righteousness which is from God by faith;
50_3_10: that I may know Him, and the power of His resurrection, and the fellowship of His sufferings — being conformed to His death,
50_3_11: if by any means I may attain to the resurrection from the dead.
