47_5_4: For indeed, while we are in this tent, we groan, being burdened — because we do not want to be unclothed, but to be clothed, so that what is mortal will be swallowed up by life.
47_5_5: Now He who prepared us for this very purpose is God — who gave to us the Spirit as a pledge.
47_5_6: Therefore, being always of good courage — and knowing that while we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord —
47_5_7: for we walk by faith, not by sight.
47_5_8: We are of good courage, I say, and prefer rather to be absent from the body and to be at home with the Lord.
47_5_9: Therefore we also have as our ambition, whether at home or absent, to be pleasing to Him.
47_5_10: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ — so that each one may be recompensed for his deeds in the body, according to what he has done, whether good or bad.
47_5_11: Therefore, knowing the fear of the Lord, we persuade men. But we are made manifest to God — and I hope that we are made manifest also in your consciences.
47_5_12: We are not again commending ourselves to you — but are giving you an occasion to be proud of us, so that you will have an answer for those who take pride in appearance and not in heart.
47_5_13: For if we are beside ourselves, it is for God; if we are of sound mind, it is for you.
47_5_14: For the love of Christ controls us — having concluded this: that one died for all, therefore all died.
47_5_15: And He died for all, so that they who live might no longer live for themselves — but for Him who died and rose again on their behalf.
47_5_16: Therefore from now on, we recognize no one according to the flesh. Even though we have known Christ according to the flesh, yet now we know Him in this way no longer.
47_5_17: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away — behold, new things have come!
47_5_18: Now all these things are from God — who reconciled us to Himself through Christ, and gave us the ministry of reconciliation.
47_5_19: Namely, that God was in Christ reconciling the world to Himself — not counting their trespasses against them — and He has committed to us the word of reconciliation.
47_5_20: Therefore, we are ambassadors for Christ — as though God were making an appeal through us. We beg you on behalf of Christ: be reconciled to God.
47_5_21: He made Him who knew no sin to be sin on our behalf — so that we might become the righteousness of God in Him.
47_6_1: And working together with Him, we also urge you not to receive the grace of God in vain —
47_6_2: for He says, "At the acceptable time I listened to you, and on the day of salvation I helped you." Behold — now is the acceptable time! Behold — now is the day of salvation!
47_6_3: Giving no cause for offense in anything — so that the ministry will not be discredited —
47_6_4: but in everything, commending ourselves as servants of God: in much endurance, in afflictions, in hardships, in distresses,
47_6_5: in beatings, in imprisonments, in tumults, in labors, in sleeplessness, in hunger,
47_6_6: in purity, in knowledge, in patience, in kindness, in the Holy Spirit, in genuine love;
47_6_7: in the word of truth, in the power of God; by the weapons of righteousness for the right hand and the left,
47_6_8: by glory and dishonor, by evil report and good report; regarded as deceivers — and yet true;
47_6_9: as unknown — yet well known; as dying — yet behold, we live; as punished — yet not put to death;
47_6_10: as sorrowful — yet always rejoicing; as poor — yet making many rich; as having nothing — yet possessing all things.
47_6_11: Our mouth has spoken freely to you, O Corinthians. Our heart is opened wide.
47_6_12: You are not restrained by us, but you are restrained in your own affections.
47_6_13: Now in a like exchange — I speak as to children — open wide to us also.
47_6_14: Do not be bound together with unbelievers — for what partnership have righteousness and lawlessness, or what fellowship has light with darkness?
47_6_15: Or what harmony has Christ with Belial, or what has a believer in common with an unbeliever?
47_6_16: Or what agreement has the temple of God with idols? For we are the temple of the living God — just as God said: "I will dwell among them, and walk among them; and I will be their God, and they shall be My people."
47_6_17: "Therefore, come out from their midst, and be separate," says the Lord, "and do not touch what is unclean — and I will welcome you.
47_6_18: And I will be a Father to you, and you shall be sons and daughters to Me," says the Lord Almighty.
47_7_1: Therefore, having these promises, beloved — let us cleanse ourselves from all defilement of flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.
47_7_2: Make room for us in your hearts. We wronged no one. We corrupted no one. We took advantage of no one.
47_7_3: I do not speak to condemn you — for I have said before that you are in our hearts, to die together and to live together.
47_7_4: Great is my confidence in you. Great is my boasting on your behalf. I am filled with comfort. I am overflowing with joy in all our affliction.
47_7_5: For even when we came into Macedonia, our flesh had no rest — but we were afflicted on every side: conflicts without, fears within.
47_7_6: But God, who comforts the depressed, comforted us by the coming of Titus.
47_7_7: And not only by his coming, but also by the comfort with which he was comforted in you — as he reported to us your longing, your mourning, your zeal for me, so that I rejoiced even more.
47_7_8: For though I caused you sorrow by my letter, I do not regret it. Though I did regret it — for I see that that letter caused you sorrow, though only for a while —
47_7_9: I now rejoice — not that you were made sorrowful, but that you were made sorrowful to the point of repentance. For you were made sorrowful according to the will of God — so that you might not suffer loss in anything through us.
47_7_10: For the sorrow that is according to the will of God produces a repentance leading to salvation, without regret. But the sorrow of the world produces death.
47_7_11: For behold, what earnestness this very thing — this godly sorrow — has produced in you. What vindication of yourselves! What indignation! What fear! What longing! What zeal! What avenging of wrong! In everything, you demonstrated yourselves to be innocent in the matter.
47_7_12: So although I wrote to you, it was not for the sake of the offender, nor for the sake of the one offended — but that your earnestness on our behalf might be made known to you in the sight of God.
47_7_13: For this reason we have been comforted. And besides our comfort, we rejoiced even much more for the joy of Titus, because his spirit has been refreshed by you all.
47_7_14: For if in anything I have boasted to him about you, I was not put to shame — but as we spoke all things to you in truth, so also our boasting before Titus proved to be the truth.
47_7_15: And his affection abounds all the more toward you, as he remembers the obedience of you all — how you received him with fear and trembling.
47_7_16: I rejoice that in everything I have confidence in you.
47_8_1: Now, brothers, we wish to make known to you the grace of God which has been given in the churches of Macedonia —
47_8_2: that in a great ordeal of affliction, their abundance of joy and their deep poverty overflowed in the wealth of their liberality.
47_8_3: For I testify that according to their ability, and beyond their ability, they gave of their own accord —
47_8_4: begging us with much urging for the favor of participation in the support of the saints.
47_8_5: And not as we had expected — but they first gave themselves to the Lord, and to us by the will of God.
47_8_6: So we urged Titus, that as he had previously begun, so he would also complete in you this gracious work as well.
47_8_7: But just as you abound in everything — in faith, in speech, in knowledge, in all earnestness, and in the love we inspired in you — see that you abound in this gracious work also.
47_8_8: I am not speaking this as a command — but as proving, through the earnestness of others, the sincerity of your love also.
47_8_9: For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ — that though He was rich, yet for your sake He became poor, so that you, through His poverty, might become rich.
47_8_10: I give my opinion in this matter — for this is to your advantage, who were the first to begin a year ago, not only to do this, but also to desire to do it.
47_8_11: But now finish doing it also — so that just as there was the readiness to desire it, so there may also be the completion of it according to your ability.
47_8_12: For if the readiness is present, it is acceptable according to what a person has — not according to what he does not have.
47_8_13: For this is not for the ease of others and for your affliction — but by way of equality.
47_8_14: At this present time, your abundance being a supply for their need, so that their abundance may also become a supply for your need — that there may be equality.
47_8_15: As it is written, "He who gathered much did not have too much, and he who gathered little did not have too little."
47_8_16: But thanks be to God — who puts the same earnestness on your behalf in the heart of Titus.
47_8_17: For he not only accepted our appeal — but being himself very earnest, he has gone to you of his own accord.
47_8_18: And we have sent along with him the brother whose fame in the things of the gospel has spread through all the churches.
47_8_19: Not only this — but he was also appointed by the churches to travel with us in this gracious work, which is being administered by us — to the glory of the Lord Himself, and to show our readiness.
47_8_20: Taking precaution so that no one will discredit us in our administration of this generous gift.
47_8_21: For we have regard for what is honorable — not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men.
47_8_22: And we have sent with them our brother — whom we have often tested and found diligent in many things, but now even more diligent because of his great confidence in you.
47_8_23: As for Titus, he is my partner and fellow worker among you — as for our brothers, they are messengers of the churches, a glory to Christ.
47_8_24: Therefore, openly before the churches, show them the proof of your love and of our reason for boasting about you.
47_9_1: For it is superfluous for me to write to you about this ministry to the saints —
47_9_2: for I know your readiness — of which I boast about you to the Macedonians, namely, that Achaia has been prepared since last year. And your zeal has stirred up most of them.
47_9_3: But I have sent the brothers — so that our boasting about you may not be made empty in this case, that, as I was saying, you may be prepared.
47_9_4: Otherwise, if any Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we — not to speak of you — would be put to shame by this confidence.
47_9_5: So I thought it necessary to urge the brothers that they would go on ahead to you, and arrange beforehand your previously promised bountiful gift — so that the same would be ready as a bountiful gift, and not affected by covetousness.
47_9_6: Now this I say: he who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly — and he who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully.
47_9_7: Each one must do just as he has purposed in his heart — not grudgingly or under compulsion. For God loves a cheerful giver.
47_9_8: And God is able to make all grace abound to you — so that always having all sufficiency in everything, you may have an abundance for every good deed.
47_9_9: As it is written, "He scattered abroad, He gave to the poor; His righteousness endures forever."
47_9_10: Now He who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food, will supply and multiply your seed for sowing — and increase the harvest of your righteousness.
47_9_11: You will be enriched in everything for all liberality — which through us is producing thanksgiving to God.
47_9_12: For the ministry of this service is not only fully supplying the needs of the saints — but is also overflowing through many thanksgivings to God.
47_9_13: Because of the proof given by this ministry, they will glorify God for your obedience to your confession of the gospel of Christ — and for the liberality of your contribution to them and to all,
47_9_14: while they also, by prayer on your behalf, yearn for you because of the surpassing grace of God in you.
47_9_15: Thanks be to God for His indescribable gift!
47_10_1: Now I, Paul, myself urge you by the meekness and gentleness of Christ — I who am meek when face to face with you, but bold toward you when absent!
47_10_2: I ask that when I am present I need not be bold with the confidence with which I propose to be courageous against some — who regard us as if we walked according to the flesh.
47_10_3: For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war according to the flesh.
47_10_4: For the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh — but divinely powerful for the destruction of strongholds.
47_10_5: We are destroying speculations and every lofty thing raised up against the knowledge of God — and we are taking every thought captive to the obedience of Christ.
47_10_6: And we are ready to punish all disobedience, whenever your obedience is complete.
47_10_7: You are looking at things as they are outwardly. If anyone is confident in himself that he is Christ's, let him consider this again within himself: that just as he is Christ's, so also are we.
47_10_8: For even if I boast somewhat further about our authority — which the Lord gave for building you up and not for tearing you down — I will not be put to shame.
47_10_9: For I do not wish to seem as if I would terrify you by my letters.
47_10_10: For they say, "His letters are weighty and strong, but his personal presence is unimpressive, and his speech contemptible."
47_10_11: Let such a person consider this: that what we are in word by letters when absent, such persons we are also in deed when present.
47_10_12: For we are not bold to class or compare ourselves with some of those who commend themselves. But when they measure themselves by themselves, and compare themselves with themselves, they are without understanding.
47_10_13: But we will not boast beyond our measure — but within the measure of the sphere which God apportioned to us as a measure, to reach even as far as you.
47_10_14: For we are not overextending ourselves — as if we did not reach to you. For we were the first to come even as far as you, in the gospel of Christ.
47_10_15: Not boasting beyond our measure — that is, in other men's labors. But with the hope that as your faith grows, we will be, within our sphere, enlarged even more by you,
47_10_16: so as to preach the gospel even to the regions beyond you — and not to boast in what has been accomplished in the sphere of another.
47_10_17: But "he who boasts is to boast in the Lord."
47_10_18: For it is not the one who commends himself who is approved — but the one whom the Lord commends.
47_11_1: I wish that you would bear with me in a little foolishness. But indeed, you are bearing with me.
47_11_2: For I am jealous for you with a godly jealousy — for I betrothed you to one husband, that I might present you as a pure virgin to Christ.
47_11_3: But I am afraid that, as the serpent deceived Eve by his craftiness, your minds will be led astray from the simplicity and purity of devotion to Christ.
47_11_4: For if one comes and preaches another Jesus whom we have not preached, or you receive a different spirit which you have not received, or a different gospel which you have not accepted — you bear this beautifully.
47_11_5: For I consider myself not in the least inferior to the most eminent apostles.
47_11_6: But even if I am unskilled in speech, yet I am not in knowledge. In every way we have made this evident to you in all things.
47_11_7: Or did I commit a sin in humbling myself, so that you might be exalted, because I preached the gospel of God to you without charge?
47_11_8: I robbed other churches by taking wages from them to serve you.
47_11_9: And when I was present with you and was in need, I was not a burden to anyone — for when the brothers came from Macedonia, they fully supplied my need. And in everything I kept myself from being a burden to you, and will continue to do so.
47_11_10: As the truth of Christ is in me — this boasting of mine will not be stopped in the regions of Achaia.
47_11_11: Why? Because I do not love you? God knows I do!
47_11_12: But what I am doing, I will continue to do — so that I may cut off opportunity from those who desire an opportunity to be regarded just as we are in the matter about which they are boasting.
47_11_13: For such men are false apostles, deceitful workers, disguising themselves as apostles of Christ.
47_11_14: And no wonder — for even Satan disguises himself as an angel of light.
47_11_15: Therefore it is not surprising if his servants also disguise themselves as servants of righteousness — whose end will be according to their deeds.
47_11_16: Again I say, let no one think me foolish. But if you do, receive me even as foolish — so that I also may boast a little.
47_11_17: What I am saying, I am not saying as the Lord would, but as in foolishness — in this confidence of boasting.
47_11_18: Since many boast according to the flesh, I will boast also.
47_11_19: For you, being so wise, tolerate the foolish gladly.
47_11_20: For you tolerate it if anyone enslaves you, anyone devours you, anyone takes advantage of you, anyone exalts himself, anyone strikes you in the face.
47_11_21: To my shame I must say that we have been weak by comparison. But in whatever respect anyone else is bold — I speak in foolishness — I am just as bold myself.
47_11_22: Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they descendants of Abraham? So am I.
47_11_23: Are they servants of Christ? — I speak as if insane — I more so. In far more labors, in far more imprisonments, beaten times without number, often in danger of death.
47_11_24: Five times I received from the Jews thirty-nine lashes.
47_11_25: Three times I was beaten with rods. Once I was stoned. Three times I was shipwrecked. A night and a day I have spent in the deep.
47_11_26: I have been on frequent journeys — in dangers from rivers, dangers from robbers, dangers from my countrymen, dangers from the Gentiles, dangers in the city, dangers in the wilderness, dangers on the sea, dangers among false brothers.
47_11_27: I have been in labor and hardship, through many sleepless nights, in hunger and thirst, often without food, in cold and exposure.
47_11_28: Apart from such external things — there is the daily pressure on me of concern for all the churches.
47_11_29: Who is weak without my being weak? Who is led into sin without my intense concern?
47_11_30: If I have to boast, I will boast of what pertains to my weakness.
47_11_31: The God and Father of the Lord Jesus — He who is blessed forever — knows that I am not lying.
47_11_32: In Damascus, the ethnarch under Aretas the king was guarding the city of the Damascenes in order to seize me.
47_11_33: And I was let down through a window in a basket through the wall — and so escaped his hands.
47_12_1: Boasting is necessary, though it is not profitable. But I will go on to visions and revelations of the Lord.
47_12_2: I know a man in Christ — who fourteen years ago was caught up to the third heaven (whether in the body, I do not know; or out of the body, I do not know — God knows).
47_12_3: And I know how such a man — whether in the body, or apart from the body, I do not know; God knows —
47_12_4: was caught up into Paradise, and heard inexpressible words, which a man is not permitted to speak.
47_12_5: On behalf of such a man I will boast — but on my own behalf I will not boast, except in regard to my weaknesses.
47_12_6: For if I do wish to boast, I will not be foolish — for I will be speaking the truth. But I refrain from this, so that no one will credit me with more than he sees in me, or hears from me.
47_12_7: Because of the surpassing greatness of the revelations — for this reason, to keep me from exalting myself, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, a messenger of Satan to torment me — to keep me from exalting myself!
47_12_8: Concerning this I implored the Lord three times, that it might leave me.
47_12_9: And He has said to me, "My grace is sufficient for you — for power is perfected in weakness." Most gladly therefore, I will rather boast about my weaknesses — so that the power of Christ may dwell in me.
47_12_10: Therefore, I am well content with weaknesses, with insults, with distresses, with persecutions, with difficulties — for Christ's sake. For when I am weak, then I am strong.
47_12_11: I have become foolish — you yourselves compelled me. Actually I should have been commended by you, for in no respect was I inferior to the most eminent apostles, even though I am a nobody.
47_12_12: The signs of a true apostle were performed among you with all perseverance — by signs and wonders and miracles.
47_12_13: For in what respect were you treated as inferior to the rest of the churches, except that I myself did not become a burden to you? Forgive me this wrong!
47_12_14: Behold — for the third time, I am ready to come to you, and I will not be a burden to you. For I do not seek what is yours, but you. For children are not responsible to save up for their parents — but parents for their children.
47_12_15: And I will most gladly spend, and be expended, for your souls. If I love you more, am I to be loved less?
47_12_16: But be that as it may — I did not burden you myself. Nevertheless, crafty fellow that I am, I took you in by deceit.
47_12_17: Certainly I have not taken advantage of you through any of those whom I have sent to you, have I?
47_12_18: I urged Titus to go, and I sent the brother with him. Titus did not take any advantage of you, did he? Did we not conduct ourselves in the same spirit, and walk in the same steps?
47_12_19: All this time, you have been thinking that we are defending ourselves to you. Actually it is in the sight of God that we have been speaking in Christ — and all for your upbuilding, beloved.
47_12_20: For I am afraid that perhaps when I come, I may find you to be not what I wish, and may be found by you to be not what you wish — that perhaps there will be strife, jealousy, angry tempers, disputes, slanders, gossip, arrogance, disturbances.
47_12_21: I am afraid that when I come again, my God may humiliate me before you — and I may mourn over many of those who have sinned in the past, and not repented of the impurity, immorality, and sensuality which they have practiced.
47_13_1: This is the third time I am coming to you. "Every fact is to be confirmed by the testimony of two or three witnesses."
47_13_2: I have previously said, when present the second time, and though now absent I say in advance to those who have sinned in the past, and to all the rest as well — that if I come again, I will not spare anyone.
47_13_3: Since you are seeking for proof of the Christ who speaks in me — and who is not weak toward you, but mighty in you.
47_13_4: For indeed, He was crucified because of weakness — yet He lives because of the power of God. For we also are weak in Him, yet we will live with Him because of the power of God directed toward you.
47_13_5: Test yourselves, to see if you are in the faith. Examine yourselves! Or do you not recognize about yourselves that Jesus Christ is in you — unless indeed you fail the test?
47_13_6: But I trust that you will realize that we ourselves do not fail the test.
47_13_7: Now we pray to God that you do no wrong — not so that we ourselves may appear approved, but that you may do what is right, even though we may appear unapproved.
47_13_8: For we can do nothing against the truth, but only for the truth.
47_13_9: For we rejoice when we ourselves are weak, but you are strong. This we also pray for: that you be made complete.
47_13_10: For this reason I am writing these things while absent — so that when present I will not need to use severity, in accordance with the authority which the Lord gave me, for building up and not for tearing down.
47_13_11: Finally, brothers, rejoice. Be made complete. Be comforted. Be like-minded. Live in peace — and the God of love and peace will be with you.
47_13_12: Greet one another with a holy kiss.
47_13_14: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all.
52_1_1: Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy — to the church of the Thessalonians, in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ: Grace to you, and peace.
52_1_2: We give thanks to God always for all of you, mentioning you in our prayers,
52_1_3: constantly remembering before our God and Father your work of faith, your labor of love, and your steadfastness of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ.
52_1_4: Knowing, brothers — beloved by God — your election;
52_1_5: for our gospel did not come to you in word only, but also in power, and in the Holy Spirit, and with full conviction — just as you know what kind of men we became among you for your sake.
52_1_6: And you became imitators of us and of the Lord, having received the word in much affliction, with the joy of the Holy Spirit —
52_1_7: so that you became an example to all the believers in Macedonia and in Achaia.
52_1_8: For from you the word of the Lord has sounded forth — not only in Macedonia and Achaia, but in every place your faith toward God has gone out, so that we have no need to say anything.
52_1_9: For they themselves report concerning us what kind of welcome we had among you — and how you turned to God from idols, to serve a living and true God,
52_1_10: and to wait for His Son from heaven — whom He raised from the dead — Jesus, who delivers us from the wrath to come.
52_2_1: For you yourselves know, brothers, that our coming to you was not in vain.
52_2_2: But after we had previously suffered and been treated shamefully at Philippi — as you know — we had courage in our God to speak to you the gospel of God, in the midst of much opposition.
52_2_3: For our exhortation does not come from error, or from impurity, or by way of deceit;
52_2_4: but just as we have been approved by God to be entrusted with the gospel, so we speak — not as pleasing men, but God who tests our hearts.
52_2_5: For we never came with flattering speech, as you know — nor with a pretext for greed; God is witness.
52_2_6: Nor did we seek glory from people — neither from you, nor from others — when we could have made demands as apostles of Christ.
52_2_7: But we were gentle in your midst, like a nursing mother caring for her own children.
52_2_8: So, having a deep affection for you, we were well-pleased to share with you not only the gospel of God, but also our own lives — because you had become beloved to us.
52_2_9: For you remember, brothers, our toil and hardship — laboring night and day so as not to be a burden to any of you, while we proclaimed to you the gospel of God.
52_2_10: You are witnesses, and so is God — how holy, righteous, and blameless was our conduct toward you who believe.
52_2_11: Just as you know how, like a father with his own children, we were exhorting each one of you, and encouraging and imploring you,
52_2_12: that you should walk in a manner worthy of God, who calls you into His own kingdom and glory.
52_2_13: And for this reason we also constantly thank God — that when you received the word of God which you heard from us, you accepted it not as the word of men, but as it truly is, the word of God — which also is at work in you who believe.
52_2_14: For you, brothers, became imitators of the churches of God in Christ Jesus that are in Judea — for you also suffered the same things from your own countrymen as they did from the Jews,
52_2_15: who killed both the Lord Jesus and their own prophets, and drove us out — and they do not please God, and are hostile to all people,
52_2_16: hindering us from speaking to the Gentiles so that they may be saved. Thus they always fill up the measure of their sins. But the wrath has come upon them at last.
52_2_17: But we, brothers — having been torn away from you for a short time, in person but not in heart — were all the more eager and longing to see your face.
52_2_18: For we wanted to come to you — I, Paul, more than once — but Satan hindered us.
52_2_19: For who is our hope, our joy, or our crown of boasting? Is it not even you, in the presence of our Lord Jesus at His coming?
52_2_20: For you are our glory and joy.
52_3_1: Therefore, when we could endure it no longer, we thought it best to be left behind in Athens alone,
52_3_2: and we sent Timothy — our brother and God's fellow worker in the gospel of Christ — to strengthen you and encourage you concerning your faith,
52_3_3: so that no one would be unsettled by these afflictions. For you yourselves know that we are appointed to this.
52_3_4: For indeed, when we were with you, we kept telling you in advance that we were going to suffer affliction — just as it has come to pass, as you know.
52_3_5: For this reason, when I could endure it no longer, I sent to find out about your faith — for fear that the tempter might have tempted you, and our labor would be in vain.
52_3_6: But now Timothy has come to us from you and brought us good news of your faith and love — and that you always have good remembrance of us, longing to see us, just as we long to see you.
52_3_7: For this reason, brothers — in all our affliction and distress — we were comforted concerning you through your faith.
52_3_8: For now we live, if you stand firm in the Lord.
52_3_9: For what thanksgiving can we render to God for you, for all the joy with which we rejoice on your account before our God,
52_3_10: as we keep praying earnestly night and day that we may see your face and supply what is lacking in your faith?
52_3_11: Now may our God and Father Himself, and our Lord Jesus, direct our way to you.
52_3_12: And may the Lord cause you to increase and abound in love for one another and for all people, just as we also do for you,
52_3_13: so that He may strengthen your hearts blameless in holiness before our God and Father at the coming of our Lord Jesus with all His saints.
52_4_1: Finally, then, brothers, we ask and exhort you in the Lord Jesus — that as you have received from us instruction concerning how you ought to walk and please God (just as you are doing) — that you excel still more.
52_4_2: For you know what commands we gave you through the Lord Jesus.
52_4_3: For this is the will of God: your sanctification — that you abstain from sexual immorality;
52_4_4: that each of you know how to possess his own vessel in sanctification and honor;
52_4_5: not in the passion of lust, like the Gentiles who do not know God;
52_4_6: and that no one transgress and defraud his brother in this matter — because the Lord is the avenger in all these things, just as we also told you before and warned solemnly.
52_4_7: For God did not call us for impurity, but for sanctification.
52_4_8: Therefore he who rejects this is not rejecting man, but God — who gives His Holy Spirit to you.
52_4_9: But concerning brotherly love, you have no need for anyone to write to you — for you yourselves are taught by God to love one another.
52_4_10: For indeed you do practice it toward all the brothers throughout Macedonia. But we urge you, brothers, to excel still more,
52_4_11: and to make it your ambition to live a quiet life, to mind your own business, and to work with your own hands — just as we commanded you,
52_4_12: so that you may walk properly toward outsiders, and have need of nothing.
52_4_13: But we do not want you to be uninformed, brothers, about those who have fallen asleep — so that you may not grieve like the rest, who have no hope.
52_4_14: For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so, through Jesus, God will bring with Him those who have fallen asleep.
52_4_15: For this we say to you by the word of the Lord: that we who are alive — who remain until the coming of the Lord — will by no means precede those who have fallen asleep.
52_4_16: For the Lord Himself will descend from heaven with a shout — with the voice of an archangel and with the trumpet of God — and the dead in Christ will rise first.
52_4_17: Then we who are alive and remain will be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air. And so we shall always be with the Lord.
52_4_18: Therefore, comfort one another with these words.
52_5_1: Now concerning the times and the seasons, brothers, you have no need that anything be written to you.
52_5_2: For you yourselves know full well that the day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night.
52_5_3: When they say, "Peace and safety!" — then sudden destruction will come upon them, like labor pains upon a pregnant woman, and they will not escape.
52_5_4: But you, brothers, are not in darkness — that the day should overtake you like a thief.
52_5_5: You are all sons of light and sons of the day. We are not of the night, nor of darkness.
52_5_6: So then, let us not sleep, as do the others — but let us watch and be sober.
52_5_7: For those who sleep, sleep at night; and those who get drunk, are drunk at night.
52_5_8: But since we are of the day, let us be sober — putting on the breastplate of faith and love, and as a helmet, the hope of salvation.
52_5_9: For God did not appoint us to wrath — but to obtain salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ,
52_5_10: who died for us, so that whether we are awake or asleep, we may live together with Him.
52_5_11: Therefore encourage one another and build one another up — just as you also are doing.
52_5_12: Now we ask you, brothers, to acknowledge those who labor among you, and are over you in the Lord, and admonish you;
52_5_13: and esteem them very highly in love, because of their work. Be at peace among yourselves.
52_5_14: And we urge you, brothers — admonish those who are unruly, encourage the fainthearted, help the weak, be patient with all.
52_5_15: See that no one repays evil for evil — but always seek what is good for one another and for all people.
52_5_18: In everything give thanks — for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you.
52_5_21: Test all things — hold fast to what is good.
52_5_22: Abstain from every form of evil.
52_5_23: Now may the God of peace Himself sanctify you completely. And may your whole spirit, soul, and body be preserved blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
52_5_24: Faithful is He who calls you — He will also do it.
52_5_26: Greet all the brothers with a holy kiss.
52_5_27: I solemnly charge you by the Lord that this letter be read to all the brothers.
52_5_28: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.
53_1_1: Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy — to the church of the Thessalonians, in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ:
53_1_2: Grace to you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
53_1_3: We are bound to thank God always for you, brothers, as is fitting — because your faith is growing exceedingly, and the love of every one of you for one another is abounding.
53_1_4: Therefore we ourselves boast about you among the churches of God — for your steadfastness and faith in all your persecutions and the afflictions you are enduring.
53_1_5: This is plain evidence of God's righteous judgment — that you may be counted worthy of the kingdom of God, for which you are also suffering.
53_1_6: For after all, it is just with God to repay with affliction those who afflict you,
53_1_7: and to give relief to you who are afflicted, and to us as well — when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with His mighty angels,
53_1_8: in flaming fire, taking vengeance on those who do not know God and who do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus.
53_1_9: These will pay the penalty of eternal destruction, away from the presence of the Lord and from the glory of His might —
53_1_10: when He comes on that Day to be glorified in His saints and to be marveled at by all who have believed (because our testimony among you was believed).
53_1_11: To this end we always pray for you — that our God may count you worthy of His calling, and may fulfill every good resolve and every work of faith with power,
53_1_12: so that the name of our Lord Jesus may be glorified in you, and you in Him, according to the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.
53_2_1: Now we ask you, brothers, concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our being gathered together to Him —
53_2_2: that you not be quickly shaken in mind, or alarmed — either by a spirit, or by a word, or by a letter seeming to be from us — to the effect that the day of the Lord has already come.
53_2_3: Let no one deceive you in any way. For that day will not come unless the falling away comes first, and the man of lawlessness is revealed — the son of destruction —
53_2_4: the one who opposes and exalts himself against every so-called god or object of worship, so that he takes his seat in the temple of God, proclaiming himself to be God.
53_2_5: Do you not remember that, while I was still with you, I was telling you these things?
53_2_6: And now you know what is restraining him — so that he may be revealed in his own time.
53_2_7: For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work; only the One who now restrains will do so until He is taken out of the way.
53_2_8: And then the lawless one will be revealed — whom the Lord Jesus will slay with the breath of His mouth, and bring to nothing by the appearance of His coming.
53_2_9: The coming of the lawless one will be in accord with the working of Satan — with all power, and with signs and lying wonders,
53_2_10: and with all unrighteous deception for those who are perishing — because they refused to love the truth and so be saved.
53_2_11: For this reason, God sends them a working of error — so that they will believe the lie,
53_2_12: in order that all may be condemned who have not believed the truth, but have taken pleasure in unrighteousness.
53_2_13: But we are bound always to thank God for you, brothers beloved by the Lord — because God chose you from the beginning for salvation, through sanctification by the Spirit and faith in the truth,
53_2_14: to which He called you by our gospel — for the obtaining of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
53_2_15: So then, brothers, stand firm — and hold to the traditions you were taught, whether by spoken word or by letter from us.
53_2_16: Now may our Lord Jesus Christ Himself, and God our Father — who has loved us and given us eternal comfort and good hope through grace —
53_2_17: comfort your hearts and establish you in every good word and work.
53_3_1: Finally, brothers, pray for us — that the word of the Lord may run swiftly and be glorified, just as it is with you,
53_3_2: and that we may be delivered from unreasonable and wicked men — for not all have the faith.
53_3_3: But the Lord is faithful. He will establish you and guard you from the evil one.
53_3_4: And we have confidence in the Lord concerning you — that you are doing, and will do, the things we command.
53_3_5: May the Lord direct your hearts into the love of God, and into the steadfastness of Christ.
53_3_6: Now we command you, brothers — in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ — that you withdraw from every brother who walks in disorder, and not according to the tradition that you received from us.
53_3_7: For you yourselves know how you ought to imitate us — because we did not behave disorderly among you,
53_3_8: nor did we eat anyone's bread without paying for it. Rather, with toil and labor we worked night and day, so as not to be a burden to any of you —
53_3_9: not because we have no right, but in order to give ourselves to you as a model to imitate.
53_3_10: For even when we were with you, we used to give you this command: "If anyone is not willing to work, neither shall he eat."
53_3_11: For we hear that some among you are walking in disorder — not working at all, but being busybodies.
53_3_12: Now such persons we command and exhort, in the Lord Jesus Christ, to work quietly and to eat their own bread.
53_3_13: But as for you, brothers — do not grow weary in doing what is right.
53_3_14: If anyone does not obey our word in this letter, take note of him and have nothing to do with him — so that he may be ashamed.
53_3_15: Yet do not regard him as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother.
53_3_16: Now may the Lord of peace Himself give you peace at all times, in every way. The Lord be with you all.
53_3_17: I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand. This is the sign in every letter — this is how I write.
53_3_18: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
54_1_1: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the command of God our Savior, and of Christ Jesus our hope —
54_1_2: to Timothy, my true child in the faith: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
54_1_3: As I urged you when I was leaving for Macedonia — remain in Ephesus, so that you may instruct certain men not to teach a different doctrine,
54_1_4: nor to give attention to myths and endless genealogies, which give rise to mere speculations rather than the stewardship from God which is by faith.
54_1_5: But the goal of our instruction is love — out of a pure heart, and a good conscience, and a sincere faith.
54_1_6: Some have wandered away from these things, and have turned aside to fruitless discussion —
54_1_7: wanting to be teachers of the Law, even though they do not understand either what they are saying, or the matters about which they make confident assertions.
54_1_8: But we know that the Law is good, if anyone uses it lawfully —
54_1_9: knowing this: that the Law is not made for a righteous man, but for those who are lawless and rebellious, for the ungodly and sinners, for the unholy and profane, for those who kill their fathers or mothers, for murderers,
54_1_10: for the sexually immoral, for those who practice homosexuality, for kidnappers, for liars, for perjurers, and whatever else is contrary to sound teaching —
54_1_11: according to the gospel of the glory of the blessed God, with which I have been entrusted.
54_1_12: I thank Him who has strengthened me — Christ Jesus our Lord — because He considered me faithful, putting me into service,
54_1_13: even though I was formerly a blasphemer and a persecutor and a violent aggressor. Yet I was shown mercy, because I had acted ignorantly in unbelief.
54_1_14: And the grace of our Lord overflowed for me — with the faith and love which are in Christ Jesus.
54_1_15: This saying is faithful and worthy of full acceptance: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners — of whom I am foremost.
54_1_16: Yet for this reason I was shown mercy: so that in me, the foremost, Jesus Christ might display His perfect patience as an example to those who would believe in Him for eternal life.
54_1_17: Now to the King eternal — immortal, invisible, the only God — be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.
54_1_18: This charge I entrust to you, Timothy my child — in accordance with the prophecies previously made concerning you — that by them you may fight the good fight,
54_1_19: keeping faith and a good conscience. Some have rejected these and have suffered shipwreck in regard to their faith.
54_1_20: Among these are Hymenaeus and Alexander — whom I have handed over to Satan, so that they will be taught not to blaspheme.
54_2_1: First of all, then, I urge that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made on behalf of all people —
54_2_2: for kings and all who are in authority — so that we may lead a tranquil and quiet life in all godliness and dignity.
54_2_3: This is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Savior,
54_2_4: who desires all people to be saved, and to come to the full knowledge of the truth.
54_2_5: For there is one God — and one mediator also between God and men: the man Christ Jesus,
54_2_6: who gave Himself as a ransom for all — the testimony given at the proper time.
54_2_7: For this purpose I was appointed a herald and an apostle — I am telling the truth, I am not lying — a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth.
54_2_8: Therefore I want the men in every place to pray, lifting up holy hands — without anger and disputing.
54_2_9: Likewise, I want women to adorn themselves with proper clothing, modestly and discreetly — not with braided hair, and gold, or pearls, or costly garments,
54_2_10: but rather, by means of good works, as is fitting for women making a claim to godliness.
54_2_11: Let a woman quietly receive instruction with full submissiveness.
54_2_12: But I do not allow a woman to teach or to exercise authority over a man — but to remain quiet.
54_2_13: For it was Adam who was first formed, and then Eve.
54_2_14: And it was not Adam who was deceived, but the woman, being deceived, fell into transgression.
54_2_15: But women will be preserved through the bearing of children — if they continue in faith and love and sanctity, with self-restraint.
54_3_1: This saying is faithful: if any man aspires to the office of overseer, it is a fine work he desires to do.
54_3_2: An overseer, then, must be above reproach — the husband of one wife, sober-minded, prudent, respectable, hospitable, able to teach,
54_3_3: not addicted to wine, not violent — but gentle, not quarrelsome, not loving money;
54_3_4: managing his own household well — keeping his children under control with all dignity
54_3_5: (for if a man does not know how to manage his own household, how will he take care of the church of God?);
54_3_6: and not a new convert — so that he will not become conceited and fall into the condemnation incurred by the devil.
54_3_7: And he must have a good reputation with those outside the church — so that he will not fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.
54_3_8: Deacons likewise must be men of dignity — not double-tongued, or addicted to much wine, or fond of dishonest gain;
54_3_9: but holding the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience.
54_3_10: And these too should first be tested — then let them serve as deacons, if they are beyond reproach.
54_3_11: Women must likewise be dignified, not malicious gossips, but sober-minded — faithful in all things.
54_3_12: Deacons must be husbands of only one wife — managing their children and their own households well.
54_3_13: For those who have served well as deacons obtain for themselves a high standing — and great confidence in the faith that is in Christ Jesus.
54_3_14: I am writing these things to you — hoping to come to you before long.
54_3_15: But in case I am delayed, I write so that you will know how one ought to conduct himself in the household of God — which is the church of the living God, the pillar and support of the truth.
54_3_16: And by common confession, great is the mystery of godliness: He who was revealed in the flesh, was vindicated in the Spirit, was seen by angels, was proclaimed among the nations, was believed on in the world, was taken up in glory.
54_4_1: But the Spirit explicitly says that in later times some will fall away from the faith — paying attention to deceitful spirits and to doctrines of demons,
54_4_2: by means of the hypocrisy of liars seared in their own conscience as with a branding iron,
54_4_3: men who forbid marriage, and who advocate abstaining from foods which God has created to be gratefully shared in by those who believe and know the truth.
54_4_4: For everything created by God is good — and nothing is to be rejected, if it is received with gratitude;
54_4_5: for it is sanctified by means of the word of God and prayer.
54_4_6: In pointing out these things to the brothers, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus — constantly nourished on the words of the faith and of the sound doctrine which you have been following.
54_4_7: But have nothing to do with worldly fables fit only for old women. On the other hand, train yourself for the purpose of godliness.
54_4_8: For bodily training is of little profit — but godliness is profitable for all things, since it holds promise for the present life and also for the life to come.
54_4_9: This saying is faithful and worthy of full acceptance.
54_4_10: For it is for this we labor and strive — because we have set our hope on the living God, who is the Savior of all men, especially of believers.
54_4_12: Let no one look down on your youthfulness — but rather, in speech, conduct, love, faith, and purity, show yourself an example of those who believe.
54_4_13: Until I come, give your attention to the public reading, to exhortation, and to teaching.
54_4_14: Do not neglect the spiritual gift within you — which was given to you through prophecy with the laying on of hands by the council of elders.
54_4_15: Take pains with these things — be absorbed in them, so that your progress will be evident to all.
54_4_16: Pay close attention to yourself and to your teaching. Persevere in these things — for as you do this, you will save both yourself and those who hear you.
54_5_1: Do not sharply rebuke an older man — but rather appeal to him as a father; and to the younger men, as brothers;
54_5_2: the older women, as mothers; the younger women, as sisters — in all purity.
54_5_3: Honor widows who are widows indeed.
54_5_4: But if any widow has children or grandchildren, let them first learn to practice piety in regard to their own family — and to make some return to their parents. For this is acceptable in the sight of God.
54_5_5: Now she who is truly a widow — and who has been left alone — has fixed her hope on God, and continues in supplications and prayers night and day.
54_5_6: But she who lives in indulgent pleasure is dead, even while she lives.
54_5_7: Prescribe these things as well, so that they may be above reproach.
54_5_8: But if anyone does not provide for his own — and especially for those of his household — he has denied the faith, and is worse than an unbeliever.
54_5_9: Let a widow be enrolled who is not less than sixty years old — having been the wife of one man,
54_5_10: having a reputation for good works: if she has brought up children, if she has shown hospitality to strangers, if she has washed the saints' feet, if she has assisted those in distress, and if she has devoted herself to every good work.
54_5_11: But refuse to enroll younger widows — for when they feel sensual desires in disregard of Christ, they want to get married,
54_5_12: thus incurring condemnation, because they have set aside their previous pledge.
54_5_13: And at the same time they also learn to be idle — going from house to house. And not merely idle, but also gossips and busybodies, talking about things they ought not to mention.
54_5_14: Therefore, I want younger widows to get married, bear children, keep house, and give the enemy no occasion for reproach.
54_5_15: For some have already turned aside to follow Satan.
54_5_16: If any believing woman has dependent widows, she must assist them — and the church must not be burdened, so that it may assist those who are widows indeed.
54_5_17: The elders who rule well are to be considered worthy of double honor — especially those who work hard at preaching and teaching.
54_5_18: For the Scripture says, "You shall not muzzle the ox while it is threshing," and, "The laborer is worthy of his wages."
54_5_19: Do not receive an accusation against an elder, except on the basis of two or three witnesses.
54_5_20: Those who continue in sin, rebuke in the presence of all — so that the rest also may be fearful of sinning.
54_5_21: I solemnly charge you in the presence of God and of Christ Jesus and of His chosen angels — to maintain these principles without bias, doing nothing in a spirit of partiality.
54_5_22: Do not lay hands upon anyone too hastily — and do not share responsibility for the sins of others. Keep yourself pure.
54_5_23: No longer drink water exclusively, but use a little wine for the sake of your stomach and your frequent ailments.
54_5_24: The sins of some men are quite evident, going before them to judgment. For others, their sins follow after.
54_5_25: Likewise also, deeds that are good are quite evident — and those which are otherwise cannot be concealed.
54_6_1: All who are under the yoke as slaves are to regard their own masters as worthy of all honor — so that the name of God and our doctrine will not be spoken against.
54_6_2: Those who have believers as their masters must not be disrespectful to them because they are brothers — but they must serve them all the more, because those who partake of the benefit are believers and beloved. Teach and preach these principles.
54_6_3: If anyone advocates a different doctrine, and does not agree with sound words — those of our Lord Jesus Christ — and with the doctrine conforming to godliness,
54_6_4: he is conceited, and understands nothing. But he has a sick craving for controversial questions and disputes about words — out of which arise envy, strife, abusive language, evil suspicions,
54_6_5: and constant friction between men of depraved mind and deprived of the truth — who suppose that godliness is a means of gain.
54_6_6: But godliness, with contentment, is great gain.
54_6_7: For we have brought nothing into the world — and we cannot take anything out of it either.
54_6_8: And if we have food and covering, with these we shall be content.
54_6_9: But those who want to get rich fall into temptation and a snare, and many foolish and harmful desires — which plunge men into ruin and destruction.
54_6_10: For the love of money is a root of all sorts of evil — and some, by longing for it, have wandered away from the faith and pierced themselves with many griefs.
54_6_11: But you, O man of God — flee from these things, and pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, perseverance, and gentleness.
54_6_12: Fight the good fight of faith. Take hold of the eternal life to which you were called — and for which you made the good confession in the presence of many witnesses.
54_6_13: I charge you in the presence of God — who gives life to all things — and of Christ Jesus, who testified the good confession before Pontius Pilate,
54_6_14: that you keep the commandment without stain or reproach until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ —
54_6_15: which He will bring about at the proper time. He is the blessed and only Sovereign — the King of kings and Lord of lords —
54_6_16: who alone has immortality — dwelling in unapproachable light, whom no man has seen or can see. To Him be honor and eternal dominion. Amen.
54_6_17: Instruct those who are rich in this present world not to be conceited, or to fix their hope on the uncertainty of riches — but on God, who richly supplies us with all things to enjoy.
54_6_18: Instruct them to do good, to be rich in good works, to be generous and ready to share —
54_6_19: storing up for themselves the treasure of a good foundation for the future — so that they may take hold of that which is life indeed.
54_6_20: O Timothy, guard what has been entrusted to you — avoiding worldly and empty chatter, and the opposing arguments of what is falsely called knowledge.
54_6_21: Some have professed it, and have gone astray from the faith. Grace be with you.
55_1_1: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, according to the promise of life that is in Christ Jesus —
55_1_2: to Timothy, my beloved son: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
55_1_3: I thank God, whom I serve with a clear conscience as my forefathers did — as I constantly remember you in my prayers, night and day.
55_1_4: Recalling your tears, I long to see you, that I may be filled with joy.
55_1_5: I am reminded of the sincere faith within you — which first lived in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and now, I am persuaded, lives in you also.
55_1_6: For this reason I remind you to fan into flame the gift of God, which is in you through the laying on of my hands.
55_1_7: For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
55_1_8: Therefore do not be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me His prisoner — but share with me in suffering for the gospel, by the power of God,
55_1_9: who has saved us and called us with a holy calling — not according to our works, but according to His own purpose and the grace given to us in Christ Jesus before the ages of time began,
55_1_10: and now has been revealed through the appearing of our Savior Christ Jesus — who has abolished death and brought life and immortality to light through the gospel,
55_1_11: for which I was appointed a herald, an apostle, and a teacher.
55_1_12: For this reason I also suffer these things — but I am not ashamed, for I know whom I have believed, and I am persuaded that He is able to guard what I have entrusted to Him until that Day.
55_1_13: Hold fast the pattern of sound words that you have heard from me — in the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.
55_1_14: Guard the good deposit entrusted to you, by the Holy Spirit who lives in us.
55_1_15: You know this: that all who are in Asia have turned away from me — among them Phygelus and Hermogenes.
55_1_16: May the Lord grant mercy to the household of Onesiphorus — for he often refreshed me, and was not ashamed of my chains.
55_1_17: But when he was in Rome, he sought me out diligently and found me.
55_1_18: May the Lord grant him to find mercy from the Lord on that Day. And you know very well how many ways he served at Ephesus.
55_2_1: You therefore, my son, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus.
55_2_2: And the things you have heard from me through many witnesses — entrust these to faithful men, who will be able to teach others also.
55_2_3: Share in suffering, as a good soldier of Christ Jesus.
55_2_4: No one engaged in warfare entangles himself with the affairs of civilian life, so that he may please the one who enlisted him.
55_2_5: And if anyone competes in athletics, he is not crowned unless he competes according to the rules.
55_2_6: The hardworking farmer ought to be the first to share in the crops.
55_2_7: Consider what I say — for the Lord will give you understanding in everything.
55_2_8: Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, descended from David, according to my gospel —
55_2_9: for which I am suffering hardship to the point of being chained as a criminal. But the word of God is not chained.
55_2_10: Therefore I endure all things for the sake of the chosen ones — so that they too may obtain the salvation that is in Christ Jesus, with eternal glory.
55_2_11: This saying is faithful: For if we have died with Him, we shall also live with Him.
55_2_12: If we endure, we shall also reign with Him. If we deny Him, He also will deny us.
55_2_13: If we are faithless, He remains faithful — for He cannot deny Himself.
55_2_14: Remind them of these things — charging them in the presence of God not to wrangle about words. It is to no profit, only the ruin of those who hear.
55_2_15: Be diligent to present yourself approved to God — a worker who has no need to be ashamed, rightly handling the word of truth.
55_2_16: But avoid worldly and empty chatter, for it will lead to more ungodliness,
55_2_17: and their word will spread like gangrene. Among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus,
55_2_18: who have strayed from the truth — saying that the resurrection has already taken place. They are upsetting the faith of some.
55_2_19: Nevertheless, the firm foundation of God stands — having this seal: "The Lord knows those who are His," and, "Let everyone who names the name of the Lord turn away from unrighteousness."
55_2_20: Now in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and earthenware — some for honorable use, some for common.
55_2_21: Therefore, if anyone cleanses himself from these things, he will be a vessel for honor — sanctified, useful to the Master, prepared for every good work.
55_2_22: Flee youthful lusts. And pursue righteousness, faith, love, peace — with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart.
55_2_23: But have nothing to do with foolish and ignorant disputes — knowing that they generate strife.
55_2_24: And the Lord's bondservant must not be quarrelsome — but kind to all, able to teach, patient when wronged,
55_2_25: in gentleness correcting those who are in opposition. Perhaps God will grant them repentance, leading to a full knowledge of the truth,
55_2_26: and they may come to their senses — escaping the snare of the devil, who has held them captive to do his will.
55_3_1: But know this: that in the last days perilous times will come.
55_3_2: For people will be lovers of self, lovers of money, boastful, arrogant, abusive, disobedient to parents, ungrateful, unholy,
55_3_3: without natural affection, unforgiving, slanderers, without self-control, brutal, despisers of good,
55_3_4: treacherous, reckless, conceited — lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God,
55_3_5: having a form of godliness, but denying its power. Avoid such people.
55_3_6: For from these are those who creep into households and captivate weak women weighed down with sins, led away by various lusts —
55_3_7: always learning, and never able to come to the full knowledge of the truth.
55_3_8: Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so these also oppose the truth — men of corrupt mind, disqualified concerning the faith.
55_3_9: But they will not advance further. For their folly will be plain to all, just as also that of those men became.
55_3_10: But you have followed my teaching, my conduct, my purpose, my faith, my patience, my love, my steadfastness,
55_3_11: my persecutions, my sufferings — what happened to me at Antioch, at Iconium, at Lystra. What persecutions I endured! Yet out of them all the Lord rescued me.
55_3_12: Indeed, all who desire to live godly in Christ Jesus will be persecuted.
55_3_13: But evil men and impostors will go from bad to worse — deceiving and being deceived.
55_3_14: But as for you — continue in the things you have learned and have been assured of, knowing from whom you have learned them.
55_3_15: And how from infancy you have known the holy Scriptures, which are able to make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.
55_3_16: All Scripture is breathed out by God, and is profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, for training in righteousness —
55_3_17: so that the man of God may be complete, equipped for every good work.
55_4_1: I solemnly charge you in the presence of God and of Christ Jesus — who will judge the living and the dead, and by His appearing and His kingdom:
55_4_2: Preach the word. Be ready in season and out of season. Reprove, rebuke, exhort — with all patience and instruction.
55_4_3: For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine — but according to their own desires they will accumulate for themselves teachers, having itching ears.
55_4_4: And they will turn their ears away from the truth, and turn aside to myths.
55_4_5: But you, be sober in all things. Endure suffering. Do the work of an evangelist. Fulfill your ministry.
55_4_6: For I am already being poured out as a drink offering, and the time of my departure has come.
55_4_7: I have fought the good fight. I have finished the race. I have kept the faith.
55_4_8: Henceforth there is laid up for me the crown of righteousness, which the Lord — the righteous Judge — will give to me on that Day. And not only to me, but also to all who have loved His appearing.
55_4_9: Be diligent to come to me quickly.
55_4_10: For Demas, having loved this present world, has forsaken me and gone to Thessalonica. Crescens has gone to Galatia, Titus to Dalmatia.
55_4_11: Only Luke is with me. Get Mark and bring him with you, for he is useful to me for ministry.
55_4_12: Tychicus I have sent to Ephesus.
55_4_13: When you come, bring the cloak that I left at Troas with Carpus — and the books, especially the parchments.
55_4_14: Alexander the coppersmith did me much harm. The Lord will repay him according to his deeds.
55_4_15: You also be on guard against him — for he greatly opposed our message.
55_4_16: At my first defense, no one stood with me — all forsook me. May it not be charged against them.
55_4_17: But the Lord stood by me and strengthened me — so that through me the proclamation might be fully accomplished, and that all the Gentiles might hear it. And I was rescued from the lion's mouth.
55_4_18: And the Lord will rescue me from every evil deed, and bring me safely into His heavenly kingdom. To Him be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
55_4_19: Greet Prisca and Aquila, and the household of Onesiphorus.
55_4_20: Erastus stayed in Corinth. Trophimus I left sick at Miletus.
55_4_21: Be diligent to come before winter. Eubulus greets you, as do Pudens and Linus and Claudia, and all the brothers.
55_4_22: The Lord be with your spirit. Grace be with you all. Amen.
59_1_1: James, a bondservant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ — to the twelve tribes scattered abroad: Greetings.
59_1_2: Consider it pure joy, my brothers, whenever you encounter trials of various kinds —
59_1_3: knowing that the testing of your faith produces steadfastness.
59_1_4: And let steadfastness have its full effect — so that you may be mature and complete, lacking in nothing.
59_1_5: If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God — who gives generously to all without reproach — and it will be given to him.
59_1_6: But let him ask in faith, doubting nothing — for the one who doubts is like the surf of the sea, driven and tossed by the wind.
59_1_7: That person should not expect to receive anything from the Lord —
59_1_8: he is a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.
59_1_9: But let the brother of humble circumstances boast in his exaltation,
59_1_10: and the rich man, in his humiliation — because like a flower of the grass, he will pass away.
59_1_11: For the sun rises with its scorching heat, and withers the grass — and its flower falls off, and the beauty of its appearance is destroyed. So also the rich man, in the midst of his pursuits, will fade away.
59_1_12: Blessed is the man who endures trial — for once he has been approved, he will receive the crown of life, which the Lord has promised to those who love Him.
59_1_13: Let no one say when he is tempted, "I am being tempted by God." For God cannot be tempted by evil, and He Himself tempts no one.
59_1_14: But each one is tempted, when he is dragged away and enticed by his own lust.
59_1_15: Then, when lust has conceived, it gives birth to sin — and sin, when it has run its course, brings forth death.
59_1_16: Do not be deceived, my beloved brothers.
59_1_17: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above — coming down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation, nor shifting shadow.
59_1_18: In the exercise of His will He brought us forth by the word of truth — so that we would be a kind of firstfruits among His creatures.
59_1_19: Know this, my beloved brothers: let everyone be quick to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger.
59_1_20: For the anger of man does not produce the righteousness of God.
59_1_21: Therefore, putting aside all filthiness and all the abundance of wickedness, in humility receive the implanted word — which is able to save your souls.
59_1_22: But be doers of the word, and not hearers only — deceiving yourselves.
59_1_23: For if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like a man who looks at his natural face in a mirror.
59_1_24: For he looks at himself, and goes away, and immediately forgets what kind of man he was.
59_1_25: But the one who looks intently into the perfect law — the law of liberty — and continues in it, not having become a forgetful hearer but a doer of the work — this man will be blessed in what he does.
59_1_26: If anyone considers himself religious, and yet does not bridle his tongue, but deceives his own heart — this man's religion is worthless.
59_1_27: Pure religion and undefiled before our God and Father is this: to visit orphans and widows in their distress — and to keep oneself unstained by the world.
59_2_1: My brothers, do not hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with an attitude of partiality.
59_2_2: For if a man comes into your assembly with a gold ring and fine clothing — and a poor man also comes in dirty clothes —
59_2_3: and you pay special attention to the one wearing the fine clothing, and say, "You sit here in a good place," and to the poor one, "You stand there," or, "Sit down by my footstool" —
59_2_4: have you not made distinctions among yourselves, and become judges with evil thoughts?
59_2_5: Listen, my beloved brothers — did not God choose the poor of this world to be rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which He promised to those who love Him?
59_2_6: But you have dishonored the poor man. Is it not the rich who oppress you and personally drag you into court?
59_2_7: Do they not blaspheme the fair name by which you have been called?
59_2_8: If, however, you fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, "You shall love your neighbor as yourself," you are doing well.
59_2_9: But if you show partiality, you are committing sin — and are convicted by the law as transgressors.
59_2_10: For whoever keeps the whole law and yet stumbles in one point — he has become guilty of all.
59_2_11: For He who said, "Do not commit adultery," also said, "Do not commit murder." Now if you do not commit adultery, but do commit murder — you have become a transgressor of the law.
59_2_12: So speak and so act, as those who are to be judged by the law of liberty.
59_2_13: For judgment will be merciless to one who has shown no mercy. Mercy triumphs over judgment.
59_2_14: What use is it, my brothers, if a man says he has faith but he has no works? Can that faith save him?
59_2_15: If a brother or sister is without clothing and lacks the daily food,
59_2_16: and one of you says to them, "Go in peace, be warmed and be filled" — and yet you do not give them what is needed for the body — what use is that?
59_2_17: Even so, faith — if it has no works — is dead, being by itself.
59_2_18: But someone may well say, "You have faith, and I have works." Show me your faith without the works, and I will show you my faith by my works.
59_2_19: You believe that God is one. You do well — the demons also believe, and shudder.
59_2_20: But are you willing to recognize, you foolish man, that faith without works is useless?
59_2_21: Was not Abraham our father justified by works, when he offered up Isaac his son on the altar?
59_2_22: You see that faith was working with his works — and as a result of the works, faith was made complete.
59_2_23: And the Scripture was fulfilled, which says, "And Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness," and he was called the friend of God.
59_2_24: You see that a man is justified by works, and not by faith alone.
59_2_25: And in the same way, was not Rahab the prostitute also justified by works, when she received the messengers and sent them out by another way?
59_2_26: For just as the body without the spirit is dead, so also faith without works is dead.
59_3_1: Let not many of you become teachers, my brothers — knowing that as such we will incur a stricter judgment.
59_3_2: For we all stumble in many ways. If anyone does not stumble in word, he is a perfect man — able to bridle the whole body as well.
59_3_3: Now if we put the bits into the horses' mouths so that they will obey us, we direct their entire body as well.
59_3_4: Look at the ships also — though they are so large, and are driven by strong winds — they are turned by a very small rudder, wherever the inclination of the pilot desires.
59_3_5: So also the tongue is a small part of the body, and yet it boasts of great things. Behold, how great a forest is set ablaze by such a small fire!
59_3_6: And the tongue is a fire — the very world of iniquity. The tongue is set among our members as that which defiles the entire body, and sets on fire the course of our life — and is set on fire by hell.
59_3_7: For every species of beasts and birds, of reptiles and creatures of the sea, is tamed and has been tamed by the human race.
59_3_8: But no one among men can tame the tongue — it is a restless evil, full of deadly poison.
59_3_9: With it we bless our Lord and Father — and with it we curse men, who have been made in the likeness of God.
59_3_10: From the same mouth come both blessing and cursing. My brothers, these things ought not to be this way.
59_3_11: Does a fountain send out from the same opening both fresh and bitter water?
59_3_12: My brothers, can a fig tree produce olives, or a vine, figs? Nor can salt water produce fresh.
59_3_13: Who among you is wise and understanding? Let him show by his good behavior his works in the gentleness of wisdom.
59_3_14: But if you have bitter envy and selfish ambition in your heart, do not be arrogant and so lie against the truth.
59_3_15: This wisdom is not the kind that comes down from above — but is earthly, natural, demonic.
59_3_16: For where envy and selfish ambition are, there is disorder and every evil thing.
59_3_17: But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, willing to yield, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, without hypocrisy.
59_3_18: And the seed whose fruit is righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.
59_4_1: What is the source of quarrels and of conflicts among you? Is it not this — that your pleasures wage war within your members?
59_4_2: You lust and do not have, so you murder. You are envious and cannot obtain, so you fight and quarrel. You do not have, because you do not ask.
59_4_3: You ask and do not receive, because you ask with wrong motives — so that you may spend it on your pleasures.
59_4_4: You adulteresses, do you not know that friendship with the world is hostility toward God? Therefore whoever wishes to be a friend of the world makes himself an enemy of God.
59_4_5: Or do you think that the Scripture speaks in vain: "He jealously desires the Spirit which He has made to dwell in us"?
59_4_6: But He gives a greater grace. Therefore it says, "God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble."
59_4_7: Submit therefore to God. Resist the devil — and he will flee from you.
59_4_8: Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners — and purify your hearts, you double-minded.
59_4_9: Be miserable and mourn and weep. Let your laughter be turned into mourning, and your joy to gloom.
59_4_10: Humble yourselves in the presence of the Lord, and He will exalt you.
59_4_11: Do not speak against one another, brothers. The one who speaks against a brother, or judges his brother, speaks against the law and judges the law. But if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law but a judge of it.
59_4_12: There is only one Lawgiver and Judge — the One who is able to save and to destroy. But who are you, who judges your neighbor?
59_4_13: Come now, you who say, "Today or tomorrow we will go into such and such a city, and spend a year there, and engage in business and make a profit" —
59_4_14: yet you do not know what your life will be like tomorrow. You are just a vapor that appears for a little while, and then vanishes away.
59_4_15: Instead, you ought to say, "If the Lord wills, we will live and also do this or that."
59_4_16: But as it is, you boast in your arrogance. All such boasting is evil.
59_4_17: Therefore, to one who knows the right thing to do, and does not do it — to him it is sin.
59_5_1: Come now, you rich — weep and howl over your miseries which are coming upon you.
59_5_2: Your riches have rotted, and your garments have become moth-eaten.
59_5_3: Your gold and your silver have rusted; and their rust will be a witness against you, and will consume your flesh like fire. You have stored up your treasure in the last days!
59_5_4: Behold, the pay of the laborers who mowed your fields — and which has been withheld by you — cries out against you. And the cries of the harvesters have reached the ears of the Lord of hosts.
59_5_5: You have lived luxuriously on the earth, and led a life of wanton pleasure. You have fattened your hearts in a day of slaughter.
59_5_6: You have condemned and put to death the righteous one — he does not resist you.
59_5_7: Therefore be patient, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. Behold, the farmer waits for the precious produce of the soil — being patient about it, until it gets the early and the late rains.
59_5_8: You too be patient. Strengthen your hearts, for the coming of the Lord is near.
59_5_9: Do not complain, brothers, against one another — so that you yourselves may not be judged. Behold, the Judge is standing right at the door.
59_5_10: As an example, brothers, of suffering and patience, take the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.
59_5_11: Behold, we count those blessed who have endured. You have heard of the endurance of Job, and have seen the outcome of the Lord's dealings — that the Lord is full of compassion and is merciful.
59_5_12: But above all, my brothers, do not swear — neither by heaven, nor by earth, nor by any other oath. But let your yes be yes, and your no, no — so that you may not fall under judgment.
59_5_13: Is anyone among you suffering? Let him pray. Is anyone cheerful? Let him sing praises.
59_5_14: Is anyone among you sick? Let him call for the elders of the church, and let them pray over him — anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord.
59_5_15: And the prayer of faith will save the one who is sick — and the Lord will raise him up. And if he has committed sins, they will be forgiven him.
59_5_16: Therefore, confess your sins to one another, and pray for one another, so that you may be healed. The effective prayer of a righteous man can accomplish much.
59_5_17: Elijah was a man with a nature like ours — and he prayed earnestly that it would not rain, and it did not rain on the earth for three years and six months.
59_5_18: And he prayed again, and the sky poured rain — and the earth produced its fruit.
59_5_19: My brothers, if any among you strays from the truth, and one turns him back —
59_5_20: let him know that he who turns a sinner from the error of his way will save his soul from death, and will cover a multitude of sins.
60_1_1: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ — to the elect exiles of the dispersion in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,
60_1_2: according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, by the sanctification of the Spirit, for obedience and sprinkling with the blood of Jesus Christ: Grace and peace be multiplied to you.
60_1_3: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ — who according to His great mercy has given us new birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
60_1_4: to an inheritance imperishable, undefiled, and unfading — kept in heaven for you,
60_1_5: who through faith are being guarded by the power of God for the salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.
60_1_6: In this you greatly rejoice — though now, for a little while if necessary, you have been distressed by various trials,
60_1_7: so that the proven character of your faith — more precious than gold which is perishable, even though tested by fire — may be found to result in praise, glory, and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ.
60_1_8: Whom not having seen, you love; in whom, though you do not see Him now, you believe — and rejoice with joy unspeakable and full of glory,
