37_1_6: “You have sown much, and bring in little; You eat, but do not have enough; You drink, but you are not filled with drink; You clothe yourselves, but no one is warm; And he who earns wages, Earns wages to put into a bag with holes.”
37_1_7: Thus says the LORD of hosts: “Consider your ways!
37_1_8: Go up to the mountains and bring wood and build the temple, that I may take pleasure in it and be glorified,” says the LORD.
37_1_9: “ You looked for much, but indeed it came to little; and when you brought it home, I blew it away. Why?” says the LORD of hosts. “Because of My house that is in ruins, while every one of you runs to his own house.
37_1_10: Therefore the heavens above you withhold the dew, and the earth withholds its fruit.
37_1_11: For I called for a drought on the land and the mountains, on the grain and the new wine and the oil, on whatever the ground brings forth, on men and livestock, and on all the labor of your hands.”
37_1_12: Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, with all the remnant of the people, obeyed the voice of the LORD their God, and the words of Haggai the prophet, as the LORD their God had sent him; and the people feared the presence of the LORD.
37_1_13: Then Haggai, the LORD’s messenger, spoke the LORD’s message to the people, saying, “I am with you, says the LORD.”
37_1_14: So the LORD stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and the spirit of Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people; and they came and worked on the house of the LORD of hosts, their God
37_1_15: on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month, in the second year of King Darius.
37_2_1: In the seventh month, on the twenty-first of the month, the word of the LORD came by Haggai the prophet, saying:
37_2_2: “Speak now to Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and to the remnant of the people, saying:
37_2_3: ‘Who is left among you who saw this temple in its former glory? And how do you see it now? In comparison with it, is this not in your eyes as nothing?
37_2_4: Yet now be strong, Zerubbabel,’ says the LORD; ‘and be strong, Joshua, son of Jehozadak, the high priest; and be strong, all you people of the land,’ says the LORD, ‘and work; for I am with you,’ says the LORD of hosts.
37_2_5: ‘ According to the word that I covenanted with you when you came out of Egypt, so My Spirit remains among you; do not fear!’
37_2_6: “For thus says the LORD of hosts: ‘Once more (it is a little while) I will shake heaven and earth, the sea and dry land
37_2_7: and I will shake all nations, and they shall come to the Desire of All Nations, and I will fill this temple with glory,’ says the LORD of hosts.
37_2_8: ‘The silver is Mine, and the gold is Mine,’ says the LORD of hosts.
37_2_9: ‘The glory of this latter temple shall be greater than the former,’ says the LORD of hosts. ‘And in this place I will give peace,’ says the LORD of hosts.”
37_2_10: On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came by Haggai the prophet, saying
37_2_11: “Thus says the LORD of hosts: ‘Now, ask the priests concerning the law, saying
37_2_12: “If one carries holy meat in the fold of his garment, and with the edge he touches bread or stew, wine or oil, or any food, will it become holy?” ’ ” Then the priests answered and said, “No.”
37_2_13: And Haggai said, “If one who is unclean because of a dead body touches any of these, will it be unclean?” So the priests answered and said, “It shall be unclean.”
37_2_14: Then Haggai answered and said, “ ‘So is this people, and so is this nation before Me,’ says the LORD, ‘and so is every work of their hands; and what they offer there is unclean.
37_2_15: ‘And now, carefully consider from this day forward: from before stone was laid upon stone in the temple of the LORD—
37_2_16: since those days, when one came to a heap of twenty ephahs, there were but ten; when one came to the wine vat to draw out fifty baths from the press, there were but twenty.
37_2_17: I struck you with blight and mildew and hail in all the labors of your hands; yet you did not turn to Me,’ says the LORD.
37_2_18: ‘Consider now from this day forward, from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, from the day that the foundation of the LORD’s temple was laid—consider it:
37_2_19: Is the seed still in the barn? As yet the vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate, and the olive tree have not yielded fruit. But from this day I will bless you. ’ ”
37_2_20: And again the word of the LORD came to Haggai on the twenty-fourth day of the month, saying
37_2_21: “Speak to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, saying: ‘I will shake heaven and earth.
37_2_22: I will overthrow the throne of kingdoms; I will destroy the strength of the Gentile kingdoms. I will overthrow the chariots And those who ride in them; The horses and their riders shall come down, Every one by the sword of his brother.
37_2_23: ‘In that day,’ says the LORD of hosts, ‘I will take you, Zerubbabel My servant, the son of Shealtiel,’ says the LORD, ‘and will make you like a signet ring; for I have chosen you,’ says the LORD of hosts.”
38_1_1: In the eighth month of the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo the prophet, saying
38_1_2: “The LORD has been very angry with your fathers.
38_1_3: Therefore say to them, ‘Thus says the LORD of hosts: “Return to Me,” says the LORD of hosts, “and I will return to you,” says the LORD of hosts.
38_1_4: “Do not be like your fathers, to whom the former prophets preached, saying, ‘Thus says the LORD of hosts: “Turn now from your evil ways and your evil deeds.” ’ But they did not hear nor heed Me,” says the LORD.
38_1_5: “Your fathers, where are they? And the prophets, do they live forever?
38_1_6: Yet surely My words and My statutes, Which I commanded My servants the prophets, Did they not overtake your fathers? “So they returned and said: ‘Just as the LORD of hosts determined to do to us, According to our ways and according to our deeds, So He has dealt with us.’ ” ’ ”
38_1_7: On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, which is the month Shebat, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo the prophet:
38_1_8: I saw by night, and behold, a man riding on a red horse, and it stood among the myrtle trees in the hollow; and behind him were horses: red, sorrel, and white.
38_1_9: Then I said, “My lord, what are these?” So the angel who talked with me said to me, “I will show you what they are. ”
38_1_10: And the man who stood among the myrtle trees answered and said, “These are the ones whom the LORD has sent to walk to and fro throughout the earth.”
38_1_11: So they answered the Angel of the LORD, who stood among the myrtle trees, and said, “We have walked to and fro throughout the earth, and behold, all the earth is resting quietly.”
38_1_12: Then the Angel of the LORD answered and said, “O LORD of hosts, how long will You not have mercy on Jerusalem and on the cities of Judah, against which You were angry these seventy years?”
38_1_13: And the LORD answered the angel who talked to me, with good and comforting words.
38_1_14: So the angel who spoke with me said to me, “Proclaim, saying, ‘Thus says the LORD of hosts: “I am zealous for Jerusalem And for Zion with great zeal.
38_1_15: I am exceedingly angry with the nations at ease; For I was a little angry, And they helped— but with evil intent. ”
38_1_16: ‘Therefore thus says the LORD: “I am returning to Jerusalem with mercy; My house shall be built in it,” says the LORD of hosts, “And a surveyor’s line shall be stretched out over Jerusalem.” ’
38_1_17: “Again proclaim, saying, ‘Thus says the LORD of hosts: “My cities shall again spread out through prosperity; The LORD will again comfort Zion, And will again choose Jerusalem.” ’ ”
38_1_18: Then I raised my eyes and looked, and there were four horns.
38_1_19: And I said to the angel who talked with me, “What are these?” So he answered me, “These are the horns that have scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem.”
38_1_20: Then the LORD showed me four craftsmen.
38_1_21: And I said, “What are these coming to do?” So he said, “These are the horns that scattered Judah, so that no one could lift up his head; but the craftsmen are coming to terrify them, to cast out the horns of the nations that lifted up their horn against the land of Judah to scatter it.”
38_2_1: Then I raised my eyes and looked, and behold, a man with a measuring line in his hand.
38_2_2: So I said, “Where are you going?” And he said to me, “To measure Jerusalem, to see what is its width and what is its length.”
38_2_3: And there was the angel who talked with me, going out; and another angel was coming out to meet him
38_2_4: who said to him, “Run, speak to this young man, saying: ‘Jerusalem shall be inhabited as towns without walls, because of the multitude of men and livestock in it.
38_2_5: For I,’ says the LORD, ‘will be a wall of fire all around her, and I will be the glory in her midst.’ ”
38_2_6: “Up, up! Flee from the land of the north,” says the LORD; “for I have spread you abroad like the four winds of heaven,” says the LORD.
38_2_7: “Up, Zion! Escape, you who dwell with the daughter of Babylon.”
38_2_8: For thus says the LORD of hosts: “He sent Me after glory, to the nations which plunder you; for he who touches you touches the apple of His eye.
38_2_9: For surely I will shake My hand against them, and they shall become spoil for their servants. Then you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent Me.
38_2_10: “Sing and rejoice, O daughter of Zion! For behold, I am coming and I will dwell in your midst,” says the LORD.
38_2_11: “Many nations shall be joined to the LORD in that day, and they shall become My people. And I will dwell in your midst. Then you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent Me to you.
38_2_12: And the LORD will take possession of Judah as His inheritance in the Holy Land, and will again choose Jerusalem.
38_2_13: Be silent, all flesh, before the LORD, for He is aroused from His holy habitation!”
38_3_1: Then he showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the Angel of the LORD, and Satan standing at his right hand to oppose him.
38_3_2: And the LORD said to Satan, “The LORD rebuke you, Satan! The LORD who has chosen Jerusalem rebuke you! Is this not a brand plucked from the fire?”
38_3_3: Now Joshua was clothed with filthy garments, and was standing before the Angel.
38_3_4: Then He answered and spoke to those who stood before Him, saying, “Take away the filthy garments from him.” And to him He said, “See, I have removed your iniquity from you, and I will clothe you with rich robes.”
38_3_5: And I said, “Let them put a clean turban on his head.” So they put a clean turban on his head, and they put the clothes on him. And the Angel of the LORD stood by.
38_3_6: Then the Angel of the LORD admonished Joshua, saying
38_3_7: “Thus says the LORD of hosts: ‘If you will walk in My ways, And if you will keep My command, Then you shall also judge My house, And likewise have charge of My courts; I will give you places to walk Among these who stand here.
38_3_8: ‘Hear, O Joshua, the high priest, You and your companions who sit before you, For they are a wondrous sign; For behold, I am bringing forth My Servant the BRANCH.
38_3_9: For behold, the stone That I have laid before Joshua: Upon the stone are seven eyes. Behold, I will engrave its inscription,’ Says the LORD of hosts, ‘And I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day.
38_3_10: In that day,’ says the LORD of hosts, ‘Everyone will invite his neighbor Under his vine and under his fig tree.’ ”
38_4_1: Now the angel who talked with me came back and wakened me, as a man who is wakened out of his sleep.
38_4_2: And he said to me, “What do you see?” So I said, “I am looking, and there is a lampstand of solid gold with a bowl on top of it, and on the stand seven lamps with seven pipes to the seven lamps.
38_4_3: Two olive trees are by it, one at the right of the bowl and the other at its left.”
38_4_4: So I answered and spoke to the angel who talked with me, saying, “What are these, my lord?”
38_4_5: Then the angel who talked with me answered and said to me, “Do you not know what these are?” And I said, “No, my lord.”
38_4_6: So he answered and said to me: “This is the word of the LORD to Zerubbabel: ‘Not by might nor by power, but by My Spirit,’ Says the LORD of hosts.
38_4_7: ‘Who are you, O great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you shall become a plain! And he shall bring forth the capstone With shouts of “Grace, grace to it!” ’ ”
38_4_8: Moreover the word of the LORD came to me, saying:
38_4_9: “The hands of Zerubbabel Have laid the foundation of this temple; His hands shall also finish it. Then you will know That the LORD of hosts has sent Me to you.
38_4_10: For who has despised the day of small things? For these seven rejoice to see The plumb line in the hand of Zerubbabel. They are the eyes of the LORD, Which scan to and fro throughout the whole earth.”
38_4_11: Then I answered and said to him, “What are these two olive trees—at the right of the lampstand and at its left?”
38_4_12: And I further answered and said to him, “What are these two olive branches that drip into the receptacles of the two gold pipes from which the golden oil drains?”
38_4_13: Then he answered me and said, “Do you not know what these are? ” And I said, “No, my lord.”
38_4_14: So he said, “These are the two anointed ones, who stand beside the Lord of the whole earth.”
38_5_1: Then I turned and raised my eyes, and saw there a flying scroll.
38_5_2: And he said to me, “What do you see?” So I answered, “I see a flying scroll. Its length is twenty cubits and its width ten cubits.”
38_5_3: Then he said to me, “This is the curse that goes out over the face of the whole earth: ‘Every thief shall be expelled,’ according to this side of the scroll; and, ‘Every perjurer shall be expelled,’ according to that side of it.”
38_5_4: “I will send out the curse, ” says the LORD of hosts; “It shall enter the house of the thief And the house of the one who swears falsely by My name. It shall remain in the midst of his house And consume it, with its timber and stones.”
38_5_5: Then the angel who talked with me came out and said to me, “Lift your eyes now, and see what this is that goes forth.”
38_5_6: So I asked, “What is it?” And he said, “It is a basket that is going forth.” He also said, “This is their resemblance throughout the earth:
38_5_7: Here is a lead disc lifted up, and this is a woman sitting inside the basket”
38_5_8: then he said, “This is Wickedness!” And he thrust her down into the basket, and threw the lead cover over its mouth.
38_5_9: Then I raised my eyes and looked, and there were two women, coming with the wind in their wings; for they had wings like the wings of a stork, and they lifted up the basket between earth and heaven.
38_5_10: So I said to the angel who talked with me, “Where are they carrying the basket?”
38_5_11: And he said to me, “To build a house for it in the land of Shinar; when it is ready, the basket will be set there on its base.”
38_6_1: Then I turned and raised my eyes and looked, and behold, four chariots were coming from between two mountains, and the mountains were mountains of bronze.
38_6_2: With the first chariot were red horses, with the second chariot black horses
38_6_3: with the third chariot white horses, and with the fourth chariot dappled horses—strong steeds.
38_6_4: Then I answered and said to the angel who talked with me, “What are these, my lord?”
38_6_5: And the angel answered and said to me, “These are four spirits of heaven, who go out from their station before the Lord of all the earth.
38_6_6: The one with the black horses is going to the north country, the white are going after them, and the dappled are going toward the south country.”
38_6_7: Then the strong steeds went out, eager to go, that they might walk to and fro throughout the earth. And He said, “Go, walk to and fro throughout the earth.” So they walked to and fro throughout the earth.
38_6_8: And He called to me, and spoke to me, saying, “See, those who go toward the north country have given rest to My Spirit in the north country.”
38_6_9: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying:
38_6_10: “Receive the gift from the captives—from Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah, who have come from Babylon—and go the same day and enter the house of Josiah the son of Zephaniah.
38_6_11: Take the silver and gold, make an elaborate crown, and set it on the head of Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest.
38_6_12: Then speak to him, saying, ‘Thus says the LORD of hosts, saying: “Behold, the Man whose name is the BRANCH! From His place He shall branch out, And He shall build the temple of the LORD
38_6_13: Yes, He shall build the temple of the LORD. He shall bear the glory, And shall sit and rule on His throne; So He shall be a priest on His throne, And the counsel of peace shall be between them both.” ’
38_6_14: “Now the elaborate crown shall be for a memorial in the temple of the LORD for Helem, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and Hen the son of Zephaniah.
38_6_15: Even those from afar shall come and build the temple of the LORD. Then you shall know that the LORD of hosts has sent Me to you. And this shall come to pass if you diligently obey the voice of the LORD your God.”
38_7_1: Now in the fourth year of King Darius it came to pass that the word of the LORD came to Zechariah, on the fourth day of the ninth month, Chislev
38_7_2: when the people sent Sherezer, with Regem-Melech and his men, to the house of God, to pray before the LORD
38_7_3: and to ask the priests who were in the house of the LORD of hosts, and the prophets, saying, “Should I weep in the fifth month and fast as I have done for so many years?”
38_7_4: Then the word of the LORD of hosts came to me, saying
38_7_5: “Say to all the people of the land, and to the priests: ‘When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and seventh months during those seventy years, did you really fast for Me—for Me?
38_7_6: When you eat and when you drink, do you not eat and drink for yourselves?
38_7_7: Should you not have obeyed the words which the LORD proclaimed through the former prophets when Jerusalem and the cities around it were inhabited and prosperous, and the South and the Lowland were inhabited?’ ”
38_7_8: Then the word of the LORD came to Zechariah, saying
38_7_9: “Thus says the LORD of hosts: ‘Execute true justice, Show mercy and compassion Everyone to his brother.
38_7_10: Do not oppress the widow or the fatherless, The alien or the poor. Let none of you plan evil in his heart Against his brother.’
38_7_11: “But they refused to heed, shrugged their shoulders, and stopped their ears so that they could not hear.
38_7_12: Yes, they made their hearts like flint, refusing to hear the law and the words which the LORD of hosts had sent by His Spirit through the former prophets. Thus great wrath came from the LORD of hosts.
38_7_13: Therefore it happened, that just as He proclaimed and they would not hear, so they called out and I would not listen,” says the LORD of hosts.
38_7_14: “But I scattered them with a whirlwind among all the nations which they had not known. Thus the land became desolate after them, so that no one passed through or returned; for they made the pleasant land desolate.”
38_8_1: Again the word of the LORD of hosts came, saying
38_8_2: “Thus says the LORD of hosts: ‘I am zealous for Zion with great zeal; With great fervor I am zealous for her.’
38_8_3: “Thus says the LORD: ‘I will return to Zion, And dwell in the midst of Jerusalem. Jerusalem shall be called the City of Truth, The Mountain of the LORD of hosts, The Holy Mountain.’
38_8_4: “Thus says the LORD of hosts: ‘Old men and old women shall again sit In the streets of Jerusalem, Each one with his staff in his hand Because of great age.
38_8_5: The streets of the city Shall be full of boys and girls Playing in its streets.’
38_8_6: “Thus says the LORD of hosts: ‘If it is marvelous in the eyes of the remnant of this people in these days, Will it also be marvelous in My eyes?’ Says the LORD of hosts.
38_8_7: “Thus says the LORD of hosts: ‘Behold, I will save My people from the land of the east And from the land of the west
38_8_8: I will bring them back, And they shall dwell in the midst of Jerusalem. They shall be My people And I will be their God, In truth and righteousness.’
38_8_9: “Thus says the LORD of hosts: ‘Let your hands be strong, You who have been hearing in these days These words by the mouth of the prophets, Who spoke in the day the foundation was laid For the house of the LORD of hosts, That the temple might be built.
38_8_10: For before these days There were no wages for man nor any hire for beast; There was no peace from the enemy for whoever went out or came in; For I set all men, everyone, against his neighbor.
38_8_11: But now I will not treat the remnant of this people as in the former days,’ says the LORD of hosts.
38_8_12: ‘For the seed shall be prosperous, The vine shall give its fruit, The ground shall give her increase, And the heavens shall give their dew— I will cause the remnant of this people To possess all these.
38_8_13: And it shall come to pass That just as you were a curse among the nations, O house of Judah and house of Israel, So I will save you, and you shall be a blessing. Do not fear, Let your hands be strong.’
38_8_14: “For thus says the LORD of hosts: ‘Just as I determined to punish you When your fathers provoked Me to wrath,’ Says the LORD of hosts, ‘And I would not relent
38_8_15: So again in these days I am determined to do good To Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. Do not fear.
38_8_16: These are the things you shall do: Speak each man the truth to his neighbor; Give judgment in your gates for truth, justice, and peace
38_8_17: Let none of you think evil in your heart against your neighbor; And do not love a false oath. For all these are things that I hate,’ Says the LORD.”
38_8_18: Then the word of the LORD of hosts came to me, saying
38_8_19: “Thus says the LORD of hosts: ‘The fast of the fourth month, The fast of the fifth, The fast of the seventh, And the fast of the tenth, Shall be joy and gladness and cheerful feasts For the house of Judah. Therefore love truth and peace.’
38_8_20: “Thus says the LORD of hosts: ‘Peoples shall yet come, Inhabitants of many cities
38_8_21: The inhabitants of one city shall go to another, saying, “Let us continue to go and pray before the LORD, And seek the LORD of hosts. I myself will go also.”
38_8_22: Yes, many peoples and strong nations Shall come to seek the LORD of hosts in Jerusalem, And to pray before the LORD.’
38_8_23: “Thus says the LORD of hosts: ‘In those days ten men from every language of the nations shall grasp the sleeve of a Jewish man, saying, “Let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.” ’ ”
38_9_1: The burden of the word of the LORD Against the land of Hadrach, And Damascus its resting place (For the eyes of men And all the tribes of Israel Are on the LORD)
38_9_2: Also against Hamath, which borders on it, And against Tyre and Sidon, though they are very wise.
38_9_3: For Tyre built herself a tower, Heaped up silver like the dust, And gold like the mire of the streets.
38_9_4: Behold, the Lord will cast her out; He will destroy her power in the sea, And she will be devoured by fire.
38_9_5: Ashkelon shall see it and fear; Gaza also shall be very sorrowful; And Ekron, for He dried up her expectation. The king shall perish from Gaza, And Ashkelon shall not be inhabited.
38_9_6: “A mixed race shall settle in Ashdod, And I will cut off the pride of the Philistines.
38_9_7: I will take away the blood from his mouth, And the abominations from between his teeth. But he who remains, even he shall be for our God, And shall be like a leader in Judah, And Ekron like a Jebusite.
38_9_8: I will camp around My house Because of the army, Because of him who passes by and him who returns. No more shall an oppressor pass through them, For now I have seen with My eyes.
38_9_9: “Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion! Shout, O daughter of Jerusalem! Behold, your King is coming to you; He is just and having salvation, Lowly and riding on a donkey, A colt, the foal of a donkey.
38_9_10: I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim And the horse from Jerusalem; The battle bow shall be cut off. He shall speak peace to the nations; His dominion shall be ‘from sea to sea, And from the River to the ends of the earth.’
38_9_11: “As for you also, Because of the blood of your covenant, I will set your prisoners free from the waterless pit.
38_9_12: Return to the stronghold, You prisoners of hope. Even today I declare That I will restore double to you.
38_9_13: For I have bent Judah, My bow, Fitted the bow with Ephraim, And raised up your sons, O Zion, Against your sons, O Greece, And made you like the sword of a mighty man.”
38_9_14: Then the LORD will be seen over them, And His arrow will go forth like lightning. The Lord GOD will blow the trumpet, And go with whirlwinds from the south.
38_9_15: The LORD of hosts will defend them; They shall devour and subdue with slingstones. They shall drink and roar as if with wine; They shall be filled with blood like basins, Like the corners of the altar.
38_9_16: The LORD their God will save them in that day, As the flock of His people. For they shall be like the jewels of a crown, Lifted like a banner over His land—
38_9_17: For how great is its goodness And how great its beauty! Grain shall make the young men thrive, And new wine the young women.
38_10_1: Ask the LORD for rain In the time of the latter rain. The LORD will make flashing clouds; He will give them showers of rain, Grass in the field for everyone.
38_10_2: For the idols speak delusion; The diviners envision lies, And tell false dreams; They comfort in vain. Therefore the people wend their way like sheep; They are in trouble because there is no shepherd.
38_10_3: “My anger is kindled against the shepherds, And I will punish the goatherds. For the LORD of hosts will visit His flock, The house of Judah, And will make them as His royal horse in the battle.
38_10_4: From him comes the cornerstone, From him the tent peg, From him the battle bow, From him every ruler together.
38_10_5: They shall be like mighty men, Who tread down their enemies In the mire of the streets in the battle. They shall fight because the LORD is with them, And the riders on horses shall be put to shame.
38_10_6: “I will strengthen the house of Judah, And I will save the house of Joseph. I will bring them back, Because I have mercy on them. They shall be as though I had not cast them aside; For I am the LORD their God, And I will hear them.
38_10_7: Those of Ephraim shall be like a mighty man, And their heart shall rejoice as if with wine. Yes, their children shall see it and be glad; Their heart shall rejoice in the LORD.
38_10_8: I will whistle for them and gather them, For I will redeem them; And they shall increase as they once increased.
38_10_9: “I will sow them among the peoples, And they shall remember Me in far countries; They shall live, together with their children, And they shall return.
38_10_10: I will also bring them back from the land of Egypt, And gather them from Assyria. I will bring them into the land of Gilead and Lebanon, Until no more room is found for them.
38_10_11: He shall pass through the sea with affliction, And strike the waves of the sea: All the depths of the River shall dry up. Then the pride of Assyria shall be brought down, And the scepter of Egypt shall depart.
38_10_12: “So I will strengthen them in the LORD, And they shall walk up and down in His name,” Says the LORD.
38_11_1: Open your doors, O Lebanon, That fire may devour your cedars.
38_11_2: Wail, O cypress, for the cedar has fallen, Because the mighty trees are ruined. Wail, O oaks of Bashan, For the thick forest has come down.
38_11_3: There is the sound of wailing shepherds! For their glory is in ruins. There is the sound of roaring lions! For the pride of the Jordan is in ruins.
38_11_4: Thus says the LORD my God, “Feed the flock for slaughter
38_11_5: whose owners slaughter them and feel no guilt; those who sell them say, ‘Blessed be the LORD, for I am rich’; and their shepherds do not pity them.
38_11_6: For I will no longer pity the inhabitants of the land,” says the LORD. “But indeed I will give everyone into his neighbor’s hand and into the hand of his king. They shall attack the land, and I will not deliver them from their hand.”
38_11_7: So I fed the flock for slaughter, in particular the poor of the flock. I took for myself two staffs: the one I called Beauty, and the other I called Bonds; and I fed the flock.
38_11_8: I dismissed the three shepherds in one month. My soul loathed them, and their soul also abhorred me.
38_11_9: Then I said, “I will not feed you. Let what is dying die, and what is perishing perish. Let those that are left eat each other’s flesh.”
38_11_10: And I took my staff, Beauty, and cut it in two, that I might break the covenant which I had made with all the peoples.
38_11_11: So it was broken on that day. Thus the poor of the flock, who were watching me, knew that it was the word of the LORD.
38_11_12: Then I said to them, “If it is agreeable to you, give me my wages; and if not, refrain.” So they weighed out for my wages thirty pieces of silver.
38_11_13: And the LORD said to me, “Throw it to the potter”—that princely price they set on me. So I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them into the house of the LORD for the potter.
38_11_14: Then I cut in two my other staff, Bonds, that I might break the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.
38_11_15: And the LORD said to me, “Next, take for yourself the implements of a foolish shepherd.
38_11_16: For indeed I will raise up a shepherd in the land who will not care for those who are cut off, nor seek the young, nor heal those that are broken, nor feed those that still stand. But he will eat the flesh of the fat and tear their hooves in pieces.
38_11_17: “Woe to the worthless shepherd, Who leaves the flock! A sword shall be against his arm And against his right eye; His arm shall completely wither, And his right eye shall be totally blinded.”
38_12_1: The burden of the word of the LORD against Israel. Thus says the LORD, who stretches out the heavens, lays the foundation of the earth, and forms the spirit of man within him:
38_12_2: “Behold, I will make Jerusalem a cup of drunkenness to all the surrounding peoples, when they lay siege against Judah and Jerusalem.
38_12_3: And it shall happen in that day that I will make Jerusalem a very heavy stone for all peoples; all who would heave it away will surely be cut in pieces, though all nations of the earth are gathered against it.
38_12_4: In that day,” says the LORD, “I will strike every horse with confusion, and its rider with madness; I will open My eyes on the house of Judah, and will strike every horse of the peoples with blindness.
38_12_5: And the governors of Judah shall say in their heart, ‘The inhabitants of Jerusalem are my strength in the LORD of hosts, their God.’
38_12_6: In that day I will make the governors of Judah like a firepan in the woodpile, and like a fiery torch in the sheaves; they shall devour all the surrounding peoples on the right hand and on the left, but Jerusalem shall be inhabited again in her own place—Jerusalem.
38_12_7: “The LORD will save the tents of Judah first, so that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem shall not become greater than that of Judah.
38_12_8: In that day the LORD will defend the inhabitants of Jerusalem; the one who is feeble among them in that day shall be like David, and the house of David shall be like God, like the Angel of the LORD before them.
38_12_9: It shall be in that day that I will seek to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem.
38_12_10: “And I will pour on the house of David and on the inhabitants of Jerusalem the Spirit of grace and supplication; then they will look on Me whom they pierced. Yes, they will mourn for Him as one mourns for his only son, and grieve for Him as one grieves for a firstborn.
38_12_11: In that day there shall be a great mourning in Jerusalem, like the mourning at Hadad Rimmon in the plain of Megiddo.
38_12_12: And the land shall mourn, every family by itself: the family of the house of David by itself, and their wives by themselves; the family of the house of Nathan by itself, and their wives by themselves
38_12_13: the family of the house of Levi by itself, and their wives by themselves; the family of Shimei by itself, and their wives by themselves
38_12_14: all the families that remain, every family by itself, and their wives by themselves.
38_13_1: “In that day a fountain shall be opened for the house of David and for the inhabitants of Jerusalem, for sin and for uncleanness.
38_13_2: “It shall be in that day,” says the LORD of hosts, “ that I will cut off the names of the idols from the land, and they shall no longer be remembered. I will also cause the prophets and the unclean spirit to depart from the land.
38_13_3: It shall come to pass that if anyone still prophesies, then his father and mother who begot him will say to him, ‘You shall not live, because you have spoken lies in the name of the LORD.’ And his father and mother who begot him shall thrust him through when he prophesies.
38_13_4: “And it shall be in that day that every prophet will be ashamed of his vision when he prophesies; they will not wear a robe of coarse hair to deceive.
38_13_5: But he will say, ‘I am no prophet, I am a farmer; for a man taught me to keep cattle from my youth.’
38_13_6: And one will say to him, ‘What are these wounds between your arms?’ Then he will answer, ‘ Those with which I was wounded in the house of my friends.’
38_13_7: “Awake, O sword, against My Shepherd, Against the Man who is My Companion,” Says the LORD of hosts. “Strike the Shepherd, And the sheep will be scattered; Then I will turn My hand against the little ones.
38_13_8: And it shall come to pass in all the land,” Says the LORD, “ That two-thirds in it shall be cut off and die, But one –third shall be left in it:
38_13_9: I will bring the one –third through the fire, Will refine them as silver is refined, And test them as gold is tested. They will call on My name, And I will answer them. I will say, ‘This is My people’; And each one will say, ‘The LORD is my God.’ ”
38_14_1: Behold, the day of the LORD is coming, And your spoil will be divided in your midst.
38_14_2: For I will gather all the nations to battle against Jerusalem; The city shall be taken, The houses rifled, And the women ravished. Half of the city shall go into captivity, But the remnant of the people shall not be cut off from the city.
38_14_3: Then the LORD will go forth And fight against those nations, As He fights in the day of battle.
38_14_4: And in that day His feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, Which faces Jerusalem on the east. And the Mount of Olives shall be split in two, From east to west, Making a very large valley; Half of the mountain shall move toward the north And half of it toward the south.
38_14_5: Then you shall flee through My mountain valley, For the mountain valley shall reach to Azal. Yes, you shall flee As you fled from the earthquake In the days of Uzziah king of Judah. Thus the LORD my God will come, And all the saints with You.
38_14_6: It shall come to pass in that day That there will be no light; The lights will diminish.
38_14_7: It shall be one day Which is known to the LORD— Neither day nor night. But at evening time it shall happen That it will be light.
38_14_8: And in that day it shall be That living waters shall flow from Jerusalem, Half of them toward the eastern sea And half of them toward the western sea; In both summer and winter it shall occur.
38_14_9: And the LORD shall be King over all the earth. In that day it shall be— “The LORD is one,” And His name one.
38_14_10: All the land shall be turned into a plain from Geba to Rimmon south of Jerusalem. Jerusalem shall be raised up and inhabited in her place from Benjamin’s Gate to the place of the First Gate and the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel to the king’s winepresses.
38_14_11: The people shall dwell in it; And no longer shall there be utter destruction, But Jerusalem shall be safely inhabited.
38_14_12: And this shall be the plague with which the LORD will strike all the people who fought against Jerusalem: Their flesh shall dissolve while they stand on their feet, Their eyes shall dissolve in their sockets, And their tongues shall dissolve in their mouths.
38_14_13: It shall come to pass in that day That a great panic from the LORD will be among them. Everyone will seize the hand of his neighbor, And raise his hand against his neighbor’s hand
38_14_14: Judah also will fight at Jerusalem. And the wealth of all the surrounding nations Shall be gathered together: Gold, silver, and apparel in great abundance.
38_14_15: Such also shall be the plague On the horse and the mule, On the camel and the donkey, And on all the cattle that will be in those camps. So shall this plague be.
38_14_16: And it shall come to pass that everyone who is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall go up from year to year to worship the King, the LORD of hosts, and to keep the Feast of Tabernacles.
38_14_17: And it shall be that whichever of the families of the earth do not come up to Jerusalem to worship the King, the LORD of hosts, on them there will be no rain.
38_14_18: If the family of Egypt will not come up and enter in, they shall have no rain; they shall receive the plague with which the LORD strikes the nations who do not come up to keep the Feast of Tabernacles.
38_14_19: This shall be the punishment of Egypt and the punishment of all the nations that do not come up to keep the Feast of Tabernacles.
38_14_20: In that day “HOLINESS TO THE LORD” shall be engraved on the bells of the horses. The pots in the LORD’s house shall be like the bowls before the altar.
38_14_21: Yes, every pot in Jerusalem and Judah shall be holiness to the LORD of hosts. Everyone who sacrifices shall come and take them and cook in them. In that day there shall no longer be a Canaanite in the house of the LORD of hosts.
39_1_1: The burden of the word of the LORD to Israel by Malachi.
39_1_2: “I have loved you,” says the LORD. “Yet you say, ‘In what way have You loved us?’ Was not Esau Jacob’s brother?” Says the LORD. “Yet Jacob I have loved
39_1_3: But Esau I have hated, And laid waste his mountains and his heritage For the jackals of the wilderness.”
39_1_4: Even though Edom has said, “We have been impoverished, But we will return and build the desolate places,” Thus says the LORD of hosts: “They may build, but I will throw down; They shall be called the Territory of Wickedness, And the people against whom the LORD will have indignation forever.
39_1_5: Your eyes shall see, And you shall say, ‘The LORD is magnified beyond the border of Israel.’
39_1_6: “A son honors his father, And a servant his master. If then I am the Father, Where is My honor? And if I am a Master, Where is My reverence? Says the LORD of hosts To you priests who despise My name. Yet you say, ‘In what way have we despised Your name?’
39_1_7: “You offer defiled food on My altar, But say, ‘In what way have we defiled You?’ By saying, ‘The table of the LORD is contemptible.’
39_1_8: And when you offer the blind as a sacrifice, Is it not evil? And when you offer the lame and sick, Is it not evil? Offer it then to your governor! Would he be pleased with you? Would he accept you favorably?” Says the LORD of hosts.
39_1_9: “But now entreat God’s favor, That He may be gracious to us. While this is being done by your hands, Will He accept you favorably?” Says the LORD of hosts.
39_1_10: “Who is there even among you who would shut the doors, So that you would not kindle fire on My altar in vain? I have no pleasure in you,” Says the LORD of hosts, “Nor will I accept an offering from your hands.
39_1_11: For from the rising of the sun, even to its going down, My name shall be great among the Gentiles; In every place incense shall be offered to My name, And a pure offering; For My name shall be great among the nations,” Says the LORD of hosts.
39_1_12: “But you profane it, In that you say, ‘The table of the LORD is defiled; And its fruit, its food, is contemptible.’
39_1_13: You also say, ‘Oh, what a weariness!’ And you sneer at it,” Says the LORD of hosts. “And you bring the stolen, the lame, and the sick; Thus you bring an offering! Should I accept this from your hand?” Says the LORD.
39_1_14: “But cursed be the deceiver Who has in his flock a male, And takes a vow, But sacrifices to the Lord what is blemished— For I am a great King,” Says the LORD of hosts, “And My name is to be feared among the nations.
39_2_1: “And now, O priests, this commandment is for you.
39_2_2: If you will not hear, And if you will not take it to heart, To give glory to My name,” Says the LORD of hosts, “I will send a curse upon you, And I will curse your blessings. Yes, I have cursed them already, Because you do not take it to heart.
39_2_3: “Behold, I will rebuke your descendants And spread refuse on your faces, The refuse of your solemn feasts; And one will take you away with it.
39_2_4: Then you shall know that I have sent this commandment to you, That My covenant with Levi may continue,” Says the LORD of hosts.
39_2_5: “My covenant was with him, one of life and peace, And I gave them to him that he might fear Me ; So he feared Me And was reverent before My name.
39_2_6: The law of truth was in his mouth, And injustice was not found on his lips. He walked with Me in peace and equity, And turned many away from iniquity.
39_2_7: “For the lips of a priest should keep knowledge, And people should seek the law from his mouth; For he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts.
39_2_8: But you have departed from the way; You have caused many to stumble at the law. You have corrupted the covenant of Levi,” Says the LORD of hosts.
39_2_9: “Therefore I also have made you contemptible and base Before all the people, Because you have not kept My ways But have shown partiality in the law.”
39_2_10: Have we not all one Father? Has not one God created us? Why do we deal treacherously with one another By profaning the covenant of the fathers?
39_2_11: Judah has dealt treacherously, And an abomination has been committed in Israel and in Jerusalem, For Judah has profaned The LORD’s holy institution which He loves: He has married the daughter of a foreign god.
39_2_12: May the LORD cut off from the tents of Jacob The man who does this, being awake and aware, Yet who brings an offering to the LORD of hosts!
39_2_13: And this is the second thing you do: You cover the altar of the LORD with tears, With weeping and crying; So He does not regard the offering anymore, Nor receive it with goodwill from your hands.
39_2_14: Yet you say, “For what reason?” Because the LORD has been witness Between you and the wife of your youth, With whom you have dealt treacherously; Yet she is your companion And your wife by covenant.
39_2_15: But did He not make them one, Having a remnant of the Spirit? And why one? He seeks godly offspring. Therefore take heed to your spirit, And let none deal treacherously with the wife of his youth.
39_2_16: “For the LORD God of Israel says That He hates divorce, For it covers one’s garment with violence,” Says the LORD of hosts. “Therefore take heed to your spirit, That you do not deal treacherously.”
39_2_17: You have wearied the LORD with your words; Yet you say, “In what way have we wearied Him? ” In that you say, “Everyone who does evil Is good in the sight of the LORD, And He delights in them,” Or, “Where is the God of justice?”
39_3_1: “Behold, I send My messenger, And he will prepare the way before Me. And the Lord, whom you seek, Will suddenly come to His temple, Even the Messenger of the covenant, In whom you delight. Behold, He is coming,” Says the LORD of hosts.
39_3_2: “But who can endure the day of His coming? And who can stand when He appears? For He is like a refiner’s fire And like launderers’ soap.
39_3_3: He will sit as a refiner and a purifier of silver; He will purify the sons of Levi, And purge them as gold and silver, That they may offer to the LORD An offering in righteousness.
39_3_4: “Then the offering of Judah and Jerusalem Will be pleasant to the LORD, As in the days of old, As in former years.
39_3_5: And I will come near you for judgment; I will be a swift witness Against sorcerers, Against adulterers, Against perjurers, Against those who exploit wage earners and widows and orphans, And against those who turn away an alien— Because they do not fear Me,” Says the LORD of hosts.
39_3_6: “For I am the LORD, I do not change; Therefore you are not consumed, O sons of Jacob.
39_3_7: Yet from the days of your fathers You have gone away from My ordinances And have not kept them . Return to Me, and I will return to you,” Says the LORD of hosts. “But you said, ‘In what way shall we return?’
39_3_8: “Will a man rob God? Yet you have robbed Me! But you say, ‘In what way have we robbed You?’ In tithes and offerings.
39_3_9: You are cursed with a curse, For you have robbed Me, Even this whole nation.
39_3_10: Bring all the tithes into the storehouse, That there may be food in My house, And try Me now in this,” Says the LORD of hosts, “If I will not open for you the windows of heaven And pour out for you such blessing That there will not be room enough to receive it.
39_3_11: “And I will rebuke the devourer for your sakes, So that he will not destroy the fruit of your ground, Nor shall the vine fail to bear fruit for you in the field,” Says the LORD of hosts
39_3_12: “And all nations will call you blessed, For you will be a delightful land,” Says the LORD of hosts.
39_3_13: “Your words have been harsh against Me,” Says the LORD, “Yet you say, ‘What have we spoken against You?’
39_3_14: You have said, ‘It is useless to serve God; What profit is it that we have kept His ordinance, And that we have walked as mourners Before the LORD of hosts?
39_3_15: So now we call the proud blessed, For those who do wickedness are raised up; They even tempt God and go free.’ ”
39_3_16: Then those who feared the LORD spoke to one another, And the LORD listened and heard them; So a book of remembrance was written before Him For those who fear the LORD And who meditate on His name.
39_3_17: “They shall be Mine,” says the LORD of hosts, “On the day that I make them My jewels. And I will spare them As a man spares his own son who serves him.”
39_3_18: Then you shall again discern Between the righteous and the wicked, Between one who serves God And one who does not serve Him.
39_4_1: “For behold, the day is coming, Burning like an oven, And all the proud, yes, all who do wickedly will be stubble. And the day which is coming shall burn them up,” Says the LORD of hosts, “That will leave them neither root nor branch.
39_4_2: But to you who fear My name The Sun of Righteousness shall arise With healing in His wings; And you shall go out And grow fat like stall-fed calves.
39_4_3: You shall trample the wicked, For they shall be ashes under the soles of your feet On the day that I do this, ” Says the LORD of hosts.
39_4_4: “Remember the Law of Moses, My servant, Which I commanded him in Horeb for all Israel, With the statutes and judgments.
39_4_5: Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet Before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the LORD.
39_4_6: And he will turn The hearts of the fathers to the children, And the hearts of the children to their fathers, Lest I come and strike the earth with a curse.”
1_21_1: And the LORD visited Sarah as He had said, and the LORD did for Sarah as He had spoken.
1_21_2: For Sarah conceived and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of which God had spoken to him.
1_21_3: And Abraham called the name of his son who was born to him—whom Sarah bore to him— Isaac.
1_21_4: Then Abraham circumcised his son Isaac when he was eight days old, as God had commanded him.
1_21_5: Now Abraham was one hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.
1_21_6: And Sarah said, “God has made me laugh, and all who hear will laugh with me.”
1_21_7: She also said, “Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? For I have borne him a son in his old age.”
1_21_8: So the child grew and was weaned. And Abraham made a great feast on the same day that Isaac was weaned.
1_21_9: And Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, scoffing.
1_21_10: Therefore she said to Abraham, “Cast out this bondwoman and her son; for the son of this bondwoman shall not be heir with my son, namely with Isaac.”
1_21_11: And the matter was very displeasing in Abraham’s sight because of his son.
1_21_12: But God said to Abraham, “Do not let it be displeasing in your sight because of the lad or because of your bondwoman. Whatever Sarah has said to you, listen to her voice; for in Isaac your seed shall be called.
1_21_13: Yet I will also make a nation of the son of the bondwoman, because he is your seed.”
1_21_14: So Abraham rose early in the morning, and took bread and a skin of water; and putting it on her shoulder, he gave it and the boy to Hagar, and sent her away. Then she departed and wandered in the Wilderness of Beersheba.
1_21_15: And the water in the skin was used up, and she placed the boy under one of the shrubs.
1_21_16: Then she went and sat down across from him at a distance of about a bowshot; for she said to herself, “Let me not see the death of the boy.” So she sat opposite him, and lifted her voice and wept.
1_21_17: And God heard the voice of the lad. Then the angel of God called to Hagar out of heaven, and said to her, “What ails you, Hagar? Fear not, for God has heard the voice of the lad where he is.
1_21_18: Arise, lift up the lad and hold him with your hand, for I will make him a great nation.”
1_21_19: Then God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. And she went and filled the skin with water, and gave the lad a drink.
1_21_20: So God was with the lad; and he grew and dwelt in the wilderness, and became an archer.
1_21_21: He dwelt in the Wilderness of Paran; and his mother took a wife for him from the land of Egypt.
1_23_1: Sarah lived one hundred and twenty-seven years; these were the years of the life of Sarah.
1_23_2: So Sarah died in Kirjath Arba (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan, and Abraham came to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her.
1_23_3: Then Abraham stood up from before his dead, and spoke to the sons of Heth, saying
1_23_4: “I am a foreigner and a visitor among you. Give me property for a burial place among you, that I may bury my dead out of my sight.”
1_23_5: And the sons of Heth answered Abraham, saying to him
1_23_6: “Hear us, my lord: You are a mighty prince among us; bury your dead in the choicest of our burial places. None of us will withhold from you his burial place, that you may bury your dead.”
1_23_7: Then Abraham stood up and bowed himself to the people of the land, the sons of Heth.
1_23_8: And he spoke with them, saying, “If it is your wish that I bury my dead out of my sight, hear me, and meet with Ephron the son of Zohar for me
1_23_9: that he may give me the cave of Machpelah which he has, which is at the end of his field. Let him give it to me at the full price, as property for a burial place among you.”
1_23_10: Now Ephron dwelt among the sons of Heth; and Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham in the presence of the sons of Heth, all who entered at the gate of his city, saying
1_23_11: “No, my lord, hear me: I give you the field and the cave that is in it; I give it to you in the presence of the sons of my people. I give it to you. Bury your dead!”
1_23_12: Then Abraham bowed himself down before the people of the land
1_23_13: and he spoke to Ephron in the hearing of the people of the land, saying, “If you will give it, please hear me. I will give you money for the field; take it from me and I will bury my dead there.”
1_23_14: And Ephron answered Abraham, saying to him
1_23_15: “My lord, listen to me; the land is worth four hundred shekels of silver. What is that between you and me? So bury your dead.”
1_23_16: And Abraham listened to Ephron; and Abraham weighed out the silver for Ephron which he had named in the hearing of the sons of Heth, four hundred shekels of silver, currency of the merchants.
1_23_17: So the field of Ephron which was in Machpelah, which was before Mamre, the field and the cave which was in it, and all the trees that were in the field, which were within all the surrounding borders, were deeded
1_23_18: to Abraham as a possession in the presence of the sons of Heth, before all who went in at the gate of his city.
1_23_19: And after this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah, before Mamre (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan.
1_23_20: So the field and the cave that is in it were deeded to Abraham by the sons of Heth as property for a burial place.
1_24_1: Now Abraham was old, well advanced in age; and the LORD had blessed Abraham in all things.
1_24_2: So Abraham said to the oldest servant of his house, who ruled over all that he had, “Please, put your hand under my thigh
1_24_3: and I will make you swear by the LORD, the God of heaven and the God of the earth, that you will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell
1_24_4: but you shall go to my country and to my family, and take a wife for my son Isaac.”
1_24_5: And the servant said to him, “Perhaps the woman will not be willing to follow me to this land. Must I take your son back to the land from which you came?”
1_24_6: But Abraham said to him, “Beware that you do not take my son back there.
1_24_7: The LORD God of heaven, who took me from my father’s house and from the land of my family, and who spoke to me and swore to me, saying, ‘To your descendants I give this land,’ He will send His angel before you, and you shall take a wife for my son from there.
1_24_8: And if the woman is not willing to follow you, then you will be released from this oath; only do not take my son back there.”
1_24_9: So the servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master, and swore to him concerning this matter.
1_24_10: Then the servant took ten of his master’s camels and departed, for all his master’s goods were in his hand. And he arose and went to Mesopotamia, to the city of Nahor.
1_24_11: And he made his camels kneel down outside the city by a well of water at evening time, the time when women go out to draw water.
1_24_12: Then he said, “O LORD God of my master Abraham, please give me success this day, and show kindness to my master Abraham.
1_24_13: Behold, here I stand by the well of water, and the daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water.
1_24_14: Now let it be that the young woman to whom I say, ‘Please let down your pitcher that I may drink,’ and she says, ‘Drink, and I will also give your camels a drink’—let her be the one You have appointed for Your servant Isaac. And by this I will know that You have shown kindness to my master.”
1_24_15: And it happened, before he had finished speaking, that behold, Rebekah, who was born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham’s brother, came out with her pitcher on her shoulder.
1_24_16: Now the young woman was very beautiful to behold, a virgin; no man had known her. And she went down to the well, filled her pitcher, and came up.
1_24_17: And the servant ran to meet her and said, “Please let me drink a little water from your pitcher.”
1_24_18: So she said, “Drink, my lord.” Then she quickly let her pitcher down to her hand, and gave him a drink.
1_24_19: And when she had finished giving him a drink, she said, “I will draw water for your camels also, until they have finished drinking.”
1_24_20: Then she quickly emptied her pitcher into the trough, ran back to the well to draw water, and drew for all his camels.
1_24_21: And the man, wondering at her, remained silent so as to know whether the LORD had made his journey prosperous or not.
1_24_22: So it was, when the camels had finished drinking, that the man took a golden nose ring weighing half a shekel, and two bracelets for her wrists weighing ten shekels of gold
1_24_23: and said, “Whose daughter are you? Tell me, please, is there room in your father’s house for us to lodge?”
1_24_24: So she said to him, “I am the daughter of Bethuel, Milcah’s son, whom she bore to Nahor.”
1_24_25: Moreover she said to him, “We have both straw and feed enough, and room to lodge.”
1_24_26: Then the man bowed down his head and worshiped the LORD.
1_24_27: And he said, “Blessed be the LORD God of my master Abraham, who has not forsaken His mercy and His truth toward my master. As for me, being on the way, the LORD led me to the house of my master’s brethren.”
1_24_28: So the young woman ran and told her mother’s household these things.
1_24_29: Now Rebekah had a brother whose name was Laban, and Laban ran out to the man by the well.
1_24_30: So it came to pass, when he saw the nose ring, and the bracelets on his sister’s wrists, and when he heard the words of his sister Rebekah, saying, “Thus the man spoke to me,” that he went to the man. And there he stood by the camels at the well.
1_24_31: And he said, “Come in, O blessed of the LORD! Why do you stand outside? For I have prepared the house, and a place for the camels.”
1_24_32: Then the man came to the house. And he unloaded the camels, and provided straw and feed for the camels, and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men who were with him.
1_24_33: Food was set before him to eat, but he said, “I will not eat until I have told about my errand.” And he said, “Speak on.”
1_24_34: So he said, “I am Abraham’s servant.
1_24_35: The LORD has blessed my master greatly, and he has become great; and He has given him flocks and herds, silver and gold, male and female servants, and camels and donkeys.
1_24_36: And Sarah my master’s wife bore a son to my master when she was old; and to him he has given all that he has.
1_24_37: Now my master made me swear, saying, ‘You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I dwell
1_24_38: but you shall go to my father’s house and to my family, and take a wife for my son.’
1_24_39: And I said to my master, ‘Perhaps the woman will not follow me.’
1_24_40: But he said to me, ‘The LORD, before whom I walk, will send His angel with you and prosper your way; and you shall take a wife for my son from my family and from my father’s house.
1_24_41: You will be clear from this oath when you arrive among my family; for if they will not give her to you, then you will be released from my oath.’
1_24_42: “And this day I came to the well and said, ‘O LORD God of my master Abraham, if You will now prosper the way in which I go
1_24_43: behold, I stand by the well of water; and it shall come to pass that when the virgin comes out to draw water, and I say to her, “Please give me a little water from your pitcher to drink,”
1_24_44: and she says to me, “Drink, and I will draw for your camels also,”—let her be the woman whom the LORD has appointed for my master’s son.’
1_24_45: “But before I had finished speaking in my heart, there was Rebekah, coming out with her pitcher on her shoulder; and she went down to the well and drew water. And I said to her, ‘Please let me drink.’
1_24_46: And she made haste and let her pitcher down from her shoulder, and said, ‘Drink, and I will give your camels a drink also.’ So I drank, and she gave the camels a drink also.
1_24_47: Then I asked her, and said, ‘Whose daughter are you?’ And she said, ‘The daughter of Bethuel, Nahor’s son, whom Milcah bore to him.’ So I put the nose ring on her nose and the bracelets on her wrists.
1_24_48: And I bowed my head and worshiped the LORD, and blessed the LORD God of my master Abraham, who had led me in the way of truth to take the daughter of my master’s brother for his son.
1_24_49: Now if you will deal kindly and truly with my master, tell me. And if not, tell me, that I may turn to the right hand or to the left.”
1_24_50: Then Laban and Bethuel answered and said, “The thing comes from the LORD; we cannot speak to you either bad or good.
1_24_51: Here is Rebekah before you; take her and go, and let her be your master’s son’s wife, as the LORD has spoken.”
1_24_52: And it came to pass, when Abraham’s servant heard their words, that he worshiped the LORD, bowing himself to the earth.
1_24_53: Then the servant brought out jewelry of silver, jewelry of gold, and clothing, and gave them to Rebekah. He also gave precious things to her brother and to her mother.
1_24_54: And he and the men who were with him ate and drank and stayed all night. Then they arose in the morning, and he said, “Send me away to my master.”
1_24_55: But her brother and her mother said, “Let the young woman stay with us a few days, at least ten; after that she may go.”
1_24_56: And he said to them, “Do not hinder me, since the LORD has prospered my way; send me away so that I may go to my master.”
1_24_57: So they said, “We will call the young woman and ask her personally.”
1_24_58: Then they called Rebekah and said to her, “Will you go with this man?” And she said, “I will go.”
1_24_59: So they sent away Rebekah their sister and her nurse, and Abraham’s servant and his men.
1_24_60: And they blessed Rebekah and said to her: “Our sister, may you become The mother of thousands of ten thousands; And may your descendants possess The gates of those who hate them.”
1_24_61: Then Rebekah and her maids arose, and they rode on the camels and followed the man. So the servant took Rebekah and departed.
1_24_62: Now Isaac came from the way of Beer Lahai Roi, for he dwelt in the South.
1_24_63: And Isaac went out to meditate in the field in the evening; and he lifted his eyes and looked, and there, the camels were coming.
1_24_64: Then Rebekah lifted her eyes, and when she saw Isaac she dismounted from her camel
1_24_65: for she had said to the servant, “Who is this man walking in the field to meet us?” The servant said, “It is my master.” So she took a veil and covered herself.
1_24_66: And the servant told Isaac all the things that he had done.
1_24_67: Then Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah’s tent; and he took Rebekah and she became his wife, and he loved her. So Isaac was comforted after his mother’s death.
1_32_1: So Jacob went on his way, and the angels of God met him.
1_32_2: When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is God’s camp.” And he called the name of that place Mahanaim.
1_32_3: Then Jacob sent messengers before him to Esau his brother in the land of Seir, the country of Edom.
1_32_4: And he commanded them, saying, “Speak thus to my lord Esau, ‘Thus your servant Jacob says: “I have dwelt with Laban and stayed there until now.
1_32_5: I have oxen, donkeys, flocks, and male and female servants; and I have sent to tell my lord, that I may find favor in your sight.” ’ ”
1_32_6: Then the messengers returned to Jacob, saying, “We came to your brother Esau, and he also is coming to meet you, and four hundred men are with him.”
1_32_7: So Jacob was greatly afraid and distressed; and he divided the people that were with him, and the flocks and herds and camels, into two companies.
1_32_8: And he said, “If Esau comes to the one company and attacks it, then the other company which is left will escape.”
1_32_9: Then Jacob said, “O God of my father Abraham and God of my father Isaac, the LORD who said to me, ‘Return to your country and to your family, and I will deal well with you’:
1_32_10: I am not worthy of the least of all the mercies and of all the truth which You have shown Your servant; for I crossed over this Jordan with my staff, and now I have become two companies.
1_32_11: Deliver me, I pray, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau; for I fear him, lest he come and attack me and the mother with the children.
1_32_12: For You said, ‘I will surely treat you well, and make your descendants as the sand of the sea, which cannot be numbered for multitude.’ ”
1_32_13: So he lodged there that same night, and took what came to his hand as a present for Esau his brother:
1_32_14: two hundred female goats and twenty male goats, two hundred ewes and twenty rams
1_32_15: thirty milk camels with their colts, forty cows and ten bulls, twenty female donkeys and ten foals.
1_32_16: Then he delivered them to the hand of his servants, every drove by itself, and said to his servants, “Pass over before me, and put some distance between successive droves.”
1_32_17: And he commanded the first one, saying, “When Esau my brother meets you and asks you, saying, ‘To whom do you belong, and where are you going? Whose are these in front of you?’
1_32_18: then you shall say, ‘They are your servant Jacob’s. It is a present sent to my lord Esau; and behold, he also is behind us.’ ”
1_32_19: So he commanded the second, the third, and all who followed the droves, saying, “In this manner you shall speak to Esau when you find him
1_32_20: and also say, ‘Behold, your servant Jacob is behind us.’ ” For he said, “I will appease him with the present that goes before me, and afterward I will see his face; perhaps he will accept me.”
1_32_21: So the present went on over before him, but he himself lodged that night in the camp.
1_32_22: And he arose that night and took his two wives, his two female servants, and his eleven sons, and crossed over the ford of Jabbok.
1_32_23: He took them, sent them over the brook, and sent over what he had.
1_32_24: Then Jacob was left alone; and a Man wrestled with him until the breaking of day.
1_32_25: Now when He saw that He did not prevail against him, He touched the socket of his hip; and the socket of Jacob’s hip was out of joint as He wrestled with him.
1_32_26: And He said, “Let Me go, for the day breaks.” But he said, “I will not let You go unless You bless me!”
1_32_27: So He said to him, “What is your name?” He said, “Jacob.”
1_32_28: And He said, “Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel; for you have struggled with God and with men, and have prevailed.”
1_32_29: Then Jacob asked, saying, “Tell me Your name, I pray.” And He said, “Why is it that you ask about My name?” And He blessed him there.
1_32_30: So Jacob called the name of the place Peniel: “For I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved.”
1_32_31: Just as he crossed over Penuel the sun rose on him, and he limped on his hip.
1_32_32: Therefore to this day the children of Israel do not eat the muscle that shrank, which is on the hip socket, because He touched the socket of Jacob’s hip in the muscle that shrank.
1_34_1: Now Dinah the daughter of Leah, whom she had borne to Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.
1_34_2: And when Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of the country, saw her, he took her and lay with her, and violated her.
1_34_3: His soul was strongly attracted to Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the young woman and spoke kindly to the young woman.
1_34_4: So Shechem spoke to his father Hamor, saying, “Get me this young woman as a wife.”
1_34_5: And Jacob heard that he had defiled Dinah his daughter. Now his sons were with his livestock in the field; so Jacob held his peace until they came.
1_34_6: Then Hamor the father of Shechem went out to Jacob to speak with him.
1_34_7: And the sons of Jacob came in from the field when they heard it; and the men were grieved and very angry, because he had done a disgraceful thing in Israel by lying with Jacob’s daughter, a thing which ought not to be done.
1_34_8: But Hamor spoke with them, saying, “The soul of my son Shechem longs for your daughter. Please give her to him as a wife.
1_34_9: And make marriages with us; give your daughters to us, and take our daughters to yourselves.
1_34_10: So you shall dwell with us, and the land shall be before you. Dwell and trade in it, and acquire possessions for yourselves in it.”
1_34_11: Then Shechem said to her father and her brothers, “Let me find favor in your eyes, and whatever you say to me I will give.
1_34_12: Ask me ever so much dowry and gift, and I will give according to what you say to me; but give me the young woman as a wife.”
1_34_13: But the sons of Jacob answered Shechem and Hamor his father, and spoke deceitfully, because he had defiled Dinah their sister.
1_34_14: And they said to them, “We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to one who is uncircumcised, for that would be a reproach to us.
1_34_15: But on this condition we will consent to you: If you will become as we are, if every male of you is circumcised
1_34_16: then we will give our daughters to you, and we will take your daughters to us; and we will dwell with you, and we will become one people.
1_34_17: But if you will not heed us and be circumcised, then we will take our daughter and be gone.”
1_34_18: And their words pleased Hamor and Shechem, Hamor’s son.
1_34_19: So the young man did not delay to do the thing, because he delighted in Jacob’s daughter. He was more honorable than all the household of his father.
1_34_20: And Hamor and Shechem his son came to the gate of their city, and spoke with the men of their city, saying:
1_34_21: “These men are at peace with us. Therefore let them dwell in the land and trade in it. For indeed the land is large enough for them. Let us take their daughters to us as wives, and let us give them our daughters.
1_34_22: Only on this condition will the men consent to dwell with us, to be one people: if every male among us is circumcised as they are circumcised.
1_34_23: Will not their livestock, their property, and every animal of theirs be ours? Only let us consent to them, and they will dwell with us.”
1_34_24: And all who went out of the gate of his city heeded Hamor and Shechem his son; every male was circumcised, all who went out of the gate of his city.
1_34_25: Now it came to pass on the third day, when they were in pain, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brothers, each took his sword and came boldly upon the city and killed all the males.
1_34_26: And they killed Hamor and Shechem his son with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah from Shechem’s house, and went out.
1_34_27: The sons of Jacob came upon the slain, and plundered the city, because their sister had been defiled.
1_34_28: They took their sheep, their oxen, and their donkeys, what was in the city and what was in the field
1_34_29: and all their wealth. All their little ones and their wives they took captive; and they plundered even all that was in the houses.
1_34_30: Then Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “You have troubled me by making me obnoxious among the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanites and the Perizzites; and since I am few in number, they will gather themselves together against me and kill me. I shall be destroyed, my household and I.”
1_34_31: But they said, “Should he treat our sister like a harlot?”
1_41_1: Then it came to pass, at the end of two full years, that Pharaoh had a dream; and behold, he stood by the river.
1_41_2: Suddenly there came up out of the river seven cows, fine looking and fat; and they fed in the meadow.
1_41_3: Then behold, seven other cows came up after them out of the river, ugly and gaunt, and stood by the other cows on the bank of the river.
1_41_4: And the ugly and gaunt cows ate up the seven fine looking and fat cows. So Pharaoh awoke.
1_41_5: He slept and dreamed a second time; and suddenly seven heads of grain came up on one stalk, plump and good.
1_41_6: Then behold, seven thin heads, blighted by the east wind, sprang up after them.
1_41_7: And the seven thin heads devoured the seven plump and full heads. So Pharaoh awoke, and indeed, it was a dream.
1_41_8: Now it came to pass in the morning that his spirit was troubled, and he sent and called for all the magicians of Egypt and all its wise men. And Pharaoh told them his dreams, but there was no one who could interpret them for Pharaoh.
1_41_9: Then the chief butler spoke to Pharaoh, saying: “I remember my faults this day.
1_41_10: When Pharaoh was angry with his servants, and put me in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, both me and the chief baker
1_41_11: we each had a dream in one night, he and I. Each of us dreamed according to the interpretation of his own dream.
1_41_12: Now there was a young Hebrew man with us there, a servant of the captain of the guard. And we told him, and he interpreted our dreams for us; to each man he interpreted according to his own dream.
1_41_13: And it came to pass, just as he interpreted for us, so it happened. He restored me to my office, and he hanged him.”
1_41_14: Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him quickly out of the dungeon; and he shaved, changed his clothing, and came to Pharaoh.
1_41_15: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I have had a dream, and there is no one who can interpret it. But I have heard it said of you that you can understand a dream, to interpret it.”
1_41_16: So Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, “It is not in me; God will give Pharaoh an answer of peace.”
1_41_17: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph: “Behold, in my dream I stood on the bank of the river.
1_41_18: Suddenly seven cows came up out of the river, fine looking and fat; and they fed in the meadow.
1_41_19: Then behold, seven other cows came up after them, poor and very ugly and gaunt, such ugliness as I have never seen in all the land of Egypt.
1_41_20: And the gaunt and ugly cows ate up the first seven, the fat cows.
1_41_21: When they had eaten them up, no one would have known that they had eaten them, for they were just as ugly as at the beginning. So I awoke.
1_41_22: Also I saw in my dream, and suddenly seven heads came up on one stalk, full and good.
1_41_23: Then behold, seven heads, withered, thin, and blighted by the east wind, sprang up after them.
1_41_24: And the thin heads devoured the seven good heads. So I told this to the magicians, but there was no one who could explain it to me.”
1_41_25: Then Joseph said to Pharaoh, “The dreams of Pharaoh are one; God has shown Pharaoh what He is about to do:
1_41_26: The seven good cows are seven years, and the seven good heads are seven years; the dreams are one.
1_41_27: And the seven thin and ugly cows which came up after them are seven years, and the seven empty heads blighted by the east wind are seven years of famine.
1_41_28: This is the thing which I have spoken to Pharaoh. God has shown Pharaoh what He is about to do.
1_41_29: Indeed seven years of great plenty will come throughout all the land of Egypt
1_41_30: but after them seven years of famine will arise, and all the plenty will be forgotten in the land of Egypt; and the famine will deplete the land.
1_41_31: So the plenty will not be known in the land because of the famine following, for it will be very severe.
1_41_32: And the dream was repeated to Pharaoh twice because the thing is established by God, and God will shortly bring it to pass.
1_41_33: “Now therefore, let Pharaoh select a discerning and wise man, and set him over the land of Egypt.
1_41_34: Let Pharaoh do this, and let him appoint officers over the land, to collect one-fifth of the produce of the land of Egypt in the seven plentiful years.
1_41_35: And let them gather all the food of those good years that are coming, and store up grain under the authority of Pharaoh, and let them keep food in the cities.
1_41_36: Then that food shall be as a reserve for the land for the seven years of famine which shall be in the land of Egypt, that the land may not perish during the famine.”
1_41_37: So the advice was good in the eyes of Pharaoh and in the eyes of all his servants.
1_41_38: And Pharaoh said to his servants, “Can we find such a one as this, a man in whom is the Spirit of God?”
1_41_39: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Inasmuch as God has shown you all this, there is no one as discerning and wise as you.
1_41_40: You shall be over my house, and all my people shall be ruled according to your word; only in regard to the throne will I be greater than you.”
1_41_41: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “See, I have set you over all the land of Egypt.”
1_41_42: Then Pharaoh took his signet ring off his hand and put it on Joseph’s hand; and he clothed him in garments of fine linen and put a gold chain around his neck.
1_41_43: And he had him ride in the second chariot which he had; and they cried out before him, “Bow the knee!” So he set him over all the land of Egypt.
1_41_44: Pharaoh also said to Joseph, “I am Pharaoh, and without your consent no man may lift his hand or foot in all the land of Egypt.”
1_41_45: And Pharaoh called Joseph’s name Zaphnath-Paaneah. And he gave him as a wife Asenath, the daughter of Poti-Pherah priest of On. So Joseph went out over all the land of Egypt.
1_41_46: Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from the presence of Pharaoh, and went throughout all the land of Egypt.
1_41_47: Now in the seven plentiful years the ground brought forth abundantly.
1_41_48: So he gathered up all the food of the seven years which were in the land of Egypt, and laid up the food in the cities; he laid up in every city the food of the fields which surrounded them.
1_41_49: Joseph gathered very much grain, as the sand of the sea, until he stopped counting, for it was immeasurable.
1_41_50: And to Joseph were born two sons before the years of famine came, whom Asenath, the daughter of Poti-Pherah priest of On, bore to him.
1_41_51: Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh: “For God has made me forget all my toil and all my father’s house.”
1_41_52: And the name of the second he called Ephraim: “For God has caused me to be fruitful in the land of my affliction.”
1_41_53: Then the seven years of plenty which were in the land of Egypt ended
1_41_54: and the seven years of famine began to come, as Joseph had said. The famine was in all lands, but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.
1_41_55: So when all the land of Egypt was famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread. Then Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians, “Go to Joseph; whatever he says to you, do.”
1_41_56: The famine was over all the face of the earth, and Joseph opened all the storehouses and sold to the Egyptians. And the famine became severe in the land of Egypt.
1_41_57: So all countries came to Joseph in Egypt to buy grain, because the famine was severe in all lands.
1_49_1: And Jacob called his sons and said, “Gather together, that I may tell you what shall befall you in the last days:
1_49_2: “Gather together and hear, you sons of Jacob, And listen to Israel your father.
1_49_3: “Reuben, you are my firstborn, My might and the beginning of my strength, The excellency of dignity and the excellency of power.
1_49_4: Unstable as water, you shall not excel, Because you went up to your father’s bed; Then you defiled it— He went up to my couch.
1_49_5: “Simeon and Levi are brothers; Instruments of cruelty are in their dwelling place.
