3_2_9: Then the priest shall take from the grain offering a memorial portion, and burn it on the altar. It is an offering made by fire, a sweet aroma to the LORD.
3_2_10: And what is left of the grain offering shall be Aaron’s and his sons’. It is most holy of the offerings to the LORD made by fire.
3_2_11: ‘No grain offering which you bring to the LORD shall be made with leaven, for you shall burn no leaven nor any honey in any offering to the LORD made by fire.
3_2_12: As for the offering of the firstfruits, you shall offer them to the LORD, but they shall not be burned on the altar for a sweet aroma.
3_2_13: And every offering of your grain offering you shall season with salt; you shall not allow the salt of the covenant of your God to be lacking from your grain offering. With all your offerings you shall offer salt.
3_2_14: ‘If you offer a grain offering of your firstfruits to the LORD, you shall offer for the grain offering of your firstfruits green heads of grain roasted on the fire, grain beaten from full heads.
3_2_15: And you shall put oil on it, and lay frankincense on it. It is a grain offering.
3_2_16: Then the priest shall burn the memorial portion: part of its beaten grain and part of its oil, with all the frankincense, as an offering made by fire to the LORD.
3_14_1: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying
3_14_2: “This shall be the law of the leper for the day of his cleansing: He shall be brought to the priest.
3_14_3: And the priest shall go out of the camp, and the priest shall examine him; and indeed, if the leprosy is healed in the leper
3_14_4: then the priest shall command to take for him who is to be cleansed two living and clean birds, cedar wood, scarlet, and hyssop.
3_14_5: And the priest shall command that one of the birds be killed in an earthen vessel over running water.
3_14_6: As for the living bird, he shall take it, the cedar wood and the scarlet and the hyssop, and dip them and the living bird in the blood of the bird that was killed over the running water.
3_14_7: And he shall sprinkle it seven times on him who is to be cleansed from the leprosy, and shall pronounce him clean, and shall let the living bird loose in the open field.
3_14_8: He who is to be cleansed shall wash his clothes, shave off all his hair, and wash himself in water, that he may be clean. After that he shall come into the camp, and shall stay outside his tent seven days.
3_14_9: But on the seventh day he shall shave all the hair off his head and his beard and his eyebrows—all his hair he shall shave off. He shall wash his clothes and wash his body in water, and he shall be clean.
3_14_10: “And on the eighth day he shall take two male lambs without blemish, one ewe lamb of the first year without blemish, three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, and one log of oil.
3_14_11: Then the priest who makes him clean shall present the man who is to be made clean, and those things, before the LORD, at the door of the tabernacle of meeting.
3_14_12: And the priest shall take one male lamb and offer it as a trespass offering, and the log of oil, and wave them as a wave offering before the LORD.
3_14_13: Then he shall kill the lamb in the place where he kills the sin offering and the burnt offering, in a holy place; for as the sin offering is the priest’s, so is the trespass offering. It is most holy.
3_14_14: The priest shall take some of the blood of the trespass offering, and the priest shall put it on the tip of the right ear of him who is to be cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
3_14_15: And the priest shall take some of the log of oil, and pour it into the palm of his own left hand.
3_14_16: Then the priest shall dip his right finger in the oil that is in his left hand, and shall sprinkle some of the oil with his finger seven times before the LORD.
3_14_17: And of the rest of the oil in his hand, the priest shall put some on the tip of the right ear of him who is to be cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, on the blood of the trespass offering.
3_14_18: The rest of the oil that is in the priest’s hand he shall put on the head of him who is to be cleansed. So the priest shall make atonement for him before the LORD.
3_14_19: “Then the priest shall offer the sin offering, and make atonement for him who is to be cleansed from his uncleanness. Afterward he shall kill the burnt offering.
3_14_20: And the priest shall offer the burnt offering and the grain offering on the altar. So the priest shall make atonement for him, and he shall be clean.
3_16_1: Now the LORD spoke to Moses after the death of the two sons of Aaron, when they offered profane fire before the LORD, and died
3_16_2: and the LORD said to Moses: “Tell Aaron your brother not to come at just any time into the Holy Place inside the veil, before the mercy seat which is on the ark, lest he die; for I will appear in the cloud above the mercy seat.
3_16_3: “Thus Aaron shall come into the Holy Place: with the blood of a young bull as a sin offering, and of a ram as a burnt offering.
3_16_4: He shall put the holy linen tunic and the linen trousers on his body; he shall be girded with a linen sash, and with the linen turban he shall be attired. These are holy garments. Therefore he shall wash his body in water, and put them on.
3_16_5: And he shall take from the congregation of the children of Israel two kids of the goats as a sin offering, and one ram as a burnt offering.
3_16_6: “Aaron shall offer the bull as a sin offering, which is for himself, and make atonement for himself and for his house.
3_16_7: He shall take the two goats and present them before the LORD at the door of the tabernacle of meeting.
3_16_8: Then Aaron shall cast lots for the two goats: one lot for the LORD and the other lot for the scapegoat.
3_16_9: And Aaron shall bring the goat on which the LORD’s lot fell, and offer it as a sin offering.
3_16_10: But the goat on which the lot fell to be the scapegoat shall be presented alive before the LORD, to make atonement upon it, and to let it go as the scapegoat into the wilderness.
3_16_11: “And Aaron shall bring the bull of the sin offering, which is for himself, and make atonement for himself and for his house, and shall kill the bull as the sin offering which is for himself.
3_16_12: Then he shall take a censer full of burning coals of fire from the altar before the LORD, with his hands full of sweet incense beaten fine, and bring it inside the veil.
3_16_13: And he shall put the incense on the fire before the LORD, that the cloud of incense may cover the mercy seat that is on the Testimony, lest he die.
3_16_14: He shall take some of the blood of the bull and sprinkle it with his finger on the mercy seat on the east side; and before the mercy seat he shall sprinkle some of the blood with his finger seven times.
3_16_15: “Then he shall kill the goat of the sin offering, which is for the people, bring its blood inside the veil, do with that blood as he did with the blood of the bull, and sprinkle it on the mercy seat and before the mercy seat.
3_16_16: So he shall make atonement for the Holy Place, because of the uncleanness of the children of Israel, and because of their transgressions, for all their sins; and so he shall do for the tabernacle of meeting which remains among them in the midst of their uncleanness.
3_16_17: There shall be no man in the tabernacle of meeting when he goes in to make atonement in the Holy Place, until he comes out, that he may make atonement for himself, for his household, and for all the assembly of Israel.
3_16_18: And he shall go out to the altar that is before the LORD, and make atonement for it, and shall take some of the blood of the bull and some of the blood of the goat, and put it on the horns of the altar all around.
3_16_19: Then he shall sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times, cleanse it, and consecrate it from the uncleanness of the children of Israel.
3_16_20: “And when he has made an end of atoning for the Holy Place, the tabernacle of meeting, and the altar, he shall bring the live goat.
3_16_21: Aaron shall lay both his hands on the head of the live goat, confess over it all the iniquities of the children of Israel, and all their transgressions, concerning all their sins, putting them on the head of the goat, and shall send it away into the wilderness by the hand of a suitable man.
3_16_22: The goat shall bear on itself all their iniquities to an uninhabited land; and he shall release the goat in the wilderness.
3_16_23: “Then Aaron shall come into the tabernacle of meeting, shall take off the linen garments which he put on when he went into the Holy Place, and shall leave them there.
3_16_24: And he shall wash his body with water in a holy place, put on his garments, come out and offer his burnt offering and the burnt offering of the people, and make atonement for himself and for the people.
3_16_25: The fat of the sin offering he shall burn on the altar.
3_16_26: And he who released the goat as the scapegoat shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and afterward he may come into the camp.
3_16_27: The bull for the sin offering and the goat for the sin offering, whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the Holy Place, shall be carried outside the camp. And they shall burn in the fire their skins, their flesh, and their offal.
3_16_28: Then he who burns them shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and afterward he may come into the camp.
3_16_29: “This shall be a statute forever for you: In the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, you shall afflict your souls, and do no work at all, whether a native of your own country or a stranger who dwells among you.
3_16_30: For on that day the priest shall make atonement for you, to cleanse you, that you may be clean from all your sins before the LORD.
3_16_31: It is a sabbath of solemn rest for you, and you shall afflict your souls. It is a statute forever.
3_16_32: And the priest, who is anointed and consecrated to minister as priest in his father’s place, shall make atonement, and put on the linen clothes, the holy garments
3_16_33: then he shall make atonement for the Holy Sanctuary, and he shall make atonement for the tabernacle of meeting and for the altar, and he shall make atonement for the priests and for all the people of the assembly.
3_16_34: This shall be an everlasting statute for you, to make atonement for the children of Israel, for all their sins, once a year.” And he did as the LORD commanded Moses.
3_19_1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying
3_19_2: “Speak to all the congregation of the children of Israel, and say to them: ‘You shall be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy.
3_19_3: ‘Every one of you shall revere his mother and his father, and keep My Sabbaths: I am the LORD your God.
3_19_4: ‘Do not turn to idols, nor make for yourselves molded gods: I am the LORD your God.
3_19_5: ‘And if you offer a sacrifice of a peace offering to the LORD, you shall offer it of your own free will.
3_19_6: It shall be eaten the same day you offer it, and on the next day. And if any remains until the third day, it shall be burned in the fire.
3_19_7: And if it is eaten at all on the third day, it is an abomination. It shall not be accepted.
3_19_8: Therefore everyone who eats it shall bear his iniquity, because he has profaned the hallowed offering of the LORD; and that person shall be cut off from his people.
3_19_9: ‘When you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not wholly reap the corners of your field, nor shall you gather the gleanings of your harvest.
3_19_10: And you shall not glean your vineyard, nor shall you gather every grape of your vineyard; you shall leave them for the poor and the stranger: I am the LORD your God.
3_19_11: ‘You shall not steal, nor deal falsely, nor lie to one another.
3_19_12: And you shall not swear by My name falsely, nor shall you profane the name of your God: I am the LORD.
3_19_13: ‘You shall not cheat your neighbor, nor rob him. The wages of him who is hired shall not remain with you all night until morning.
3_19_14: You shall not curse the deaf, nor put a stumbling block before the blind, but shall fear your God: I am the LORD.
3_19_15: ‘You shall do no injustice in judgment. You shall not be partial to the poor, nor honor the person of the mighty. In righteousness you shall judge your neighbor.
3_19_16: You shall not go about as a talebearer among your people; nor shall you take a stand against the life of your neighbor: I am the LORD.
3_19_17: ‘You shall not hate your brother in your heart. You shall surely rebuke your neighbor, and not bear sin because of him.
3_19_18: You shall not take vengeance, nor bear any grudge against the children of your people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself: I am the LORD.
3_19_19: ‘You shall keep My statutes. You shall not let your livestock breed with another kind. You shall not sow your field with mixed seed. Nor shall a garment of mixed linen and wool come upon you.
3_19_20: ‘Whoever lies carnally with a woman who is betrothed to a man as a concubine, and who has not at all been redeemed nor given her freedom, for this there shall be scourging; but they shall not be put to death, because she was not free.
3_19_21: And he shall bring his trespass offering to the LORD, to the door of the tabernacle of meeting, a ram as a trespass offering.
3_19_22: The priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the trespass offering before the LORD for his sin which he has committed. And the sin which he has committed shall be forgiven him.
3_19_23: ‘When you come into the land, and have planted all kinds of trees for food, then you shall count their fruit as uncircumcised. Three years it shall be as uncircumcised to you. It shall not be eaten.
3_19_24: But in the fourth year all its fruit shall be holy, a praise to the LORD.
3_19_25: And in the fifth year you may eat its fruit, that it may yield to you its increase: I am the LORD your God.
3_19_26: ‘You shall not eat anything with the blood, nor shall you practice divination or soothsaying.
3_19_27: You shall not shave around the sides of your head, nor shall you disfigure the edges of your beard.
3_19_28: You shall not make any cuttings in your flesh for the dead, nor tattoo any marks on you: I am the LORD.
3_19_29: ‘Do not prostitute your daughter, to cause her to be a harlot, lest the land fall into harlotry, and the land become full of wickedness.
3_19_30: ‘You shall keep My Sabbaths and reverence My sanctuary: I am the LORD.
3_19_31: ‘Give no regard to mediums and familiar spirits; do not seek after them, to be defiled by them: I am the LORD your God.
3_19_32: ‘You shall rise before the gray headed and honor the presence of an old man, and fear your God: I am the LORD.
3_19_33: ‘And if a stranger dwells with you in your land, you shall not mistreat him.
3_19_34: The stranger who dwells among you shall be to you as one born among you, and you shall love him as yourself; for you were strangers in the land of Egypt: I am the LORD your God.
3_19_35: ‘You shall do no injustice in judgment, in measurement of length, weight, or volume.
3_19_36: You shall have honest scales, honest weights, an honest ephah, and an honest hin: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
3_19_37: ‘Therefore you shall observe all My statutes and all My judgments, and perform them: I am the LORD.’ ”
3_20_1: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying
3_20_2: “Again, you shall say to the children of Israel: ‘Whoever of the children of Israel, or of the strangers who dwell in Israel, who gives any of his descendants to Molech, he shall surely be put to death. The people of the land shall stone him with stones.
3_20_3: I will set My face against that man, and will cut him off from his people, because he has given some of his descendants to Molech, to defile My sanctuary and profane My holy name.
3_20_4: And if the people of the land should in any way hide their eyes from the man, when he gives some of his descendants to Molech, and they do not kill him
3_20_5: then I will set My face against that man and against his family; and I will cut him off from his people, and all who prostitute themselves with him to commit harlotry with Molech.
3_20_6: ‘And the person who turns to mediums and familiar spirits, to prostitute himself with them, I will set My face against that person and cut him off from his people.
3_20_7: Consecrate yourselves therefore, and be holy, for I am the LORD your God.
3_20_8: And you shall keep My statutes, and perform them: I am the LORD who sanctifies you.
3_20_9: ‘For everyone who curses his father or his mother shall surely be put to death. He has cursed his father or his mother. His blood shall be upon him.
3_20_10: ‘The man who commits adultery with another man’s wife, he who commits adultery with his neighbor’s wife, the adulterer and the adulteress, shall surely be put to death.
3_20_11: The man who lies with his father’s wife has uncovered his father’s nakedness; both of them shall surely be put to death. Their blood shall be upon them.
3_20_12: If a man lies with his daughter-in-law, both of them shall surely be put to death. They have committed perversion. Their blood shall be upon them.
3_20_13: If a man lies with a male as he lies with a woman, both of them have committed an abomination. They shall surely be put to death. Their blood shall be upon them.
3_20_14: If a man marries a woman and her mother, it is wickedness. They shall be burned with fire, both he and they, that there may be no wickedness among you.
3_20_15: If a man mates with an animal, he shall surely be put to death, and you shall kill the animal.
3_20_16: If a woman approaches any animal and mates with it, you shall kill the woman and the animal. They shall surely be put to death. Their blood is upon them.
3_20_17: ‘If a man takes his sister, his father’s daughter or his mother’s daughter, and sees her nakedness and she sees his nakedness, it is a wicked thing. And they shall be cut off in the sight of their people. He has uncovered his sister’s nakedness. He shall bear his guilt.
3_20_18: If a man lies with a woman during her sickness and uncovers her nakedness, he has exposed her flow, and she has uncovered the flow of her blood. Both of them shall be cut off from their people.
3_20_19: ‘You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother’s sister nor of your father’s sister, for that would uncover his near of kin. They shall bear their guilt.
3_20_20: If a man lies with his uncle’s wife, he has uncovered his uncle’s nakedness. They shall bear their sin; they shall die childless.
3_20_21: If a man takes his brother’s wife, it is an unclean thing. He has uncovered his brother’s nakedness. They shall be childless.
3_20_22: ‘You shall therefore keep all My statutes and all My judgments, and perform them, that the land where I am bringing you to dwell may not vomit you out.
3_20_23: And you shall not walk in the statutes of the nation which I am casting out before you; for they commit all these things, and therefore I abhor them.
3_20_24: But I have said to you, “You shall inherit their land, and I will give it to you to possess, a land flowing with milk and honey.” I am the LORD your God, who has separated you from the peoples.
3_20_25: You shall therefore distinguish between clean animals and unclean, between unclean birds and clean, and you shall not make yourselves abominable by beast or by bird, or by any kind of living thing that creeps on the ground, which I have separated from you as unclean.
3_20_26: And you shall be holy to Me, for I the LORD am holy, and have separated you from the peoples, that you should be Mine.
3_20_27: ‘A man or a woman who is a medium, or who has familiar spirits, shall surely be put to death; they shall stone them with stones. Their blood shall be upon them.’ ”
3_22_1: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying
3_22_2: “Speak to Aaron and his sons, that they separate themselves from the holy things of the children of Israel, and that they do not profane My holy name by what they dedicate to Me: I am the LORD.
3_22_3: Say to them: ‘Whoever of all your descendants throughout your generations, who goes near the holy things which the children of Israel dedicate to the LORD, while he has uncleanness upon him, that person shall be cut off from My presence: I am the LORD.
3_22_4: ‘Whatever man of the descendants of Aaron, who is a leper or has a discharge, shall not eat the holy offerings until he is clean. And whoever touches anything made unclean by a corpse, or a man who has had an emission of semen
3_22_5: or whoever touches any creeping thing by which he would be made unclean, or any person by whom he would become unclean, whatever his uncleanness may be—
3_22_6: the person who has touched any such thing shall be unclean until evening, and shall not eat the holy offerings unless he washes his body with water.
3_22_7: And when the sun goes down he shall be clean; and afterward he may eat the holy offerings, because it is his food.
3_22_8: Whatever dies naturally or is torn by beasts he shall not eat, to defile himself with it: I am the LORD.
3_22_9: ‘They shall therefore keep My ordinance, lest they bear sin for it and die thereby, if they profane it: I the LORD sanctify them.
3_22_10: ‘No outsider shall eat the holy offering; one who dwells with the priest, or a hired servant, shall not eat the holy thing.
3_22_11: But if the priest buys a person with his money, he may eat it; and one who is born in his house may eat his food.
3_22_12: If the priest’s daughter is married to an outsider, she may not eat of the holy offerings.
3_22_13: But if the priest’s daughter is a widow or divorced, and has no child, and has returned to her father’s house as in her youth, she may eat her father’s food; but no outsider shall eat it.
3_22_14: ‘And if a man eats the holy offering unintentionally, then he shall restore a holy offering to the priest, and add one-fifth to it.
3_22_15: They shall not profane the holy offerings of the children of Israel, which they offer to the LORD
3_22_16: or allow them to bear the guilt of trespass when they eat their holy offerings; for I the LORD sanctify them.’ ”
3_22_17: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying
3_22_18: “Speak to Aaron and his sons, and to all the children of Israel, and say to them: ‘Whatever man of the house of Israel, or of the strangers in Israel, who offers his sacrifice for any of his vows or for any of his freewill offerings, which they offer to the LORD as a burnt offering—
3_22_19: you shall offer of your own free will a male without blemish from the cattle, from the sheep, or from the goats.
3_22_20: Whatever has a defect, you shall not offer, for it shall not be acceptable on your behalf.
3_22_21: And whoever offers a sacrifice of a peace offering to the LORD, to fulfill his vow, or a freewill offering from the cattle or the sheep, it must be perfect to be accepted; there shall be no defect in it.
3_22_22: Those that are blind or broken or maimed, or have an ulcer or eczema or scabs, you shall not offer to the LORD, nor make an offering by fire of them on the altar to the LORD.
3_22_23: Either a bull or a lamb that has any limb too long or too short you may offer as a freewill offering, but for a vow it shall not be accepted.
3_22_24: ‘You shall not offer to the LORD what is bruised or crushed, or torn or cut; nor shall you make any offering of them in your land.
3_22_25: Nor from a foreigner’s hand shall you offer any of these as the bread of your God, because their corruption is in them, and defects are in them. They shall not be accepted on your behalf.’ ”
3_22_26: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
3_22_27: “When a bull or a sheep or a goat is born, it shall be seven days with its mother; and from the eighth day and thereafter it shall be accepted as an offering made by fire to the LORD.
3_22_28: Whether it is a cow or ewe, do not kill both her and her young on the same day.
3_22_29: And when you offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving to the LORD, offer it of your own free will.
3_22_30: On the same day it shall be eaten; you shall leave none of it until morning: I am the LORD.
3_22_31: “Therefore you shall keep My commandments, and perform them: I am the LORD.
3_22_32: You shall not profane My holy name, but I will be hallowed among the children of Israel. I am the LORD who sanctifies you
3_22_33: who brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God: I am the LORD.”
3_24_1: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
3_24_2: “Command the children of Israel that they bring to you pure oil of pressed olives for the light, to make the lamps burn continually.
3_24_3: Outside the veil of the Testimony, in the tabernacle of meeting, Aaron shall be in charge of it from evening until morning before the LORD continually; it shall be a statute forever in your generations.
3_24_4: He shall be in charge of the lamps on the pure gold lampstand before the LORD continually.
3_24_5: “And you shall take fine flour and bake twelve cakes with it. Two-tenths of an ephah shall be in each cake.
3_24_6: You shall set them in two rows, six in a row, on the pure gold table before the LORD.
3_24_7: And you shall put pure frankincense on each row, that it may be on the bread for a memorial, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
3_24_8: Every Sabbath he shall set it in order before the LORD continually, being taken from the children of Israel by an everlasting covenant.
3_24_9: And it shall be for Aaron and his sons, and they shall eat it in a holy place; for it is most holy to him from the offerings of the LORD made by fire, by a perpetual statute.”
3_24_10: Now the son of an Israelite woman, whose father was an Egyptian, went out among the children of Israel; and this Israelite woman’s son and a man of Israel fought each other in the camp.
3_24_11: And the Israelite woman’s son blasphemed the name of the LORD and cursed; and so they brought him to Moses. (His mother’s name was Shelomith the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.)
3_24_12: Then they put him in custody, that the mind of the LORD might be shown to them.
3_24_13: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying
3_24_14: “Take outside the camp him who has cursed; then let all who heard him lay their hands on his head, and let all the congregation stone him.
3_24_15: “Then you shall speak to the children of Israel, saying: ‘Whoever curses his God shall bear his sin.
3_24_16: And whoever blasphemes the name of the LORD shall surely be put to death. All the congregation shall certainly stone him, the stranger as well as him who is born in the land. When he blasphemes the name of the LORD, he shall be put to death.
3_24_17: ‘Whoever kills any man shall surely be put to death.
3_24_18: Whoever kills an animal shall make it good, animal for animal.
3_24_19: ‘If a man causes disfigurement of his neighbor, as he has done, so shall it be done to him—
3_24_20: fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth; as he has caused disfigurement of a man, so shall it be done to him.
3_24_21: And whoever kills an animal shall restore it; but whoever kills a man shall be put to death.
3_24_22: You shall have the same law for the stranger and for one from your own country; for I am the LORD your God.’ ”
3_24_23: Then Moses spoke to the children of Israel; and they took outside the camp him who had cursed, and stoned him with stones. So the children of Israel did as the LORD commanded Moses.
4_1_1: Now the LORD spoke to Moses in the Wilderness of Sinai, in the tabernacle of meeting, on the first day of the second month, in the second year after they had come out of the land of Egypt, saying:
4_1_2: “Take a census of all the congregation of the children of Israel, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of names, every male individually
4_1_3: from twenty years old and above—all who are able to go to war in Israel. You and Aaron shall number them by their armies.
4_1_4: And with you there shall be a man from every tribe, each one the head of his father’s house.
4_1_5: “These are the names of the men who shall stand with you: from Reuben, Elizur the son of Shedeur
4_1_6: from Simeon, Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai
4_1_7: from Judah, Nahshon the son of Amminadab
4_1_8: from Issachar, Nethanel the son of Zuar
4_1_9: from Zebulun, Eliab the son of Helon
4_1_10: from the sons of Joseph: from Ephraim, Elishama the son of Ammihud; from Manasseh, Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur
4_1_11: from Benjamin, Abidan the son of Gideoni
4_1_12: from Dan, Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai
4_1_13: from Asher, Pagiel the son of Ocran
4_1_14: from Gad, Eliasaph the son of Deuel
4_1_15: from Naphtali, Ahira the son of Enan.”
4_1_16: These were chosen from the congregation, leaders of their fathers’ tribes, heads of the divisions in Israel.
4_1_17: Then Moses and Aaron took these men who had been mentioned by name
4_1_18: and they assembled all the congregation together on the first day of the second month; and they recited their ancestry by families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, each one individually.
4_1_19: As the LORD commanded Moses, so he numbered them in the Wilderness of Sinai.
4_1_20: Now the children of Reuben, Israel’s oldest son, their genealogies by their families, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, every male individually, from twenty years old and above, all who were able to go to war:
4_1_21: those who were numbered of the tribe of Reuben were forty-six thousand five hundred.
4_1_22: From the children of Simeon, their genealogies by their families, by their fathers’ house, of those who were numbered, according to the number of names, every male individually, from twenty years old and above, all who were able to go to war:
4_1_23: those who were numbered of the tribe of Simeon were fifty-nine thousand three hundred.
4_1_24: From the children of Gad, their genealogies by their families, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, all who were able to go to war:
4_1_25: those who were numbered of the tribe of Gad were forty-five thousand six hundred and fifty.
4_1_26: From the children of Judah, their genealogies by their families, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, all who were able to go to war:
4_1_27: those who were numbered of the tribe of Judah were seventy-four thousand six hundred.
4_1_28: From the children of Issachar, their genealogies by their families, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, all who were able to go to war:
4_1_29: those who were numbered of the tribe of Issachar were fifty-four thousand four hundred.
4_1_30: From the children of Zebulun, their genealogies by their families, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, all who were able to go to war:
4_1_31: those who were numbered of the tribe of Zebulun were fifty-seven thousand four hundred.
4_1_32: From the sons of Joseph, the children of Ephraim, their genealogies by their families, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, all who were able to go to war:
4_1_33: those who were numbered of the tribe of Ephraim were forty thousand five hundred.
4_1_34: From the children of Manasseh, their genealogies by their families, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, all who were able to go to war:
4_1_35: those who were numbered of the tribe of Manasseh were thirty-two thousand two hundred.
4_1_36: From the children of Benjamin, their genealogies by their families, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, all who were able to go to war:
4_1_37: those who were numbered of the tribe of Benjamin were thirty-five thousand four hundred.
4_1_38: From the children of Dan, their genealogies by their families, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, all who were able to go to war:
4_1_39: those who were numbered of the tribe of Dan were sixty-two thousand seven hundred.
4_1_40: From the children of Asher, their genealogies by their families, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, all who were able to go to war:
4_1_41: those who were numbered of the tribe of Asher were forty-one thousand five hundred.
4_1_42: From the children of Naphtali, their genealogies by their families, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, all who were able to go to war:
4_1_43: those who were numbered of the tribe of Naphtali were fifty-three thousand four hundred.
4_1_44: These are the ones who were numbered, whom Moses and Aaron numbered, with the leaders of Israel, twelve men, each one representing his father’s house.
4_1_45: So all who were numbered of the children of Israel, by their fathers’ houses, from twenty years old and above, all who were able to go to war in Israel—
4_1_46: all who were numbered were six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty.
4_1_47: But the Levites were not numbered among them by their fathers’ tribe
4_1_48: for the LORD had spoken to Moses, saying:
4_1_49: “Only the tribe of Levi you shall not number, nor take a census of them among the children of Israel
4_1_50: but you shall appoint the Levites over the tabernacle of the Testimony, over all its furnishings, and over all things that belong to it; they shall carry the tabernacle and all its furnishings; they shall attend to it and camp around the tabernacle.
4_1_51: And when the tabernacle is to go forward, the Levites shall take it down; and when the tabernacle is to be set up, the Levites shall set it up. The outsider who comes near shall be put to death.
4_1_52: The children of Israel shall pitch their tents, everyone by his own camp, everyone by his own standard, according to their armies
4_1_53: but the Levites shall camp around the tabernacle of the Testimony, that there may be no wrath on the congregation of the children of Israel; and the Levites shall keep charge of the tabernacle of the Testimony.”
4_1_54: Thus the children of Israel did; according to all that the LORD commanded Moses, so they did.
4_3_1: Now these are the records of Aaron and Moses when the LORD spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai.
4_3_2: And these are the names of the sons of Aaron: Nadab, the firstborn, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
4_3_3: These are the names of the sons of Aaron, the anointed priests, whom he consecrated to minister as priests.
4_3_4: Nadab and Abihu had died before the LORD when they offered profane fire before the LORD in the Wilderness of Sinai; and they had no children. So Eleazar and Ithamar ministered as priests in the presence of Aaron their father.
4_3_5: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
4_3_6: “Bring the tribe of Levi near, and present them before Aaron the priest, that they may serve him.
4_3_7: And they shall attend to his needs and the needs of the whole congregation before the tabernacle of meeting, to do the work of the tabernacle.
4_3_8: Also they shall attend to all the furnishings of the tabernacle of meeting, and to the needs of the children of Israel, to do the work of the tabernacle.
4_3_9: And you shall give the Levites to Aaron and his sons; they are given entirely to him from among the children of Israel.
4_3_10: So you shall appoint Aaron and his sons, and they shall attend to their priesthood; but the outsider who comes near shall be put to death.”
4_3_11: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
4_3_12: “Now behold, I Myself have taken the Levites from among the children of Israel instead of every firstborn who opens the womb among the children of Israel. Therefore the Levites shall be Mine
4_3_13: because all the firstborn are Mine. On the day that I struck all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, I sanctified to Myself all the firstborn in Israel, both man and beast. They shall be Mine: I am the LORD.”
4_3_14: Then the LORD spoke to Moses in the Wilderness of Sinai, saying:
4_3_15: “Number the children of Levi by their fathers’ houses, by their families; you shall number every male from a month old and above.”
4_3_16: So Moses numbered them according to the word of the LORD, as he was commanded.
4_3_17: These were the sons of Levi by their names: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
4_3_18: And these are the names of the sons of Gershon by their families: Libni and Shimei.
4_3_19: And the sons of Kohath by their families: Amram, Izehar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
4_3_20: And the sons of Merari by their families: Mahli and Mushi. These are the families of the Levites by their fathers’ houses.
4_3_21: From Gershon came the family of the Libnites and the family of the Shimites; these were the families of the Gershonites.
4_3_22: Those who were numbered, according to the number of all the males from a month old and above—of those who were numbered there were seven thousand five hundred.
4_3_23: The families of the Gershonites were to camp behind the tabernacle westward.
4_3_24: And the leader of the father’s house of the Gershonites was Eliasaph the son of Lael.
4_3_25: The duties of the children of Gershon in the tabernacle of meeting included the tabernacle, the tent with its covering, the screen for the door of the tabernacle of meeting
4_3_26: the screen for the door of the court, the hangings of the court which are around the tabernacle and the altar, and their cords, according to all the work relating to them.
4_3_27: From Kohath came the family of the Amramites, the family of the Izharites, the family of the Hebronites, and the family of the Uzzielites; these were the families of the Kohathites.
4_3_28: According to the number of all the males, from a month old and above, there were eight thousand six hundred keeping charge of the sanctuary.
4_3_29: The families of the children of Kohath were to camp on the south side of the tabernacle.
4_3_30: And the leader of the fathers’ house of the families of the Kohathites was Elizaphan the son of Uzziel.
4_3_31: Their duty included the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the utensils of the sanctuary with which they ministered, the screen, and all the work relating to them.
4_3_32: And Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest was to be chief over the leaders of the Levites, with oversight of those who kept charge of the sanctuary.
4_3_33: From Merari came the family of the Mahlites and the family of the Mushites; these were the families of Merari.
4_3_34: And those who were numbered, according to the number of all the males from a month old and above, were six thousand two hundred.
4_3_35: The leader of the fathers’ house of the families of Merari was Zuriel the son of Abihail. These were to camp on the north side of the tabernacle.
4_3_36: And the appointed duty of the children of Merari included the boards of the tabernacle, its bars, its pillars, its sockets, its utensils, all the work relating to them
4_3_37: and the pillars of the court all around, with their sockets, their pegs, and their cords.
4_3_38: Moreover those who were to camp before the tabernacle on the east, before the tabernacle of meeting, were Moses, Aaron, and his sons, keeping charge of the sanctuary, to meet the needs of the children of Israel; but the outsider who came near was to be put to death.
4_3_39: All who were numbered of the Levites, whom Moses and Aaron numbered at the commandment of the LORD, by their families, all the males from a month old and above, were twenty-two thousand.
4_3_40: Then the LORD said to Moses: “Number all the firstborn males of the children of Israel from a month old and above, and take the number of their names.
4_3_41: And you shall take the Levites for Me—I am the LORD—instead of all the firstborn among the children of Israel, and the livestock of the Levites instead of all the firstborn among the livestock of the children of Israel.”
4_3_42: So Moses numbered all the firstborn among the children of Israel, as the LORD commanded him.
4_3_43: And all the firstborn males, according to the number of names from a month old and above, of those who were numbered of them, were twenty-two thousand two hundred and seventy-three.
4_3_44: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
4_3_45: “Take the Levites instead of all the firstborn among the children of Israel, and the livestock of the Levites instead of their livestock. The Levites shall be Mine: I am the LORD.
4_3_46: And for the redemption of the two hundred and seventy-three of the firstborn of the children of Israel, who are more than the number of the Levites
4_3_47: you shall take five shekels for each one individually; you shall take them in the currency of the shekel of the sanctuary, the shekel of twenty gerahs.
4_3_48: And you shall give the money, with which the excess number of them is redeemed, to Aaron and his sons.”
4_3_49: So Moses took the redemption money from those who were over and above those who were redeemed by the Levites.
4_3_50: From the firstborn of the children of Israel he took the money, one thousand three hundred and sixty-five shekels, according to the shekel of the sanctuary.
4_3_51: And Moses gave their redemption money to Aaron and his sons, according to the word of the LORD, as the LORD commanded Moses.
4_5_1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
4_5_2: “Command the children of Israel that they put out of the camp every leper, everyone who has a discharge, and whoever becomes defiled by a corpse.
4_5_3: You shall put out both male and female; you shall put them outside the camp, that they may not defile their camps in the midst of which I dwell.”
4_5_4: And the children of Israel did so, and put them outside the camp; as the LORD spoke to Moses, so the children of Israel did.
4_5_5: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying
4_5_6: “Speak to the children of Israel: ‘When a man or woman commits any sin that men commit in unfaithfulness against the LORD, and that person is guilty
4_5_7: then he shall confess the sin which he has committed. He shall make restitution for his trespass in full, plus one-fifth of it, and give it to the one he has wronged.
4_5_8: But if the man has no relative to whom restitution may be made for the wrong, the restitution for the wrong must go to the LORD for the priest, in addition to the ram of the atonement with which atonement is made for him.
4_5_9: Every offering of all the holy things of the children of Israel, which they bring to the priest, shall be his.
4_5_10: And every man’s holy things shall be his; whatever any man gives the priest shall be his.’ ”
4_5_11: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying
4_5_12: “Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them: ‘If any man’s wife goes astray and behaves unfaithfully toward him
4_5_13: and a man lies with her carnally, and it is hidden from the eyes of her husband, and it is concealed that she has defiled herself, and there was no witness against her, nor was she caught—
4_5_14: if the spirit of jealousy comes upon him and he becomes jealous of his wife, who has defiled herself; or if the spirit of jealousy comes upon him and he becomes jealous of his wife, although she has not defiled herself—
4_5_15: then the man shall bring his wife to the priest. He shall bring the offering required for her, one-tenth of an ephah of barley meal; he shall pour no oil on it and put no frankincense on it, because it is a grain offering of jealousy, an offering for remembering, for bringing iniquity to remembrance.
4_5_16: ‘And the priest shall bring her near, and set her before the LORD.
4_5_17: The priest shall take holy water in an earthen vessel, and take some of the dust that is on the floor of the tabernacle and put it into the water.
4_5_18: Then the priest shall stand the woman before the LORD, uncover the woman’s head, and put the offering for remembering in her hands, which is the grain offering of jealousy. And the priest shall have in his hand the bitter water that brings a curse.
4_5_19: And the priest shall put her under oath, and say to the woman, “If no man has lain with you, and if you have not gone astray to uncleanness while under your husband’s authority, be free from this bitter water that brings a curse.
4_5_20: But if you have gone astray while under your husband’s authority, and if you have defiled yourself and some man other than your husband has lain with you”—
4_5_21: then the priest shall put the woman under the oath of the curse, and he shall say to the woman— “the LORD make you a curse and an oath among your people, when the LORD makes your thigh rot and your belly swell
4_5_22: and may this water that causes the curse go into your stomach, and make your belly swell and your thigh rot.” ‘ Then the woman shall say, “Amen, so be it.”
4_5_23: ‘Then the priest shall write these curses in a book, and he shall scrape them off into the bitter water.
4_5_24: And he shall make the woman drink the bitter water that brings a curse, and the water that brings the curse shall enter her to become bitter.
4_5_25: Then the priest shall take the grain offering of jealousy from the woman’s hand, shall wave the offering before the LORD, and bring it to the altar
4_5_26: and the priest shall take a handful of the offering, as its memorial portion, burn it on the altar, and afterward make the woman drink the water.
4_5_27: When he has made her drink the water, then it shall be, if she has defiled herself and behaved unfaithfully toward her husband, that the water that brings a curse will enter her and become bitter, and her belly will swell, her thigh will rot, and the woman will become a curse among her people.
4_5_28: But if the woman has not defiled herself, and is clean, then she shall be free and may conceive children.
4_5_29: ‘This is the law of jealousy, when a wife, while under her husband’s authority, goes astray and defiles herself
4_5_30: or when the spirit of jealousy comes upon a man, and he becomes jealous of his wife; then he shall stand the woman before the LORD, and the priest shall execute all this law upon her.
4_5_31: Then the man shall be free from iniquity, but that woman shall bear her guilt.’ ”
4_6_1: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying
4_6_2: “Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them: ‘When either a man or woman consecrates an offering to take the vow of a Nazirite, to separate himself to the LORD
4_6_3: he shall separate himself from wine and similar drink; he shall drink neither vinegar made from wine nor vinegar made from similar drink; neither shall he drink any grape juice, nor eat fresh grapes or raisins.
4_6_4: All the days of his separation he shall eat nothing that is produced by the grapevine, from seed to skin.
4_6_5: ‘All the days of the vow of his separation no razor shall come upon his head; until the days are fulfilled for which he separated himself to the LORD, he shall be holy. Then he shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow.
4_6_6: All the days that he separates himself to the LORD he shall not go near a dead body.
4_6_7: He shall not make himself unclean even for his father or his mother, for his brother or his sister, when they die, because his separation to God is on his head.
4_6_8: All the days of his separation he shall be holy to the LORD.
4_6_9: ‘And if anyone dies very suddenly beside him, and he defiles his consecrated head, then he shall shave his head on the day of his cleansing; on the seventh day he shall shave it.
4_6_10: Then on the eighth day he shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest, to the door of the tabernacle of meeting
4_6_11: and the priest shall offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, and make atonement for him, because he sinned in regard to the corpse; and he shall sanctify his head that same day.
4_6_12: He shall consecrate to the LORD the days of his separation, and bring a male lamb in its first year as a trespass offering; but the former days shall be lost, because his separation was defiled.
4_6_13: ‘Now this is the law of the Nazirite: When the days of his separation are fulfilled, he shall be brought to the door of the tabernacle of meeting.
4_6_14: And he shall present his offering to the LORD: one male lamb in its first year without blemish as a burnt offering, one ewe lamb in its first year without blemish as a sin offering, one ram without blemish as a peace offering
4_6_15: a basket of unleavened bread, cakes of fine flour mixed with oil, unleavened wafers anointed with oil, and their grain offering with their drink offerings.
4_6_16: Then the priest shall bring them before the LORD and offer his sin offering and his burnt offering
4_6_17: and he shall offer the ram as a sacrifice of a peace offering to the LORD, with the basket of unleavened bread; the priest shall also offer its grain offering and its drink offering.
4_6_18: Then the Nazirite shall shave his consecrated head at the door of the tabernacle of meeting, and shall take the hair from his consecrated head and put it on the fire which is under the sacrifice of the peace offering.
4_6_19: ‘And the priest shall take the boiled shoulder of the ram, one unleavened cake from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and put them upon the hands of the Nazirite after he has shaved his consecrated hair
4_6_20: and the priest shall wave them as a wave offering before the LORD; they are holy for the priest, together with the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the heave offering. After that the Nazirite may drink wine.’
4_6_21: “This is the law of the Nazirite who vows to the LORD the offering for his separation, and besides that, whatever else his hand is able to provide; according to the vow which he takes, so he must do according to the law of his separation.”
4_6_22: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
4_6_23: “Speak to Aaron and his sons, saying, ‘This is the way you shall bless the children of Israel. Say to them:
4_6_24: “The LORD bless you and keep you
4_6_25: The LORD make His face shine upon you, And be gracious to you
4_6_26: The LORD lift up His countenance upon you, And give you peace.” ’
4_6_27: “So they shall put My name on the children of Israel, and I will bless them.”
4_7_1: Now it came to pass, when Moses had finished setting up the tabernacle, that he anointed it and consecrated it and all its furnishings, and the altar and all its utensils; so he anointed them and consecrated them.
4_7_2: Then the leaders of Israel, the heads of their fathers’ houses, who were the leaders of the tribes and over those who were numbered, made an offering.
4_7_3: And they brought their offering before the LORD, six covered carts and twelve oxen, a cart for every two of the leaders, and for each one an ox; and they presented them before the tabernacle.
4_7_4: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying
4_7_5: “Accept these from them, that they may be used in doing the work of the tabernacle of meeting; and you shall give them to the Levites, to every man according to his service.”
4_7_6: So Moses took the carts and the oxen, and gave them to the Levites.
4_7_7: Two carts and four oxen he gave to the sons of Gershon, according to their service
4_7_8: and four carts and eight oxen he gave to the sons of Merari, according to their service, under the authority of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest.
4_7_9: But to the sons of Kohath he gave none, because theirs was the service of the holy things, which they carried on their shoulders.
4_7_10: Now the leaders offered the dedication offering for the altar when it was anointed; so the leaders offered their offering before the altar.
4_7_11: For the LORD said to Moses, “They shall offer their offering, one leader each day, for the dedication of the altar.”
4_7_12: And the one who offered his offering on the first day was Nahshon the son of Amminadab, from the tribe of Judah.
4_7_13: His offering was one silver platter, the weight of which was one hundred and thirty shekels, and one silver bowl of seventy shekels, according to the shekel of the sanctuary, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering
4_7_14: one gold pan of ten shekels, full of incense
4_7_15: one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb in its first year, as a burnt offering
4_7_16: one kid of the goats as a sin offering
4_7_17: and for the sacrifice of peace offerings: two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs in their first year. This was the offering of Nahshon the son of Amminadab.
4_10_1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
4_10_2: “Make two silver trumpets for yourself; you shall make them of hammered work; you shall use them for calling the congregation and for directing the movement of the camps.
4_10_3: When they blow both of them, all the congregation shall gather before you at the door of the tabernacle of meeting.
4_10_4: But if they blow only one, then the leaders, the heads of the divisions of Israel, shall gather to you.
4_10_5: When you sound the advance, the camps that lie on the east side shall then begin their journey.
4_10_6: When you sound the advance the second time, then the camps that lie on the south side shall begin their journey; they shall sound the call for them to begin their journeys.
4_10_7: And when the assembly is to be gathered together, you shall blow, but not sound the advance.
4_10_8: The sons of Aaron, the priests, shall blow the trumpets; and these shall be to you as an ordinance forever throughout your generations.
4_10_9: “When you go to war in your land against the enemy who oppresses you, then you shall sound an alarm with the trumpets, and you will be remembered before the LORD your God, and you will be saved from your enemies.
4_10_10: Also in the day of your gladness, in your appointed feasts, and at the beginning of your months, you shall blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and over the sacrifices of your peace offerings; and they shall be a memorial for you before your God: I am the LORD your God.”
4_10_11: Now it came to pass on the twentieth day of the second month, in the second year, that the cloud was taken up from above the tabernacle of the Testimony.
4_10_12: And the children of Israel set out from the Wilderness of Sinai on their journeys; then the cloud settled down in the Wilderness of Paran.
4_10_13: So they started out for the first time according to the command of the LORD by the hand of Moses.
4_10_14: The standard of the camp of the children of Judah set out first according to their armies; over their army was Nahshon the son of Amminadab.
4_10_15: Over the army of the tribe of the children of Issachar was Nethanel the son of Zuar.
4_10_16: And over the army of the tribe of the children of Zebulun was Eliab the son of Helon.
4_10_17: Then the tabernacle was taken down; and the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari set out, carrying the tabernacle.
4_10_18: And the standard of the camp of Reuben set out according to their armies; over their army was Elizur the son of Shedeur.
4_10_19: Over the army of the tribe of the children of Simeon was Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai.
4_10_20: And over the army of the tribe of the children of Gad was Eliasaph the son of Deuel.
4_10_21: Then the Kohathites set out, carrying the holy things. (The tabernacle would be prepared for their arrival.)
4_10_22: And the standard of the camp of the children of Ephraim set out according to their armies; over their army was Elishama the son of Ammihud.
4_10_23: Over the army of the tribe of the children of Manasseh was Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur.
4_10_24: And over the army of the tribe of the children of Benjamin was Abidan the son of Gideoni.
4_10_25: Then the standard of the camp of the children of Dan (the rear guard of all the camps) set out according to their armies; over their army was Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai.
4_10_26: Over the army of the tribe of the children of Asher was Pagiel the son of Ocran.
4_10_27: And over the army of the tribe of the children of Naphtali was Ahira the son of Enan.
4_10_28: Thus was the order of march of the children of Israel, according to their armies, when they began their journey.
4_10_29: Now Moses said to Hobab the son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses’ father-in-law, “We are setting out for the place of which the LORD said, ‘I will give it to you.’ Come with us, and we will treat you well; for the LORD has promised good things to Israel.”
4_10_30: And he said to him, “I will not go, but I will depart to my own land and to my relatives.”
4_10_31: So Moses said, “Please do not leave, inasmuch as you know how we are to camp in the wilderness, and you can be our eyes.
4_10_32: And it shall be, if you go with us—indeed it shall be—that whatever good the LORD will do to us, the same we will do to you.”
4_10_33: So they departed from the mountain of the LORD on a journey of three days; and the ark of the covenant of the LORD went before them for the three days’ journey, to search out a resting place for them.
4_10_34: And the cloud of the LORD was above them by day when they went out from the camp.
4_10_35: So it was, whenever the ark set out, that Moses said: “Rise up, O LORD! Let Your enemies be scattered, And let those who hate You flee before You.”
4_10_36: And when it rested, he said: “Return, O LORD, To the many thousands of Israel.”
4_11_1: Now when the people complained, it displeased the LORD; for the LORD heard it, and His anger was aroused. So the fire of the LORD burned among them, and consumed some in the outskirts of the camp.
4_11_2: Then the people cried out to Moses, and when Moses prayed to the LORD, the fire was quenched.
4_11_3: So he called the name of the place Taberah, because the fire of the LORD had burned among them.
4_11_4: Now the mixed multitude who were among them yielded to intense craving; so the children of Israel also wept again and said: “Who will give us meat to eat?
4_11_5: We remember the fish which we ate freely in Egypt, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlic
4_11_6: but now our whole being is dried up; there is nothing at all except this manna before our eyes!”
4_11_7: Now the manna was like coriander seed, and its color like the color of bdellium.
4_11_8: The people went about and gathered it, ground it on millstones or beat it in the mortar, cooked it in pans, and made cakes of it; and its taste was like the taste of pastry prepared with oil.
4_11_9: And when the dew fell on the camp in the night, the manna fell on it.
4_11_10: Then Moses heard the people weeping throughout their families, everyone at the door of his tent; and the anger of the LORD was greatly aroused; Moses also was displeased.
4_11_12: Did I conceive all these people? Did I beget them, that You should say to me, ‘Carry them in your bosom, as a guardian carries a nursing child,’ to the land which You swore to their fathers?
4_11_13: Where am I to get meat to give to all these people? For they weep all over me, saying, ‘Give us meat, that we may eat.’
4_11_14: I am not able to bear all these people alone, because the burden is too heavy for me.
4_11_15: If You treat me like this, please kill me here and now—if I have found favor in Your sight—and do not let me see my wretchedness!”
4_11_16: So the LORD said to Moses: “Gather to Me seventy men of the elders of Israel, whom you know to be the elders of the people and officers over them; bring them to the tabernacle of meeting, that they may stand there with you.
4_11_17: Then I will come down and talk with you there. I will take of the Spirit that is upon you and will put the same upon them; and they shall bear the burden of the people with you, that you may not bear it yourself alone.
4_11_18: Then you shall say to the people, ‘Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, and you shall eat meat; for you have wept in the hearing of the LORD, saying, “Who will give us meat to eat? For it was well with us in Egypt.” Therefore the LORD will give you meat, and you shall eat.
4_11_19: You shall eat, not one day, nor two days, nor five days, nor ten days, nor twenty days
4_11_20: but for a whole month, until it comes out of your nostrils and becomes loathsome to you, because you have despised the LORD who is among you, and have wept before Him, saying, “Why did we ever come up out of Egypt?” ’ ”
4_11_21: And Moses said, “The people whom I am among are six hundred thousand men on foot; yet You have said, ‘I will give them meat, that they may eat for a whole month.’
4_11_22: Shall flocks and herds be slaughtered for them, to provide enough for them? Or shall all the fish of the sea be gathered together for them, to provide enough for them?”
4_11_23: And the LORD said to Moses, “Has the LORD’s arm been shortened? Now you shall see whether what I say will happen to you or not.”
4_11_24: So Moses went out and told the people the words of the LORD, and he gathered the seventy men of the elders of the people and placed them around the tabernacle.
4_11_25: Then the LORD came down in the cloud, and spoke to him, and took of the Spirit that was upon him, and placed the same upon the seventy elders; and it happened, when the Spirit rested upon them, that they prophesied, although they never did so again.
4_11_26: But two men had remained in the camp: the name of one was Eldad, and the name of the other Medad. And the Spirit rested upon them. Now they were among those listed, but who had not gone out to the tabernacle; yet they prophesied in the camp.
4_11_27: And a young man ran and told Moses, and said, “Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp.”
4_11_28: So Joshua the son of Nun, Moses’ assistant, one of his choice men, answered and said, “Moses my lord, forbid them!”
4_11_29: Then Moses said to him, “Are you zealous for my sake? Oh, that all the LORD’s people were prophets and that the LORD would put His Spirit upon them!”
4_11_30: And Moses returned to the camp, he and the elders of Israel.
4_11_31: Now a wind went out from the LORD, and it brought quail from the sea and left them fluttering near the camp, about a day’s journey on this side and about a day’s journey on the other side, all around the camp, and about two cubits above the surface of the ground.
4_11_32: And the people stayed up all that day, all night, and all the next day, and gathered the quail (he who gathered least gathered ten homers); and they spread them out for themselves all around the camp.
4_11_33: But while the meat was still between their teeth, before it was chewed, the wrath of the LORD was aroused against the people, and the LORD struck the people with a very great plague.
4_11_34: So he called the name of that place Kibroth Hattaavah, because there they buried the people who had yielded to craving.
4_11_35: From Kibroth Hattaavah the people moved to Hazeroth, and camped at Hazeroth.
4_12_1: Then Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married; for he had married an Ethiopian woman.
4_12_2: So they said, “Has the LORD indeed spoken only through Moses? Has He not spoken through us also?” And the LORD heard it.
4_12_3: (Now the man Moses was very humble, more than all men who were on the face of the earth.)
4_12_4: Suddenly the LORD said to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, “Come out, you three, to the tabernacle of meeting!” So the three came out.
4_12_5: Then the LORD came down in the pillar of cloud and stood in the door of the tabernacle, and called Aaron and Miriam. And they both went forward.
4_12_6: Then He said, “Hear now My words: If there is a prophet among you, I, the LORD, make Myself known to him in a vision; I speak to him in a dream.
4_12_7: Not so with My servant Moses; He is faithful in all My house.
4_12_8: I speak with him face to face, Even plainly, and not in dark sayings; And he sees the form of the LORD. Why then were you not afraid To speak against My servant Moses?”
4_12_9: So the anger of the LORD was aroused against them, and He departed.
4_12_10: And when the cloud departed from above the tabernacle, suddenly Miriam became leprous, as white as snow. Then Aaron turned toward Miriam, and there she was, a leper.
4_12_11: So Aaron said to Moses, “Oh, my lord! Please do not lay this sin on us, in which we have done foolishly and in which we have sinned.
4_12_12: Please do not let her be as one dead, whose flesh is half consumed when he comes out of his mother’s womb!”
4_12_13: So Moses cried out to the LORD, saying, “Please heal her, O God, I pray!”
4_12_14: Then the LORD said to Moses, “If her father had but spit in her face, would she not be shamed seven days? Let her be shut out of the camp seven days, and afterward she may be received again.”
4_12_15: So Miriam was shut out of the camp seven days, and the people did not journey till Miriam was brought in again.
4_12_16: And afterward the people moved from Hazeroth and camped in the Wilderness of Paran.
4_13_1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying

4_13_5: from the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat the son of Hori
4_13_6: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb the son of Jephunneh
4_13_7: from the tribe of Issachar, Igal the son of Joseph
4_13_8: from the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea the son of Nun
4_13_9: from the tribe of Benjamin, Palti the son of Raphu
4_13_10: from the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel the son of Sodi
4_13_11: from the tribe of Joseph, that is, from the tribe of Manasseh, Gaddi the son of Susi
4_13_12: from the tribe of Dan, Ammiel the son of Gemalli
4_13_13: from the tribe of Asher, Sethur the son of Michael
4_13_14: from the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi the son of Vophsi

4_13_18: and see what the land is like: whether the people who dwell in it are strong or weak, few or many
4_13_19: whether the land they dwell in is good or bad; whether the cities they inhabit are like camps or strongholds

4_13_25: And they returned from spying out the land after forty days.
4_13_26: Now they departed and came back to Moses and Aaron and all the congregation of the children of Israel in the Wilderness of Paran, at Kadesh; they brought back word to them and to all the congregation, and showed them the fruit of the land.
4_13_27: Then they told him, and said: “We went to the land where you sent us. It truly flows with milk and honey, and this is its fruit.
4_13_28: Nevertheless the people who dwell in the land are strong; the cities are fortified and very large; moreover we saw the descendants of Anak there.
4_13_29: The Amalekites dwell in the land of the South; the Hittites, the Jebusites, and the Amorites dwell in the mountains; and the Canaanites dwell by the sea and along the banks of the Jordan.”
4_13_30: Then Caleb quieted the people before Moses, and said, “Let us go up at once and take possession, for we are well able to overcome it.”
4_13_31: But the men who had gone up with him said, “We are not able to go up against the people, for they are stronger than we.”
4_13_32: And they gave the children of Israel a bad report of the land which they had spied out, saying, “The land through which we have gone as spies is a land that devours its inhabitants, and all the people whom we saw in it are men of great stature.
4_13_33: There we saw the giants ( the descendants of Anak came from the giants); and we were like grasshoppers in our own sight, and so we were in their sight.”
4_14_1: So all the congregation lifted up their voices and cried, and the people wept that night.
4_14_2: And all the children of Israel complained against Moses and Aaron, and the whole congregation said to them, “If only we had died in the land of Egypt! Or if only we had died in this wilderness!
4_14_3: Why has the LORD brought us to this land to fall by the sword, that our wives and children should become victims? Would it not be better for us to return to Egypt?”
4_14_4: So they said to one another, “Let us select a leader and return to Egypt.”
4_14_5: Then Moses and Aaron fell on their faces before all the assembly of the congregation of the children of Israel.
4_14_6: But Joshua the son of Nun and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, who were among those who had spied out the land, tore their clothes
4_14_7: and they spoke to all the congregation of the children of Israel, saying: “The land we passed through to spy out is an exceedingly good land.
4_14_8: If the LORD delights in us, then He will bring us into this land and give it to us, ‘a land which flows with milk and honey.’
4_14_9: Only do not rebel against the LORD, nor fear the people of the land, for they are our bread; their protection has departed from them, and the LORD is with us. Do not fear them.”
4_14_10: And all the congregation said to stone them with stones. Now the glory of the LORD appeared in the tabernacle of meeting before all the children of Israel.
4_14_11: Then the LORD said to Moses: “How long will these people reject Me? And how long will they not believe Me, with all the signs which I have performed among them?
4_14_12: I will strike them with the pestilence and disinherit them, and I will make of you a nation greater and mightier than they.”
4_14_13: And Moses said to the LORD: “Then the Egyptians will hear it, for by Your might You brought these people up from among them
4_14_14: and they will tell it to the inhabitants of this land. They have heard that You, LORD, are among these people; that You, LORD, are seen face to face and Your cloud stands above them, and You go before them in a pillar of cloud by day and in a pillar of fire by night.
4_14_15: Now if You kill these people as one man, then the nations which have heard of Your fame will speak, saying
4_14_16: ‘Because the LORD was not able to bring this people to the land which He swore to give them, therefore He killed them in the wilderness.’
4_14_17: And now, I pray, let the power of my Lord be great, just as You have spoken, saying
4_14_18: ‘The LORD is longsuffering and abundant in mercy, forgiving iniquity and transgression; but He by no means clears the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children to the third and fourth generation.’
4_14_19: Pardon the iniquity of this people, I pray, according to the greatness of Your mercy, just as You have forgiven this people, from Egypt even until now.”
4_14_20: Then the LORD said: “I have pardoned, according to your word
4_14_21: but truly, as I live, all the earth shall be filled with the glory of the LORD—
4_14_22: because all these men who have seen My glory and the signs which I did in Egypt and in the wilderness, and have put Me to the test now these ten times, and have not heeded My voice
4_14_23: they certainly shall not see the land of which I swore to their fathers, nor shall any of those who rejected Me see it.
4_14_24: But My servant Caleb, because he has a different spirit in him and has followed Me fully, I will bring into the land where he went, and his descendants shall inherit it.
4_14_25: Now the Amalekites and the Canaanites dwell in the valley; tomorrow turn and move out into the wilderness by the Way of the Red Sea.”
4_14_26: And the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying
4_14_27: “How long shall I bear with this evil congregation who complain against Me? I have heard the complaints which the children of Israel make against Me.
4_14_28: Say to them, ‘As I live,’ says the LORD, ‘just as you have spoken in My hearing, so I will do to you:
4_14_29: The carcasses of you who have complained against Me shall fall in this wilderness, all of you who were numbered, according to your entire number, from twenty years old and above.
4_14_30: Except for Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun, you shall by no means enter the land which I swore I would make you dwell in.
4_14_31: But your little ones, whom you said would be victims, I will bring in, and they shall know the land which you have despised.
4_14_32: But as for you, your carcasses shall fall in this wilderness.
4_14_33: And your sons shall be shepherds in the wilderness forty years, and bear the brunt of your infidelity, until your carcasses are consumed in the wilderness.
4_14_34: According to the number of the days in which you spied out the land, forty days, for each day you shall bear your guilt one year, namely forty years, and you shall know My rejection.
4_14_35: I the LORD have spoken this. I will surely do so to all this evil congregation who are gathered together against Me. In this wilderness they shall be consumed, and there they shall die.’ ”
4_14_36: Now the men whom Moses sent to spy out the land, who returned and made all the congregation complain against him by bringing a bad report of the land
4_14_37: those very men who brought the evil report about the land, died by the plague before the LORD.
4_14_38: But Joshua the son of Nun and Caleb the son of Jephunneh remained alive, of the men who went to spy out the land.
4_14_39: Then Moses told these words to all the children of Israel, and the people mourned greatly.
4_14_40: And they rose early in the morning and went up to the top of the mountain, saying, “Here we are, and we will go up to the place which the LORD has promised, for we have sinned!”
4_14_41: And Moses said, “Now why do you transgress the command of the LORD? For this will not succeed.
4_14_42: Do not go up, lest you be defeated by your enemies, for the LORD is not among you.
4_14_43: For the Amalekites and the Canaanites are there before you, and you shall fall by the sword; because you have turned away from the LORD, the LORD will not be with you.”
4_14_44: But they presumed to go up to the mountaintop. Nevertheless, neither the ark of the covenant of the LORD nor Moses departed from the camp.
4_14_45: Then the Amalekites and the Canaanites who dwelt in that mountain came down and attacked them, and drove them back as far as Hormah.
4_15_1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying
4_15_2: “Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them: ‘When you have come into the land you are to inhabit, which I am giving to you
4_15_3: and you make an offering by fire to the LORD, a burnt offering or a sacrifice, to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering or in your appointed feasts, to make a sweet aroma to the LORD, from the herd or the flock
4_15_4: then he who presents his offering to the LORD shall bring a grain offering of one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with one-fourth of a hin of oil
4_15_5: and one-fourth of a hin of wine as a drink offering you shall prepare with the burnt offering or the sacrifice, for each lamb.
4_15_6: Or for a ram you shall prepare as a grain offering two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with one-third of a hin of oil
4_15_7: and as a drink offering you shall offer one-third of a hin of wine as a sweet aroma to the LORD.
4_15_8: And when you prepare a young bull as a burnt offering, or as a sacrifice to fulfill a vow, or as a peace offering to the LORD
4_15_9: then shall be offered with the young bull a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with half a hin of oil
4_15_10: and you shall bring as the drink offering half a hin of wine as an offering made by fire, a sweet aroma to the LORD.
4_15_11: ‘Thus it shall be done for each young bull, for each ram, or for each lamb or young goat.
4_15_12: According to the number that you prepare, so you shall do with everyone according to their number.
4_15_13: All who are native-born shall do these things in this manner, in presenting an offering made by fire, a sweet aroma to the LORD.
4_15_14: And if a stranger dwells with you, or whoever is among you throughout your generations, and would present an offering made by fire, a sweet aroma to the LORD, just as you do, so shall he do.
4_15_15: One ordinance shall be for you of the assembly and for the stranger who dwells with you, an ordinance forever throughout your generations; as you are, so shall the stranger be before the LORD.
4_15_16: One law and one custom shall be for you and for the stranger who dwells with you.’ ”
4_15_17: Again the LORD spoke to Moses, saying
4_15_18: “Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them: ‘When you come into the land to which I bring you
4_15_19: then it will be, when you eat of the bread of the land, that you shall offer up a heave offering to the LORD.
4_15_20: You shall offer up a cake of the first of your ground meal as a heave offering; as a heave offering of the threshing floor, so shall you offer it up.
4_15_21: Of the first of your ground meal you shall give to the LORD a heave offering throughout your generations.
4_15_22: ‘If you sin unintentionally, and do not observe all these commandments which the LORD has spoken to Moses—
4_15_23: all that the LORD has commanded you by the hand of Moses, from the day the LORD gave commandment and onward throughout your generations—
4_15_24: then it will be, if it is unintentionally committed, without the knowledge of the congregation, that the whole congregation shall offer one young bull as a burnt offering, as a sweet aroma to the LORD, with its grain offering and its drink offering, according to the ordinance, and one kid of the goats as a sin offering.
4_15_25: So the priest shall make atonement for the whole congregation of the children of Israel, and it shall be forgiven them, for it was unintentional; they shall bring their offering, an offering made by fire to the LORD, and their sin offering before the LORD, for their unintended sin.
4_15_26: It shall be forgiven the whole congregation of the children of Israel and the stranger who dwells among them, because all the people did it unintentionally.
4_15_27: ‘And if a person sins unintentionally, then he shall bring a female goat in its first year as a sin offering.
4_15_28: So the priest shall make atonement for the person who sins unintentionally, when he sins unintentionally before the LORD, to make atonement for him; and it shall be forgiven him.
4_15_29: You shall have one law for him who sins unintentionally, for him who is native-born among the children of Israel and for the stranger who dwells among them.
4_15_30: ‘But the person who does anything presumptuously, whether he is native-born or a stranger, that one brings reproach on the LORD, and he shall be cut off from among his people.
4_15_31: Because he has despised the word of the LORD, and has broken His commandment, that person shall be completely cut off; his guilt shall be upon him.’ ”
4_15_32: Now while the children of Israel were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering sticks on the Sabbath day.
4_15_33: And those who found him gathering sticks brought him to Moses and Aaron, and to all the congregation.
4_15_34: They put him under guard, because it had not been explained what should be done to him.
4_15_35: Then the LORD said to Moses, “The man must surely be put to death; all the congregation shall stone him with stones outside the camp.”
4_15_36: So, as the LORD commanded Moses, all the congregation brought him outside the camp and stoned him with stones, and he died.
4_15_37: Again the LORD spoke to Moses, saying
4_15_38: “Speak to the children of Israel: Tell them to make tassels on the corners of their garments throughout their generations, and to put a blue thread in the tassels of the corners.
4_15_39: And you shall have the tassel, that you may look upon it and remember all the commandments of the LORD and do them, and that you may not follow the harlotry to which your own heart and your own eyes are inclined
4_15_40: and that you may remember and do all My commandments, and be holy for your God.
