4_15_41: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God: I am the LORD your God.”
4_16_1: Now Korah the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, with Dathan and Abiram the sons of Eliab, and On the son of Peleth, sons of Reuben, took men
4_16_2: and they rose up before Moses with some of the children of Israel, two hundred and fifty leaders of the congregation, representatives of the congregation, men of renown.
4_16_3: They gathered together against Moses and Aaron, and said to them, “You take too much upon yourselves, for all the congregation is holy, every one of them, and the LORD is among them. Why then do you exalt yourselves above the assembly of the LORD?”
4_16_4: So when Moses heard it, he fell on his face
4_16_5: and he spoke to Korah and all his company, saying, “Tomorrow morning the LORD will show who is His and who is holy, and will cause him to come near to Him. That one whom He chooses He will cause to come near to Him.
4_16_6: Do this: Take censers, Korah and all your company
4_16_7: put fire in them and put incense in them before the LORD tomorrow, and it shall be that the man whom the LORD chooses is the holy one. You take too much upon yourselves, you sons of Levi!”
4_16_8: Then Moses said to Korah, “Hear now, you sons of Levi:
4_16_9: Is it a small thing to you that the God of Israel has separated you from the congregation of Israel, to bring you near to Himself, to do the work of the tabernacle of the LORD, and to stand before the congregation to serve them
4_16_10: and that He has brought you near to Himself, you and all your brethren, the sons of Levi, with you? And are you seeking the priesthood also?
4_16_11: Therefore you and all your company are gathered together against the LORD. And what is Aaron that you complain against him?”
4_16_12: And Moses sent to call Dathan and Abiram the sons of Eliab, but they said, “We will not come up!
4_16_13: Is it a small thing that you have brought us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey, to kill us in the wilderness, that you should keep acting like a prince over us?
4_16_14: Moreover you have not brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey, nor given us inheritance of fields and vineyards. Will you put out the eyes of these men? We will not come up!”
4_16_15: Then Moses was very angry, and said to the LORD, “Do not respect their offering. I have not taken one donkey from them, nor have I hurt one of them.”
4_16_16: And Moses said to Korah, “Tomorrow, you and all your company be present before the LORD—you and they, as well as Aaron.
4_16_17: Let each take his censer and put incense in it, and each of you bring his censer before the LORD, two hundred and fifty censers; both you and Aaron, each with his censer.”
4_16_18: So every man took his censer, put fire in it, laid incense on it, and stood at the door of the tabernacle of meeting with Moses and Aaron.
4_16_19: And Korah gathered all the congregation against them at the door of the tabernacle of meeting. Then the glory of the LORD appeared to all the congregation.
4_16_20: And the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying
4_16_21: “Separate yourselves from among this congregation, that I may consume them in a moment.”
4_16_22: Then they fell on their faces, and said, “O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, shall one man sin, and You be angry with all the congregation?”
4_16_23: So the LORD spoke to Moses, saying
4_16_24: “Speak to the congregation, saying, ‘Get away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.’ ”
4_16_25: Then Moses rose and went to Dathan and Abiram, and the elders of Israel followed him.
4_16_26: And he spoke to the congregation, saying, “Depart now from the tents of these wicked men! Touch nothing of theirs, lest you be consumed in all their sins.”
4_16_27: So they got away from around the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram; and Dathan and Abiram came out and stood at the door of their tents, with their wives, their sons, and their little children.
4_16_28: And Moses said: “By this you shall know that the LORD has sent me to do all these works, for I have not done them of my own will.
4_16_29: If these men die naturally like all men, or if they are visited by the common fate of all men, then the LORD has not sent me.
4_16_30: But if the LORD creates a new thing, and the earth opens its mouth and swallows them up with all that belongs to them, and they go down alive into the pit, then you will understand that these men have rejected the LORD.”
4_16_31: Now it came to pass, as he finished speaking all these words, that the ground split apart under them
4_16_32: and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up, with their households and all the men with Korah, with all their goods.
4_16_33: So they and all those with them went down alive into the pit; the earth closed over them, and they perished from among the assembly.
4_16_34: Then all Israel who were around them fled at their cry, for they said, “Lest the earth swallow us up also!”
4_16_35: And a fire came out from the LORD and consumed the two hundred and fifty men who were offering incense.
4_16_36: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
4_16_37: “Tell Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, to pick up the censers out of the blaze, for they are holy, and scatter the fire some distance away.
4_16_38: The censers of these men who sinned against their own souls, let them be made into hammered plates as a covering for the altar. Because they presented them before the LORD, therefore they are holy; and they shall be a sign to the children of Israel.”
4_16_39: So Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers, which those who were burned up had presented, and they were hammered out as a covering on the altar
4_16_40: to be a memorial to the children of Israel that no outsider, who is not a descendant of Aaron, should come near to offer incense before the LORD, that he might not become like Korah and his companions, just as the LORD had said to him through Moses.
4_16_41: On the next day all the congregation of the children of Israel complained against Moses and Aaron, saying, “You have killed the people of the LORD.”
4_16_42: Now it happened, when the congregation had gathered against Moses and Aaron, that they turned toward the tabernacle of meeting; and suddenly the cloud covered it, and the glory of the LORD appeared.
4_16_43: Then Moses and Aaron came before the tabernacle of meeting.
4_16_44: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying
4_16_45: “Get away from among this congregation, that I may consume them in a moment.” And they fell on their faces.
4_16_46: So Moses said to Aaron, “Take a censer and put fire in it from the altar, put incense on it, and take it quickly to the congregation and make atonement for them; for wrath has gone out from the LORD. The plague has begun.”
4_16_47: Then Aaron took it as Moses commanded, and ran into the midst of the assembly; and already the plague had begun among the people. So he put in the incense and made atonement for the people.
4_16_48: And he stood between the dead and the living; so the plague was stopped.
4_16_49: Now those who died in the plague were fourteen thousand seven hundred, besides those who died in the Korah incident.
4_16_50: So Aaron returned to Moses at the door of the tabernacle of meeting, for the plague had stopped.
4_17_1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
4_17_2: “Speak to the children of Israel, and get from them a rod from each father’s house, all their leaders according to their fathers’ houses—twelve rods. Write each man’s name on his rod.
4_17_3: And you shall write Aaron’s name on the rod of Levi. For there shall be one rod for the head of each father’s house.
4_17_4: Then you shall place them in the tabernacle of meeting before the Testimony, where I meet with you.
4_17_5: And it shall be that the rod of the man whom I choose will blossom; thus I will rid Myself of the complaints of the children of Israel, which they make against you.”
4_17_6: So Moses spoke to the children of Israel, and each of their leaders gave him a rod apiece, for each leader according to their fathers’ houses, twelve rods; and the rod of Aaron was among their rods.
4_17_7: And Moses placed the rods before the LORD in the tabernacle of witness.
4_17_8: Now it came to pass on the next day that Moses went into the tabernacle of witness, and behold, the rod of Aaron, of the house of Levi, had sprouted and put forth buds, had produced blossoms and yielded ripe almonds.
4_17_9: Then Moses brought out all the rods from before the LORD to all the children of Israel; and they looked, and each man took his rod.
4_17_10: And the LORD said to Moses, “Bring Aaron’s rod back before the Testimony, to be kept as a sign against the rebels, that you may put their complaints away from Me, lest they die.”
4_17_11: Thus did Moses; just as the LORD had commanded him, so he did.
4_17_12: So the children of Israel spoke to Moses, saying, “Surely we die, we perish, we all perish!
4_17_13: Whoever even comes near the tabernacle of the LORD must die. Shall we all utterly die?”
4_18_1: Then the LORD said to Aaron: “You and your sons and your father’s house with you shall bear the iniquity related to the sanctuary, and you and your sons with you shall bear the iniquity associated with your priesthood.
4_18_2: Also bring with you your brethren of the tribe of Levi, the tribe of your father, that they may be joined with you and serve you while you and your sons are with you before the tabernacle of witness.
4_18_3: They shall attend to your needs and all the needs of the tabernacle; but they shall not come near the articles of the sanctuary and the altar, lest they die—they and you also.
4_18_4: They shall be joined with you and attend to the needs of the tabernacle of meeting, for all the work of the tabernacle; but an outsider shall not come near you.
4_18_5: And you shall attend to the duties of the sanctuary and the duties of the altar, that there may be no more wrath on the children of Israel.
4_18_6: Behold, I Myself have taken your brethren the Levites from among the children of Israel; they are a gift to you, given by the LORD, to do the work of the tabernacle of meeting.
4_18_7: Therefore you and your sons with you shall attend to your priesthood for everything at the altar and behind the veil; and you shall serve. I give your priesthood to you as a gift for service, but the outsider who comes near shall be put to death.”
4_18_8: And the LORD spoke to Aaron: “Here, I Myself have also given you charge of My heave offerings, all the holy gifts of the children of Israel; I have given them as a portion to you and your sons, as an ordinance forever.
4_18_9: This shall be yours of the most holy things reserved from the fire: every offering of theirs, every grain offering and every sin offering and every trespass offering which they render to Me, shall be most holy for you and your sons.
4_18_10: In a most holy place you shall eat it; every male shall eat it. It shall be holy to you.
4_18_11: “This also is yours: the heave offering of their gift, with all the wave offerings of the children of Israel; I have given them to you, and your sons and daughters with you, as an ordinance forever. Everyone who is clean in your house may eat it.
4_18_12: “All the best of the oil, all the best of the new wine and the grain, their firstfruits which they offer to the LORD, I have given them to you.
4_18_13: Whatever first ripe fruit is in their land, which they bring to the LORD, shall be yours. Everyone who is clean in your house may eat it.
4_18_14: “Every devoted thing in Israel shall be yours.
4_18_15: “Everything that first opens the womb of all flesh, which they bring to the LORD, whether man or beast, shall be yours; nevertheless the firstborn of man you shall surely redeem, and the firstborn of unclean animals you shall redeem.
4_18_16: And those redeemed of the devoted things you shall redeem when one month old, according to your valuation, for five shekels of silver, according to the shekel of the sanctuary, which is twenty gerahs.
4_18_17: But the firstborn of a cow, the firstborn of a sheep, or the firstborn of a goat you shall not redeem; they are holy. You shall sprinkle their blood on the altar, and burn their fat as an offering made by fire for a sweet aroma to the LORD.
4_18_18: And their flesh shall be yours, just as the wave breast and the right thigh are yours.
4_18_19: “All the heave offerings of the holy things, which the children of Israel offer to the LORD, I have given to you and your sons and daughters with you as an ordinance forever; it is a covenant of salt forever before the LORD with you and your descendants with you.”
4_18_20: Then the LORD said to Aaron: “You shall have no inheritance in their land, nor shall you have any portion among them; I am your portion and your inheritance among the children of Israel.
4_18_21: “Behold, I have given the children of Levi all the tithes in Israel as an inheritance in return for the work which they perform, the work of the tabernacle of meeting.
4_18_22: Hereafter the children of Israel shall not come near the tabernacle of meeting, lest they bear sin and die.
4_18_23: But the Levites shall perform the work of the tabernacle of meeting, and they shall bear their iniquity; it shall be a statute forever, throughout your generations, that among the children of Israel they shall have no inheritance.
4_18_24: For the tithes of the children of Israel, which they offer up as a heave offering to the LORD, I have given to the Levites as an inheritance; therefore I have said to them, ‘Among the children of Israel they shall have no inheritance.’ ”
4_18_25: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying
4_18_26: “Speak thus to the Levites, and say to them: ‘When you take from the children of Israel the tithes which I have given you from them as your inheritance, then you shall offer up a heave offering of it to the LORD, a tenth of the tithe.
4_18_27: And your heave offering shall be reckoned to you as though it were the grain of the threshing floor and as the fullness of the winepress.
4_18_28: Thus you shall also offer a heave offering to the LORD from all your tithes which you receive from the children of Israel, and you shall give the LORD’s heave offering from it to Aaron the priest.
4_18_29: Of all your gifts you shall offer up every heave offering due to the LORD, from all the best of them, the consecrated part of them.’
4_18_30: Therefore you shall say to them: ‘When you have lifted up the best of it, then the rest shall be accounted to the Levites as the produce of the threshing floor and as the produce of the winepress.
4_18_31: You may eat it in any place, you and your households, for it is your reward for your work in the tabernacle of meeting.
4_18_32: And you shall bear no sin because of it, when you have lifted up the best of it. But you shall not profane the holy gifts of the children of Israel, lest you die.’ ”
4_19_1: Now the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying
4_19_2: “This is the ordinance of the law which the LORD has commanded, saying: ‘Speak to the children of Israel, that they bring you a red heifer without blemish, in which there is no defect and on which a yoke has never come.
4_19_3: You shall give it to Eleazar the priest, that he may take it outside the camp, and it shall be slaughtered before him
4_19_4: and Eleazar the priest shall take some of its blood with his finger, and sprinkle some of its blood seven times directly in front of the tabernacle of meeting.
4_19_5: Then the heifer shall be burned in his sight: its hide, its flesh, its blood, and its offal shall be burned.
4_19_6: And the priest shall take cedar wood and hyssop and scarlet, and cast them into the midst of the fire burning the heifer.
4_19_7: Then the priest shall wash his clothes, he shall bathe in water, and afterward he shall come into the camp; the priest shall be unclean until evening.
4_19_8: And the one who burns it shall wash his clothes in water, bathe in water, and shall be unclean until evening.
4_19_9: Then a man who is clean shall gather up the ashes of the heifer, and store them outside the camp in a clean place; and they shall be kept for the congregation of the children of Israel for the water of purification; it is for purifying from sin.
4_19_10: And the one who gathers the ashes of the heifer shall wash his clothes, and be unclean until evening. It shall be a statute forever to the children of Israel and to the stranger who dwells among them.
4_19_11: ‘He who touches the dead body of anyone shall be unclean seven days.
4_19_12: He shall purify himself with the water on the third day and on the seventh day; then he will be clean. But if he does not purify himself on the third day and on the seventh day, he will not be clean.
4_19_13: Whoever touches the body of anyone who has died, and does not purify himself, defiles the tabernacle of the LORD. That person shall be cut off from Israel. He shall be unclean, because the water of purification was not sprinkled on him; his uncleanness is still on him.
4_19_14: ‘This is the law when a man dies in a tent: All who come into the tent and all who are in the tent shall be unclean seven days
4_19_15: and every open vessel, which has no cover fastened on it, is unclean.
4_19_16: Whoever in the open field touches one who is slain by a sword or who has died, or a bone of a man, or a grave, shall be unclean seven days.
4_19_17: ‘And for an unclean person they shall take some of the ashes of the heifer burnt for purification from sin, and running water shall be put on them in a vessel.
4_19_18: A clean person shall take hyssop and dip it in the water, sprinkle it on the tent, on all the vessels, on the persons who were there, or on the one who touched a bone, the slain, the dead, or a grave.
4_19_19: The clean person shall sprinkle the unclean on the third day and on the seventh day; and on the seventh day he shall purify himself, wash his clothes, and bathe in water; and at evening he shall be clean.
4_19_20: ‘But the man who is unclean and does not purify himself, that person shall be cut off from among the assembly, because he has defiled the sanctuary of the LORD. The water of purification has not been sprinkled on him; he is unclean.
4_19_21: It shall be a perpetual statute for them. He who sprinkles the water of purification shall wash his clothes; and he who touches the water of purification shall be unclean until evening.
4_19_22: Whatever the unclean person touches shall be unclean; and the person who touches it shall be unclean until evening.’ ”
4_20_1: Then the children of Israel, the whole congregation, came into the Wilderness of Zin in the first month, and the people stayed in Kadesh; and Miriam died there and was buried there.
4_20_2: Now there was no water for the congregation; so they gathered together against Moses and Aaron.
4_20_3: And the people contended with Moses and spoke, saying: “If only we had died when our brethren died before the LORD!
4_20_4: Why have you brought up the assembly of the LORD into this wilderness, that we and our animals should die here?
4_20_5: And why have you made us come up out of Egypt, to bring us to this evil place? It is not a place of grain or figs or vines or pomegranates; nor is there any water to drink.”
4_20_6: So Moses and Aaron went from the presence of the assembly to the door of the tabernacle of meeting, and they fell on their faces. And the glory of the LORD appeared to them.
4_20_7: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying
4_20_8: “Take the rod; you and your brother Aaron gather the congregation together. Speak to the rock before their eyes, and it will yield its water; thus you shall bring water for them out of the rock, and give drink to the congregation and their animals.”
4_20_9: So Moses took the rod from before the LORD as He commanded him.
4_20_10: And Moses and Aaron gathered the assembly together before the rock; and he said to them, “Hear now, you rebels! Must we bring water for you out of this rock?”
4_20_11: Then Moses lifted his hand and struck the rock twice with his rod; and water came out abundantly, and the congregation and their animals drank.
4_20_12: Then the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, “Because you did not believe Me, to hallow Me in the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore you shall not bring this assembly into the land which I have given them.”
4_20_13: This was the water of Meribah, because the children of Israel contended with the LORD, and He was hallowed among them.
4_20_14: Now Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom. “Thus says your brother Israel: ‘You know all the hardship that has befallen us
4_20_15: how our fathers went down to Egypt, and we dwelt in Egypt a long time, and the Egyptians afflicted us and our fathers.
4_20_16: When we cried out to the LORD, He heard our voice and sent the Angel and brought us up out of Egypt; now here we are in Kadesh, a city on the edge of your border.
4_20_17: Please let us pass through your country. We will not pass through fields or vineyards, nor will we drink water from wells; we will go along the King’s Highway; we will not turn aside to the right hand or to the left until we have passed through your territory.’ ”
4_20_18: Then Edom said to him, “You shall not pass through my land, lest I come out against you with the sword.”
4_20_19: So the children of Israel said to him, “We will go by the Highway, and if I or my livestock drink any of your water, then I will pay for it; let me only pass through on foot, nothing more.”
4_20_20: Then he said, “You shall not pass through.” So Edom came out against them with many men and with a strong hand.
4_20_21: Thus Edom refused to give Israel passage through his territory; so Israel turned away from him.
4_20_22: Now the children of Israel, the whole congregation, journeyed from Kadesh and came to Mount Hor.
4_20_23: And the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron in Mount Hor by the border of the land of Edom, saying:
4_20_24: “Aaron shall be gathered to his people, for he shall not enter the land which I have given to the children of Israel, because you rebelled against My word at the water of Meribah.
4_20_25: Take Aaron and Eleazar his son, and bring them up to Mount Hor
4_20_26: and strip Aaron of his garments and put them on Eleazar his son; for Aaron shall be gathered to his people and die there.”
4_20_27: So Moses did just as the LORD commanded, and they went up to Mount Hor in the sight of all the congregation.
4_20_28: Moses stripped Aaron of his garments and put them on Eleazar his son; and Aaron died there on the top of the mountain. Then Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.
4_20_29: Now when all the congregation saw that Aaron was dead, all the house of Israel mourned for Aaron thirty days.
4_21_1: The king of Arad, the Canaanite, who dwelt in the South, heard that Israel was coming on the road to Atharim. Then he fought against Israel and took some of them prisoners.
4_21_2: So Israel made a vow to the LORD, and said, “If You will indeed deliver this people into my hand, then I will utterly destroy their cities.”
4_21_3: And the LORD listened to the voice of Israel and delivered up the Canaanites, and they utterly destroyed them and their cities. So the name of that place was called Hormah.
4_21_4: Then they journeyed from Mount Hor by the Way of the Red Sea, to go around the land of Edom; and the soul of the people became very discouraged on the way.
4_21_5: And the people spoke against God and against Moses: “Why have you brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? For there is no food and no water, and our soul loathes this worthless bread.”
4_21_6: So the LORD sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people; and many of the people of Israel died.
4_21_7: Therefore the people came to Moses, and said, “We have sinned, for we have spoken against the LORD and against you; pray to the LORD that He take away the serpents from us.” So Moses prayed for the people.
4_21_8: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Make a fiery serpent, and set it on a pole; and it shall be that everyone who is bitten, when he looks at it, shall live.”
4_21_9: So Moses made a bronze serpent, and put it on a pole; and so it was, if a serpent had bitten anyone, when he looked at the bronze serpent, he lived.
4_21_10: Now the children of Israel moved on and camped in Oboth.
4_21_11: And they journeyed from Oboth and camped at Ije Abarim, in the wilderness which is east of Moab, toward the sunrise.
4_21_12: From there they moved and camped in the Valley of Zered.
4_21_13: From there they moved and camped on the other side of the Arnon, which is in the wilderness that extends from the border of the Amorites; for the Arnon is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites.
4_21_14: Therefore it is said in the Book of the Wars of the LORD: “Waheb in Suphah, The brooks of the Arnon
4_21_15: And the slope of the brooks That reaches to the dwelling of Ar, And lies on the border of Moab.”
4_21_16: From there they went to Beer, which is the well where the LORD said to Moses, “Gather the people together, and I will give them water.”
4_21_17: Then Israel sang this song: “Spring up, O well! All of you sing to it—
4_21_18: The well the leaders sank, Dug by the nation’s nobles, By the lawgiver, with their staves.” And from the wilderness they went to Mattanah
4_21_19: from Mattanah to Nahaliel, from Nahaliel to Bamoth
4_21_20: and from Bamoth, in the valley that is in the country of Moab, to the top of Pisgah which looks down on the wasteland.
4_21_21: Then Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, saying
4_21_22: “Let me pass through your land. We will not turn aside into fields or vineyards; we will not drink water from wells. We will go by the King’s Highway until we have passed through your territory.”
4_21_23: But Sihon would not allow Israel to pass through his territory. So Sihon gathered all his people together and went out against Israel in the wilderness, and he came to Jahaz and fought against Israel.
4_21_24: Then Israel defeated him with the edge of the sword, and took possession of his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, as far as the people of Ammon; for the border of the people of Ammon was fortified.
4_21_25: So Israel took all these cities, and Israel dwelt in all the cities of the Amorites, in Heshbon and in all its villages.
4_21_26: For Heshbon was the city of Sihon king of the Amorites, who had fought against the former king of Moab, and had taken all his land from his hand as far as the Arnon.
4_21_27: Therefore those who speak in proverbs say: “Come to Heshbon, let it be built; Let the city of Sihon be repaired.
4_21_28: “For fire went out from Heshbon, A flame from the city of Sihon; It consumed Ar of Moab, The lords of the heights of the Arnon.
4_21_29: Woe to you, Moab! You have perished, O people of Chemosh! He has given his sons as fugitives, And his daughters into captivity, To Sihon king of the Amorites.
4_21_30: “But we have shot at them; Heshbon has perished as far as Dibon. Then we laid waste as far as Nophah, Which reaches to Medeba.”
4_21_31: Thus Israel dwelt in the land of the Amorites.
4_21_32: Then Moses sent to spy out Jazer; and they took its villages and drove out the Amorites who were there.
4_21_33: And they turned and went up by the way to Bashan. So Og king of Bashan went out against them, he and all his people, to battle at Edrei.
4_21_34: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Do not fear him, for I have delivered him into your hand, with all his people and his land; and you shall do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt at Heshbon.”
4_21_35: So they defeated him, his sons, and all his people, until there was no survivor left him; and they took possession of his land.
4_22_1: Then the children of Israel moved, and camped in the plains of Moab on the side of the Jordan across from Jericho.
4_22_2: Now Balak the son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites.
4_22_3: And Moab was exceedingly afraid of the people because they were many, and Moab was sick with dread because of the children of Israel.
4_22_4: So Moab said to the elders of Midian, “Now this company will lick up everything around us, as an ox licks up the grass of the field.” And Balak the son of Zippor was king of the Moabites at that time.
4_22_5: Then he sent messengers to Balaam the son of Beor at Pethor, which is near the River in the land of the sons of his people, to call him, saying: “Look, a people has come from Egypt. See, they cover the face of the earth, and are settling next to me!
4_22_6: Therefore please come at once, curse this people for me, for they are too mighty for me. Perhaps I shall be able to defeat them and drive them out of the land, for I know that he whom you bless is blessed, and he whom you curse is cursed.”
4_22_7: So the elders of Moab and the elders of Midian departed with the diviner’s fee in their hand, and they came to Balaam and spoke to him the words of Balak.
4_22_8: And he said to them, “Lodge here tonight, and I will bring back word to you, as the LORD speaks to me.” So the princes of Moab stayed with Balaam.
4_22_9: Then God came to Balaam and said, “Who are these men with you?”
4_22_10: So Balaam said to God, “Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, has sent to me, saying
4_22_11: ‘Look, a people has come out of Egypt, and they cover the face of the earth. Come now, curse them for me; perhaps I shall be able to overpower them and drive them out.’ ”
4_22_12: And God said to Balaam, “You shall not go with them; you shall not curse the people, for they are blessed.”
4_22_13: So Balaam rose in the morning and said to the princes of Balak, “Go back to your land, for the LORD has refused to give me permission to go with you.”
4_22_14: And the princes of Moab rose and went to Balak, and said, “Balaam refuses to come with us.”
4_22_15: Then Balak again sent princes, more numerous and more honorable than they.
4_22_16: And they came to Balaam and said to him, “Thus says Balak the son of Zippor: ‘Please let nothing hinder you from coming to me
4_22_17: for I will certainly honor you greatly, and I will do whatever you say to me. Therefore please come, curse this people for me.’ ”
4_22_18: Then Balaam answered and said to the servants of Balak, “Though Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the word of the LORD my God, to do less or more.
4_22_19: Now therefore, please, you also stay here tonight, that I may know what more the LORD will say to me.”
4_22_20: And God came to Balaam at night and said to him, “If the men come to call you, rise and go with them; but only the word which I speak to you—that you shall do.”
4_22_21: So Balaam rose in the morning, saddled his donkey, and went with the princes of Moab.
4_22_22: Then God’s anger was aroused because he went, and the Angel of the LORD took His stand in the way as an adversary against him. And he was riding on his donkey, and his two servants were with him.
4_22_23: Now the donkey saw the Angel of the LORD standing in the way with His drawn sword in His hand, and the donkey turned aside out of the way and went into the field. So Balaam struck the donkey to turn her back onto the road.
4_22_24: Then the Angel of the LORD stood in a narrow path between the vineyards, with a wall on this side and a wall on that side.
4_22_25: And when the donkey saw the Angel of the LORD, she pushed herself against the wall and crushed Balaam’s foot against the wall; so he struck her again.
4_22_26: Then the Angel of the LORD went further, and stood in a narrow place where there was no way to turn either to the right hand or to the left.
4_22_27: And when the donkey saw the Angel of the LORD, she lay down under Balaam; so Balaam’s anger was aroused, and he struck the donkey with his staff.
4_22_28: Then the LORD opened the mouth of the donkey, and she said to Balaam, “What have I done to you, that you have struck me these three times?”
4_22_29: And Balaam said to the donkey, “Because you have abused me. I wish there were a sword in my hand, for now I would kill you!”
4_22_30: So the donkey said to Balaam, “Am I not your donkey on which you have ridden, ever since I became yours, to this day? Was I ever disposed to do this to you?” And he said, “No.”
4_22_31: Then the LORD opened Balaam’s eyes, and he saw the Angel of the LORD standing in the way with His drawn sword in His hand; and he bowed his head and fell flat on his face.
4_22_32: And the Angel of the LORD said to him, “Why have you struck your donkey these three times? Behold, I have come out to stand against you, because your way is perverse before Me.
4_22_33: The donkey saw Me and turned aside from Me these three times. If she had not turned aside from Me, surely I would also have killed you by now, and let her live.”
4_22_34: And Balaam said to the Angel of the LORD, “I have sinned, for I did not know You stood in the way against me. Now therefore, if it displeases You, I will turn back.”
4_22_35: Then the Angel of the LORD said to Balaam, “Go with the men, but only the word that I speak to you, that you shall speak.” So Balaam went with the princes of Balak.
4_22_36: Now when Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went out to meet him at the city of Moab, which is on the border at the Arnon, the boundary of the territory.
4_22_37: Then Balak said to Balaam, “Did I not earnestly send to you, calling for you? Why did you not come to me? Am I not able to honor you?”
4_22_38: And Balaam said to Balak, “Look, I have come to you! Now, have I any power at all to say anything? The word that God puts in my mouth, that I must speak.”
4_22_39: So Balaam went with Balak, and they came to Kirjath Huzoth.
4_22_40: Then Balak offered oxen and sheep, and he sent some to Balaam and to the princes who were with him.
4_22_41: So it was, the next day, that Balak took Balaam and brought him up to the high places of Baal, that from there he might observe the extent of the people.
4_23_1: Then Balaam said to Balak, “Build seven altars for me here, and prepare for me here seven bulls and seven rams.”
4_23_2: And Balak did just as Balaam had spoken, and Balak and Balaam offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
4_23_3: Then Balaam said to Balak, “Stand by your burnt offering, and I will go; perhaps the LORD will come to meet me, and whatever He shows me I will tell you.” So he went to a desolate height.
4_23_4: And God met Balaam, and he said to Him, “I have prepared the seven altars, and I have offered on each altar a bull and a ram.”
4_23_5: Then the LORD put a word in Balaam’s mouth, and said, “Return to Balak, and thus you shall speak.”
4_23_6: So he returned to him, and there he was, standing by his burnt offering, he and all the princes of Moab.
4_23_7: And he took up his oracle and said: “Balak the king of Moab has brought me from Aram, From the mountains of the east. ‘Come, curse Jacob for me, And come, denounce Israel!’
4_23_8: “How shall I curse whom God has not cursed? And how shall I denounce whom the LORD has not denounced?
4_23_9: For from the top of the rocks I see him, And from the hills I behold him; There! A people dwelling alone, Not reckoning itself among the nations.
4_23_10: “Who can count the dust of Jacob, Or number one-fourth of Israel? Let me die the death of the righteous, And let my end be like his!”
4_23_11: Then Balak said to Balaam, “What have you done to me? I took you to curse my enemies, and look, you have blessed them bountifully!”
4_23_12: So he answered and said, “Must I not take heed to speak what the LORD has put in my mouth?”
4_23_13: Then Balak said to him, “Please come with me to another place from which you may see them; you shall see only the outer part of them, and shall not see them all; curse them for me from there.”
4_23_14: So he brought him to the field of Zophim, to the top of Pisgah, and built seven altars, and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
4_23_15: And he said to Balak, “Stand here by your burnt offering while I meet the LORD over there.”
4_23_16: Then the LORD met Balaam, and put a word in his mouth, and said, “Go back to Balak, and thus you shall speak.”
4_23_17: So he came to him, and there he was, standing by his burnt offering, and the princes of Moab were with him. And Balak said to him, “What has the LORD spoken?”
4_23_18: Then he took up his oracle and said: “Rise up, Balak, and hear! Listen to me, son of Zippor!
4_23_19: “God is not a man, that He should lie, Nor a son of man, that He should repent. Has He said, and will He not do? Or has He spoken, and will He not make it good?
4_23_20: Behold, I have received a command to bless; He has blessed, and I cannot reverse it.
4_23_21: “He has not observed iniquity in Jacob, Nor has He seen wickedness in Israel. The LORD his God is with him, And the shout of a King is among them.
4_23_22: God brings them out of Egypt; He has strength like a wild ox.
4_23_23: “For there is no sorcery against Jacob, Nor any divination against Israel. It now must be said of Jacob And of Israel, ‘Oh, what God has done!’
4_23_24: Look, a people rises like a lioness, And lifts itself up like a lion; It shall not lie down until it devours the prey, And drinks the blood of the slain.”
4_23_25: Then Balak said to Balaam, “Neither curse them at all, nor bless them at all!”
4_23_26: So Balaam answered and said to Balak, “Did I not tell you, saying, ‘All that the LORD speaks, that I must do’?”
4_23_27: Then Balak said to Balaam, “Please come, I will take you to another place; perhaps it will please God that you may curse them for me from there.”
4_23_28: So Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, that overlooks the wasteland.
4_23_29: Then Balaam said to Balak, “Build for me here seven altars, and prepare for me here seven bulls and seven rams.”
4_23_30: And Balak did as Balaam had said, and offered a bull and a ram on every altar.
4_24_1: Now when Balaam saw that it pleased the LORD to bless Israel, he did not go as at other times, to seek to use sorcery, but he set his face toward the wilderness.
4_24_2: And Balaam raised his eyes, and saw Israel encamped according to their tribes; and the Spirit of God came upon him.
4_24_3: Then he took up his oracle and said: “The utterance of Balaam the son of Beor, The utterance of the man whose eyes are opened
4_24_4: The utterance of him who hears the words of God, Who sees the vision of the Almighty, Who falls down, with eyes wide open:
4_24_5: “How lovely are your tents, O Jacob! Your dwellings, O Israel!
4_24_6: Like valleys that stretch out, Like gardens by the riverside, Like aloes planted by the LORD, Like cedars beside the waters.
4_24_7: He shall pour water from his buckets, And his seed shall be in many waters. “His king shall be higher than Agag, And his kingdom shall be exalted.
4_24_8: “God brings him out of Egypt; He has strength like a wild ox; He shall consume the nations, his enemies; He shall break their bones And pierce them with his arrows.
4_24_9: ‘He bows down, he lies down as a lion; And as a lion, who shall rouse him?’ “Blessed is he who blesses you, And cursed is he who curses you.”
4_24_10: Then Balak’s anger was aroused against Balaam, and he struck his hands together; and Balak said to Balaam, “I called you to curse my enemies, and look, you have bountifully blessed them these three times!
4_24_11: Now therefore, flee to your place. I said I would greatly honor you, but in fact, the LORD has kept you back from honor.”
4_24_12: So Balaam said to Balak, “Did I not also speak to your messengers whom you sent to me, saying
4_24_13: ‘If Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the word of the LORD, to do good or bad of my own will. What the LORD says, that I must speak’?
4_24_14: And now, indeed, I am going to my people. Come, I will advise you what this people will do to your people in the latter days.”
4_24_15: So he took up his oracle and said: “The utterance of Balaam the son of Beor, And the utterance of the man whose eyes are opened
4_24_16: The utterance of him who hears the words of God, And has the knowledge of the Most High, Who sees the vision of the Almighty, Who falls down, with eyes wide open:
4_24_17: “I see Him, but not now; I behold Him, but not near; A Star shall come out of Jacob; A Scepter shall rise out of Israel, And batter the brow of Moab, And destroy all the sons of tumult.
4_24_18: “And Edom shall be a possession; Seir also, his enemies, shall be a possession, While Israel does valiantly.
4_24_19: Out of Jacob One shall have dominion, And destroy the remains of the city.”
4_24_20: Then he looked on Amalek, and he took up his oracle and said: “Amalek was first among the nations, But shall be last until he perishes.”
4_24_21: Then he looked on the Kenites, and he took up his oracle and said: “Firm is your dwelling place, And your nest is set in the rock
4_24_22: Nevertheless Kain shall be burned. How long until Asshur carries you away captive?”
4_24_23: Then he took up his oracle and said: “Alas! Who shall live when God does this?
4_24_24: But ships shall come from the coasts of Cyprus, And they shall afflict Asshur and afflict Eber, And so shall Amalek, until he perishes.”
4_24_25: So Balaam rose and departed and returned to his place; Balak also went his way.
4_25_1: Now Israel remained in Acacia Grove, and the people began to commit harlotry with the women of Moab.
4_25_2: They invited the people to the sacrifices of their gods, and the people ate and bowed down to their gods.
4_25_3: So Israel was joined to Baal of Peor, and the anger of the LORD was aroused against Israel.
4_25_4: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Take all the leaders of the people and hang the offenders before the LORD, out in the sun, that the fierce anger of the LORD may turn away from Israel.”
4_25_5: So Moses said to the judges of Israel, “Every one of you kill his men who were joined to Baal of Peor.”
4_25_6: And indeed, one of the children of Israel came and presented to his brethren a Midianite woman in the sight of Moses and in the sight of all the congregation of the children of Israel, who were weeping at the door of the tabernacle of meeting.
4_25_7: Now when Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose from among the congregation and took a javelin in his hand
4_25_8: and he went after the man of Israel into the tent and thrust both of them through, the man of Israel, and the woman through her body. So the plague was stopped among the children of Israel.
4_25_9: And those who died in the plague were twenty-four thousand.
4_25_10: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
4_25_11: “Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, has turned back My wrath from the children of Israel, because he was zealous with My zeal among them, so that I did not consume the children of Israel in My zeal.
4_25_12: Therefore say, ‘Behold, I give to him My covenant of peace
4_25_13: and it shall be to him and his descendants after him a covenant of an everlasting priesthood, because he was zealous for his God, and made atonement for the children of Israel.’ ”
4_25_14: Now the name of the Israelite who was killed, who was killed with the Midianite woman, was Zimri the son of Salu, a leader of a father’s house among the Simeonites.
4_25_15: And the name of the Midianite woman who was killed was Cozbi the daughter of Zur; he was head of the people of a father’s house in Midian.
4_25_16: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
4_25_18: for they harassed you with their schemes by which they seduced you in the matter of Peor and in the matter of Cozbi, the daughter of a leader of Midian, their sister, who was killed in the day of the plague because of Peor.”
4_26_1: And it came to pass, after the plague, that the LORD spoke to Moses and Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest, saying:
4_26_2: “Take a census of all the congregation of the children of Israel from twenty years old and above, by their fathers’ houses, all who are able to go to war in Israel.”
4_26_3: So Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke with them in the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho, saying:
4_26_4: “Take a census of the people from twenty years old and above, just as the LORD commanded Moses and the children of Israel who came out of the land of Egypt.”
4_26_5: Reuben was the firstborn of Israel. The children of Reuben were: of Hanoch, the family of the Hanochites; of Pallu, the family of the Palluites
4_26_6: of Hezron, the family of the Hezronites; of Carmi, the family of the Carmites.
4_26_7: These are the families of the Reubenites: those who were numbered of them were forty-three thousand seven hundred and thirty.
4_26_8: And the son of Pallu was Eliab.
4_26_9: The sons of Eliab were Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These are the Dathan and Abiram, representatives of the congregation, who contended against Moses and Aaron in the company of Korah, when they contended against the LORD
4_26_10: and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up together with Korah when that company died, when the fire devoured two hundred and fifty men; and they became a sign.
4_26_11: Nevertheless the children of Korah did not die.
4_26_12: The sons of Simeon according to their families were: of Nemuel, the family of the Nemuelites; of Jamin, the family of the Jaminites; of Jachin, the family of the Jachinites
4_26_13: of Zerah, the family of the Zarhites; of Shaul, the family of the Shaulites.
4_26_14: These are the families of the Simeonites: twenty-two thousand two hundred.
4_26_15: The sons of Gad according to their families were: of Zephon, the family of the Zephonites; of Haggi, the family of the Haggites; of Shuni, the family of the Shunites
4_26_16: of Ozni, the family of the Oznites; of Eri, the family of the Erites
4_26_17: of Arod, the family of the Arodites; of Areli, the family of the Arelites.
4_26_18: These are the families of the sons of Gad according to those who were numbered of them: forty thousand five hundred.
4_26_19: The sons of Judah were Er and Onan; and Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.
4_26_20: And the sons of Judah according to their families were: of Shelah, the family of the Shelanites; of Perez, the family of the Parzites; of Zerah, the family of the Zarhites.
4_26_21: And the sons of Perez were: of Hezron, the family of the Hezronites; of Hamul, the family of the Hamulites.
4_26_22: These are the families of Judah according to those who were numbered of them: seventy-six thousand five hundred.
4_26_23: The sons of Issachar according to their families were: of Tola, the family of the Tolaites; of Puah, the family of the Punites
4_26_24: of Jashub, the family of the Jashubites; of Shimron, the family of the Shimronites.
4_26_25: These are the families of Issachar according to those who were numbered of them: sixty-four thousand three hundred.
4_26_26: The sons of Zebulun according to their families were: of Sered, the family of the Sardites; of Elon, the family of the Elonites; of Jahleel, the family of the Jahleelites.
4_26_27: These are the families of the Zebulunites according to those who were numbered of them: sixty thousand five hundred.
4_26_28: The sons of Joseph according to their families, by Manasseh and Ephraim, were:
4_26_29: The sons of Manasseh: of Machir, the family of the Machirites; and Machir begot Gilead; of Gilead, the family of the Gileadites.
4_26_30: These are the sons of Gilead: of Jeezer, the family of the Jeezerites; of Helek, the family of the Helekites
4_26_31: of Asriel, the family of the Asrielites; of Shechem, the family of the Shechemites
4_26_32: of Shemida, the family of the Shemidaites; of Hepher, the family of the Hepherites.
4_26_33: Now Zelophehad the son of Hepher had no sons, but daughters; and the names of the daughters of Zelophehad were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
4_26_34: These are the families of Manasseh; and those who were numbered of them were fifty-two thousand seven hundred.
4_26_35: These are the sons of Ephraim according to their families: of Shuthelah, the family of the Shuthalhites; of Becher, the family of the Bachrites; of Tahan, the family of the Tahanites.
4_26_36: And these are the sons of Shuthelah: of Eran, the family of the Eranites.
4_26_37: These are the families of the sons of Ephraim according to those who were numbered of them: thirty-two thousand five hundred. These are the sons of Joseph according to their families.
4_26_38: The sons of Benjamin according to their families were: of Bela, the family of the Belaites; of Ashbel, the family of the Ashbelites; of Ahiram, the family of the Ahiramites
4_26_39: of Shupham, the family of the Shuphamites; of Hupham, the family of the Huphamites.
4_26_40: And the sons of Bela were Ard and Naaman: of Ard, the family of the Ardites; of Naaman, the family of the Naamites.
4_26_41: These are the sons of Benjamin according to their families; and those who were numbered of them were forty-five thousand six hundred.
4_26_42: These are the sons of Dan according to their families: of Shuham, the family of the Shuhamites. These are the families of Dan according to their families.
4_26_43: All the families of the Shuhamites, according to those who were numbered of them, were sixty-four thousand four hundred.
4_26_44: The sons of Asher according to their families were: of Jimna, the family of the Jimnites; of Jesui, the family of the Jesuites; of Beriah, the family of the Beriites.
4_26_45: Of the sons of Beriah: of Heber, the family of the Heberites; of Malchiel, the family of the Malchielites.
4_26_46: And the name of the daughter of Asher was Serah.
4_26_47: These are the families of the sons of Asher according to those who were numbered of them: fifty-three thousand four hundred.
4_26_48: The sons of Naphtali according to their families were: of Jahzeel, the family of the Jahzeelites; of Guni, the family of the Gunites
4_26_49: of Jezer, the family of the Jezerites; of Shillem, the family of the Shillemites.
4_26_50: These are the families of Naphtali according to their families; and those who were numbered of them were forty-five thousand four hundred.
4_26_51: These are those who were numbered of the children of Israel: six hundred and one thousand seven hundred and thirty.
4_26_52: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
4_26_53: “To these the land shall be divided as an inheritance, according to the number of names.
4_26_54: To a large tribe you shall give a larger inheritance, and to a small tribe you shall give a smaller inheritance. Each shall be given its inheritance according to those who were numbered of them.
4_26_55: But the land shall be divided by lot; they shall inherit according to the names of the tribes of their fathers.
4_26_56: According to the lot their inheritance shall be divided between the larger and the smaller.”
4_26_57: And these are those who were numbered of the Levites according to their families: of Gershon, the family of the Gershonites; of Kohath, the family of the Kohathites; of Merari, the family of the Merarites.
4_26_58: These are the families of the Levites: the family of the Libnites, the family of the Hebronites, the family of the Mahlites, the family of the Mushites, and the family of the Korathites. And Kohath begot Amram.
4_26_59: The name of Amram’s wife was Jochebed the daughter of Levi, who was born to Levi in Egypt; and to Amram she bore Aaron and Moses and their sister Miriam.
4_26_60: To Aaron were born Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
4_26_61: And Nadab and Abihu died when they offered profane fire before the LORD.
4_26_62: Now those who were numbered of them were twenty-three thousand, every male from a month old and above; for they were not numbered among the other children of Israel, because there was no inheritance given to them among the children of Israel.
4_26_63: These are those who were numbered by Moses and Eleazar the priest, who numbered the children of Israel in the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho.
4_26_64: But among these there was not a man of those who were numbered by Moses and Aaron the priest when they numbered the children of Israel in the Wilderness of Sinai.
4_26_65: For the LORD had said of them, “They shall surely die in the wilderness.” So there was not left a man of them, except Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun.
4_27_1: Then came the daughters of Zelophehad the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, from the families of Manasseh the son of Joseph; and these were the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
4_27_2: And they stood before Moses, before Eleazar the priest, and before the leaders and all the congregation, by the doorway of the tabernacle of meeting, saying:
4_27_3: “Our father died in the wilderness; but he was not in the company of those who gathered together against the LORD, in company with Korah, but he died in his own sin; and he had no sons.
4_27_4: Why should the name of our father be removed from among his family because he had no son? Give us a possession among our father’s brothers.”
4_27_5: So Moses brought their case before the LORD.
4_27_6: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
4_27_7: “The daughters of Zelophehad speak what is right; you shall surely give them a possession of inheritance among their father’s brothers, and cause the inheritance of their father to pass to them.
4_27_8: And you shall speak to the children of Israel, saying: ‘If a man dies and has no son, then you shall cause his inheritance to pass to his daughter.
4_27_9: If he has no daughter, then you shall give his inheritance to his brothers.
4_27_10: If he has no brothers, then you shall give his inheritance to his father’s brothers.
4_27_11: And if his father has no brothers, then you shall give his inheritance to the relative closest to him in his family, and he shall possess it.’ ” And it shall be to the children of Israel a statute of judgment, just as the LORD commanded Moses.
4_27_12: Now the LORD said to Moses: “Go up into this Mount Abarim, and see the land which I have given to the children of Israel.
4_27_13: And when you have seen it, you also shall be gathered to your people, as Aaron your brother was gathered.
4_27_14: For in the Wilderness of Zin, during the strife of the congregation, you rebelled against My command to hallow Me at the waters before their eyes.” (These are the waters of Meribah, at Kadesh in the Wilderness of Zin.)
4_27_15: Then Moses spoke to the LORD, saying:
4_27_16: “Let the LORD, the God of the spirits of all flesh, set a man over the congregation
4_27_17: who may go out before them and go in before them, who may lead them out and bring them in, that the congregation of the LORD may not be like sheep which have no shepherd.”
4_27_18: And the LORD said to Moses: “Take Joshua the son of Nun with you, a man in whom is the Spirit, and lay your hand on him
4_27_19: set him before Eleazar the priest and before all the congregation, and inaugurate him in their sight.
4_27_20: And you shall give some of your authority to him, that all the congregation of the children of Israel may be obedient.
4_27_21: He shall stand before Eleazar the priest, who shall inquire before the LORD for him by the judgment of the Urim. At his word they shall go out, and at his word they shall come in, he and all the children of Israel with him—all the congregation.”
4_27_22: So Moses did as the LORD commanded him. He took Joshua and set him before Eleazar the priest and before all the congregation.
4_27_23: And he laid his hands on him and inaugurated him, just as the LORD commanded by the hand of Moses.
4_28_1: Now the LORD spoke to Moses, saying
4_28_2: “Command the children of Israel, and say to them, ‘My offering, My food for My offerings made by fire as a sweet aroma to Me, you shall be careful to offer to Me at their appointed time.’
4_28_3: “And you shall say to them, ‘This is the offering made by fire which you shall offer to the LORD: two male lambs in their first year without blemish, day by day, as a regular burnt offering.
4_28_4: The one lamb you shall offer in the morning, the other lamb you shall offer in the evening
4_28_5: and one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a grain offering mixed with one-fourth of a hin of pressed oil.
4_28_6: It is a regular burnt offering which was ordained at Mount Sinai for a sweet aroma, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
4_28_7: And its drink offering shall be one-fourth of a hin for each lamb; in a holy place you shall pour out the drink to the LORD as an offering.
4_28_8: The other lamb you shall offer in the evening; as the morning grain offering and its drink offering, you shall offer it as an offering made by fire, a sweet aroma to the LORD.
4_28_9: ‘And on the Sabbath day two lambs in their first year, without blemish, and two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour as a grain offering, mixed with oil, with its drink offering—
4_28_10: this is the burnt offering for every Sabbath, besides the regular burnt offering with its drink offering.
4_28_11: ‘At the beginnings of your months you shall present a burnt offering to the LORD: two young bulls, one ram, and seven lambs in their first year, without blemish
4_28_12: three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour as a grain offering, mixed with oil, for each bull; two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour as a grain offering, mixed with oil, for the one ram
4_28_13: and one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour, mixed with oil, as a grain offering for each lamb, as a burnt offering of sweet aroma, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
4_28_14: Their drink offering shall be half a hin of wine for a bull, one-third of a hin for a ram, and one-fourth of a hin for a lamb; this is the burnt offering for each month throughout the months of the year.
4_28_15: Also one kid of the goats as a sin offering to the LORD shall be offered, besides the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.
4_28_16: ‘On the fourteenth day of the first month is the Passover of the LORD.
4_28_17: And on the fifteenth day of this month is the feast; unleavened bread shall be eaten for seven days.
4_28_18: On the first day you shall have a holy convocation. You shall do no customary work.
4_28_19: And you shall present an offering made by fire as a burnt offering to the LORD: two young bulls, one ram, and seven lambs in their first year. Be sure they are without blemish.
4_28_20: Their grain offering shall be of fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths of an ephah you shall offer for a bull, and two-tenths for a ram
4_28_21: you shall offer one-tenth of an ephah for each of the seven lambs
4_28_22: also one goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for you.
4_28_23: You shall offer these besides the burnt offering of the morning, which is for a regular burnt offering.
4_28_24: In this manner you shall offer the food of the offering made by fire daily for seven days, as a sweet aroma to the LORD; it shall be offered besides the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.
4_28_25: And on the seventh day you shall have a holy convocation. You shall do no customary work.
4_28_26: ‘Also on the day of the firstfruits, when you bring a new grain offering to the LORD at your Feast of Weeks, you shall have a holy convocation. You shall do no customary work.
4_28_27: You shall present a burnt offering as a sweet aroma to the LORD: two young bulls, one ram, and seven lambs in their first year
4_28_28: with their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths of an ephah for each bull, two-tenths for the one ram
4_28_29: and one-tenth for each of the seven lambs
4_28_30: also one kid of the goats, to make atonement for you.
4_28_31: Be sure they are without blemish. You shall present them with their drink offerings, besides the regular burnt offering with its grain offering.
4_29_1: ‘And in the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall have a holy convocation. You shall do no customary work. For you it is a day of blowing the trumpets.
4_29_2: You shall offer a burnt offering as a sweet aroma to the LORD: one young bull, one ram, and seven lambs in their first year, without blemish.
4_29_3: Their grain offering shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths of an ephah for the bull, two-tenths for the ram
4_29_4: and one-tenth for each of the seven lambs
4_29_5: also one kid of the goats as a sin offering, to make atonement for you
4_29_6: besides the burnt offering with its grain offering for the New Moon, the regular burnt offering with its grain offering, and their drink offerings, according to their ordinance, as a sweet aroma, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
4_29_7: ‘On the tenth day of this seventh month you shall have a holy convocation. You shall afflict your souls; you shall not do any work.
4_29_8: You shall present a burnt offering to the LORD as a sweet aroma: one young bull, one ram, and seven lambs in their first year. Be sure they are without blemish.
4_29_9: Their grain offering shall be of fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths of an ephah for the bull, two-tenths for the one ram
4_29_10: and one-tenth for each of the seven lambs
4_29_11: also one kid of the goats as a sin offering, besides the sin offering for atonement, the regular burnt offering with its grain offering, and their drink offerings.
4_29_12: ‘On the fifteenth day of the seventh month you shall have a holy convocation. You shall do no customary work, and you shall keep a feast to the LORD seven days.
4_29_13: You shall present a burnt offering, an offering made by fire as a sweet aroma to the LORD: thirteen young bulls, two rams, and fourteen lambs in their first year. They shall be without blemish.
4_29_14: Their grain offering shall be of fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths of an ephah for each of the thirteen bulls, two-tenths for each of the two rams
4_29_15: and one-tenth for each of the fourteen lambs
4_29_16: also one kid of the goats as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
4_29_17: ‘On the second day present twelve young bulls, two rams, fourteen lambs in their first year without blemish
4_29_18: and their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, by their number, according to the ordinance
4_29_19: also one kid of the goats as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering with its grain offering, and their drink offerings.
4_29_20: ‘On the third day present eleven bulls, two rams, fourteen lambs in their first year without blemish
4_29_21: and their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, by their number, according to the ordinance
4_29_22: also one goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
4_29_23: ‘On the fourth day present ten bulls, two rams, and fourteen lambs in their first year, without blemish
4_29_24: and their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, by their number, according to the ordinance
4_29_25: also one kid of the goats as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
4_29_26: ‘On the fifth day present nine bulls, two rams, and fourteen lambs in their first year without blemish
4_29_27: and their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, by their number, according to the ordinance
4_29_28: also one goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
4_29_29: ‘On the sixth day present eight bulls, two rams, and fourteen lambs in their first year without blemish
4_29_30: and their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, by their number, according to the ordinance
4_29_31: also one goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
4_29_32: ‘On the seventh day present seven bulls, two rams, and fourteen lambs in their first year without blemish
4_29_33: and their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs, by their number, according to the ordinance
4_29_34: also one goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
4_29_35: ‘On the eighth day you shall have a sacred assembly. You shall do no customary work.
4_29_36: You shall present a burnt offering, an offering made by fire as a sweet aroma to the LORD: one bull, one ram, seven lambs in their first year without blemish
4_29_37: and their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bull, for the ram, and for the lambs, by their number, according to the ordinance
4_29_38: also one goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
4_29_39: ‘These you shall present to the LORD at your appointed feasts (besides your vowed offerings and your freewill offerings) as your burnt offerings and your grain offerings, as your drink offerings and your peace offerings.’ ”
4_29_40: So Moses told the children of Israel everything, just as the LORD commanded Moses.
4_30_1: Then Moses spoke to the heads of the tribes concerning the children of Israel, saying, “This is the thing which the LORD has commanded:
4_30_2: If a man makes a vow to the LORD, or swears an oath to bind himself by some agreement, he shall not break his word; he shall do according to all that proceeds out of his mouth.
4_30_3: “Or if a woman makes a vow to the LORD, and binds herself by some agreement while in her father’s house in her youth
4_30_4: and her father hears her vow and the agreement by which she has bound herself, and her father holds his peace, then all her vows shall stand, and every agreement with which she has bound herself shall stand.
4_30_5: But if her father overrules her on the day that he hears, then none of her vows nor her agreements by which she has bound herself shall stand; and the LORD will release her, because her father overruled her.
4_30_6: “If indeed she takes a husband, while bound by her vows or by a rash utterance from her lips by which she bound herself
4_30_7: and her husband hears it, and makes no response to her on the day that he hears, then her vows shall stand, and her agreements by which she bound herself shall stand.
4_30_8: But if her husband overrules her on the day that he hears it, he shall make void her vow which she took and what she uttered with her lips, by which she bound herself, and the LORD will release her.
4_30_9: “Also any vow of a widow or a divorced woman, by which she has bound herself, shall stand against her.
4_30_10: “If she vowed in her husband’s house, or bound herself by an agreement with an oath
4_30_11: and her husband heard it, and made no response to her and did not overrule her, then all her vows shall stand, and every agreement by which she bound herself shall stand.
4_30_12: But if her husband truly made them void on the day he heard them, then whatever proceeded from her lips concerning her vows or concerning the agreement binding her, it shall not stand; her husband has made them void, and the LORD will release her.
4_30_13: Every vow and every binding oath to afflict her soul, her husband may confirm it, or her husband may make it void.
4_30_14: Now if her husband makes no response whatever to her from day to day, then he confirms all her vows or all the agreements that bind her; he confirms them, because he made no response to her on the day that he heard them.
4_30_15: But if he does make them void after he has heard them, then he shall bear her guilt.”
4_30_16: These are the statutes which the LORD commanded Moses, between a man and his wife, and between a father and his daughter in her youth in her father’s house.
4_31_1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
4_31_2: “Take vengeance on the Midianites for the children of Israel. Afterward you shall be gathered to your people.”
4_31_3: So Moses spoke to the people, saying, “Arm some of yourselves for war, and let them go against the Midianites to take vengeance for the LORD on Midian.
4_31_4: A thousand from each tribe of all the tribes of Israel you shall send to the war.”
4_31_5: So there were recruited from the divisions of Israel one thousand from each tribe, twelve thousand armed for war.
4_31_6: Then Moses sent them to the war, one thousand from each tribe; he sent them to the war with Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest, with the holy articles and the signal trumpets in his hand.
4_31_7: And they warred against the Midianites, just as the LORD commanded Moses, and they killed all the males.
4_31_8: They killed the kings of Midian with the rest of those who were killed— Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, the five kings of Midian. Balaam the son of Beor they also killed with the sword.
4_31_9: And the children of Israel took the women of Midian captive, with their little ones, and took as spoil all their cattle, all their flocks, and all their goods.
4_31_10: They also burned with fire all the cities where they dwelt, and all their forts.
4_31_11: And they took all the spoil and all the booty—of man and beast.
4_31_12: Then they brought the captives, the booty, and the spoil to Moses, to Eleazar the priest, and to the congregation of the children of Israel, to the camp in the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho.
4_31_13: And Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the congregation, went to meet them outside the camp.
4_31_14: But Moses was angry with the officers of the army, with the captains over thousands and captains over hundreds, who had come from the battle.
4_31_15: And Moses said to them: “Have you kept all the women alive?
4_31_16: Look, these women caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to trespass against the LORD in the incident of Peor, and there was a plague among the congregation of the LORD.
4_31_17: Now therefore, kill every male among the little ones, and kill every woman who has known a man intimately.
4_31_18: But keep alive for yourselves all the young girls who have not known a man intimately.
4_31_19: And as for you, remain outside the camp seven days; whoever has killed any person, and whoever has touched any slain, purify yourselves and your captives on the third day and on the seventh day.
4_31_20: Purify every garment, everything made of leather, everything woven of goats’ hair, and everything made of wood.”
4_31_21: Then Eleazar the priest said to the men of war who had gone to the battle, “This is the ordinance of the law which the LORD commanded Moses:
4_31_22: Only the gold, the silver, the bronze, the iron, the tin, and the lead
4_31_23: everything that can endure fire, you shall put through the fire, and it shall be clean; and it shall be purified with the water of purification. But all that cannot endure fire you shall put through water.
4_31_24: And you shall wash your clothes on the seventh day and be clean, and afterward you may come into the camp.”
4_31_25: Now the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
4_31_26: “Count up the plunder that was taken—of man and beast—you and Eleazar the priest and the chief fathers of the congregation
4_31_27: and divide the plunder into two parts, between those who took part in the war, who went out to battle, and all the congregation.
4_31_28: And levy a tribute for the LORD on the men of war who went out to battle: one of every five hundred of the persons, the cattle, the donkeys, and the sheep
4_31_29: take it from their half, and give it to Eleazar the priest as a heave offering to the LORD.
4_31_30: And from the children of Israel’s half you shall take one of every fifty, drawn from the persons, the cattle, the donkeys, and the sheep, from all the livestock, and give them to the Levites who keep charge of the tabernacle of the LORD.”
4_31_31: So Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the LORD commanded Moses.
4_31_32: The booty remaining from the plunder, which the men of war had taken, was six hundred and seventy-five thousand sheep
4_31_35: and thirty-two thousand persons in all, of women who had not known a man intimately.
4_31_36: And the half, the portion for those who had gone out to war, was in number three hundred and thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep
4_31_37: and the LORD’s tribute of the sheep was six hundred and seventy-five.
4_31_38: The cattle were thirty-six thousand, of which the LORD’s tribute was seventy-two.
4_31_39: The donkeys were thirty thousand five hundred, of which the LORD’s tribute was sixty-one.
4_31_40: The persons were sixteen thousand, of which the LORD’s tribute was thirty-two persons.
4_31_41: So Moses gave the tribute which was the LORD’s heave offering to Eleazar the priest, as the LORD commanded Moses.
4_31_42: And from the children of Israel’s half, which Moses separated from the men who fought—
4_31_43: now the half belonging to the congregation was three hundred and thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep
4_31_47: and from the children of Israel’s half Moses took one of every fifty, drawn from man and beast, and gave them to the Levites, who kept charge of the tabernacle of the LORD, as the LORD commanded Moses.
4_31_48: Then the officers who were over thousands of the army, the captains of thousands and captains of hundreds, came near to Moses
4_31_49: and they said to Moses, “Your servants have taken a count of the men of war who are under our command, and not a man of us is missing.
4_31_50: Therefore we have brought an offering for the LORD, what every man found of ornaments of gold: armlets and bracelets and signet rings and earrings and necklaces, to make atonement for ourselves before the LORD.”
4_31_51: So Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from them, all the fashioned ornaments.
4_31_52: And all the gold of the offering that they offered to the LORD, from the captains of thousands and captains of hundreds, was sixteen thousand seven hundred and fifty shekels.
4_31_53: (The men of war had taken spoil, every man for himself.)
4_31_54: And Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from the captains of thousands and of hundreds, and brought it into the tabernacle of meeting as a memorial for the children of Israel before the LORD.
4_32_1: Now the children of Reuben and the children of Gad had a very great multitude of livestock; and when they saw the land of Jazer and the land of Gilead, that indeed the region was a place for livestock
4_32_2: the children of Gad and the children of Reuben came and spoke to Moses, to Eleazar the priest, and to the leaders of the congregation, saying
4_32_3: “Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Shebam, Nebo, and Beon
4_32_4: the country which the LORD defeated before the congregation of Israel, is a land for livestock, and your servants have livestock.”
4_32_5: Therefore they said, “If we have found favor in your sight, let this land be given to your servants as a possession. Do not take us over the Jordan.”
4_32_6: And Moses said to the children of Gad and to the children of Reuben: “Shall your brethren go to war while you sit here?
4_32_7: Now why will you discourage the heart of the children of Israel from going over into the land which the LORD has given them?
4_32_8: Thus your fathers did when I sent them away from Kadesh Barnea to see the land.
4_32_9: For when they went up to the Valley of Eshcol and saw the land, they discouraged the heart of the children of Israel, so that they did not go into the land which the LORD had given them.
4_32_10: So the LORD’s anger was aroused on that day, and He swore an oath, saying
4_32_11: ‘Surely none of the men who came up from Egypt, from twenty years old and above, shall see the land of which I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, because they have not wholly followed Me
4_32_12: except Caleb the son of Jephunneh, the Kenizzite, and Joshua the son of Nun, for they have wholly followed the LORD.’
4_32_13: So the LORD’s anger was aroused against Israel, and He made them wander in the wilderness forty years, until all the generation that had done evil in the sight of the LORD was gone.
4_32_14: And look! You have risen in your fathers’ place, a brood of sinful men, to increase still more the fierce anger of the LORD against Israel.
4_32_15: For if you turn away from following Him, He will once again leave them in the wilderness, and you will destroy all these people.”
4_32_16: Then they came near to him and said: “We will build sheepfolds here for our livestock, and cities for our little ones
4_32_17: but we ourselves will be armed, ready to go before the children of Israel until we have brought them to their place; and our little ones will dwell in the fortified cities because of the inhabitants of the land.
4_32_18: We will not return to our homes until every one of the children of Israel has received his inheritance.
4_32_19: For we will not inherit with them on the other side of the Jordan and beyond, because our inheritance has fallen to us on this eastern side of the Jordan.”
4_32_20: Then Moses said to them: “If you do this thing, if you arm yourselves before the LORD for the war
4_32_21: and all your armed men cross over the Jordan before the LORD until He has driven out His enemies from before Him
4_32_22: and the land is subdued before the LORD, then afterward you may return and be blameless before the LORD and before Israel; and this land shall be your possession before the LORD.
4_32_23: But if you do not do so, then take note, you have sinned against the LORD; and be sure your sin will find you out.
4_32_24: Build cities for your little ones and folds for your sheep, and do what has proceeded out of your mouth.”
4_32_25: And the children of Gad and the children of Reuben spoke to Moses, saying: “Your servants will do as my lord commands.
4_32_26: Our little ones, our wives, our flocks, and all our livestock will be there in the cities of Gilead
4_32_27: but your servants will cross over, every man armed for war, before the LORD to battle, just as my lord says.”
4_32_28: So Moses gave command concerning them to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua the son of Nun, and to the chief fathers of the tribes of the children of Israel.
4_32_29: And Moses said to them: “If the children of Gad and the children of Reuben cross over the Jordan with you, every man armed for battle before the LORD, and the land is subdued before you, then you shall give them the land of Gilead as a possession.
4_32_30: But if they do not cross over armed with you, they shall have possessions among you in the land of Canaan.”
4_32_31: Then the children of Gad and the children of Reuben answered, saying: “As the LORD has said to your servants, so we will do.
4_32_32: We will cross over armed before the LORD into the land of Canaan, but the possession of our inheritance shall remain with us on this side of the Jordan.”
4_32_33: So Moses gave to the children of Gad, to the children of Reuben, and to half the tribe of Manasseh the son of Joseph, the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, the land with its cities within the borders, the cities of the surrounding country.
4_32_34: And the children of Gad built Dibon and Ataroth and Aroer
4_32_35: Atroth and Shophan and Jazer and Jogbehah
4_32_36: Beth Nimrah and Beth Haran, fortified cities, and folds for sheep.
4_32_37: And the children of Reuben built Heshbon and Elealeh and Kirjathaim
4_32_38: Nebo and Baal Meon (their names being changed) and Shibmah; and they gave other names to the cities which they built.
