16_7_60: All the Nethinim, and the sons of Solomon’s servants, were three hundred and ninety-two.
16_7_61: And these were the ones who came up from Tel Melah, Tel Harsha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer, but they could not identify their father’s house nor their lineage, whether they were of Israel:
16_7_62: the sons of Delaiah, the sons of Tobiah, the sons of Nekoda, six hundred and forty-two
16_7_63: and of the priests: the sons of Habaiah, the sons of Koz, the sons of Barzillai, who took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called by their name.
16_7_65: And the governor said to them that they should not eat of the most holy things till a priest could consult with the Urim and Thummim.
16_7_66: Altogether the whole assembly was forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty
16_7_67: besides their male and female servants, of whom there were seven thousand three hundred and thirty-seven; and they had two hundred and forty-five men and women singers.
16_7_68: Their horses were seven hundred and thirty-six, their mules two hundred and forty-five
16_7_69: their camels four hundred and thirty-five, and donkeys six thousand seven hundred and twenty.
16_7_70: And some of the heads of the fathers’ houses gave to the work. The governor gave to the treasury one thousand gold drachmas, fifty basins, and five hundred and thirty priestly garments.
16_7_71: Some of the heads of the fathers’ houses gave to the treasury of the work twenty thousand gold drachmas, and two thousand two hundred silver minas.
16_7_72: And that which the rest of the people gave was twenty thousand gold drachmas, two thousand silver minas, and sixty-seven priestly garments.
16_7_73: So the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, some of the people, the Nethinim, and all Israel dwelt in their cities. When the seventh month came, the children of Israel were in their cities.
16_8_1: Now all the people gathered together as one man in the open square that was in front of the Water Gate; and they told Ezra the scribe to bring the Book of the Law of Moses, which the LORD had commanded Israel.
16_8_2: So Ezra the priest brought the Law before the assembly of men and women and all who could hear with understanding on the first day of the seventh month.
16_8_3: Then he read from it in the open square that was in front of the Water Gate from morning until midday, before the men and women and those who could understand; and the ears of all the people were attentive to the Book of the Law.
16_8_4: So Ezra the scribe stood on a platform of wood which they had made for the purpose; and beside him, at his right hand, stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Urijah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah; and at his left hand Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbadana, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
16_8_5: And Ezra opened the book in the sight of all the people, for he was standing above all the people; and when he opened it, all the people stood up.
16_8_6: And Ezra blessed the LORD, the great God. Then all the people answered, “Amen, Amen!” while lifting up their hands. And they bowed their heads and worshiped the LORD with their faces to the ground.
16_8_7: Also Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodijah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the Levites, helped the people to understand the Law; and the people stood in their place.
16_8_8: So they read distinctly from the book, in the Law of God; and they gave the sense, and helped them to understand the reading.
16_8_9: And Nehemiah, who was the governor, Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who taught the people said to all the people, “This day is holy to the LORD your God; do not mourn nor weep.” For all the people wept, when they heard the words of the Law.
16_8_10: Then he said to them, “Go your way, eat the fat, drink the sweet, and send portions to those for whom nothing is prepared; for this day is holy to our Lord. Do not sorrow, for the joy of the LORD is your strength.”
16_8_11: So the Levites quieted all the people, saying, “Be still, for the day is holy; do not be grieved.”
16_8_12: And all the people went their way to eat and drink, to send portions and rejoice greatly, because they understood the words that were declared to them.
16_8_13: Now on the second day the heads of the fathers’ houses of all the people, with the priests and Levites, were gathered to Ezra the scribe, in order to understand the words of the Law.
16_8_14: And they found written in the Law, which the LORD had commanded by Moses, that the children of Israel should dwell in booths during the feast of the seventh month
16_8_15: and that they should announce and proclaim in all their cities and in Jerusalem, saying, “Go out to the mountain, and bring olive branches, branches of oil trees, myrtle branches, palm branches, and branches of leafy trees, to make booths, as it is written.”
16_8_16: Then the people went out and brought them and made themselves booths, each one on the roof of his house, or in their courtyards or the courts of the house of God, and in the open square of the Water Gate and in the open square of the Gate of Ephraim.
16_8_17: So the whole assembly of those who had returned from the captivity made booths and sat under the booths; for since the days of Joshua the son of Nun until that day the children of Israel had not done so. And there was very great gladness.
16_8_18: Also day by day, from the first day until the last day, he read from the Book of the Law of God. And they kept the feast seven days; and on the eighth day there was a sacred assembly, according to the prescribed manner.
16_9_1: Now on the twenty-fourth day of this month the children of Israel were assembled with fasting, in sackcloth, and with dust on their heads.
16_9_2: Then those of Israelite lineage separated themselves from all foreigners; and they stood and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers.
16_9_3: And they stood up in their place and read from the Book of the Law of the LORD their God for one–fourth of the day; and for another fourth they confessed and worshiped the LORD their God.
16_9_4: Then Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani stood on the stairs of the Levites and cried out with a loud voice to the LORD their God.
16_9_5: And the Levites, Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabniah, Sherebiah, Hodijah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah, said: “Stand up and bless the LORD your God Forever and ever! “Blessed be Your glorious name, Which is exalted above all blessing and praise!
16_9_6: You alone are the LORD; You have made heaven, The heaven of heavens, with all their host, The earth and everything on it, The seas and all that is in them, And You preserve them all. The host of heaven worships You.
16_9_7: “You are the LORD God, Who chose Abram, And brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans, And gave him the name Abraham
16_9_8: You found his heart faithful before You, And made a covenant with him To give the land of the Canaanites, The Hittites, the Amorites, The Perizzites, the Jebusites, And the Girgashites— To give it to his descendants. You have performed Your words, For You are righteous.
16_9_9: “You saw the affliction of our fathers in Egypt, And heard their cry by the Red Sea.
16_9_10: You showed signs and wonders against Pharaoh, Against all his servants, And against all the people of his land. For You knew that they acted proudly against them. So You made a name for Yourself, as it is this day.
16_9_11: And You divided the sea before them, So that they went through the midst of the sea on the dry land; And their persecutors You threw into the deep, As a stone into the mighty waters.
16_9_12: Moreover You led them by day with a cloudy pillar, And by night with a pillar of fire, To give them light on the road Which they should travel.
16_9_13: “You came down also on Mount Sinai, And spoke with them from heaven, And gave them just ordinances and true laws, Good statutes and commandments.
16_9_14: You made known to them Your holy Sabbath, And commanded them precepts, statutes and laws, By the hand of Moses Your servant.
16_9_15: You gave them bread from heaven for their hunger, And brought them water out of the rock for their thirst, And told them to go in to possess the land Which You had sworn to give them.
16_9_16: “But they and our fathers acted proudly, Hardened their necks, And did not heed Your commandments.
16_9_17: They refused to obey, And they were not mindful of Your wonders That You did among them. But they hardened their necks, And in their rebellion They appointed a leader To return to their bondage. But You are God, Ready to pardon, Gracious and merciful, Slow to anger, Abundant in kindness, And did not forsake them.
16_9_18: “Even when they made a molded calf for themselves, And said, ‘This is your god That brought you up out of Egypt,’ And worked great provocations
16_9_19: Yet in Your manifold mercies You did not forsake them in the wilderness. The pillar of the cloud did not depart from them by day, To lead them on the road; Nor the pillar of fire by night, To show them light, And the way they should go.
16_9_20: You also gave Your good Spirit to instruct them, And did not withhold Your manna from their mouth, And gave them water for their thirst.
16_9_21: Forty years You sustained them in the wilderness; They lacked nothing; Their clothes did not wear out And their feet did not swell.
16_9_22: “Moreover You gave them kingdoms and nations, And divided them into districts. So they took possession of the land of Sihon, The land of the king of Heshbon, And the land of Og king of Bashan.
16_9_23: You also multiplied their children as the stars of heaven, And brought them into the land Which You had told their fathers To go in and possess.
16_9_24: So the people went in And possessed the land; You subdued before them the inhabitants of the land, The Canaanites, And gave them into their hands, With their kings And the people of the land, That they might do with them as they wished.
16_9_25: And they took strong cities and a rich land, And possessed houses full of all goods, Cisterns already dug, vineyards, olive groves, And fruit trees in abundance. So they ate and were filled and grew fat, And delighted themselves in Your great goodness.
16_9_26: “Nevertheless they were disobedient And rebelled against You, Cast Your law behind their backs And killed Your prophets, who testified against them To turn them to Yourself; And they worked great provocations.
16_9_27: Therefore You delivered them into the hand of their enemies, Who oppressed them; And in the time of their trouble, When they cried to You, You heard from heaven; And according to Your abundant mercies You gave them deliverers who saved them From the hand of their enemies.
16_9_28: “But after they had rest, They again did evil before You. Therefore You left them in the hand of their enemies, So that they had dominion over them; Yet when they returned and cried out to You, You heard from heaven; And many times You delivered them according to Your mercies
16_9_29: And testified against them, That You might bring them back to Your law. Yet they acted proudly, And did not heed Your commandments, But sinned against Your judgments, ‘Which if a man does, he shall live by them.’ And they shrugged their shoulders, Stiffened their necks, And would not hear.
16_9_30: Yet for many years You had patience with them, And testified against them by Your Spirit in Your prophets. Yet they would not listen; Therefore You gave them into the hand of the peoples of the lands.
16_9_31: Nevertheless in Your great mercy You did not utterly consume them nor forsake them; For You are God, gracious and merciful.
16_9_32: “Now therefore, our God, The great, the mighty, and awesome God, Who keeps covenant and mercy: Do not let all the trouble seem small before You That has come upon us, Our kings and our princes, Our priests and our prophets, Our fathers and on all Your people, From the days of the kings of Assyria until this day.
16_9_33: However You are just in all that has befallen us; For You have dealt faithfully, But we have done wickedly.
16_9_34: Neither our kings nor our princes, Our priests nor our fathers, Have kept Your law, Nor heeded Your commandments and Your testimonies, With which You testified against them.
16_9_35: For they have not served You in their kingdom, Or in the many good things that You gave them, Or in the large and rich land which You set before them; Nor did they turn from their wicked works.
16_9_36: “Here we are, servants today! And the land that You gave to our fathers, To eat its fruit and its bounty, Here we are, servants in it!
16_9_37: And it yields much increase to the kings You have set over us, Because of our sins; Also they have dominion over our bodies and our cattle At their pleasure; And we are in great distress.
16_9_38: “And because of all this, We make a sure covenant and write it; Our leaders, our Levites, and our priests seal it.”

16_10_29: these joined with their brethren, their nobles, and entered into a curse and an oath to walk in God’s Law, which was given by Moses the servant of God, and to observe and do all the commandments of the LORD our Lord, and His ordinances and His statutes:
16_10_30: We would not give our daughters as wives to the peoples of the land, nor take their daughters for our sons
16_10_31: if the peoples of the land brought wares or any grain to sell on the Sabbath day, we would not buy it from them on the Sabbath, or on a holy day; and we would forego the seventh year’s produce and the exacting of every debt.
16_10_32: Also we made ordinances for ourselves, to exact from ourselves yearly one-third of a shekel for the service of the house of our God:
16_10_33: for the showbread, for the regular grain offering, for the regular burnt offering of the Sabbaths, the New Moons, and the set feasts; for the holy things, for the sin offerings to make atonement for Israel, and all the work of the house of our God.
16_10_34: We cast lots among the priests, the Levites, and the people, for bringing the wood offering into the house of our God, according to our fathers’ houses, at the appointed times year by year, to burn on the altar of the LORD our God as it is written in the Law.
16_10_35: And we made ordinances to bring the firstfruits of our ground and the firstfruits of all fruit of all trees, year by year, to the house of the LORD
16_10_36: to bring the firstborn of our sons and our cattle, as it is written in the Law, and the firstborn of our herds and our flocks, to the house of our God, to the priests who minister in the house of our God
16_10_37: to bring the firstfruits of our dough, our offerings, the fruit from all kinds of trees, the new wine and oil, to the priests, to the storerooms of the house of our God; and to bring the tithes of our land to the Levites, for the Levites should receive the tithes in all our farming communities.
16_10_38: And the priest, the descendant of Aaron, shall be with the Levites when the Levites receive tithes; and the Levites shall bring up a tenth of the tithes to the house of our God, to the rooms of the storehouse.
16_10_39: For the children of Israel and the children of Levi shall bring the offering of the grain, of the new wine and the oil, to the storerooms where the articles of the sanctuary are, where the priests who minister and the gatekeepers and the singers are; and we will not neglect the house of our God.

16_13_1: On that day they read from the Book of Moses in the hearing of the people, and in it was found written that no Ammonite or Moabite should ever come into the assembly of God

16_13_6: But during all this I was not in Jerusalem, for in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I had returned to the king. Then after certain days I obtained leave from the king
16_13_7: and I came to Jerusalem and discovered the evil that Eliashib had done for Tobiah, in preparing a room for him in the courts of the house of God.
16_13_8: And it grieved me bitterly; therefore I threw all the household goods of Tobiah out of the room.
16_13_9: Then I commanded them to cleanse the rooms; and I brought back into them the articles of the house of God, with the grain offering and the frankincense.
16_13_10: I also realized that the portions for the Levites had not been given them; for each of the Levites and the singers who did the work had gone back to his field.
16_13_11: So I contended with the rulers, and said, “Why is the house of God forsaken?” And I gathered them together and set them in their place.
16_13_12: Then all Judah brought the tithe of the grain and the new wine and the oil to the storehouse.
16_13_13: And I appointed as treasurers over the storehouse Shelemiah the priest and Zadok the scribe, and of the Levites, Pedaiah; and next to them was Hanan the son of Zaccur, the son of Mattaniah; for they were considered faithful, and their task was to distribute to their brethren.
16_13_14: Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and do not wipe out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God, and for its services!
16_13_15: In those days I saw people in Judah treading wine presses on the Sabbath, and bringing in sheaves, and loading donkeys with wine, grapes, figs, and all kinds of burdens, which they brought into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day. And I warned them about the day on which they were selling provisions.
16_13_16: Men of Tyre dwelt there also, who brought in fish and all kinds of goods, and sold them on the Sabbath to the children of Judah, and in Jerusalem.
16_13_17: Then I contended with the nobles of Judah, and said to them, “What evil thing is this that you do, by which you profane the Sabbath day?
16_13_18: Did not your fathers do thus, and did not our God bring all this disaster on us and on this city? Yet you bring added wrath on Israel by profaning the Sabbath.”
16_13_19: So it was, at the gates of Jerusalem, as it began to be dark before the Sabbath, that I commanded the gates to be shut, and charged that they must not be opened till after the Sabbath. Then I posted some of my servants at the gates, so that no burdens would be brought in on the Sabbath day.
16_13_20: Now the merchants and sellers of all kinds of wares lodged outside Jerusalem once or twice.
16_13_21: Then I warned them, and said to them, “Why do you spend the night around the wall? If you do so again, I will lay hands on you!” From that time on they came no more on the Sabbath.
16_13_22: And I commanded the Levites that they should cleanse themselves, and that they should go and guard the gates, to sanctify the Sabbath day. Remember me, O my God, concerning this also, and spare me according to the greatness of Your mercy!
16_13_23: In those days I also saw Jews who had married women of Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.
16_13_24: And half of their children spoke the language of Ashdod, and could not speak the language of Judah, but spoke according to the language of one or the other people.
16_13_25: So I contended with them and cursed them, struck some of them and pulled out their hair, and made them swear by God, saying, “You shall not give your daughters as wives to their sons, nor take their daughters for your sons or yourselves.
16_13_26: Did not Solomon king of Israel sin by these things? Yet among many nations there was no king like him, who was beloved of his God; and God made him king over all Israel. Nevertheless pagan women caused even him to sin.
16_13_27: Should we then hear of your doing all this great evil, transgressing against our God by marrying pagan women?”
16_13_28: And one of the sons of Joiada, the son of Eliashib the high priest, was a son-in-law of Sanballat the Horonite; therefore I drove him from me.
16_13_29: Remember them, O my God, because they have defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and the Levites.
16_13_30: Thus I cleansed them of everything pagan. I also assigned duties to the priests and the Levites, each to his service
16_13_31: and to bringing the wood offering and the firstfruits at appointed times. Remember me, O my God, for good!
17_1_1: Now it came to pass in the days of Ahasuerus (this was the Ahasuerus who reigned over one hundred and twenty-seven provinces, from India to Ethiopia)
17_1_2: in those days when King Ahasuerus sat on the throne of his kingdom, which was in Shushan the citadel
17_1_3: that in the third year of his reign he made a feast for all his officials and servants—the powers of Persia and Media, the nobles, and the princes of the provinces being before him—
17_1_4: when he showed the riches of his glorious kingdom and the splendor of his excellent majesty for many days, one hundred and eighty days in all.
17_1_5: And when these days were completed, the king made a feast lasting seven days for all the people who were present in Shushan the citadel, from great to small, in the court of the garden of the king’s palace.
17_1_6: There were white and blue linen curtains fastened with cords of fine linen and purple on silver rods and marble pillars; and the couches were of gold and silver on a mosaic pavement of alabaster, turquoise, and white and black marble.
17_1_7: And they served drinks in golden vessels, each vessel being different from the other, with royal wine in abundance, according to the generosity of the king.
17_1_8: In accordance with the law, the drinking was not compulsory; for so the king had ordered all the officers of his household, that they should do according to each man’s pleasure.
17_1_9: Queen Vashti also made a feast for the women in the royal palace which belonged to King Ahasuerus.
17_1_10: On the seventh day, when the heart of the king was merry with wine, he commanded Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcas, seven eunuchs who served in the presence of King Ahasuerus
17_1_11: to bring Queen Vashti before the king, wearing her royal crown, in order to show her beauty to the people and the officials, for she was beautiful to behold.
17_1_12: But Queen Vashti refused to come at the king’s command brought by his eunuchs; therefore the king was furious, and his anger burned within him.
17_1_13: Then the king said to the wise men who understood the times (for this was the king’s manner toward all who knew law and justice
17_1_14: those closest to him being Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan, the seven princes of Persia and Media, who had access to the king’s presence, and who ranked highest in the kingdom):
17_1_15: “What shall we do to Queen Vashti, according to law, because she did not obey the command of King Ahasuerus brought to her by the eunuchs?”
17_1_16: And Memucan answered before the king and the princes: “Queen Vashti has not only wronged the king, but also all the princes, and all the people who are in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus.
17_1_17: For the queen’s behavior will become known to all women, so that they will despise their husbands in their eyes, when they report, ‘King Ahasuerus commanded Queen Vashti to be brought in before him, but she did not come.’
17_1_18: This very day the noble ladies of Persia and Media will say to all the king’s officials that they have heard of the behavior of the queen. Thus there will be excessive contempt and wrath.
17_1_19: If it pleases the king, let a royal decree go out from him, and let it be recorded in the laws of the Persians and the Medes, so that it will not be altered, that Vashti shall come no more before King Ahasuerus; and let the king give her royal position to another who is better than she.
17_1_20: When the king’s decree which he will make is proclaimed throughout all his empire (for it is great), all wives will honor their husbands, both great and small.”
17_1_21: And the reply pleased the king and the princes, and the king did according to the word of Memucan.
17_1_22: Then he sent letters to all the king’s provinces, to each province in its own script, and to every people in their own language, that each man should be master in his own house, and speak in the language of his own people.
17_2_1: After these things, when the wrath of King Ahasuerus subsided, he remembered Vashti, what she had done, and what had been decreed against her.
17_2_2: Then the king’s servants who attended him said: “Let beautiful young virgins be sought for the king
17_2_3: and let the king appoint officers in all the provinces of his kingdom, that they may gather all the beautiful young virgins to Shushan the citadel, into the women’s quarters, under the custody of Hegai the king’s eunuch, custodian of the women. And let beauty preparations be given them.
17_2_4: Then let the young woman who pleases the king be queen instead of Vashti.” This thing pleased the king, and he did so.
17_2_5: In Shushan the citadel there was a certain Jew whose name was Mordecai the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjamite.
17_2_6: Kish had been carried away from Jerusalem with the captives who had been captured with Jeconiah king of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon had carried away.
17_2_7: And Mordecai had brought up Hadassah, that is, Esther, his uncle’s daughter, for she had neither father nor mother. The young woman was lovely and beautiful. When her father and mother died, Mordecai took her as his own daughter.
17_2_8: So it was, when the king’s command and decree were heard, and when many young women were gathered at Shushan the citadel, under the custody of Hegai, that Esther also was taken to the king’s palace, into the care of Hegai the custodian of the women.
17_2_9: Now the young woman pleased him, and she obtained his favor; so he readily gave beauty preparations to her, besides her allowance. Then seven choice maidservants were provided for her from the king’s palace, and he moved her and her maidservants to the best place in the house of the women.
17_2_10: Esther had not revealed her people or family, for Mordecai had charged her not to reveal it.
17_2_11: And every day Mordecai paced in front of the court of the women’s quarters, to learn of Esther’s welfare and what was happening to her.
17_2_12: Each young woman’s turn came to go in to King Ahasuerus after she had completed twelve months’ preparation, according to the regulations for the women, for thus were the days of their preparation apportioned: six months with oil of myrrh, and six months with perfumes and preparations for beautifying women.
17_2_13: Thus prepared, each young woman went to the king, and she was given whatever she desired to take with her from the women’s quarters to the king’s palace.
17_2_14: In the evening she went, and in the morning she returned to the second house of the women, to the custody of Shaashgaz, the king’s eunuch who kept the concubines. She would not go in to the king again unless the king delighted in her and called for her by name.
17_2_15: Now when the turn came for Esther the daughter of Abihail the uncle of Mordecai, who had taken her as his daughter, to go in to the king, she requested nothing but what Hegai the king’s eunuch, the custodian of the women, advised. And Esther obtained favor in the sight of all who saw her.
17_2_16: So Esther was taken to King Ahasuerus, into his royal palace, in the tenth month, which is the month of Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign.
17_2_17: The king loved Esther more than all the other women, and she obtained grace and favor in his sight more than all the virgins; so he set the royal crown upon her head and made her queen instead of Vashti.
17_2_18: Then the king made a great feast, the Feast of Esther, for all his officials and servants; and he proclaimed a holiday in the provinces and gave gifts according to the generosity of a king.
17_2_19: When virgins were gathered together a second time, Mordecai sat within the king’s gate.
17_2_20: Now Esther had not revealed her family and her people, just as Mordecai had charged her, for Esther obeyed the command of Mordecai as when she was brought up by him.
17_2_21: In those days, while Mordecai sat within the king’s gate, two of the king’s eunuchs, Bigthan and Teresh, doorkeepers, became furious and sought to lay hands on King Ahasuerus.
17_2_22: So the matter became known to Mordecai, who told Queen Esther, and Esther informed the king in Mordecai’s name.
17_2_23: And when an inquiry was made into the matter, it was confirmed, and both were hanged on a gallows; and it was written in the book of the chronicles in the presence of the king.
17_3_1: After these things King Ahasuerus promoted Haman, the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and advanced him and set his seat above all the princes who were with him.
17_3_2: And all the king’s servants who were within the king’s gate bowed and paid homage to Haman, for so the king had commanded concerning him. But Mordecai would not bow or pay homage.
17_3_3: Then the king’s servants who were within the king’s gate said to Mordecai, “Why do you transgress the king’s command?”
17_3_4: Now it happened, when they spoke to him daily and he would not listen to them, that they told it to Haman, to see whether Mordecai’s words would stand; for Mordecai had told them that he was a Jew.
17_3_5: When Haman saw that Mordecai did not bow or pay him homage, Haman was filled with wrath.
17_3_6: But he disdained to lay hands on Mordecai alone, for they had told him of the people of Mordecai. Instead, Haman sought to destroy all the Jews who were throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus—the people of Mordecai.
17_3_7: In the first month, which is the month of Nisan, in the twelfth year of King Ahasuerus, they cast Pur (that is, the lot), before Haman to determine the day and the month, until it fell on the twelfth month, which is the month of Adar.
17_3_8: Then Haman said to King Ahasuerus, “There is a certain people scattered and dispersed among the people in all the provinces of your kingdom; their laws are different from all other people’s, and they do not keep the king’s laws. Therefore it is not fitting for the king to let them remain.
17_3_9: If it pleases the king, let a decree be written that they be destroyed, and I will pay ten thousand talents of silver into the hands of those who do the work, to bring it into the king’s treasuries.”
17_3_10: So the king took his signet ring from his hand and gave it to Haman, the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the enemy of the Jews.
17_3_11: And the king said to Haman, “The money and the people are given to you, to do with them as seems good to you.”
17_3_12: Then the king’s scribes were called on the thirteenth day of the first month, and a decree was written according to all that Haman commanded—to the king’s satraps, to the governors who were over each province, to the officials of all people, to every province according to its script, and to every people in their language. In the name of King Ahasuerus it was written, and sealed with the king’s signet ring.
17_3_13: And the letters were sent by couriers into all the king’s provinces, to destroy, to kill, and to annihilate all the Jews, both young and old, little children and women, in one day, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month of Adar, and to plunder their possessions.
17_3_14: A copy of the document was to be issued as law in every province, being published for all people, that they should be ready for that day.
17_3_15: The couriers went out, hastened by the king’s command; and the decree was proclaimed in Shushan the citadel. So the king and Haman sat down to drink, but the city of Shushan was perplexed.
17_4_1: When Mordecai learned all that had happened, he tore his clothes and put on sackcloth and ashes, and went out into the midst of the city. He cried out with a loud and bitter cry.
17_4_2: He went as far as the front of the king’s gate, for no one might enter the king’s gate clothed with sackcloth.
17_4_3: And in every province where the king’s command and decree arrived, there was great mourning among the Jews, with fasting, weeping, and wailing; and many lay in sackcloth and ashes.
17_4_4: So Esther’s maids and eunuchs came and told her, and the queen was deeply distressed. Then she sent garments to clothe Mordecai and take his sackcloth away from him, but he would not accept them.
17_4_5: Then Esther called Hathach, one of the king’s eunuchs whom he had appointed to attend her, and she gave him a command concerning Mordecai, to learn what and why this was.
17_4_6: So Hathach went out to Mordecai in the city square that was in front of the king’s gate.
17_4_7: And Mordecai told him all that had happened to him, and the sum of money that Haman had promised to pay into the king’s treasuries to destroy the Jews.
17_4_8: He also gave him a copy of the written decree for their destruction, which was given at Shushan, that he might show it to Esther and explain it to her, and that he might command her to go in to the king to make supplication to him and plead before him for her people.
17_4_9: So Hathach returned and told Esther the words of Mordecai.
17_4_10: Then Esther spoke to Hathach, and gave him a command for Mordecai:
17_4_11: “All the king’s servants and the people of the king’s provinces know that any man or woman who goes into the inner court to the king, who has not been called, he has but one law: put all to death, except the one to whom the king holds out the golden scepter, that he may live. Yet I myself have not been called to go in to the king these thirty days.”
17_4_12: So they told Mordecai Esther’s words.
17_4_13: And Mordecai told them to answer Esther: “Do not think in your heart that you will escape in the king’s palace any more than all the other Jews.
17_4_14: For if you remain completely silent at this time, relief and deliverance will arise for the Jews from another place, but you and your father’s house will perish. Yet who knows whether you have come to the kingdom for such a time as this?”
17_4_15: Then Esther told them to reply to Mordecai:
17_4_16: “Go, gather all the Jews who are present in Shushan, and fast for me; neither eat nor drink for three days, night or day. My maids and I will fast likewise. And so I will go to the king, which is against the law; and if I perish, I perish!”
17_4_17: So Mordecai went his way and did according to all that Esther commanded him.
17_5_1: Now it happened on the third day that Esther put on her royal robes and stood in the inner court of the king’s palace, across from the king’s house, while the king sat on his royal throne in the royal house, facing the entrance of the house.
17_5_2: So it was, when the king saw Queen Esther standing in the court, that she found favor in his sight, and the king held out to Esther the golden scepter that was in his hand. Then Esther went near and touched the top of the scepter.
17_5_3: And the king said to her, “What do you wish, Queen Esther? What is your request? It shall be given to you—up to half the kingdom!”
17_5_4: So Esther answered, “If it pleases the king, let the king and Haman come today to the banquet that I have prepared for him.”
17_5_5: Then the king said, “Bring Haman quickly, that he may do as Esther has said.” So the king and Haman went to the banquet that Esther had prepared.
17_5_6: At the banquet of wine the king said to Esther, “What is your petition? It shall be granted you. What is your request, up to half the kingdom? It shall be done!”
17_5_7: Then Esther answered and said, “My petition and request is this:
17_5_8: If I have found favor in the sight of the king, and if it pleases the king to grant my petition and fulfill my request, then let the king and Haman come to the banquet which I will prepare for them, and tomorrow I will do as the king has said.”
17_5_9: So Haman went out that day joyful and with a glad heart; but when Haman saw Mordecai in the king’s gate, and that he did not stand or tremble before him, he was filled with indignation against Mordecai.
17_5_10: Nevertheless Haman restrained himself and went home, and he sent and called for his friends and his wife Zeresh.
17_5_11: Then Haman told them of his great riches, the multitude of his children, everything in which the king had promoted him, and how he had advanced him above the officials and servants of the king.
17_5_12: Moreover Haman said, “Besides, Queen Esther invited no one but me to come in with the king to the banquet that she prepared; and tomorrow I am again invited by her, along with the king.
17_5_13: Yet all this avails me nothing, so long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king’s gate.”
17_5_14: Then his wife Zeresh and all his friends said to him, “Let a gallows be made, fifty cubits high, and in the morning suggest to the king that Mordecai be hanged on it; then go merrily with the king to the banquet.” And the thing pleased Haman; so he had the gallows made.
17_6_1: That night the king could not sleep. So one was commanded to bring the book of the records of the chronicles; and they were read before the king.
17_6_2: And it was found written that Mordecai had told of Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king’s eunuchs, the doorkeepers who had sought to lay hands on King Ahasuerus.
17_6_3: Then the king said, “What honor or dignity has been bestowed on Mordecai for this?” And the king’s servants who attended him said, “Nothing has been done for him.”
17_6_4: So the king said, “Who is in the court?” Now Haman had just entered the outer court of the king’s palace to suggest that the king hang Mordecai on the gallows that he had prepared for him.
17_6_5: The king’s servants said to him, “Haman is there, standing in the court.” And the king said, “Let him come in.”
17_6_6: So Haman came in, and the king asked him, “What shall be done for the man whom the king delights to honor?” Now Haman thought in his heart, “Whom would the king delight to honor more than me?”
17_6_7: And Haman answered the king, “For the man whom the king delights to honor
17_6_8: let a royal robe be brought which the king has worn, and a horse on which the king has ridden, which has a royal crest placed on its head.
17_6_9: Then let this robe and horse be delivered to the hand of one of the king’s most noble princes, that he may array the man whom the king delights to honor. Then parade him on horseback through the city square, and proclaim before him: ‘Thus shall it be done to the man whom the king delights to honor!’ ”
17_6_10: Then the king said to Haman, “Hurry, take the robe and the horse, as you have suggested, and do so for Mordecai the Jew who sits within the king’s gate! Leave nothing undone of all that you have spoken.”
17_6_11: So Haman took the robe and the horse, arrayed Mordecai and led him on horseback through the city square, and proclaimed before him, “Thus shall it be done to the man whom the king delights to honor!”
17_6_12: Afterward Mordecai went back to the king’s gate. But Haman hurried to his house, mourning and with his head covered.
17_6_13: When Haman told his wife Zeresh and all his friends everything that had happened to him, his wise men and his wife Zeresh said to him, “If Mordecai, before whom you have begun to fall, is of Jewish descent, you will not prevail against him but will surely fall before him.”
17_6_14: While they were still talking with him, the king’s eunuchs came, and hastened to bring Haman to the banquet which Esther had prepared.
17_7_1: So the king and Haman went to dine with Queen Esther.
17_7_2: And on the second day, at the banquet of wine, the king again said to Esther, “What is your petition, Queen Esther? It shall be granted you. And what is your request, up to half the kingdom? It shall be done!”
17_7_3: Then Queen Esther answered and said, “If I have found favor in your sight, O king, and if it pleases the king, let my life be given me at my petition, and my people at my request.
17_7_4: For we have been sold, my people and I, to be destroyed, to be killed, and to be annihilated. Had we been sold as male and female slaves, I would have held my tongue, although the enemy could never compensate for the king’s loss.”
17_7_5: So King Ahasuerus answered and said to Queen Esther, “Who is he, and where is he, who would dare presume in his heart to do such a thing?”
17_7_6: And Esther said, “The adversary and enemy is this wicked Haman!” So Haman was terrified before the king and queen.
17_7_7: Then the king arose in his wrath from the banquet of wine and went into the palace garden; but Haman stood before Queen Esther, pleading for his life, for he saw that evil was determined against him by the king.
17_7_8: When the king returned from the palace garden to the place of the banquet of wine, Haman had fallen across the couch where Esther was. Then the king said, “Will he also assault the queen while I am in the house?” As the word left the king’s mouth, they covered Haman’s face.
17_7_9: Now Harbonah, one of the eunuchs, said to the king, “Look! The gallows, fifty cubits high, which Haman made for Mordecai, who spoke good on the king’s behalf, is standing at the house of Haman.” Then the king said, “Hang him on it!”
17_7_10: So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then the king’s wrath subsided.
17_8_1: On that day King Ahasuerus gave Queen Esther the house of Haman, the enemy of the Jews. And Mordecai came before the king, for Esther had told how he was related to her.
17_8_2: So the king took off his signet ring, which he had taken from Haman, and gave it to Mordecai; and Esther appointed Mordecai over the house of Haman.
17_8_3: Now Esther spoke again to the king, fell down at his feet, and implored him with tears to counteract the evil of Haman the Agagite, and the scheme which he had devised against the Jews.
17_8_4: And the king held out the golden scepter toward Esther. So Esther arose and stood before the king
17_8_5: and said, “If it pleases the king, and if I have found favor in his sight and the thing seems right to the king and I am pleasing in his eyes, let it be written to revoke the letters devised by Haman, the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, which he wrote to annihilate the Jews who are in all the king’s provinces.
17_8_6: For how can I endure to see the evil that will come to my people? Or how can I endure to see the destruction of my countrymen?”
17_8_7: Then King Ahasuerus said to Queen Esther and Mordecai the Jew, “Indeed, I have given Esther the house of Haman, and they have hanged him on the gallows because he tried to lay his hand on the Jews.
17_8_8: You yourselves write a decree concerning the Jews, as you please, in the king’s name, and seal it with the king’s signet ring; for whatever is written in the king’s name and sealed with the king’s signet ring no one can revoke.”
17_8_9: So the king’s scribes were called at that time, in the third month, which is the month of Sivan, on the twenty-third day; and it was written, according to all that Mordecai commanded, to the Jews, the satraps, the governors, and the princes of the provinces from India to Ethiopia, one hundred and twenty-seven provinces in all, to every province in its own script, to every people in their own language, and to the Jews in their own script and language.
17_8_10: And he wrote in the name of King Ahasuerus, sealed it with the king’s signet ring, and sent letters by couriers on horseback, riding on royal horses bred from swift steeds.
17_8_11: By these letters the king permitted the Jews who were in every city to gather together and protect their lives—to destroy, kill, and annihilate all the forces of any people or province that would assault them, both little children and women, and to plunder their possessions
17_8_12: on one day in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month of Adar.
17_8_13: A copy of the document was to be issued as a decree in every province and published for all people, so that the Jews would be ready on that day to avenge themselves on their enemies.
17_8_14: The couriers who rode on royal horses went out, hastened and pressed on by the king’s command. And the decree was issued in Shushan the citadel.
17_8_15: So Mordecai went out from the presence of the king in royal apparel of blue and white, with a great crown of gold and a garment of fine linen and purple; and the city of Shushan rejoiced and was glad.
17_8_16: The Jews had light and gladness, joy and honor.
17_8_17: And in every province and city, wherever the king’s command and decree came, the Jews had joy and gladness, a feast and a holiday. Then many of the people of the land became Jews, because fear of the Jews fell upon them.
17_9_1: Now in the twelfth month, that is, the month of Adar, on the thirteenth day, the time came for the king’s command and his decree to be executed. On the day that the enemies of the Jews had hoped to overpower them, the opposite occurred, in that the Jews themselves overpowered those who hated them.
17_9_2: The Jews gathered together in their cities throughout all the provinces of King Ahasuerus to lay hands on those who sought their harm. And no one could withstand them, because fear of them fell upon all people.
17_9_3: And all the officials of the provinces, the satraps, the governors, and all those doing the king’s work, helped the Jews, because the fear of Mordecai fell upon them.
17_9_4: For Mordecai was great in the king’s palace, and his fame spread throughout all the provinces; for this man Mordecai became increasingly prominent.
17_9_5: Thus the Jews defeated all their enemies with the stroke of the sword, with slaughter and destruction, and did what they pleased with those who hated them.
17_9_6: And in Shushan the citadel the Jews killed and destroyed five hundred men.
17_9_10: the ten sons of Haman the son of Hammedatha, the enemy of the Jews—they killed; but they did not lay a hand on the plunder.
17_9_11: On that day the number of those who were killed in Shushan the citadel was brought to the king.
17_9_12: And the king said to Queen Esther, “The Jews have killed and destroyed five hundred men in Shushan the citadel, and the ten sons of Haman. What have they done in the rest of the king’s provinces? Now what is your petition? It shall be granted to you. Or what is your further request? It shall be done.”
17_9_13: Then Esther said, “If it pleases the king, let it be granted to the Jews who are in Shushan to do again tomorrow according to today’s decree, and let Haman’s ten sons be hanged on the gallows.”
17_9_14: So the king commanded this to be done; the decree was issued in Shushan, and they hanged Haman’s ten sons.
17_9_15: And the Jews who were in Shushan gathered together again on the fourteenth day of the month of Adar and killed three hundred men at Shushan; but they did not lay a hand on the plunder.
17_9_16: The remainder of the Jews in the king’s provinces gathered together and protected their lives, had rest from their enemies, and killed seventy-five thousand of their enemies; but they did not lay a hand on the plunder.
17_9_17: This was on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar. And on the fourteenth of the month they rested and made it a day of feasting and gladness.
17_9_18: But the Jews who were at Shushan assembled together on the thirteenth day, as well as on the fourteenth; and on the fifteenth of the month they rested, and made it a day of feasting and gladness.
17_9_19: Therefore the Jews of the villages who dwelt in the unwalled towns celebrated the fourteenth day of the month of Adar with gladness and feasting, as a holiday, and for sending presents to one another.
17_9_20: And Mordecai wrote these things and sent letters to all the Jews, near and far, who were in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus
17_9_21: to establish among them that they should celebrate yearly the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the month of Adar
17_9_22: as the days on which the Jews had rest from their enemies, as the month which was turned from sorrow to joy for them, and from mourning to a holiday; that they should make them days of feasting and joy, of sending presents to one another and gifts to the poor.
17_9_23: So the Jews accepted the custom which they had begun, as Mordecai had written to them
17_9_24: because Haman, the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had plotted against the Jews to annihilate them, and had cast Pur (that is, the lot), to consume them and destroy them
17_9_25: but when Esther came before the king, he commanded by letter that this wicked plot which Haman had devised against the Jews should return on his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.
17_9_26: So they called these days Purim, after the name Pur. Therefore, because of all the words of this letter, what they had seen concerning this matter, and what had happened to them
17_9_27: the Jews established and imposed it upon themselves and their descendants and all who would join them, that without fail they should celebrate these two days every year, according to the written instructions and according to the prescribed time
17_9_28: that these days should be remembered and kept throughout every generation, every family, every province, and every city, that these days of Purim should not fail to be observed among the Jews, and that the memory of them should not perish among their descendants.
17_9_29: Then Queen Esther, the daughter of Abihail, with Mordecai the Jew, wrote with full authority to confirm this second letter about Purim.
17_9_30: And Mordecai sent letters to all the Jews, to the one hundred and twenty-seven provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, with words of peace and truth
17_9_31: to confirm these days of Purim at their appointed time, as Mordecai the Jew and Queen Esther had prescribed for them, and as they had decreed for themselves and their descendants concerning matters of their fasting and lamenting.
17_9_32: So the decree of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim, and it was written in the book.
17_10_1: And King Ahasuerus imposed tribute on the land and on the islands of the sea.
17_10_2: Now all the acts of his power and his might, and the account of the greatness of Mordecai, to which the king advanced him, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia?
17_10_3: For Mordecai the Jew was second to King Ahasuerus, and was great among the Jews and well received by the multitude of his brethren, seeking the good of his people and speaking peace to all his countrymen.
18_1_2: And seven sons and three daughters were born to him.
18_1_3: Also, his possessions were seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, five hundred female donkeys, and a very large household, so that this man was the greatest of all the people of the East.
18_1_4: And his sons would go and feast in their houses, each on his appointed day, and would send and invite their three sisters to eat and drink with them.
18_1_5: So it was, when the days of feasting had run their course, that Job would send and sanctify them, and he would rise early in the morning and offer burnt offerings according to the number of them all. For Job said, “It may be that my sons have sinned and cursed God in their hearts.” Thus Job did regularly.
18_1_6: Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan also came among them.
18_1_7: And the LORD said to Satan, “From where do you come?” So Satan answered the LORD and said, “From going to and fro on the earth, and from walking back and forth on it.”
18_1_8: Then the LORD said to Satan, “Have you considered My servant Job, that there is none like him on the earth, a blameless and upright man, one who fears God and shuns evil?”
18_1_9: So Satan answered the LORD and said, “Does Job fear God for nothing?
18_1_10: Have You not made a hedge around him, around his household, and around all that he has on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his possessions have increased in the land.
18_1_11: But now, stretch out Your hand and touch all that he has, and he will surely curse You to Your face!”
18_1_12: And the LORD said to Satan, “Behold, all that he has is in your power; only do not lay a hand on his person.” So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD.
18_1_13: Now there was a day when his sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house
18_1_14: and a messenger came to Job and said, “The oxen were plowing and the donkeys feeding beside them
18_1_15: when the Sabeans raided them and took them away—indeed they have killed the servants with the edge of the sword; and I alone have escaped to tell you!”
18_1_16: While he was still speaking, another also came and said, “The fire of God fell from heaven and burned up the sheep and the servants, and consumed them; and I alone have escaped to tell you!”
18_1_17: While he was still speaking, another also came and said, “The Chaldeans formed three bands, raided the camels and took them away, yes, and killed the servants with the edge of the sword; and I alone have escaped to tell you!”
18_1_18: While he was still speaking, another also came and said, “Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house
18_1_19: and suddenly a great wind came from across the wilderness and struck the four corners of the house, and it fell on the young people, and they are dead; and I alone have escaped to tell you!”
18_1_20: Then Job arose, tore his robe, and shaved his head; and he fell to the ground and worshiped.
18_1_21: And he said: “Naked I came from my mother’s womb, And naked shall I return there. The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away; Blessed be the name of the LORD.”
18_1_22: In all this Job did not sin nor charge God with wrong.
18_2_1: Again there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan came also among them to present himself before the LORD.
18_2_2: And the LORD said to Satan, “From where do you come?” Satan answered the LORD and said, “From going to and fro on the earth, and from walking back and forth on it.”
18_2_3: Then the LORD said to Satan, “Have you considered My servant Job, that there is none like him on the earth, a blameless and upright man, one who fears God and shuns evil? And still he holds fast to his integrity, although you incited Me against him, to destroy him without cause.”
18_2_4: So Satan answered the LORD and said, “Skin for skin! Yes, all that a man has he will give for his life.
18_2_5: But stretch out Your hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will surely curse You to Your face!”
18_2_6: And the LORD said to Satan, “Behold, he is in your hand, but spare his life.”
18_2_7: So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD, and struck Job with painful boils from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head.
18_2_8: And he took for himself a potsherd with which to scrape himself while he sat in the midst of the ashes.
18_2_9: Then his wife said to him, “Do you still hold fast to your integrity? Curse God and die!”
18_2_10: But he said to her, “You speak as one of the foolish women speaks. Shall we indeed accept good from God, and shall we not accept adversity?” In all this Job did not sin with his lips.
18_2_11: Now when Job’s three friends heard of all this adversity that had come upon him, each one came from his own place—Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite. For they had made an appointment together to come and mourn with him, and to comfort him.
18_2_12: And when they raised their eyes from afar, and did not recognize him, they lifted their voices and wept; and each one tore his robe and sprinkled dust on his head toward heaven.
18_2_13: So they sat down with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that his grief was very great.
18_3_1: After this Job opened his mouth and cursed the day of his birth.
18_3_4: May that day be darkness; May God above not seek it, Nor the light shine upon it.
18_3_5: May darkness and the shadow of death claim it; May a cloud settle on it; May the blackness of the day terrify it.
18_3_6: As for that night, may darkness seize it; May it not rejoice among the days of the year, May it not come into the number of the months.
18_3_7: Oh, may that night be barren! May no joyful shout come into it!
18_3_8: May those curse it who curse the day, Those who are ready to arouse Leviathan.
18_3_9: May the stars of its morning be dark; May it look for light, but have none, And not see the dawning of the day
18_3_10: Because it did not shut up the doors of my mother’s womb, Nor hide sorrow from my eyes.
18_3_11: “Why did I not die at birth? Why did I not perish when I came from the womb?
18_3_12: Why did the knees receive me? Or why the breasts, that I should nurse?
18_3_13: For now I would have lain still and been quiet, I would have been asleep; Then I would have been at rest
18_3_14: With kings and counselors of the earth, Who built ruins for themselves
18_3_15: Or with princes who had gold, Who filled their houses with silver
18_3_16: Or why was I not hidden like a stillborn child, Like infants who never saw light?
18_3_17: There the wicked cease from troubling, And there the weary are at rest.
18_3_18: There the prisoners rest together; They do not hear the voice of the oppressor.
18_3_19: The small and great are there, And the servant is free from his master.
18_3_20: “Why is light given to him who is in misery, And life to the bitter of soul
18_3_21: Who long for death, but it does not come, And search for it more than hidden treasures
18_3_22: Who rejoice exceedingly, And are glad when they can find the grave?
18_3_23: Why is light given to a man whose way is hidden, And whom God has hedged in?
18_3_24: For my sighing comes before I eat, And my groanings pour out like water.
18_3_25: For the thing I greatly feared has come upon me, And what I dreaded has happened to me.
18_3_26: I am not at ease, nor am I quiet; I have no rest, for trouble comes.”
18_4_1: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
18_4_2: “If one attempts a word with you, will you become weary? But who can withhold himself from speaking?
18_4_3: Surely you have instructed many, And you have strengthened weak hands.
18_4_4: Your words have upheld him who was stumbling, And you have strengthened the feeble knees
18_4_5: But now it comes upon you, and you are weary; It touches you, and you are troubled.
18_4_6: Is not your reverence your confidence? And the integrity of your ways your hope?
18_4_7: “Remember now, who ever perished being innocent? Or where were the upright ever cut off?
18_4_8: Even as I have seen, Those who plow iniquity And sow trouble reap the same.
18_4_9: By the blast of God they perish, And by the breath of His anger they are consumed.
18_4_10: The roaring of the lion, The voice of the fierce lion, And the teeth of the young lions are broken.
18_4_11: The old lion perishes for lack of prey, And the cubs of the lioness are scattered.
18_4_12: “Now a word was secretly brought to me, And my ear received a whisper of it.
18_4_13: In disquieting thoughts from the visions of the night, When deep sleep falls on men
18_4_14: Fear came upon me, and trembling, Which made all my bones shake.
18_4_15: Then a spirit passed before my face; The hair on my body stood up.
18_4_16: It stood still, But I could not discern its appearance. A form was before my eyes; There was silence; Then I heard a voice saying:
18_4_17: ‘Can a mortal be more righteous than God? Can a man be more pure than his Maker?
18_4_18: If He puts no trust in His servants, If He charges His angels with error
18_4_19: How much more those who dwell in houses of clay, Whose foundation is in the dust, Who are crushed before a moth?
18_4_20: They are broken in pieces from morning till evening; They perish forever, with no one regarding.
18_4_21: Does not their own excellence go away? They die, even without wisdom.’
18_5_1: “Call out now; Is there anyone who will answer you? And to which of the holy ones will you turn?
18_5_2: For wrath kills a foolish man, And envy slays a simple one.
18_5_3: I have seen the foolish taking root, But suddenly I cursed his dwelling place.
18_5_4: His sons are far from safety, They are crushed in the gate, And there is no deliverer.
18_5_5: Because the hungry eat up his harvest, Taking it even from the thorns, And a snare snatches their substance.
18_5_6: For affliction does not come from the dust, Nor does trouble spring from the ground
18_5_7: Yet man is born to trouble, As the sparks fly upward.
18_5_8: “But as for me, I would seek God, And to God I would commit my cause—
18_5_9: Who does great things, and unsearchable, Marvelous things without number.
18_5_10: He gives rain on the earth, And sends waters on the fields.
18_5_11: He sets on high those who are lowly, And those who mourn are lifted to safety.
18_5_12: He frustrates the devices of the crafty, So that their hands cannot carry out their plans.
18_5_13: He catches the wise in their own craftiness, And the counsel of the cunning comes quickly upon them.
18_5_14: They meet with darkness in the daytime, And grope at noontime as in the night.
18_5_15: But He saves the needy from the sword, From the mouth of the mighty, And from their hand.
18_5_16: So the poor have hope, And injustice shuts her mouth.
18_5_17: “Behold, happy is the man whom God corrects; Therefore do not despise the chastening of the Almighty.
18_5_18: For He bruises, but He binds up; He wounds, but His hands make whole.
18_5_19: He shall deliver you in six troubles, Yes, in seven no evil shall touch you.
18_5_20: In famine He shall redeem you from death, And in war from the power of the sword.
18_5_21: You shall be hidden from the scourge of the tongue, And you shall not be afraid of destruction when it comes.
18_5_22: You shall laugh at destruction and famine, And you shall not be afraid of the beasts of the earth.
18_5_23: For you shall have a covenant with the stones of the field, And the beasts of the field shall be at peace with you.
18_5_24: You shall know that your tent is in peace; You shall visit your dwelling and find nothing amiss.
18_5_25: You shall also know that your descendants shall be many, And your offspring like the grass of the earth.
18_5_26: You shall come to the grave at a full age, As a sheaf of grain ripens in its season.
18_5_27: Behold, this we have searched out; It is true. Hear it, and know for yourself.”
18_6_2: “Oh, that my grief were fully weighed, And my calamity laid with it on the scales!
18_6_3: For then it would be heavier than the sand of the sea— Therefore my words have been rash.
18_6_4: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me; My spirit drinks in their poison; The terrors of God are arrayed against me.
18_6_5: Does the wild donkey bray when it has grass, Or does the ox low over its fodder?
18_6_6: Can flavorless food be eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in the white of an egg?
18_6_7: My soul refuses to touch them; They are as loathsome food to me.
18_6_8: “Oh, that I might have my request, That God would grant me the thing that I long for!
18_6_9: That it would please God to crush me, That He would loose His hand and cut me off!
18_6_10: Then I would still have comfort; Though in anguish I would exult, He will not spare; For I have not concealed the words of the Holy One.
18_6_11: “What strength do I have, that I should hope? And what is my end, that I should prolong my life?
18_6_12: Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh bronze?
18_6_13: Is my help not within me? And is success driven from me?
18_6_14: “To him who is afflicted, kindness should be shown by his friend, Even though he forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
18_6_15: My brothers have dealt deceitfully like a brook, Like the streams of the brooks that pass away
18_6_16: Which are dark because of the ice, And into which the snow vanishes.
18_6_17: When it is warm, they cease to flow; When it is hot, they vanish from their place.
18_6_18: The paths of their way turn aside, They go nowhere and perish.
18_6_19: The caravans of Tema look, The travelers of Sheba hope for them.
18_6_20: They are disappointed because they were confident; They come there and are confused.
18_6_21: For now you are nothing, You see terror and are afraid.
18_6_22: Did I ever say, ‘Bring something to me’? Or, ‘Offer a bribe for me from your wealth’?
18_6_23: Or, ‘Deliver me from the enemy’s hand’? Or, ‘Redeem me from the hand of oppressors’?
18_6_24: “Teach me, and I will hold my tongue; Cause me to understand wherein I have erred.
18_6_25: How forceful are right words! But what does your arguing prove?
18_6_26: Do you intend to rebuke my words, And the speeches of a desperate one, which are as wind?
18_6_27: Yes, you overwhelm the fatherless, And you undermine your friend.
18_6_28: Now therefore, be pleased to look at me; For I would never lie to your face.
18_6_29: Yield now, let there be no injustice! Yes, concede, my righteousness still stands!
18_6_30: Is there injustice on my tongue? Cannot my taste discern the unsavory?
18_7_1: “Is there not a time of hard service for man on earth? Are not his days also like the days of a hired man?
18_7_2: Like a servant who earnestly desires the shade, And like a hired man who eagerly looks for his wages
18_7_3: So I have been allotted months of futility, And wearisome nights have been appointed to me.
18_7_4: When I lie down, I say, ‘When shall I arise, And the night be ended?’ For I have had my fill of tossing till dawn.
18_7_5: My flesh is caked with worms and dust, My skin is cracked and breaks out afresh.
18_7_6: “My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, And are spent without hope.
18_7_7: Oh, remember that my life is a breath! My eye will never again see good.
18_7_8: The eye of him who sees me will see me no more; While your eyes are upon me, I shall no longer be.
18_7_9: As the cloud disappears and vanishes away, So he who goes down to the grave does not come up.
18_7_10: He shall never return to his house, Nor shall his place know him anymore.
18_7_11: “Therefore I will not restrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
18_7_12: Am I a sea, or a sea serpent, That You set a guard over me?
18_7_13: When I say, ‘My bed will comfort me, My couch will ease my complaint,’
18_7_14: Then You scare me with dreams And terrify me with visions
18_7_15: So that my soul chooses strangling And death rather than my body.
18_7_16: I loathe my life; I would not live forever. Let me alone, For my days are but a breath.
18_7_17: “What is man, that You should exalt him, That You should set Your heart on him
18_7_18: That You should visit him every morning, And test him every moment?
18_7_19: How long? Will You not look away from me, And let me alone till I swallow my saliva?
18_7_20: Have I sinned? What have I done to You, O watcher of men? Why have You set me as Your target, So that I am a burden to myself?
18_7_21: Why then do You not pardon my transgression, And take away my iniquity? For now I will lie down in the dust, And You will seek me diligently, But I will no longer be.”
18_8_1: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
18_8_2: “How long will you speak these things, And the words of your mouth be like a strong wind?
18_8_3: Does God subvert judgment? Or does the Almighty pervert justice?
18_8_4: If your sons have sinned against Him, He has cast them away for their transgression.
18_8_5: If you would earnestly seek God And make your supplication to the Almighty
18_8_6: If you were pure and upright, Surely now He would awake for you, And prosper your rightful dwelling place.
18_8_7: Though your beginning was small, Yet your latter end would increase abundantly.
18_8_8: “For inquire, please, of the former age, And consider the things discovered by their fathers
18_8_9: For we were born yesterday, and know nothing, Because our days on earth are a shadow.
18_8_10: Will they not teach you and tell you, And utter words from their heart?
18_8_11: “Can the papyrus grow up without a marsh? Can the reeds flourish without water?
18_8_12: While it is yet green and not cut down, It withers before any other plant.
18_8_13: So are the paths of all who forget God; And the hope of the hypocrite shall perish
18_8_14: Whose confidence shall be cut off, And whose trust is a spider’s web.
18_8_15: He leans on his house, but it does not stand. He holds it fast, but it does not endure.
18_8_16: He grows green in the sun, And his branches spread out in his garden.
18_8_17: His roots wrap around the rock heap, And look for a place in the stones.
18_8_18: If he is destroyed from his place, Then it will deny him, saying, ‘I have not seen you.’
18_8_19: “Behold, this is the joy of His way, And out of the earth others will grow.
18_8_20: Behold, God will not cast away the blameless, Nor will He uphold the evildoers.
18_8_21: He will yet fill your mouth with laughing, And your lips with rejoicing.
18_8_22: Those who hate you will be clothed with shame, And the dwelling place of the wicked will come to nothing.”
18_9_2: “Truly I know it is so, But how can a man be righteous before God?
18_9_3: If one wished to contend with Him, He could not answer Him one time out of a thousand.
18_9_4: God is wise in heart and mighty in strength. Who has hardened himself against Him and prospered?
18_9_5: He removes the mountains, and they do not know When He overturns them in His anger
18_9_6: He shakes the earth out of its place, And its pillars tremble
18_9_7: He commands the sun, and it does not rise; He seals off the stars
18_9_8: He alone spreads out the heavens, And treads on the waves of the sea
18_9_9: He made the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, And the chambers of the south
18_9_10: He does great things past finding out, Yes, wonders without number.
18_9_11: If He goes by me, I do not see Him; If He moves past, I do not perceive Him
18_9_12: If He takes away, who can hinder Him? Who can say to Him, ‘What are You doing?’
18_9_13: God will not withdraw His anger, The allies of the proud lie prostrate beneath Him.
18_9_14: “How then can I answer Him, And choose my words to reason with Him?
18_9_15: For though I were righteous, I could not answer Him; I would beg mercy of my Judge.
18_9_16: If I called and He answered me, I would not believe that He was listening to my voice.
18_9_17: For He crushes me with a tempest, And multiplies my wounds without cause.
18_9_18: He will not allow me to catch my breath, But fills me with bitterness.
18_9_19: If it is a matter of strength, indeed He is strong; And if of justice, who will appoint my day in court?
18_9_20: Though I were righteous, my own mouth would condemn me; Though I were blameless, it would prove me perverse.
18_9_21: “I am blameless, yet I do not know myself; I despise my life.
18_9_22: It is all one thing; Therefore I say, ‘He destroys the blameless and the wicked.’
18_9_23: If the scourge slays suddenly, He laughs at the plight of the innocent.
18_9_24: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked. He covers the faces of its judges. If it is not He, who else could it be?
18_9_25: “Now my days are swifter than a runner; They flee away, they see no good.
18_9_26: They pass by like swift ships, Like an eagle swooping on its prey.
18_9_27: If I say, ‘I will forget my complaint, I will put off my sad face and wear a smile,’
18_9_28: I am afraid of all my sufferings; I know that You will not hold me innocent.
18_9_29: If I am condemned, Why then do I labor in vain?
18_9_30: If I wash myself with snow water, And cleanse my hands with soap
18_9_31: Yet You will plunge me into the pit, And my own clothes will abhor me.
18_9_32: “For He is not a man, as I am, That I may answer Him, And that we should go to court together.
18_9_33: Nor is there any mediator between us, Who may lay his hand on us both.
18_9_34: Let Him take His rod away from me, And do not let dread of Him terrify me.
18_9_35: Then I would speak and not fear Him, But it is not so with me.
18_10_1: “My soul loathes my life; I will give free course to my complaint, I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
18_10_2: I will say to God, ‘Do not condemn me; Show me why You contend with me.
18_10_3: Does it seem good to You that You should oppress, That You should despise the work of Your hands, And smile on the counsel of the wicked?
18_10_4: Do You have eyes of flesh? Or do You see as man sees?
18_10_5: Are Your days like the days of a mortal man? Are Your years like the days of a mighty man
18_10_6: That You should seek for my iniquity And search out my sin
18_10_7: Although You know that I am not wicked, And there is no one who can deliver from Your hand?
18_10_8: ‘Your hands have made me and fashioned me, An intricate unity; Yet You would destroy me.
18_10_9: Remember, I pray, that You have made me like clay. And will You turn me into dust again?
18_10_10: Did You not pour me out like milk, And curdle me like cheese
18_10_11: Clothe me with skin and flesh, And knit me together with bones and sinews?
18_10_12: You have granted me life and favor, And Your care has preserved my spirit.
18_10_13: ‘And these things You have hidden in Your heart; I know that this was with You:
18_10_14: If I sin, then You mark me, And will not acquit me of my iniquity.
18_10_15: If I am wicked, woe to me; Even if I am righteous, I cannot lift up my head. I am full of disgrace; See my misery!
18_10_16: If my head is exalted, You hunt me like a fierce lion, And again You show Yourself awesome against me.
18_10_17: You renew Your witnesses against me, And increase Your indignation toward me; Changes and war are ever with me.
18_10_18: ‘Why then have You brought me out of the womb? Oh, that I had perished and no eye had seen me!
18_10_19: I would have been as though I had not been. I would have been carried from the womb to the grave.
18_10_20: Are not my days few? Cease! Leave me alone, that I may take a little comfort
18_10_21: Before I go to the place from which I shall not return, To the land of darkness and the shadow of death
18_10_22: A land as dark as darkness itself, As the shadow of death, without any order, Where even the light is like darkness.’ ”
18_11_1: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered and said:
18_11_2: “Should not the multitude of words be answered? And should a man full of talk be vindicated?
18_11_3: Should your empty talk make men hold their peace? And when you mock, should no one rebuke you?
18_11_4: For you have said, ‘My doctrine is pure, And I am clean in your eyes.’
18_11_5: But oh, that God would speak, And open His lips against you
18_11_6: That He would show you the secrets of wisdom! For they would double your prudence. Know therefore that God exacts from you Less than your iniquity deserves.
18_11_7: “Can you search out the deep things of God? Can you find out the limits of the Almighty?
18_11_8: They are higher than heaven— what can you do? Deeper than Sheol— what can you know?
18_11_9: Their measure is longer than the earth And broader than the sea.
18_11_10: “If He passes by, imprisons, and gathers to judgment, Then who can hinder Him?
18_11_11: For He knows deceitful men; He sees wickedness also. Will He not then consider it?
18_11_12: For an empty-headed man will be wise, When a wild donkey’s colt is born a man.
18_11_13: “If you would prepare your heart, And stretch out your hands toward Him
18_11_14: If iniquity were in your hand, and you put it far away, And would not let wickedness dwell in your tents
18_11_15: Then surely you could lift up your face without spot; Yes, you could be steadfast, and not fear
18_11_16: Because you would forget your misery, And remember it as waters that have passed away
18_11_17: And your life would be brighter than noonday. Though you were dark, you would be like the morning.
18_11_18: And you would be secure, because there is hope; Yes, you would dig around you, and take your rest in safety.
18_11_19: You would also lie down, and no one would make you afraid; Yes, many would court your favor.
18_11_20: But the eyes of the wicked will fail, And they shall not escape, And their hope—loss of life!”
18_12_2: “No doubt you are the people, And wisdom will die with you!
18_12_3: But I have understanding as well as you; I am not inferior to you. Indeed, who does not know such things as these?
18_12_4: “I am one mocked by his friends, Who called on God, and He answered him, The just and blameless who is ridiculed.
18_12_5: A lamp is despised in the thought of one who is at ease; It is made ready for those whose feet slip.
18_12_6: The tents of robbers prosper, And those who provoke God are secure— In what God provides by His hand.
18_12_7: “But now ask the beasts, and they will teach you; And the birds of the air, and they will tell you
18_12_8: Or speak to the earth, and it will teach you; And the fish of the sea will explain to you.
18_12_9: Who among all these does not know That the hand of the LORD has done this
18_12_10: In whose hand is the life of every living thing, And the breath of all mankind?
18_12_11: Does not the ear test words And the mouth taste its food?
18_12_12: Wisdom is with aged men, And with length of days, understanding.
18_12_13: “With Him are wisdom and strength, He has counsel and understanding.
18_12_14: If He breaks a thing down, it cannot be rebuilt; If He imprisons a man, there can be no release.
18_12_15: If He withholds the waters, they dry up; If He sends them out, they overwhelm the earth.
18_12_16: With Him are strength and prudence. The deceived and the deceiver are His.
18_12_17: He leads counselors away plundered, And makes fools of the judges.
18_12_18: He loosens the bonds of kings, And binds their waist with a belt.
18_12_19: He leads princes away plundered, And overthrows the mighty.
18_12_20: He deprives the trusted ones of speech, And takes away the discernment of the elders.
18_12_21: He pours contempt on princes, And disarms the mighty.
18_12_22: He uncovers deep things out of darkness, And brings the shadow of death to light.
18_12_23: He makes nations great, and destroys them; He enlarges nations, and guides them.
18_12_24: He takes away the understanding of the chiefs of the people of the earth, And makes them wander in a pathless wilderness.
18_12_25: They grope in the dark without light, And He makes them stagger like a drunken man.
18_13_1: “Behold, my eye has seen all this, My ear has heard and understood it.
18_13_2: What you know, I also know; I am not inferior to you.
18_13_3: But I would speak to the Almighty, And I desire to reason with God.
18_13_4: But you forgers of lies, You are all worthless physicians.
18_13_5: Oh, that you would be silent, And it would be your wisdom!
18_13_6: Now hear my reasoning, And heed the pleadings of my lips.
18_13_7: Will you speak wickedly for God, And talk deceitfully for Him?
18_13_8: Will you show partiality for Him? Will you contend for God?
18_13_9: Will it be well when He searches you out? Or can you mock Him as one mocks a man?
18_13_10: He will surely rebuke you If you secretly show partiality.
18_13_11: Will not His excellence make you afraid, And the dread of Him fall upon you?
18_13_12: Your platitudes are proverbs of ashes, Your defenses are defenses of clay.
18_13_13: “Hold your peace with me, and let me speak, Then let come on me what may!
18_13_14: Why do I take my flesh in my teeth, And put my life in my hands?
18_13_15: Though He slay me, yet will I trust Him. Even so, I will defend my own ways before Him.
18_13_16: He also shall be my salvation, For a hypocrite could not come before Him.
