18_13_17: Listen carefully to my speech, And to my declaration with your ears.
18_13_18: See now, I have prepared my case, I know that I shall be vindicated.
18_13_19: Who is he who will contend with me? If now I hold my tongue, I perish.
18_13_20: “Only two things do not do to me, Then I will not hide myself from You:
18_13_21: Withdraw Your hand far from me, And let not the dread of You make me afraid.
18_13_22: Then call, and I will answer; Or let me speak, then You respond to me.
18_13_23: How many are my iniquities and sins? Make me know my transgression and my sin.
18_13_24: Why do You hide Your face, And regard me as Your enemy?
18_13_25: Will You frighten a leaf driven to and fro? And will You pursue dry stubble?
18_13_26: For You write bitter things against me, And make me inherit the iniquities of my youth.
18_13_27: You put my feet in the stocks, And watch closely all my paths. You set a limit for the soles of my feet.
18_13_28: “Man decays like a rotten thing, Like a garment that is moth-eaten.
18_14_1: “Man who is born of woman Is of few days and full of trouble.
18_14_2: He comes forth like a flower and fades away; He flees like a shadow and does not continue.
18_14_3: And do You open Your eyes on such a one, And bring me to judgment with Yourself?
18_14_4: Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? No one!
18_14_5: Since his days are determined, The number of his months is with You; You have appointed his limits, so that he cannot pass.
18_14_6: Look away from him that he may rest, Till like a hired man he finishes his day.
18_14_7: “For there is hope for a tree, If it is cut down, that it will sprout again, And that its tender shoots will not cease.
18_14_8: Though its root may grow old in the earth, And its stump may die in the ground
18_14_9: Yet at the scent of water it will bud And bring forth branches like a plant.
18_14_10: But man dies and is laid away; Indeed he breathes his last And where is he?
18_14_11: As water disappears from the sea, And a river becomes parched and dries up
18_14_12: So man lies down and does not rise. Till the heavens are no more, They will not awake Nor be roused from their sleep.
18_14_13: “Oh, that You would hide me in the grave, That You would conceal me until Your wrath is past, That You would appoint me a set time, and remember me!
18_14_14: If a man dies, shall he live again? All the days of my hard service I will wait, Till my change comes.
18_14_15: You shall call, and I will answer You; You shall desire the work of Your hands.
18_14_16: For now You number my steps, But do not watch over my sin.
18_14_17: My transgression is sealed up in a bag, And You cover my iniquity.
18_14_18: “But as a mountain falls and crumbles away, And as a rock is moved from its place
18_14_19: As water wears away stones, And as torrents wash away the soil of the earth; So You destroy the hope of man.
18_14_20: You prevail forever against him, and he passes on; You change his countenance and send him away.
18_14_21: His sons come to honor, and he does not know it; They are brought low, and he does not perceive it.
18_14_22: But his flesh will be in pain over it, And his soul will mourn over it.”
18_15_1: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
18_15_2: “Should a wise man answer with empty knowledge, And fill himself with the east wind?
18_15_3: Should he reason with unprofitable talk, Or by speeches with which he can do no good?
18_15_4: Yes, you cast off fear, And restrain prayer before God.
18_15_5: For your iniquity teaches your mouth, And you choose the tongue of the crafty.
18_15_6: Your own mouth condemns you, and not I; Yes, your own lips testify against you.
18_15_7: “Are you the first man who was born? Or were you made before the hills?
18_15_8: Have you heard the counsel of God? Do you limit wisdom to yourself?
18_15_9: What do you know that we do not know? What do you understand that is not in us?
18_15_10: Both the gray-haired and the aged are among us, Much older than your father.
18_15_11: Are the consolations of God too small for you, And the word spoken gently with you?
18_15_12: Why does your heart carry you away, And what do your eyes wink at
18_15_13: That you turn your spirit against God, And let such words go out of your mouth?
18_15_14: “What is man, that he could be pure? And he who is born of a woman, that he could be righteous?
18_15_15: If God puts no trust in His saints, And the heavens are not pure in His sight
18_15_16: How much less man, who is abominable and filthy, Who drinks iniquity like water!
18_15_17: “I will tell you, hear me; What I have seen I will declare
18_15_18: What wise men have told, Not hiding anything received from their fathers
18_15_19: To whom alone the land was given, And no alien passed among them:
18_15_20: The wicked man writhes with pain all his days, And the number of years is hidden from the oppressor.
18_15_21: Dreadful sounds are in his ears; In prosperity the destroyer comes upon him.
18_15_22: He does not believe that he will return from darkness, For a sword is waiting for him.
18_15_23: He wanders about for bread, saying, ‘Where is it?’ He knows that a day of darkness is ready at his hand.
18_15_24: Trouble and anguish make him afraid; They overpower him, like a king ready for battle.
18_15_25: For he stretches out his hand against God, And acts defiantly against the Almighty
18_15_26: Running stubbornly against Him With his strong, embossed shield.
18_15_27: “Though he has covered his face with his fatness, And made his waist heavy with fat
18_15_28: He dwells in desolate cities, In houses which no one inhabits, Which are destined to become ruins.
18_15_29: He will not be rich, Nor will his wealth continue, Nor will his possessions overspread the earth.
18_15_30: He will not depart from darkness; The flame will dry out his branches, And by the breath of His mouth he will go away.
18_15_31: Let him not trust in futile things, deceiving himself, For futility will be his reward.
18_15_32: It will be accomplished before his time, And his branch will not be green.
18_15_33: He will shake off his unripe grape like a vine, And cast off his blossom like an olive tree.
18_15_34: For the company of hypocrites will be barren, And fire will consume the tents of bribery.
18_15_35: They conceive trouble and bring forth futility; Their womb prepares deceit.”
18_16_2: “I have heard many such things; Miserable comforters are you all!
18_16_3: Shall words of wind have an end? Or what provokes you that you answer?
18_16_4: I also could speak as you do, If your soul were in my soul’s place. I could heap up words against you, And shake my head at you
18_16_5: But I would strengthen you with my mouth, And the comfort of my lips would relieve your grief.
18_16_6: “Though I speak, my grief is not relieved; And if I remain silent, how am I eased?
18_16_7: But now He has worn me out; You have made desolate all my company.
18_16_8: You have shriveled me up, And it is a witness against me; My leanness rises up against me And bears witness to my face.
18_16_9: He tears me in His wrath, and hates me; He gnashes at me with His teeth; My adversary sharpens His gaze on me.
18_16_10: They gape at me with their mouth, They strike me reproachfully on the cheek, They gather together against me.
18_16_11: God has delivered me to the ungodly, And turned me over to the hands of the wicked.
18_16_12: I was at ease, but He has shattered me; He also has taken me by my neck, and shaken me to pieces; He has set me up for His target
18_16_13: His archers surround me. He pierces my heart and does not pity; He pours out my gall on the ground.
18_16_14: He breaks me with wound upon wound; He runs at me like a warrior.
18_16_15: “I have sewn sackcloth over my skin, And laid my head in the dust.
18_16_16: My face is flushed from weeping, And on my eyelids is the shadow of death
18_16_17: Although no violence is in my hands, And my prayer is pure.
18_16_18: “O earth, do not cover my blood, And let my cry have no resting place!
18_16_19: Surely even now my witness is in heaven, And my evidence is on high.
18_16_20: My friends scorn me; My eyes pour out tears to God.
18_16_21: Oh, that one might plead for a man with God, As a man pleads for his neighbor!
18_16_22: For when a few years are finished, I shall go the way of no return.
18_17_1: “My spirit is broken, My days are extinguished, The grave is ready for me.
18_17_2: Are not mockers with me? And does not my eye dwell on their provocation?
18_17_3: “Now put down a pledge for me with Yourself. Who is he who will shake hands with me?
18_17_4: For You have hidden their heart from understanding; Therefore You will not exalt them.
18_17_5: He who speaks flattery to his friends, Even the eyes of his children will fail.
18_17_6: “But He has made me a byword of the people, And I have become one in whose face men spit.
18_17_7: My eye has also grown dim because of sorrow, And all my members are like shadows.
18_17_8: Upright men are astonished at this, And the innocent stirs himself up against the hypocrite.
18_17_9: Yet the righteous will hold to his way, And he who has clean hands will be stronger and stronger.
18_17_10: “But please, come back again, all of you, For I shall not find one wise man among you.
18_17_11: My days are past, My purposes are broken off, Even the thoughts of my heart.
18_17_12: They change the night into day; ‘The light is near,’ they say, in the face of darkness.
18_17_13: If I wait for the grave as my house, If I make my bed in the darkness
18_17_14: If I say to corruption, ‘You are my father,’ And to the worm, ‘You are my mother and my sister,’
18_17_15: Where then is my hope? As for my hope, who can see it?
18_17_16: Will they go down to the gates of Sheol? Shall we have rest together in the dust?”
18_18_1: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
18_18_2: “How long till you put an end to words? Gain understanding, and afterward we will speak.
18_18_3: Why are we counted as beasts, And regarded as stupid in your sight?
18_18_4: You who tear yourself in anger, Shall the earth be forsaken for you? Or shall the rock be removed from its place?
18_18_5: “The light of the wicked indeed goes out, And the flame of his fire does not shine.
18_18_6: The light is dark in his tent, And his lamp beside him is put out.
18_18_7: The steps of his strength are shortened, And his own counsel casts him down.
18_18_8: For he is cast into a net by his own feet, And he walks into a snare.
18_18_9: The net takes him by the heel, And a snare lays hold of him.
18_18_10: A noose is hidden for him on the ground, And a trap for him in the road.
18_18_11: Terrors frighten him on every side, And drive him to his feet.
18_18_12: His strength is starved, And destruction is ready at his side.
18_18_13: It devours patches of his skin; The firstborn of death devours his limbs.
18_18_14: He is uprooted from the shelter of his tent, And they parade him before the king of terrors.
18_18_15: They dwell in his tent who are none of his; Brimstone is scattered on his dwelling.
18_18_16: His roots are dried out below, And his branch withers above.
18_18_17: The memory of him perishes from the earth, And he has no name among the renowned.
18_18_18: He is driven from light into darkness, And chased out of the world.
18_18_19: He has neither son nor posterity among his people, Nor any remaining in his dwellings.
18_18_20: Those in the west are astonished at his day, As those in the east are frightened.
18_18_21: Surely such are the dwellings of the wicked, And this is the place of him who does not know God.”
18_19_2: “How long will you torment my soul, And break me in pieces with words?
18_19_3: These ten times you have reproached me; You are not ashamed that you have wronged me.
18_19_4: And if indeed I have erred, My error remains with me.
18_19_5: If indeed you exalt yourselves against me, And plead my disgrace against me
18_19_6: Know then that God has wronged me, And has surrounded me with His net.
18_19_7: “If I cry out concerning wrong, I am not heard. If I cry aloud, there is no justice.
18_19_8: He has fenced up my way, so that I cannot pass; And He has set darkness in my paths.
18_19_9: He has stripped me of my glory, And taken the crown from my head.
18_19_10: He breaks me down on every side, And I am gone; My hope He has uprooted like a tree.
18_19_11: He has also kindled His wrath against me, And He counts me as one of His enemies.
18_19_12: His troops come together And build up their road against me; They encamp all around my tent.
18_19_13: “He has removed my brothers far from me, And my acquaintances are completely estranged from me.
18_19_14: My relatives have failed, And my close friends have forgotten me.
18_19_15: Those who dwell in my house, and my maidservants, Count me as a stranger; I am an alien in their sight.
18_19_16: I call my servant, but he gives no answer; I beg him with my mouth.
18_19_17: My breath is offensive to my wife, And I am repulsive to the children of my own body.
18_19_18: Even young children despise me; I arise, and they speak against me.
18_19_19: All my close friends abhor me, And those whom I love have turned against me.
18_19_20: My bone clings to my skin and to my flesh, And I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.
18_19_21: “Have pity on me, have pity on me, O you my friends, For the hand of God has struck me!
18_19_22: Why do you persecute me as God does, And are not satisfied with my flesh?
18_19_23: “Oh, that my words were written! Oh, that they were inscribed in a book!
18_19_24: That they were engraved on a rock With an iron pen and lead, forever!
18_19_25: For I know that my Redeemer lives, And He shall stand at last on the earth
18_19_26: And after my skin is destroyed, this I know, That in my flesh I shall see God
18_19_27: Whom I shall see for myself, And my eyes shall behold, and not another. How my heart yearns within me!
18_19_28: If you should say, ‘How shall we persecute him?’— Since the root of the matter is found in me
18_19_29: Be afraid of the sword for yourselves; For wrath brings the punishment of the sword, That you may know there is a judgment.”
18_20_1: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered and said:
18_20_2: “Therefore my anxious thoughts make me answer, Because of the turmoil within me.
18_20_3: I have heard the rebuke that reproaches me, And the spirit of my understanding causes me to answer.
18_20_4: “Do you not know this of old, Since man was placed on earth
18_20_5: That the triumphing of the wicked is short, And the joy of the hypocrite is but for a moment?
18_20_6: Though his haughtiness mounts up to the heavens, And his head reaches to the clouds
18_20_7: Yet he will perish forever like his own refuse; Those who have seen him will say, ‘Where is he?’
18_20_8: He will fly away like a dream, and not be found; Yes, he will be chased away like a vision of the night.
18_20_9: The eye that saw him will see him no more, Nor will his place behold him anymore.
18_20_10: His children will seek the favor of the poor, And his hands will restore his wealth.
18_20_11: His bones are full of his youthful vigor, But it will lie down with him in the dust.
18_20_12: “Though evil is sweet in his mouth, And he hides it under his tongue
18_20_13: Though he spares it and does not forsake it, But still keeps it in his mouth
18_20_14: Yet his food in his stomach turns sour; It becomes cobra venom within him.
18_20_15: He swallows down riches And vomits them up again; God casts them out of his belly.
18_20_16: He will suck the poison of cobras; The viper’s tongue will slay him.
18_20_17: He will not see the streams, The rivers flowing with honey and cream.
18_20_18: He will restore that for which he labored, And will not swallow it down; From the proceeds of business He will get no enjoyment.
18_20_19: For he has oppressed and forsaken the poor, He has violently seized a house which he did not build.
18_20_20: “Because he knows no quietness in his heart, He will not save anything he desires.
18_20_21: Nothing is left for him to eat; Therefore his well-being will not last.
18_20_22: In his self-sufficiency he will be in distress; Every hand of misery will come against him.
18_20_23: When he is about to fill his stomach, God will cast on him the fury of His wrath, And will rain it on him while he is eating.
18_20_24: He will flee from the iron weapon; A bronze bow will pierce him through.
18_20_25: It is drawn, and comes out of the body; Yes, the glittering point comes out of his gall. Terrors come upon him
18_20_26: Total darkness is reserved for his treasures. An unfanned fire will consume him; It shall go ill with him who is left in his tent.
18_20_27: The heavens will reveal his iniquity, And the earth will rise up against him.
18_20_28: The increase of his house will depart, And his goods will flow away in the day of His wrath.
18_20_29: This is the portion from God for a wicked man, The heritage appointed to him by God.”
18_21_2: “Listen carefully to my speech, And let this be your consolation.
18_21_3: Bear with me that I may speak, And after I have spoken, keep mocking.
18_21_4: “As for me, is my complaint against man? And if it were, why should I not be impatient?
18_21_5: Look at me and be astonished; Put your hand over your mouth.
18_21_6: Even when I remember I am terrified, And trembling takes hold of my flesh.
18_21_7: Why do the wicked live and become old, Yes, become mighty in power?
18_21_8: Their descendants are established with them in their sight, And their offspring before their eyes.
18_21_9: Their houses are safe from fear, Neither is the rod of God upon them.
18_21_10: Their bull breeds without failure; Their cow calves without miscarriage.
18_21_11: They send forth their little ones like a flock, And their children dance.
18_21_12: They sing to the tambourine and harp, And rejoice to the sound of the flute.
18_21_13: They spend their days in wealth, And in a moment go down to the grave.
18_21_14: Yet they say to God, ‘Depart from us, For we do not desire the knowledge of Your ways.
18_21_15: Who is the Almighty, that we should serve Him? And what profit do we have if we pray to Him?’
18_21_16: Indeed their prosperity is not in their hand; The counsel of the wicked is far from me.
18_21_17: “How often is the lamp of the wicked put out? How often does their destruction come upon them, The sorrows God distributes in His anger?
18_21_18: They are like straw before the wind, And like chaff that a storm carries away.
18_21_19: They say, ‘God lays up one’s iniquity for his children’; Let Him recompense him, that he may know it.
18_21_20: Let his eyes see his destruction, And let him drink of the wrath of the Almighty.
18_21_21: For what does he care about his household after him, When the number of his months is cut in half?
18_21_22: “Can anyone teach God knowledge, Since He judges those on high?
18_21_23: One dies in his full strength, Being wholly at ease and secure
18_21_24: His pails are full of milk, And the marrow of his bones is moist.
18_21_25: Another man dies in the bitterness of his soul, Never having eaten with pleasure.
18_21_26: They lie down alike in the dust, And worms cover them.
18_21_27: “Look, I know your thoughts, And the schemes with which you would wrong me.
18_21_28: For you say, ‘Where is the house of the prince? And where is the tent, The dwelling place of the wicked?’
18_21_29: Have you not asked those who travel the road? And do you not know their signs?
18_21_30: For the wicked are reserved for the day of doom; They shall be brought out on the day of wrath.
18_21_31: Who condemns his way to his face? And who repays him for what he has done?
18_21_32: Yet he shall be brought to the grave, And a vigil kept over the tomb.
18_21_33: The clods of the valley shall be sweet to him; Everyone shall follow him, As countless have gone before him.
18_21_34: How then can you comfort me with empty words, Since falsehood remains in your answers?”
18_22_1: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
18_22_2: “Can a man be profitable to God, Though he who is wise may be profitable to himself?
18_22_3: Is it any pleasure to the Almighty that you are righteous? Or is it gain to Him that you make your ways blameless?
18_22_4: “Is it because of your fear of Him that He corrects you, And enters into judgment with you?
18_22_5: Is not your wickedness great, And your iniquity without end?
18_22_6: For you have taken pledges from your brother for no reason, And stripped the naked of their clothing.
18_22_7: You have not given the weary water to drink, And you have withheld bread from the hungry.
18_22_8: But the mighty man possessed the land, And the honorable man dwelt in it.
18_22_9: You have sent widows away empty, And the strength of the fatherless was crushed.
18_22_10: Therefore snares are all around you, And sudden fear troubles you
18_22_11: Or darkness so that you cannot see; And an abundance of water covers you.
18_22_12: “Is not God in the height of heaven? And see the highest stars, how lofty they are!
18_22_13: And you say, ‘What does God know? Can He judge through the deep darkness?
18_22_14: Thick clouds cover Him, so that He cannot see, And He walks above the circle of heaven.’
18_22_15: Will you keep to the old way Which wicked men have trod
18_22_16: Who were cut down before their time, Whose foundations were swept away by a flood?
18_22_17: They said to God, ‘Depart from us! What can the Almighty do to them?’
18_22_18: Yet He filled their houses with good things; But the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
18_22_19: “The righteous see it and are glad, And the innocent laugh at them:
18_22_20: ‘Surely our adversaries are cut down, And the fire consumes their remnant.’
18_22_21: “Now acquaint yourself with Him, and be at peace; Thereby good will come to you.
18_22_22: Receive, please, instruction from His mouth, And lay up His words in your heart.
18_22_23: If you return to the Almighty, you will be built up; You will remove iniquity far from your tents.
18_22_24: Then you will lay your gold in the dust, And the gold of Ophir among the stones of the brooks.
18_22_25: Yes, the Almighty will be your gold And your precious silver
18_22_26: For then you will have your delight in the Almighty, And lift up your face to God.
18_22_27: You will make your prayer to Him, He will hear you, And you will pay your vows.
18_22_28: You will also declare a thing, And it will be established for you; So light will shine on your ways.
18_22_29: When they cast you down, and you say, ‘Exaltation will come!’ Then He will save the humble person.
18_22_30: He will even deliver one who is not innocent; Yes, he will be delivered by the purity of your hands.”
18_23_2: “Even today my complaint is bitter; My hand is listless because of my groaning.
18_23_3: Oh, that I knew where I might find Him, That I might come to His seat!
18_23_4: I would present my case before Him, And fill my mouth with arguments.
18_23_5: I would know the words which He would answer me, And understand what He would say to me.
18_23_6: Would He contend with me in His great power? No! But He would take note of me.
18_23_7: There the upright could reason with Him, And I would be delivered forever from my Judge.
18_23_8: “Look, I go forward, but He is not there, And backward, but I cannot perceive Him
18_23_9: When He works on the left hand, I cannot behold Him; When He turns to the right hand, I cannot see Him.
18_23_10: But He knows the way that I take; When He has tested me, I shall come forth as gold.
18_23_11: My foot has held fast to His steps; I have kept His way and not turned aside.
18_23_12: I have not departed from the commandment of His lips; I have treasured the words of His mouth More than my necessary food.
18_23_13: “But He is unique, and who can make Him change? And whatever His soul desires, that He does.
18_23_14: For He performs what is appointed for me, And many such things are with Him.
18_23_15: Therefore I am terrified at His presence; When I consider this, I am afraid of Him.
18_23_16: For God made my heart weak, And the Almighty terrifies me
18_23_17: Because I was not cut off from the presence of darkness, And He did not hide deep darkness from my face.
18_24_1: “Since times are not hidden from the Almighty, Why do those who know Him see not His days?
18_24_2: “Some remove landmarks; They seize flocks violently and feed on them
18_24_3: They drive away the donkey of the fatherless; They take the widow’s ox as a pledge.
18_24_4: They push the needy off the road; All the poor of the land are forced to hide.
18_24_5: Indeed, like wild donkeys in the desert, They go out to their work, searching for food. The wilderness yields food for them and for their children.
18_24_6: They gather their fodder in the field And glean in the vineyard of the wicked.
18_24_7: They spend the night naked, without clothing, And have no covering in the cold.
18_24_8: They are wet with the showers of the mountains, And huddle around the rock for want of shelter.
18_24_9: “Some snatch the fatherless from the breast, And take a pledge from the poor.
18_24_10: They cause the poor to go naked, without clothing; And they take away the sheaves from the hungry.
18_24_11: They press out oil within their walls, And tread winepresses, yet suffer thirst.
18_24_12: The dying groan in the city, And the souls of the wounded cry out; Yet God does not charge them with wrong.
18_24_13: “There are those who rebel against the light; They do not know its ways Nor abide in its paths.
18_24_14: The murderer rises with the light; He kills the poor and needy; And in the night he is like a thief.
18_24_15: The eye of the adulterer waits for the twilight, Saying, ‘No eye will see me’; And he disguises his face.
18_24_16: In the dark they break into houses Which they marked for themselves in the daytime; They do not know the light.
18_24_17: For the morning is the same to them as the shadow of death; If someone recognizes them, They are in the terrors of the shadow of death.
18_24_18: “They should be swift on the face of the waters, Their portion should be cursed in the earth, So that no one would turn into the way of their vineyards.
18_24_19: As drought and heat consume the snow waters, So the grave consumes those who have sinned.
18_24_20: The womb should forget him, The worm should feed sweetly on him; He should be remembered no more, And wickedness should be broken like a tree.
18_24_21: For he preys on the barren who do not bear, And does no good for the widow.
18_24_22: “But God draws the mighty away with His power; He rises up, but no man is sure of life.
18_24_23: He gives them security, and they rely on it; Yet His eyes are on their ways.
18_24_24: They are exalted for a little while, Then they are gone. They are brought low; They are taken out of the way like all others; They dry out like the heads of grain.
18_24_25: “Now if it is not so, who will prove me a liar, And make my speech worth nothing?”
18_25_1: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
18_25_2: “Dominion and fear belong to Him; He makes peace in His high places.
18_25_3: Is there any number to His armies? Upon whom does His light not rise?
18_25_4: How then can man be righteous before God? Or how can he be pure who is born of a woman?
18_25_5: If even the moon does not shine, And the stars are not pure in His sight
18_25_6: How much less man, who is a maggot, And a son of man, who is a worm?”
18_26_2: “How have you helped him who is without power? How have you saved the arm that has no strength?
18_26_3: How have you counseled one who has no wisdom? And how have you declared sound advice to many?
18_26_4: To whom have you uttered words? And whose spirit came from you?
18_26_5: “The dead tremble, Those under the waters and those inhabiting them.
18_26_6: Sheol is naked before Him, And Destruction has no covering.
18_26_7: He stretches out the north over empty space; He hangs the earth on nothing.
18_26_8: He binds up the water in His thick clouds, Yet the clouds are not broken under it.
18_26_9: He covers the face of His throne, And spreads His cloud over it.
18_26_10: He drew a circular horizon on the face of the waters, At the boundary of light and darkness.
18_26_11: The pillars of heaven tremble, And are astonished at His rebuke.
18_26_12: He stirs up the sea with His power, And by His understanding He breaks up the storm.
18_26_13: By His Spirit He adorned the heavens; His hand pierced the fleeing serpent.
18_26_14: Indeed these are the mere edges of His ways, And how small a whisper we hear of Him! But the thunder of His power who can understand?”
18_27_1: Moreover Job continued his discourse, and said:
18_27_2: “As God lives, who has taken away my justice, And the Almighty, who has made my soul bitter
18_27_3: As long as my breath is in me, And the breath of God in my nostrils
18_27_4: My lips will not speak wickedness, Nor my tongue utter deceit.
18_27_5: Far be it from me That I should say you are right; Till I die I will not put away my integrity from me.
18_27_6: My righteousness I hold fast, and will not let it go; My heart shall not reproach me as long as I live.
18_27_7: “May my enemy be like the wicked, And he who rises up against me like the unrighteous.
18_27_8: For what is the hope of the hypocrite, Though he may gain much, If God takes away his life?
18_27_9: Will God hear his cry When trouble comes upon him?
18_27_10: Will he delight himself in the Almighty? Will he always call on God?
18_27_11: “I will teach you about the hand of God; What is with the Almighty I will not conceal.
18_27_12: Surely all of you have seen it; Why then do you behave with complete nonsense?
18_27_13: “This is the portion of a wicked man with God, And the heritage of oppressors, received from the Almighty:
18_27_14: If his children are multiplied, it is for the sword; And his offspring shall not be satisfied with bread.
18_27_15: Those who survive him shall be buried in death, And their widows shall not weep
18_27_16: Though he heaps up silver like dust, And piles up clothing like clay—
18_27_17: He may pile it up, but the just will wear it, And the innocent will divide the silver.
18_27_18: He builds his house like a moth, Like a booth which a watchman makes.
18_27_19: The rich man will lie down, But not be gathered up; He opens his eyes, And he is no more.
18_27_20: Terrors overtake him like a flood; A tempest steals him away in the night.
18_27_21: The east wind carries him away, and he is gone; It sweeps him out of his place.
18_27_22: It hurls against him and does not spare; He flees desperately from its power.
18_27_23: Men shall clap their hands at him, And shall hiss him out of his place.
18_28_1: “Surely there is a mine for silver, And a place where gold is refined.
18_28_2: Iron is taken from the earth, And copper is smelted from ore.
18_28_3: Man puts an end to darkness, And searches every recess For ore in the darkness and the shadow of death.
18_28_4: He breaks open a shaft away from people; In places forgotten by feet They hang far away from men; They swing to and fro.
18_28_5: As for the earth, from it comes bread, But underneath it is turned up as by fire
18_28_6: Its stones are the source of sapphires, And it contains gold dust.
18_28_7: That path no bird knows, Nor has the falcon’s eye seen it.
18_28_8: The proud lions have not trodden it, Nor has the fierce lion passed over it.
18_28_9: He puts his hand on the flint; He overturns the mountains at the roots.
18_28_10: He cuts out channels in the rocks, And his eye sees every precious thing.
18_28_11: He dams up the streams from trickling; What is hidden he brings forth to light.
18_28_12: “But where can wisdom be found? And where is the place of understanding?
18_28_13: Man does not know its value, Nor is it found in the land of the living.
18_28_14: The deep says, ‘It is not in me’; And the sea says, ‘It is not with me.’
18_28_15: It cannot be purchased for gold, Nor can silver be weighed for its price.
18_28_16: It cannot be valued in the gold of Ophir, In precious onyx or sapphire.
18_28_17: Neither gold nor crystal can equal it, Nor can it be exchanged for jewelry of fine gold.
18_28_18: No mention shall be made of coral or quartz, For the price of wisdom is above rubies.
18_28_19: The topaz of Ethiopia cannot equal it, Nor can it be valued in pure gold.
18_28_20: “From where then does wisdom come? And where is the place of understanding?
18_28_21: It is hidden from the eyes of all living, And concealed from the birds of the air.
18_28_22: Destruction and Death say, ‘We have heard a report about it with our ears.’
18_28_23: God understands its way, And He knows its place.
18_28_24: For He looks to the ends of the earth, And sees under the whole heavens
18_28_25: To establish a weight for the wind, And apportion the waters by measure.
18_28_26: When He made a law for the rain, And a path for the thunderbolt
18_28_27: Then He saw wisdom and declared it; He prepared it, indeed, He searched it out.
18_28_28: And to man He said, ‘Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom, And to depart from evil is understanding.’ ”
18_29_1: Job further continued his discourse, and said:
18_29_2: “Oh, that I were as in months past, As in the days when God watched over me
18_29_3: When His lamp shone upon my head, And when by His light I walked through darkness
18_29_4: Just as I was in the days of my prime, When the friendly counsel of God was over my tent
18_29_5: When the Almighty was yet with me, When my children were around me
18_29_6: When my steps were bathed with cream, And the rock poured out rivers of oil for me!
18_29_7: “When I went out to the gate by the city, When I took my seat in the open square
18_29_8: The young men saw me and hid, And the aged arose and stood
18_29_9: The princes refrained from talking, And put their hand on their mouth
18_29_10: The voice of nobles was hushed, And their tongue stuck to the roof of their mouth.
18_29_11: When the ear heard, then it blessed me, And when the eye saw, then it approved me
18_29_12: Because I delivered the poor who cried out, The fatherless and the one who had no helper.
18_29_13: The blessing of a perishing man came upon me, And I caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy.
18_29_14: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me; My justice was like a robe and a turban.
18_29_15: I was eyes to the blind, And I was feet to the lame.
18_29_16: I was a father to the poor, And I searched out the case that I did not know.
18_29_17: I broke the fangs of the wicked, And plucked the victim from his teeth.
18_29_18: “Then I said, ‘I shall die in my nest, And multiply my days as the sand.
18_29_19: My root is spread out to the waters, And the dew lies all night on my branch.
18_29_20: My glory is fresh within me, And my bow is renewed in my hand.’
18_29_21: “Men listened to me and waited, And kept silence for my counsel.
18_29_22: After my words they did not speak again, And my speech settled on them as dew.
18_29_23: They waited for me as for the rain, And they opened their mouth wide as for the spring rain.
18_29_24: If I mocked at them, they did not believe it, And the light of my countenance they did not cast down.
18_29_25: I chose the way for them, and sat as chief; So I dwelt as a king in the army, As one who comforts mourners.
18_30_1: “But now they mock at me, men younger than I, Whose fathers I disdained to put with the dogs of my flock.
18_30_2: Indeed, what profit is the strength of their hands to me? Their vigor has perished.
18_30_3: They are gaunt from want and famine, Fleeing late to the wilderness, desolate and waste
18_30_4: Who pluck mallow by the bushes, And broom tree roots for their food.
18_30_5: They were driven out from among men, They shouted at them as at a thief.
18_30_6: They had to live in the clefts of the valleys, In caves of the earth and the rocks.
18_30_7: Among the bushes they brayed, Under the nettles they nestled.
18_30_8: They were sons of fools, Yes, sons of vile men; They were scourged from the land.
18_30_9: “And now I am their taunting song; Yes, I am their byword.
18_30_10: They abhor me, they keep far from me; They do not hesitate to spit in my face.
18_30_11: Because He has loosed my bowstring and afflicted me, They have cast off restraint before me.
18_30_12: At my right hand the rabble arises; They push away my feet, And they raise against me their ways of destruction.
18_30_13: They break up my path, They promote my calamity; They have no helper.
18_30_14: They come as broad breakers; Under the ruinous storm they roll along.
18_30_15: Terrors are turned upon me; They pursue my honor as the wind, And my prosperity has passed like a cloud.
18_30_16: “And now my soul is poured out because of my plight; The days of affliction take hold of me.
18_30_17: My bones are pierced in me at night, And my gnawing pains take no rest.
18_30_18: By great force my garment is disfigured; It binds me about as the collar of my coat.
18_30_19: He has cast me into the mire, And I have become like dust and ashes.
18_30_20: “I cry out to You, but You do not answer me; I stand up, and You regard me.
18_30_21: But You have become cruel to me; With the strength of Your hand You oppose me.
18_30_22: You lift me up to the wind and cause me to ride on it; You spoil my success.
18_30_23: For I know that You will bring me to death, And to the house appointed for all living.
18_30_24: “Surely He would not stretch out His hand against a heap of ruins, If they cry out when He destroys it.
18_30_25: Have I not wept for him who was in trouble? Has not my soul grieved for the poor?
18_30_26: But when I looked for good, evil came to me; And when I waited for light, then came darkness.
18_30_27: My heart is in turmoil and cannot rest; Days of affliction confront me.
18_30_28: I go about mourning, but not in the sun; I stand up in the assembly and cry out for help.
18_30_29: I am a brother of jackals, And a companion of ostriches.
18_30_30: My skin grows black and falls from me; My bones burn with fever.
18_30_31: My harp is turned to mourning, And my flute to the voice of those who weep.
18_31_1: “I have made a covenant with my eyes; Why then should I look upon a young woman?
18_31_2: For what is the allotment of God from above, And the inheritance of the Almighty from on high?
18_31_3: Is it not destruction for the wicked, And disaster for the workers of iniquity?
18_31_4: Does He not see my ways, And count all my steps?
18_31_5: “If I have walked with falsehood, Or if my foot has hastened to deceit
18_31_6: Let me be weighed on honest scales, That God may know my integrity.
18_31_7: If my step has turned from the way, Or my heart walked after my eyes, Or if any spot adheres to my hands
18_31_8: Then let me sow, and another eat; Yes, let my harvest be rooted out.
18_31_9: “If my heart has been enticed by a woman, Or if I have lurked at my neighbor’s door
18_31_10: Then let my wife grind for another, And let others bow down over her.
18_31_11: For that would be wickedness; Yes, it would be iniquity deserving of judgment.
18_31_12: For that would be a fire that consumes to destruction, And would root out all my increase.
18_31_13: “If I have despised the cause of my male or female servant When they complained against me
18_31_14: What then shall I do when God rises up? When He punishes, how shall I answer Him?
18_31_15: Did not He who made me in the womb make them? Did not the same One fashion us in the womb?
18_31_16: “If I have kept the poor from their desire, Or caused the eyes of the widow to fail
18_31_17: Or eaten my morsel by myself, So that the fatherless could not eat of it
18_31_18: (But from my youth I reared him as a father, And from my mother’s womb I guided the widow)
18_31_19: If I have seen anyone perish for lack of clothing, Or any poor man without covering
18_31_20: If his heart has not blessed me, And if he was not warmed with the fleece of my sheep
18_31_21: If I have raised my hand against the fatherless, When I saw I had help in the gate
18_31_22: Then let my arm fall from my shoulder, Let my arm be torn from the socket.
18_31_23: For destruction from God is a terror to me, And because of His magnificence I cannot endure.
18_31_24: “If I have made gold my hope, Or said to fine gold, ‘You are my confidence’
18_31_25: If I have rejoiced because my wealth was great, And because my hand had gained much
18_31_26: If I have observed the sun when it shines, Or the moon moving in brightness
18_31_27: So that my heart has been secretly enticed, And my mouth has kissed my hand
18_31_28: This also would be an iniquity deserving of judgment, For I would have denied God who is above.
18_31_29: “If I have rejoiced at the destruction of him who hated me, Or lifted myself up when evil found him
18_31_30: (Indeed I have not allowed my mouth to sin By asking for a curse on his soul)
18_31_31: If the men of my tent have not said, ‘Who is there that has not been satisfied with his meat?’
18_31_32: (But no sojourner had to lodge in the street, For I have opened my doors to the traveler)
18_31_33: If I have covered my transgressions as Adam, By hiding my iniquity in my bosom
18_31_34: Because I feared the great multitude, And dreaded the contempt of families, So that I kept silence And did not go out of the door—
18_31_35: Oh, that I had one to hear me! Here is my mark. Oh, that the Almighty would answer me, That my Prosecutor had written a book!
18_31_36: Surely I would carry it on my shoulder, And bind it on me like a crown
18_31_37: I would declare to Him the number of my steps; Like a prince I would approach Him.
18_31_38: “If my land cries out against me, And its furrows weep together
18_31_39: If I have eaten its fruit without money, Or caused its owners to lose their lives
18_31_40: Then let thistles grow instead of wheat, And weeds instead of barley.” The words of Job are ended.
18_32_1: So these three men ceased answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
18_32_2: Then the wrath of Elihu, the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, was aroused against Job; his wrath was aroused because he justified himself rather than God.
18_32_3: Also against his three friends his wrath was aroused, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.
18_32_4: Now because they were years older than he, Elihu had waited to speak to Job.
18_32_5: When Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, his wrath was aroused.
18_32_6: So Elihu, the son of Barachel the Buzite, answered and said: “I am young in years, and you are very old; Therefore I was afraid, And dared not declare my opinion to you.
18_32_7: I said, ‘Age should speak, And multitude of years should teach wisdom.’
18_32_8: But there is a spirit in man, And the breath of the Almighty gives him understanding.
18_32_9: Great men are not always wise, Nor do the aged always understand justice.
18_32_10: “Therefore I say, ‘Listen to me, I also will declare my opinion.’
18_32_11: Indeed I waited for your words, I listened to your reasonings, while you searched out what to say.
18_32_12: I paid close attention to you; And surely not one of you convinced Job, Or answered his words—
18_32_13: Lest you say, ‘We have found wisdom’; God will vanquish him, not man.
18_32_14: Now he has not directed his words against me; So I will not answer him with your words.
18_32_15: “They are dismayed and answer no more; Words escape them.
18_32_16: And I have waited, because they did not speak, Because they stood still and answered no more.
18_32_17: I also will answer my part, I too will declare my opinion.
18_32_18: For I am full of words; The spirit within me compels me.
18_32_19: Indeed my belly is like wine that has no vent; It is ready to burst like new wineskins.
18_32_20: I will speak, that I may find relief; I must open my lips and answer.
18_32_21: Let me not, I pray, show partiality to anyone; Nor let me flatter any man.
18_32_22: For I do not know how to flatter, Else my Maker would soon take me away.
18_33_1: “But please, Job, hear my speech, And listen to all my words.
18_33_2: Now, I open my mouth; My tongue speaks in my mouth.
18_33_3: My words come from my upright heart; My lips utter pure knowledge.
18_33_4: The Spirit of God has made me, And the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
18_33_5: If you can answer me, Set your words in order before me; Take your stand.
18_33_6: Truly I am as your spokesman before God; I also have been formed out of clay.
18_33_7: Surely no fear of me will terrify you, Nor will my hand be heavy on you.
18_33_8: “Surely you have spoken in my hearing, And I have heard the sound of your words, saying
18_33_9: ‘I am pure, without transgression; I am innocent, and there is no iniquity in me.
18_33_10: Yet He finds occasions against me, He counts me as His enemy
18_33_11: He puts my feet in the stocks, He watches all my paths.’
18_33_12: “Look, in this you are not righteous. I will answer you, For God is greater than man.
18_33_13: Why do you contend with Him? For He does not give an accounting of any of His words.
18_33_14: For God may speak in one way, or in another, Yet man does not perceive it.
18_33_15: In a dream, in a vision of the night, When deep sleep falls upon men, While slumbering on their beds
18_33_16: Then He opens the ears of men, And seals their instruction.
18_33_17: In order to turn man from his deed, And conceal pride from man
18_33_18: He keeps back his soul from the Pit, And his life from perishing by the sword.
18_33_19: “Man is also chastened with pain on his bed, And with strong pain in many of his bones
18_33_20: So that his life abhors bread, And his soul succulent food.
18_33_21: His flesh wastes away from sight, And his bones stick out which once were not seen.
18_33_22: Yes, his soul draws near the Pit, And his life to the executioners.
18_33_23: “If there is a messenger for him, A mediator, one among a thousand, To show man His uprightness
18_33_24: Then He is gracious to him, and says, ‘Deliver him from going down to the Pit; I have found a ransom’
18_33_25: His flesh shall be young like a child’s, He shall return to the days of his youth.
18_33_26: He shall pray to God, and He will delight in him, He shall see His face with joy, For He restores to man His righteousness.
18_33_27: Then he looks at men and says, ‘I have sinned, and perverted what was right, And it did not profit me.’
18_33_28: He will redeem his soul from going down to the Pit, And his life shall see the light.
18_33_29: “Behold, God works all these things, Twice, in fact, three times with a man
18_33_30: To bring back his soul from the Pit, That he may be enlightened with the light of life.
18_33_31: “Give ear, Job, listen to me; Hold your peace, and I will speak.
18_33_32: If you have anything to say, answer me; Speak, for I desire to justify you.
18_33_33: If not, listen to me; Hold your peace, and I will teach you wisdom.”
18_34_2: “Hear my words, you wise men; Give ear to me, you who have knowledge.
18_34_3: For the ear tests words As the palate tastes food.
18_34_4: Let us choose justice for ourselves; Let us know among ourselves what is good.
18_34_5: “For Job has said, ‘I am righteous, But God has taken away my justice
18_34_6: Should I lie concerning my right? My wound is incurable, though I am without transgression.’
18_34_7: What man is like Job, Who drinks scorn like water
18_34_8: Who goes in company with the workers of iniquity, And walks with wicked men?
18_34_9: For he has said, ‘It profits a man nothing That he should delight in God.’
18_34_10: “Therefore listen to me, you men of understanding: Far be it from God to do wickedness, And from the Almighty to commit iniquity.
18_34_11: For He repays man according to his work, And makes man to find a reward according to his way.
18_34_12: Surely God will never do wickedly, Nor will the Almighty pervert justice.
18_34_13: Who gave Him charge over the earth? Or who appointed Him over the whole world?
18_34_14: If He should set His heart on it, If He should gather to Himself His Spirit and His breath
18_34_15: All flesh would perish together, And man would return to dust.
18_34_16: “If you have understanding, hear this; Listen to the sound of my words:
18_34_17: Should one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn Him who is most just?
18_34_18: Is it fitting to say to a king, ‘You are worthless,’ And to nobles, ‘You are wicked’?
18_34_19: Yet He is not partial to princes, Nor does He regard the rich more than the poor; For they are all the work of His hands.
18_34_20: In a moment they die, in the middle of the night; The people are shaken and pass away; The mighty are taken away without a hand.
18_34_21: “For His eyes are on the ways of man, And He sees all his steps.
18_34_22: There is no darkness nor shadow of death Where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.
18_34_23: For He need not further consider a man, That he should go before God in judgment.
18_34_24: He breaks in pieces mighty men without inquiry, And sets others in their place.
18_34_25: Therefore He knows their works; He overthrows them in the night, And they are crushed.
18_34_26: He strikes them as wicked men In the open sight of others
18_34_27: Because they turned back from Him, And would not consider any of His ways
18_34_28: So that they caused the cry of the poor to come to Him; For He hears the cry of the afflicted.
18_34_29: When He gives quietness, who then can make trouble? And when He hides His face, who then can see Him, Whether it is against a nation or a man alone?—
18_34_30: That the hypocrite should not reign, Lest the people be ensnared.
18_34_31: “For has anyone said to God, ‘I have borne chastening; I will offend no more
18_34_32: Teach me what I do not see; If I have done iniquity, I will do no more’?
18_34_33: Should He repay it according to your terms, Just because you disavow it? You must choose, and not I; Therefore speak what you know.
18_34_34: “Men of understanding say to me, Wise men who listen to me:
18_34_35: ‘Job speaks without knowledge, His words are without wisdom.’
18_34_36: Oh, that Job were tried to the utmost, Because his answers are like those of wicked men!
18_34_37: For he adds rebellion to his sin; He claps his hands among us, And multiplies his words against God.”
21_1_1: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.
21_1_2: “Vanity of vanities,” says the Preacher; “Vanity of vanities, all is vanity.”
21_1_3: What profit has a man from all his labor In which he toils under the sun?
21_1_4: One generation passes away, and another generation comes; But the earth abides forever.
21_1_5: The sun also rises, and the sun goes down, And hastens to the place where it arose.
21_1_6: The wind goes toward the south, And turns around to the north; The wind whirls about continually, And comes again on its circuit.
21_1_7: All the rivers run into the sea, Yet the sea is not full; To the place from which the rivers come, There they return again.
21_1_8: All things are full of labor; Man cannot express it. The eye is not satisfied with seeing, Nor the ear filled with hearing.
21_1_9: That which has been is what will be, That which is done is what will be done, And there is nothing new under the sun.
21_1_10: Is there anything of which it may be said, “See, this is new”? It has already been in ancient times before us.
21_1_11: There is no remembrance of former things, Nor will there be any remembrance of things that are to come By those who will come after.
21_1_12: I, the Preacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
21_1_13: And I set my heart to seek and search out by wisdom concerning all that is done under heaven; this burdensome task God has given to the sons of man, by which they may be exercised.
21_1_14: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and indeed, all is vanity and grasping for the wind.
21_1_15: What is crooked cannot be made straight, And what is lacking cannot be numbered.
21_1_16: I communed with my heart, saying, “Look, I have attained greatness, and have gained more wisdom than all who were before me in Jerusalem. My heart has understood great wisdom and knowledge.”
21_1_17: And I set my heart to know wisdom and to know madness and folly. I perceived that this also is grasping for the wind.
21_1_18: For in much wisdom is much grief, And he who increases knowledge increases sorrow.
21_2_1: I said in my heart, “Come now, I will test you with mirth; therefore enjoy pleasure”; but surely, this also was vanity.
21_2_2: I said of laughter—“Madness!”; and of mirth, “What does it accomplish?”
21_2_3: I searched in my heart how to gratify my flesh with wine, while guiding my heart with wisdom, and how to lay hold on folly, till I might see what was good for the sons of men to do under heaven all the days of their lives.
21_2_4: I made my works great, I built myself houses, and planted myself vineyards.
21_2_5: I made myself gardens and orchards, and I planted all kinds of fruit trees in them.
21_2_6: I made myself water pools from which to water the growing trees of the grove.
21_2_7: I acquired male and female servants, and had servants born in my house. Yes, I had greater possessions of herds and flocks than all who were in Jerusalem before me.
21_2_8: I also gathered for myself silver and gold and the special treasures of kings and of the provinces. I acquired male and female singers, the delights of the sons of men, and musical instruments of all kinds.
21_2_9: So I became great and excelled more than all who were before me in Jerusalem. Also my wisdom remained with me.
21_2_10: Whatever my eyes desired I did not keep from them. I did not withhold my heart from any pleasure, For my heart rejoiced in all my labor; And this was my reward from all my labor.
21_2_11: Then I looked on all the works that my hands had done And on the labor in which I had toiled; And indeed all was vanity and grasping for the wind. There was no profit under the sun.
21_2_12: Then I turned myself to consider wisdom and madness and folly; For what can the man do who succeeds the king?— Only what he has already done.
21_2_13: Then I saw that wisdom excels folly As light excels darkness.
21_2_14: The wise man’s eyes are in his head, But the fool walks in darkness. Yet I myself perceived That the same event happens to them all.
21_2_15: So I said in my heart, “As it happens to the fool, It also happens to me, And why was I then more wise?” Then I said in my heart, “This also is vanity.”
21_2_16: For there is no more remembrance of the wise than of the fool forever, Since all that now is will be forgotten in the days to come. And how does a wise man die? As the fool!
21_2_17: Therefore I hated life because the work that was done under the sun was distressing to me, for all is vanity and grasping for the wind.
21_2_18: Then I hated all my labor in which I had toiled under the sun, because I must leave it to the man who will come after me.
21_2_19: And who knows whether he will be wise or a fool? Yet he will rule over all my labor in which I toiled and in which I have shown myself wise under the sun. This also is vanity.
21_2_20: Therefore I turned my heart and despaired of all the labor in which I had toiled under the sun.
21_2_21: For there is a man whose labor is with wisdom, knowledge, and skill; yet he must leave his heritage to a man who has not labored for it. This also is vanity and a great evil.
21_2_22: For what has man for all his labor, and for the striving of his heart with which he has toiled under the sun?
21_2_23: For all his days are sorrowful, and his work burdensome; even in the night his heart takes no rest. This also is vanity.
21_2_24: Nothing is better for a man than that he should eat and drink, and that his soul should enjoy good in his labor. This also, I saw, was from the hand of God.
21_2_25: For who can eat, or who can have enjoyment, more than I?
21_2_26: For God gives wisdom and knowledge and joy to a man who is good in His sight; but to the sinner He gives the work of gathering and collecting, that he may give to him who is good before God. This also is vanity and grasping for the wind.
21_3_1: To everything there is a season, A time for every purpose under heaven:
21_3_2: A time to be born, And a time to die; A time to plant, And a time to pluck what is planted
21_3_3: A time to kill, And a time to heal; A time to break down, And a time to build up
21_3_4: A time to weep, And a time to laugh; A time to mourn, And a time to dance
21_3_5: A time to cast away stones, And a time to gather stones; A time to embrace, And a time to refrain from embracing
21_3_6: A time to gain, And a time to lose; A time to keep, And a time to throw away
21_3_7: A time to tear, And a time to sew; A time to keep silence, And a time to speak
21_3_8: A time to love, And a time to hate; A time of war, And a time of peace.
21_3_9: What profit has the worker from that in which he labors?
21_3_10: I have seen the God-given task with which the sons of men are to be occupied.
21_3_11: He has made everything beautiful in its time. Also He has put eternity in their hearts, except that no one can find out the work that God does from beginning to end.
21_3_12: I know that nothing is better for them than to rejoice, and to do good in their lives
21_3_13: and also that every man should eat and drink and enjoy the good of all his labor—it is the gift of God.
21_3_14: I know that whatever God does, It shall be forever. Nothing can be added to it, And nothing taken from it. God does it, that men should fear before Him.
21_3_15: That which is has already been, And what is to be has already been; And God requires an account of what is past.
21_3_16: Moreover I saw under the sun: In the place of judgment, Wickedness was there; And in the place of righteousness, Iniquity was there.
21_3_17: I said in my heart, “God shall judge the righteous and the wicked, For there is a time there for every purpose and for every work.”
21_3_18: I said in my heart, “Concerning the condition of the sons of men, God tests them, that they may see that they themselves are like animals.”
21_3_19: For what happens to the sons of men also happens to animals; one thing befalls them: as one dies, so dies the other. Surely, they all have one breath; man has no advantage over animals, for all is vanity.
21_3_20: All go to one place: all are from the dust, and all return to dust.
21_3_21: Who knows the spirit of the sons of men, which goes upward, and the spirit of the animal, which goes down to the earth?
21_3_22: So I perceived that nothing is better than that a man should rejoice in his own works, for that is his heritage. For who can bring him to see what will happen after him?
21_4_1: Then I returned and considered all the oppression that is done under the sun: And look! The tears of the oppressed, But they have no comforter— On the side of their oppressors there is power, But they have no comforter.
21_4_2: Therefore I praised the dead who were already dead, More than the living who are still alive.
21_4_3: Yet, better than both is he who has never existed, Who has not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.
21_4_4: Again, I saw that for all toil and every skillful work a man is envied by his neighbor. This also is vanity and grasping for the wind.
21_4_5: The fool folds his hands And consumes his own flesh.
21_4_6: Better a handful with quietness Than both hands full, together with toil and grasping for the wind.
21_4_7: Then I returned, and I saw vanity under the sun:
21_4_8: There is one alone, without companion: He has neither son nor brother. Yet there is no end to all his labors, Nor is his eye satisfied with riches. But he never asks, “For whom do I toil and deprive myself of good?” This also is vanity and a grave misfortune.
21_4_9: Two are better than one, Because they have a good reward for their labor.
21_4_10: For if they fall, one will lift up his companion. But woe to him who is alone when he falls, For he has no one to help him up.
21_4_11: Again, if two lie down together, they will keep warm; But how can one be warm alone?
21_4_12: Though one may be overpowered by another, two can withstand him. And a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
21_4_13: Better a poor and wise youth Than an old and foolish king who will be admonished no more.
21_4_14: For he comes out of prison to be king, Although he was born poor in his kingdom.
21_4_15: I saw all the living who walk under the sun; They were with the second youth who stands in his place.
21_4_16: There was no end of all the people over whom he was made king; Yet those who come afterward will not rejoice in him. Surely this also is vanity and grasping for the wind.
21_5_1: Walk prudently when you go to the house of God; and draw near to hear rather than to give the sacrifice of fools, for they do not know that they do evil.
21_5_2: Do not be rash with your mouth, And let not your heart utter anything hastily before God. For God is in heaven, and you on earth; Therefore let your words be few.
21_5_3: For a dream comes through much activity, And a fool’s voice is known by his many words.
21_5_4: When you make a vow to God, do not delay to pay it; For He has no pleasure in fools. Pay what you have vowed—
21_5_5: Better not to vow than to vow and not pay.
21_5_6: Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, nor say before the messenger of God that it was an error. Why should God be angry at your excuse and destroy the work of your hands?
21_5_7: For in the multitude of dreams and many words there is also vanity. But fear God.
21_5_8: If you see the oppression of the poor, and the violent perversion of justice and righteousness in a province, do not marvel at the matter; for high official watches over high official, and higher officials are over them.
21_5_9: Moreover the profit of the land is for all; even the king is served from the field.
21_5_10: He who loves silver will not be satisfied with silver; Nor he who loves abundance, with increase. This also is vanity.
21_5_11: When goods increase, They increase who eat them; So what profit have the owners Except to see them with their eyes?
21_5_12: The sleep of a laboring man is sweet, Whether he eats little or much; But the abundance of the rich will not permit him to sleep.
21_5_13: There is a severe evil which I have seen under the sun: Riches kept for their owner to his hurt.
21_5_14: But those riches perish through misfortune; When he begets a son, there is nothing in his hand.
21_5_15: As he came from his mother’s womb, naked shall he return, To go as he came; And he shall take nothing from his labor Which he may carry away in his hand.
21_5_16: And this also is a severe evil— Just exactly as he came, so shall he go. And what profit has he who has labored for the wind?
21_5_17: All his days he also eats in darkness, And he has much sorrow and sickness and anger.
21_5_18: Here is what I have seen: It is good and fitting for one to eat and drink, and to enjoy the good of all his labor in which he toils under the sun all the days of his life which God gives him; for it is his heritage.
21_5_19: As for every man to whom God has given riches and wealth, and given him power to eat of it, to receive his heritage and rejoice in his labor—this is the gift of God.
21_5_20: For he will not dwell unduly on the days of his life, because God keeps him busy with the joy of his heart.
21_6_1: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is common among men:
21_6_2: A man to whom God has given riches and wealth and honor, so that he lacks nothing for himself of all he desires; yet God does not give him power to eat of it, but a foreigner consumes it. This is vanity, and it is an evil affliction.
21_6_3: If a man begets a hundred children and lives many years, so that the days of his years are many, but his soul is not satisfied with goodness, or indeed he has no burial, I say that a stillborn child is better than he—
21_6_4: for it comes in vanity and departs in darkness, and its name is covered with darkness.
21_6_5: Though it has not seen the sun or known anything, this has more rest than that man
21_6_6: even if he lives a thousand years twice—but has not seen goodness. Do not all go to one place?
21_6_7: All the labor of man is for his mouth, And yet the soul is not satisfied.
21_6_8: For what more has the wise man than the fool? What does the poor man have, Who knows how to walk before the living?
21_6_9: Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of desire. This also is vanity and grasping for the wind.
21_6_10: Whatever one is, he has been named already, For it is known that he is man; And he cannot contend with Him who is mightier than he.
21_6_11: Since there are many things that increase vanity, How is man the better?
21_6_12: For who knows what is good for man in life, all the days of his vain life which he passes like a shadow? Who can tell a man what will happen after him under the sun?
21_7_1: A good name is better than precious ointment, And the day of death than the day of one’s birth
21_7_2: Better to go to the house of mourning Than to go to the house of feasting, For that is the end of all men; And the living will take it to heart.
21_7_3: Sorrow is better than laughter, For by a sad countenance the heart is made better.
21_7_4: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, But the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
21_7_5: It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise Than for a man to hear the song of fools.
21_7_6: For like the crackling of thorns under a pot, So is the laughter of the fool. This also is vanity.
21_7_7: Surely oppression destroys a wise man’s reason, And a bribe debases the heart.
21_7_8: The end of a thing is better than its beginning; The patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
21_7_9: Do not hasten in your spirit to be angry, For anger rests in the bosom of fools.
21_7_10: Do not say, “Why were the former days better than these?” For you do not inquire wisely concerning this.
21_7_11: Wisdom is good with an inheritance, And profitable to those who see the sun.
21_7_12: For wisdom is a defense as money is a defense, But the excellence of knowledge is that wisdom gives life to those who have it.
21_7_13: Consider the work of God; For who can make straight what He has made crooked?
21_7_14: In the day of prosperity be joyful, But in the day of adversity consider: Surely God has appointed the one as well as the other, So that man can find out nothing that will come after him.
21_7_15: I have seen everything in my days of vanity: There is a just man who perishes in his righteousness, And there is a wicked man who prolongs life in his wickedness.
21_7_16: Do not be overly righteous, Nor be overly wise: Why should you destroy yourself?
21_7_17: Do not be overly wicked, Nor be foolish: Why should you die before your time?
21_7_18: It is good that you grasp this, And also not remove your hand from the other; For he who fears God will escape them all.
21_7_19: Wisdom strengthens the wise More than ten rulers of the city.
21_7_20: For there is not a just man on earth who does good And does not sin.
21_7_21: Also do not take to heart everything people say, Lest you hear your servant cursing you.
21_7_22: For many times, also, your own heart has known That even you have cursed others.
21_7_23: All this I have proved by wisdom. I said, “I will be wise”; But it was far from me.
21_7_24: As for that which is far off and exceedingly deep, Who can find it out?
21_7_25: I applied my heart to know, To search and seek out wisdom and the reason of things, To know the wickedness of folly, Even of foolishness and madness.
21_7_26: And I find more bitter than death The woman whose heart is snares and nets, Whose hands are fetters. He who pleases God shall escape from her, But the sinner shall be trapped by her.
21_7_27: Here is what I have found,” says the Preacher, “ Adding one thing to the other to find out the reason
21_7_28: Which my soul still seeks but I cannot find: One man among a thousand I have found, But a woman among all these I have not found.
21_7_29: Truly, this only I have found: That God made man upright, But they have sought out many schemes.”
21_8_1: Who is like a wise man? And who knows the interpretation of a thing? A man’s wisdom makes his face shine, And the sternness of his face is changed.
21_8_2: I say, “Keep the king’s commandment for the sake of your oath to God.
21_8_3: Do not be hasty to go from his presence. Do not take your stand for an evil thing, for he does whatever pleases him.”
21_8_4: Where the word of a king is, there is power; And who may say to him, “What are you doing?”
21_8_5: He who keeps his command will experience nothing harmful; And a wise man’s heart discerns both time and judgment
21_8_6: Because for every matter there is a time and judgment, Though the misery of man increases greatly.
21_8_7: For he does not know what will happen; So who can tell him when it will occur?
21_8_8: No one has power over the spirit to retain the spirit, And no one has power in the day of death. There is no release from that war, And wickedness will not deliver those who are given to it.
21_8_9: All this I have seen, and applied my heart to every work that is done under the sun: There is a time in which one man rules over another to his own hurt.
21_8_10: Then I saw the wicked buried, who had come and gone from the place of holiness, and they were forgotten in the city where they had so done. This also is vanity.
21_8_11: Because the sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.
21_8_12: Though a sinner does evil a hundred times, and his days are prolonged, yet I surely know that it will be well with those who fear God, who fear before Him.
21_8_13: But it will not be well with the wicked; nor will he prolong his days, which are as a shadow, because he does not fear before God.
21_8_14: There is a vanity which occurs on earth, that there are just men to whom it happens according to the work of the wicked; again, there are wicked men to whom it happens according to the work of the righteous. I said that this also is vanity.
21_8_15: So I commended enjoyment, because a man has nothing better under the sun than to eat, drink, and be merry; for this will remain with him in his labor all the days of his life which God gives him under the sun.
21_8_16: When I applied my heart to know wisdom and to see the business that is done on earth, even though one sees no sleep day or night
21_8_17: then I saw all the work of God, that a man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun. For though a man labors to discover it, yet he will not find it; moreover, though a wise man attempts to know it, he will not be able to find it.
21_9_1: For I considered all this in my heart, so that I could declare it all: that the righteous and the wise and their works are in the hand of God. People know neither love nor hatred by anything they see before them.
21_9_2: All things come alike to all: One event happens to the righteous and the wicked; To the good, the clean, and the unclean; To him who sacrifices and him who does not sacrifice. As is the good, so is the sinner; He who takes an oath as he who fears an oath.
21_9_3: This is an evil in all that is done under the sun: that one thing happens to all. Truly the hearts of the sons of men are full of evil; madness is in their hearts while they live, and after that they go to the dead.
21_9_4: But for him who is joined to all the living there is hope, for a living dog is better than a dead lion.
21_9_5: For the living know that they will die; But the dead know nothing, And they have no more reward, For the memory of them is forgotten.
21_9_6: Also their love, their hatred, and their envy have now perished; Nevermore will they have a share In anything done under the sun.
21_9_7: Go, eat your bread with joy, And drink your wine with a merry heart; For God has already accepted your works.
21_9_8: Let your garments always be white, And let your head lack no oil.
21_9_9: Live joyfully with the wife whom you love all the days of your vain life which He has given you under the sun, all your days of vanity; for that is your portion in life, and in the labor which you perform under the sun.
21_9_10: Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your might; for there is no work or device or knowledge or wisdom in the grave where you are going.
21_9_11: I returned and saw under the sun that— The race is not to the swift, Nor the battle to the strong, Nor bread to the wise, Nor riches to men of understanding, Nor favor to men of skill; But time and chance happen to them all.
21_9_12: For man also does not know his time: Like fish taken in a cruel net, Like birds caught in a snare, So the sons of men are snared in an evil time, When it falls suddenly upon them.
21_9_13: This wisdom I have also seen under the sun, and it seemed great to me:
21_9_14: There was a little city with few men in it; and a great king came against it, besieged it, and built great snares around it.
21_9_15: Now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom delivered the city. Yet no one remembered that same poor man.
21_9_16: Then I said: “Wisdom is better than strength. Nevertheless the poor man’s wisdom is despised, And his words are not heard.
21_9_17: Words of the wise, spoken quietly, should be heard Rather than the shout of a ruler of fools.
21_9_18: Wisdom is better than weapons of war; But one sinner destroys much good.”
21_10_1: Dead flies putrefy the perfumer’s ointment, And cause it to give off a foul odor; So does a little folly to one respected for wisdom and honor.
21_10_2: A wise man’s heart is at his right hand, But a fool’s heart at his left.
21_10_3: Even when a fool walks along the way, He lacks wisdom, And he shows everyone that he is a fool.
21_10_4: If the spirit of the ruler rises against you, Do not leave your post; For conciliation pacifies great offenses.
21_10_5: There is an evil I have seen under the sun, As an error proceeding from the ruler:
21_10_6: Folly is set in great dignity, While the rich sit in a lowly place.
21_10_7: I have seen servants on horses, While princes walk on the ground like servants.
21_10_8: He who digs a pit will fall into it, And whoever breaks through a wall will be bitten by a serpent.
21_10_9: He who quarries stones may be hurt by them, And he who splits wood may be endangered by it.
21_10_10: If the ax is dull, And one does not sharpen the edge, Then he must use more strength; But wisdom brings success.
21_10_11: A serpent may bite when it is not charmed; The babbler is no different.
21_10_12: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious, But the lips of a fool shall swallow him up
21_10_13: The words of his mouth begin with foolishness, And the end of his talk is raving madness.
21_10_14: A fool also multiplies words. No man knows what is to be; Who can tell him what will be after him?
21_10_15: The labor of fools wearies them, For they do not even know how to go to the city!
21_10_16: Woe to you, O land, when your king is a child, And your princes feast in the morning!
21_10_17: Blessed are you, O land, when your king is the son of nobles, And your princes feast at the proper time— For strength and not for drunkenness!
21_10_18: Because of laziness the building decays, And through idleness of hands the house leaks.
21_10_19: A feast is made for laughter, And wine makes merry; But money answers everything.
21_10_20: Do not curse the king, even in your thought; Do not curse the rich, even in your bedroom; For a bird of the air may carry your voice, And a bird in flight may tell the matter.
21_11_1: Cast your bread upon the waters, For you will find it after many days.
21_11_2: Give a serving to seven, and also to eight, For you do not know what evil will be on the earth.
21_11_3: If the clouds are full of rain, They empty themselves upon the earth; And if a tree falls to the south or the north, In the place where the tree falls, there it shall lie.
21_11_4: He who observes the wind will not sow, And he who regards the clouds will not reap.
21_11_5: As you do not know what is the way of the wind, Or how the bones grow in the womb of her who is with child, So you do not know the works of God who makes everything.
21_11_6: In the morning sow your seed, And in the evening do not withhold your hand; For you do not know which will prosper, Either this or that, Or whether both alike will be good.
21_11_7: Truly the light is sweet, And it is pleasant for the eyes to behold the sun
21_11_8: But if a man lives many years And rejoices in them all, Yet let him remember the days of darkness, For they will be many. All that is coming is vanity.
21_11_9: Rejoice, O young man, in your youth, And let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth; Walk in the ways of your heart, And in the sight of your eyes; But know that for all these God will bring you into judgment.
21_11_10: Therefore remove sorrow from your heart, And put away evil from your flesh, For childhood and youth are vanity.
21_12_1: Remember now your Creator in the days of your youth, Before the difficult days come, And the years draw near when you say, “I have no pleasure in them”:
21_12_2: While the sun and the light, The moon and the stars, Are not darkened, And the clouds do not return after the rain
21_12_3: In the day when the keepers of the house tremble, And the strong men bow down; When the grinders cease because they are few, And those that look through the windows grow dim
21_12_4: When the doors are shut in the streets, And the sound of grinding is low; When one rises up at the sound of a bird, And all the daughters of music are brought low.
21_12_5: Also they are afraid of height, And of terrors in the way; When the almond tree blossoms, The grasshopper is a burden, And desire fails. For man goes to his eternal home, And the mourners go about the streets.
21_12_6: Remember your Creator before the silver cord is loosed, Or the golden bowl is broken, Or the pitcher shattered at the fountain, Or the wheel broken at the well.
21_12_7: Then the dust will return to the earth as it was, And the spirit will return to God who gave it.
21_12_8: “Vanity of vanities,” says the Preacher, “All is vanity.”
21_12_9: And moreover, because the Preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; yes, he pondered and sought out and set in order many proverbs.
21_12_10: The Preacher sought to find acceptable words; and what was written was upright—words of truth.
21_12_11: The words of the wise are like goads, and the words of scholars are like well-driven nails, given by one Shepherd.
21_12_12: And further, my son, be admonished by these. Of making many books there is no end, and much study is wearisome to the flesh.
21_12_13: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God and keep His commandments, For this is man’s all.
21_12_14: For God will bring every work into judgment, Including every secret thing, Whether good or evil.
22_1_1: The song of songs, which is Solomon’s.
22_1_2: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth— For your love is better than wine.
22_1_3: Because of the fragrance of your good ointments, Your name is ointment poured forth; Therefore the virgins love you.
22_1_4: Draw me away! We will run after you. The king has brought me into his chambers. We will be glad and rejoice in you. We will remember your love more than wine. Rightly do they love you.
22_1_5: I am dark, but lovely, O daughters of Jerusalem, Like the tents of Kedar, Like the curtains of Solomon.
