22_1_6: Do not look upon me, because I am dark, Because the sun has tanned me. My mother’s sons were angry with me; They made me the keeper of the vineyards, But my own vineyard I have not kept.
22_1_7: Tell me, O you whom I love, Where you feed your flock, Where you make it rest at noon. For why should I be as one who veils herself By the flocks of your companions?
22_1_8: If you do not know, O fairest among women, Follow in the footsteps of the flock, And feed your little goats Beside the shepherds’ tents.
22_1_9: I have compared you, my love, To my filly among Pharaoh’s chariots.
22_1_10: Your cheeks are lovely with ornaments, Your neck with chains of gold.
22_1_11: We will make you ornaments of gold With studs of silver.
22_1_12: While the king is at his table, My spikenard sends forth its fragrance.
22_1_13: A bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me, That lies all night between my breasts.
22_1_14: My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blooms In the vineyards of En Gedi.
22_1_15: Behold, you are fair, my love! Behold, you are fair! You have dove’s eyes.
22_1_16: Behold, you are handsome, my beloved! Yes, pleasant! Also our bed is green.
22_1_17: The beams of our houses are cedar, And our rafters of fir.
22_2_1: I am the rose of Sharon, And the lily of the valleys.
22_2_2: Like a lily among thorns, So is my love among the daughters.
22_2_3: Like an apple tree among the trees of the woods, So is my beloved among the sons. I sat down in his shade with great delight, And his fruit was sweet to my taste.
22_2_4: He brought me to the banqueting house, And his banner over me was love.
22_2_5: Sustain me with cakes of raisins, Refresh me with apples, For I am lovesick.
22_2_6: His left hand is under my head, And his right hand embraces me.
22_2_7: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, By the gazelles or by the does of the field, Do not stir up nor awaken love Until it pleases.
22_2_8: The voice of my beloved! Behold, he comes Leaping upon the mountains, Skipping upon the hills.
22_2_9: My beloved is like a gazelle or a young stag. Behold, he stands behind our wall; He is looking through the windows, Gazing through the lattice.
22_2_10: My beloved spoke, and said to me: “Rise up, my love, my fair one, And come away.
22_2_11: For lo, the winter is past, The rain is over and gone.
22_2_12: The flowers appear on the earth; The time of singing has come, And the voice of the turtledove Is heard in our land.
22_2_13: The fig tree puts forth her green figs, And the vines with the tender grapes Give a good smell. Rise up, my love, my fair one, And come away!
22_2_14: “O my dove, in the clefts of the rock, In the secret places of the cliff, Let me see your face, Let me hear your voice; For your voice is sweet, And your face is lovely.”
22_2_15: Catch us the foxes, The little foxes that spoil the vines, For our vines have tender grapes.
22_2_16: My beloved is mine, and I am his. He feeds his flock among the lilies.
22_2_17: Until the day breaks And the shadows flee away, Turn, my beloved, And be like a gazelle Or a young stag Upon the mountains of Bether.
22_3_1: By night on my bed I sought the one I love; I sought him, but I did not find him.
22_3_2: “I will rise now,” I said, “And go about the city; In the streets and in the squares I will seek the one I love.” I sought him, but I did not find him.
22_3_3: The watchmen who go about the city found me; I said, “Have you seen the one I love?”
22_3_4: Scarcely had I passed by them, When I found the one I love. I held him and would not let him go, Until I had brought him to the house of my mother, And into the chamber of her who conceived me.
22_3_5: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, By the gazelles or by the does of the field, Do not stir up nor awaken love Until it pleases.
22_3_6: Who is this coming out of the wilderness Like pillars of smoke, Perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, With all the merchant’s fragrant powders?
22_3_7: Behold, it is Solomon’s couch, With sixty valiant men around it, Of the valiant of Israel.
22_3_8: They all hold swords, Being expert in war. Every man has his sword on his thigh Because of fear in the night.
22_3_9: Of the wood of Lebanon Solomon the King Made himself a palanquin:
22_3_10: He made its pillars of silver, Its support of gold, Its seat of purple, Its interior paved with love By the daughters of Jerusalem.
22_3_11: Go forth, O daughters of Zion, And see King Solomon with the crown With which his mother crowned him On the day of his wedding, The day of the gladness of his heart.
22_4_1: Behold, you are fair, my love! Behold, you are fair! You have dove’s eyes behind your veil. Your hair is like a flock of goats, Going down from Mount Gilead.
22_4_2: Your teeth are like a flock of shorn sheep Which have come up from the washing, Every one of which bears twins, And none is barren among them.
22_4_3: Your lips are like a strand of scarlet, And your mouth is lovely. Your temples behind your veil Are like a piece of pomegranate.
22_4_4: Your neck is like the tower of David, Built for an armory, On which hang a thousand bucklers, All shields of mighty men.
22_4_5: Your two breasts are like two fawns, Twins of a gazelle, Which feed among the lilies.
22_4_6: Until the day breaks And the shadows flee away, I will go my way to the mountain of myrrh And to the hill of frankincense.
22_4_7: You are all fair, my love, And there is no spot in you.
22_4_8: Come with me from Lebanon, my spouse, With me from Lebanon. Look from the top of Amana, From the top of Senir and Hermon, From the lions’ dens, From the mountains of the leopards.
22_4_9: You have ravished my heart, My sister, my spouse; You have ravished my heart With one look of your eyes, With one link of your necklace.
22_4_10: How fair is your love, My sister, my spouse! How much better than wine is your love, And the scent of your perfumes Than all spices!
22_4_11: Your lips, O my spouse, Drip as the honeycomb; Honey and milk are under your tongue; And the fragrance of your garments Is like the fragrance of Lebanon.
22_4_12: A garden enclosed Is my sister, my spouse, A spring shut up, A fountain sealed.
22_4_13: Your plants are an orchard of pomegranates With pleasant fruits, Fragrant henna with spikenard
22_4_14: Spikenard and saffron, Calamus and cinnamon, With all trees of frankincense, Myrrh and aloes, With all the chief spices—
22_4_15: A fountain of gardens, A well of living waters, And streams from Lebanon.
22_4_16: Awake, O north wind, And come, O south! Blow upon my garden, That its spices may flow out. Let my beloved come to his garden And eat its pleasant fruits.
22_5_1: I have come to my garden, my sister, my spouse; I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, O friends! Drink, yes, drink deeply, O beloved ones!
22_5_2: I sleep, but my heart is awake; It is the voice of my beloved! He knocks, saying, “Open for me, my sister, my love, My dove, my perfect one; For my head is covered with dew, My locks with the drops of the night.”
22_5_3: I have taken off my robe; How can I put it on again? I have washed my feet; How can I defile them?
22_5_4: My beloved put his hand By the latch of the door, And my heart yearned for him.
22_5_5: I arose to open for my beloved, And my hands dripped with myrrh, My fingers with liquid myrrh, On the handles of the lock.
22_5_6: I opened for my beloved, But my beloved had turned away and was gone. My heart leaped up when he spoke. I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.
22_5_7: The watchmen who went about the city found me. They struck me, they wounded me; The keepers of the walls Took my veil away from me.
22_5_8: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, If you find my beloved, That you tell him I am lovesick!
22_5_9: What is your beloved More than another beloved, O fairest among women? What is your beloved More than another beloved, That you so charge us?
22_5_10: My beloved is white and ruddy, Chief among ten thousand.
22_5_11: His head is like the finest gold; His locks are wavy, And black as a raven.
22_5_12: His eyes are like doves By the rivers of waters, Washed with milk, And fitly set.
22_5_13: His cheeks are like a bed of spices, Banks of scented herbs. His lips are lilies, Dripping liquid myrrh.
22_5_14: His hands are rods of gold Set with beryl. His body is carved ivory Inlaid with sapphires.
22_5_15: His legs are pillars of marble Set on bases of fine gold. His countenance is like Lebanon, Excellent as the cedars.
22_5_16: His mouth is most sweet, Yes, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, And this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem!
22_6_1: Where has your beloved gone, O fairest among women? Where has your beloved turned aside, That we may seek him with you?
22_6_2: My beloved has gone to his garden, To the beds of spices, To feed his flock in the gardens, And to gather lilies.
22_6_3: I am my beloved’s, And my beloved is mine. He feeds his flock among the lilies.
22_6_4: O my love, you are as beautiful as Tirzah, Lovely as Jerusalem, Awesome as an army with banners!
22_6_5: Turn your eyes away from me, For they have overcome me. Your hair is like a flock of goats Going down from Gilead.
22_6_6: Your teeth are like a flock of sheep Which have come up from the washing; Every one bears twins, And none is barren among them.
22_6_7: Like a piece of pomegranate Are your temples behind your veil.
22_6_8: There are sixty queens And eighty concubines, And virgins without number.
22_6_9: My dove, my perfect one, Is the only one, The only one of her mother, The favorite of the one who bore her. The daughters saw her And called her blessed, The queens and the concubines, And they praised her.
22_6_10: Who is she who looks forth as the morning, Fair as the moon, Clear as the sun, Awesome as an army with banners?
22_6_11: I went down to the garden of nuts To see the verdure of the valley, To see whether the vine had budded And the pomegranates had bloomed.
22_6_12: Before I was even aware, My soul had made me As the chariots of my noble people.
22_6_13: Return, return, O Shulamite; Return, return, that we may look upon you! What would you see in the Shulamite— As it were, the dance of the two camps?
22_7_1: How beautiful are your feet in sandals, O prince’s daughter! The curves of your thighs are like jewels, The work of the hands of a skillful workman.
22_7_2: Your navel is a rounded goblet; It lacks no blended beverage. Your waist is a heap of wheat Set about with lilies.
22_7_3: Your two breasts are like two fawns, Twins of a gazelle.
22_7_4: Your neck is like an ivory tower, Your eyes like the pools in Heshbon By the gate of Bath Rabbim. Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon Which looks toward Damascus.
22_7_5: Your head crowns you like Mount Carmel, And the hair of your head is like purple; A king is held captive by your tresses.
22_7_6: How fair and how pleasant you are, O love, with your delights!
22_7_7: This stature of yours is like a palm tree, And your breasts like its clusters.
22_7_8: I said, “I will go up to the palm tree, I will take hold of its branches.” Let now your breasts be like clusters of the vine, The fragrance of your breath like apples
22_7_9: And the roof of your mouth like the best wine. The wine goes down smoothly for my beloved, Moving gently the lips of sleepers.
22_7_10: I am my beloved’s, And his desire is toward me.
22_7_11: Come, my beloved, Let us go forth to the field; Let us lodge in the villages.
22_7_12: Let us get up early to the vineyards; Let us see if the vine has budded, Whether the grape blossoms are open, And the pomegranates are in bloom. There I will give you my love.
22_7_13: The mandrakes give off a fragrance, And at our gates are pleasant fruits, All manner, new and old, Which I have laid up for you, my beloved.
22_8_1: Oh, that you were like my brother, Who nursed at my mother’s breasts! If I should find you outside, I would kiss you; I would not be despised.
22_8_2: I would lead you and bring you Into the house of my mother, She who used to instruct me. I would cause you to drink of spiced wine, Of the juice of my pomegranate.
22_8_3: His left hand is under my head, And his right hand embraces me.
22_8_4: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, Do not stir up nor awaken love Until it pleases.
22_8_5: Who is this coming up from the wilderness, Leaning upon her beloved? I awakened you under the apple tree. There your mother brought you forth; There she who bore you brought you forth.
22_8_6: Set me as a seal upon your heart, As a seal upon your arm; For love is as strong as death, Jealousy as cruel as the grave; Its flames are flames of fire, A most vehement flame.
22_8_7: Many waters cannot quench love, Nor can the floods drown it. If a man would give for love All the wealth of his house, It would be utterly despised.
22_8_8: We have a little sister, And she has no breasts. What shall we do for our sister In the day when she is spoken for?
22_8_9: If she is a wall, We will build upon her A battlement of silver; And if she is a door, We will enclose her With boards of cedar.
22_8_10: I am a wall, And my breasts like towers; Then I became in his eyes As one who found peace.
22_8_11: Solomon had a vineyard at Baal Hamon; He leased the vineyard to keepers; Everyone was to bring for its fruit A thousand silver coins .
22_8_12: My own vineyard is before me. You, O Solomon, may have a thousand, And those who tend its fruit two hundred.
22_8_13: You who dwell in the gardens, The companions listen for your voice— Let me hear it!
22_8_14: Make haste, my beloved, And be like a gazelle Or a young stag On the mountains of spices.
27_3_31: So all that you have brought upon us, and all that you have done to us, you have done by a true judgment.
27_3_32: You have handed us over to our enemies, lawless and hateful rebels, and to an unjust king, the most wicked in all the world.
27_3_33: And now we cannot open our mouths; we, your servants who worship you, have become a shame and a reproach.
27_3_34: For your name’s sake do not give us up forever, and do not annul your covenant.
27_3_35: Do not withdraw your mercy from us, for the sake of Abraham your beloved and for the sake of your servant Isaac and Israel your holy one,
27_3_36: to whom you promised to multiply their descendants like the stars of heaven and like the sand on the shore of the sea.
27_3_37: For we, O Lord, have become fewer than any other nation, and are brought low this day in all the world because of our sins.
27_3_38: In our day we have no ruler, or prophet, or leader, no burnt offering, or sacrifice, or oblation, or incense, no place to make an offering before you and to find mercy.
27_3_39: Yet with a contrite heart and a humble spirit may we be accepted,
27_3_40: as though it were with burnt offerings of rams and bulls, or with tens of thousands of fat lambs; such may our sacrifice be in your sight today, and may we unreservedly follow you, for no shame will come to those who trust in you.
27_3_41: And now with all our heart we follow you; we fear you and seek your presence.
27_3_42: Do not put us to shame, but deal with us in your patience and in your abundant mercy.
27_3_43: Deliver us in accordance with your marvelous works, and bring glory to your name, O Lord.
27_3_44: Let all who do harm to your servants be put to shame; let them be disgraced and deprived of all power, and let their strength be broken.
27_3_45: Let them know that you alone are the Lord God, glorious over the whole world.”
27_3_46: Now the king’s servants who threw them in kept stoking the furnace with naphtha, pitch, tow, and brushwood.
27_3_47: And the flames poured out above the furnace forty-nine cubits,
27_3_48: and spread out and burned those Chaldeans who were caught near the furnace.
27_3_49: But the angel of the Lord came down into the furnace to be with Azariah and his companions, and drove the fiery flame out of the furnace,
27_3_50: and made the inside of the furnace as though a moist wind were whistling through it. The fire did not touch them at all and caused them no pain or distress.
27_3_51: Then the three with one voice praised and glorified and blessed God in the furnace:
27_3_52: “Blessed are you, O Lord, God of our ancestors, and to be praised and highly exalted forever; And blessed is your glorious, holy name, and to be highly praised and highly exalted forever.
27_3_53: Blessed are you in the temple of your holy glory, and to be extolled and highly glorified forever.
27_3_54: Blessed are you who look into the depths from your throne on the cherubim, and to be praised and highly exalted forever.
27_3_55: Blessed are you on the throne of your kingdom, and to be extolled and highly exalted forever.
27_3_56: Blessed are you in the firmament of heaven, and to be sung and glorified forever.
27_3_57: “Bless the Lord, all you works of the Lord; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_58: Bless the Lord, you heavens; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_59: Bless the Lord, you angels of the Lord; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_60: Bless the Lord, all you waters above the heavens; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_61: Bless the Lord, all you powers of the Lord; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_62: Bless the Lord, sun and moon; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_63: Bless the Lord, stars of heaven; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_64: “Bless the Lord, all rain and dew; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_65: Bless the Lord, all you winds; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_66: Bless the Lord, fire and heat; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_67: Bless the Lord, winter cold and summer heat; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_68: Bless the Lord, dews and falling snow; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_69: Bless the Lord, ice and cold; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_70: Bless the Lord, frosts and snows; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_71: Bless the Lord, nights and days; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_72: Bless the Lord, light and darkness; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_73: Bless the Lord, lightnings and clouds; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_74: “Let the earth bless the Lord; let it sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_75: Bless the Lord, mountains and hills; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_76: Bless the Lord, all that grows in the ground; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_77: Bless the Lord, you springs; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_78: Bless the Lord, seas and rivers; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_79: Bless the Lord, you whales and all that swim in the waters; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_80: Bless the Lord, all birds of the air; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_81: Bless the Lord, all wild animals and cattle; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_82: “Bless the Lord, all people on earth; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_83: Bless the Lord, O Israel; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_84: Bless the Lord, you priests of the Lord; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_85: Bless the Lord, you servants of the Lord; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_86: Bless the Lord, spirits and souls of the righteous; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_87: Bless the Lord, you who are holy and humble in heart; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
27_3_88: “Bless the Lord, Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever. For he has rescued us from Hades and saved us from the power of death, and delivered us from the midst of the burning fiery furnace; from the midst of the fire he has delivered us.
27_3_89: Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever.
27_3_90: All who worship the Lord, bless the God of gods, sing praise to him and give thanks to him, for his mercy endures forever.”
27_3_91: Hearing them sing, and amazed at seeing them alive, King Nebuchadnezzar rose up quickly. He said to his counselors, “Was it not three men that we threw bound into the fire?” They answered the king, “True, O king.”
27_3_92: He replied, “But I see four men unbound, walking in the middle of the fire, and they are not hurt; and the fourth has the appearance of a god.”
27_3_93: Nebuchadnezzar then approached the door of the furnace of blazing fire and said, “Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come out! Come here!” So Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego came out from the fire.
27_3_94: And the satraps, the prefects, the governors, and the king’s counselors gathered together and saw that the fire had not had any power over the bodies of those men; the hair of their heads was not singed, their tunics were not harmed, and not even the smell of fire came from them.
27_3_95: Nebuchadnezzar said, “Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who has sent his angel and delivered his servants who trusted in him. They disobeyed the king’s command and yielded up their bodies rather than serve and worship any god except their own God.
27_3_96: Therefore I make a decree: Any people, nation, or language that utters blasphemy against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego shall be torn limb from limb, and their houses laid in ruins; for there is no other god who is able to deliver in this way.”
27_3_97: Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego in the province of Babylon.
45_14_24: Now to Him who is able to establish you according to my gospel and the preaching of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery kept secret since the world began,
45_14_25: but now made manifest, and by the prophetic Scriptures made known to all nations, according to the commandment of the everlasting God, for obedience to the faith—
45_14_26: to God, alone wise, be glory through Jesus Christ forever. Amen.
62_2_1: My little children, I am writing these things to you so that you may not sin. But if anyone does sin, we have an Advocate with the Father — Jesus Christ, the Righteous One.
62_2_2: And He Himself is the propitiation for our sins — and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world.
62_2_3: And by this we know that we have come to know Him: if we keep His commandments.
62_2_4: The one who says, "I have come to know Him," and yet does not keep His commandments — that one is a liar, and the truth is not in him.
62_2_5: But whoever keeps His word, in him truly the love of God has been made perfect. By this we know that we are in Him:
62_2_6: the one who says he remains in Him ought himself to walk in the same way that He walked.
62_2_7: Beloved, I am not writing a new commandment to you, but an old commandment that you have had from the beginning. The old commandment is the word that you have heard.
62_2_8: Yet again, it is a new commandment that I am writing to you — which is true in Him and in you, because the darkness is passing away, and the true Light is already shining.
62_2_9: The one who says he is in the Light, and yet hates his brother, is in the darkness still.
62_2_10: The one who loves his brother remains in the Light — and in him there is no cause for stumbling.
62_2_11: But the one who hates his brother is in the darkness, and walks in the darkness, and does not know where he is going — because the darkness has blinded his eyes.
62_2_12: I am writing to you, little children, because your sins are forgiven for the sake of His name.
62_2_13: I am writing to you, fathers, because you have known Him who is from the beginning. I am writing to you, young men, because you have overcome the evil one.
62_2_14: I have written to you, little children, because you have known the Father. I have written to you, fathers, because you have known Him who is from the beginning. I have written to you, young men, because you are strong, and the word of God remains in you, and you have overcome the evil one.
62_2_15: Do not love the world, nor the things in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him.
62_2_16: For everything in the world — the desire of the flesh, the desire of the eyes, and the pride of life — is not from the Father, but is from the world.
62_2_17: And the world is passing away, along with its desire — but the one who does the will of God remains forever.
62_2_18: Little children, it is the last hour. And just as you have heard that Antichrist is coming, even now many antichrists have appeared. By this we know that it is the last hour.
62_2_19: They went out from us, but they were not of us. For if they had been of us, they would have remained with us. But this happened so that it would be made plain that none of them are of us.
62_2_20: But you have an anointing from the Holy One, and all of you know.
62_2_21: I have not written to you because you do not know the truth, but because you do know it — and because no lie comes from the truth.
62_2_22: Who is the liar but the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the Antichrist — the one who denies the Father and the Son.
62_2_23: Everyone who denies the Son does not have the Father either. The one who confesses the Son has the Father also.
62_2_24: As for you, let what you have heard from the beginning remain in you. If what you have heard from the beginning remains in you, you also will remain in the Son and in the Father.
62_2_25: And this is the promise He Himself made to us: eternal life.
62_2_26: I have written these things to you concerning those who are trying to deceive you.
62_2_27: As for you, the anointing you have received from Him remains in you, and you do not need anyone to teach you. But just as His anointing teaches you about all things — and is true and is no lie — and just as it has taught you, so remain in Him.
62_2_28: And now, little children, remain in Him, so that when He appears, we may have boldness, and not shrink away from Him in shame at His coming.
62_2_29: If you know that He is righteous, you also know that everyone who practices righteousness has been born of Him.
62_3_1: See what kind of love the Father has given to us — that we should be called children of God! And we are! The reason the world does not know us is that it did not know Him.
62_3_2: Beloved, now we are children of God; and what we shall be has not yet appeared. We do know this: when He appears, we shall be like Him — for we shall see Him as He is.
62_3_3: And everyone who has this hope set on Him purifies himself, just as He is pure.
62_3_4: Everyone who practices sin practices lawlessness — for sin is lawlessness.
62_3_5: And you know that He appeared in order to take away sins, and in Him there is no sin.
62_3_6: Everyone who remains in Him does not keep on sinning. The one who keeps on sinning has not seen Him, nor has known Him.
62_3_7: Little children, let no one deceive you. The one who practices righteousness is righteous, just as He is righteous.
62_3_8: The one who practices sin is of the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the beginning. The reason the Son of God appeared was to destroy the works of the devil.
62_3_9: No one born of God keeps on sinning, because His seed remains in him; and he is not able to keep on sinning, because he has been born of God.
62_3_10: By this it is clear who are the children of God, and who are the children of the devil: anyone who does not practice righteousness is not of God — nor anyone who does not love his brother.
62_3_11: For this is the message you have heard from the beginning: that we should love one another.
62_3_12: Not as Cain, who was of the evil one and murdered his brother. And why did he murder him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother's were righteous.
62_3_13: Do not be amazed, brothers, if the world hates you.
62_3_14: We know that we have crossed over from death into life, because we love the brothers. The one who does not love remains in death.
62_3_15: Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer — and you know that no murderer has eternal life remaining in him.
62_3_16: By this we have come to know love: He laid down His life for us. And we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers.
62_3_17: But whoever has the world's goods, and sees his brother in need, and closes his heart against him — how does the love of God remain in him?
62_3_18: Little children, let us not love in word, nor with the tongue, but in deed and in truth.
62_3_19: By this we will know that we are of the truth, and we will reassure our heart before Him —
62_3_20: whenever our heart condemns us. For God is greater than our heart, and He knows everything.
62_3_21: Beloved, if our heart does not condemn us, we have confidence before God.
62_3_22: And whatever we ask, we receive from Him — because we keep His commandments and do what is pleasing in His sight.
62_3_23: And this is His commandment: that we believe in the name of His Son Jesus Christ, and love one another, just as He gave us the commandment.
62_3_24: The one who keeps His commandments remains in Him, and He in him. And by this we know that He remains in us — by the Spirit He has given us.
62_4_1: Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God — for many false prophets have gone out into the world.
62_4_2: By this you know the Spirit of God: every spirit that confesses Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God.
62_4_3: And every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God. This is the spirit of the Antichrist, of which you have heard that it is coming — and now it is already in the world.
62_4_4: You are from God, little children, and you have overcome them — because greater is the One who is in you than the one who is in the world.
62_4_5: They are from the world. Therefore they speak from the world, and the world listens to them.
62_4_6: We are from God. The one who knows God listens to us. The one who is not from God does not listen to us. By this we know the Spirit of truth — and the spirit of error.
62_4_7: Beloved, let us love one another — for love is from God. And everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God.
62_4_8: The one who does not love does not know God — for God is love.
62_4_9: By this the love of God was revealed among us: that God sent His one-and-only Son into the world, so that we might live through Him.
62_4_10: In this is love — not that we have loved God, but that He loved us, and sent His Son to be the propitiation for our sins.
62_4_11: Beloved, if God so loved us, we also ought to love one another.
62_4_12: No one has ever seen God. If we love one another, God remains in us, and His love has been made perfect in us.
62_4_13: By this we know that we remain in Him, and He in us: because He has given us of His Spirit.
62_4_14: And we have seen, and we testify, that the Father has sent the Son to be the Savior of the world.
62_4_15: Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God — God remains in him, and he in God.
62_4_16: And we have come to know and to believe the love that God has for us. God is love. And the one who remains in love remains in God, and God in him.
62_4_17: By this love has been perfected with us — so that we may have boldness on the day of judgment, because as He is, so also are we in this world.
62_4_18: There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear — for fear involves punishment, and the one who fears has not been perfected in love.
62_4_19: We love because He first loved us.
62_4_20: If anyone says, "I love God," and yet hates his brother, he is a liar. For the one who does not love his brother, whom he has seen, cannot love God, whom he has not seen.
62_4_21: And this is the commandment that we have from Him: the one who loves God must also love his brother.
62_5_1: Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God. And everyone who loves the Father loves the One born of Him.
62_5_2: By this we know that we love the children of God: when we love God and keep His commandments.
62_5_3: For this is the love of God: that we keep His commandments. And His commandments are not burdensome,
62_5_4: because everyone who has been born of God overcomes the world. And this is the victory that has overcome the world: our faith.
62_5_5: And who is the one who overcomes the world, except the one who believes that Jesus is the Son of God?
62_5_6: This is the One who came by water and blood — Jesus Christ. He came not by water alone, but by the water and the blood. And the Spirit is the One who testifies — because the Spirit is the truth.
62_5_7: For there are three who testify:
62_5_8: the Spirit, and the water, and the blood — and these three agree as one.
62_5_9: If we receive the testimony of men, the testimony of God is greater. For this is the testimony of God: that He has testified concerning His Son.
62_5_10: The one who believes in the Son of God has the testimony in himself. The one who does not believe God has made Him a liar — because he has not believed in the testimony that God has borne concerning His Son.
62_5_11: And this is the testimony: that God has given us eternal life — and this life is in His Son.
62_5_12: The one who has the Son has the life. The one who does not have the Son of God does not have the life.
62_5_13: These things I have written to you who believe in the name of the Son of God — so that you may know that you have eternal life.
62_5_14: And this is the confidence that we have toward Him: that if we ask anything according to His will, He hears us.
62_5_15: And if we know that He hears us — whatever we ask — we know that we have the requests we have asked of Him.
62_5_16: If anyone sees his brother committing a sin not leading to death, he shall ask, and God will give him life — for those committing sin not leading to death. There is a sin that leads to death; I do not say that he should pray about that.
62_5_17: All unrighteousness is sin — and there is sin not leading to death.
62_5_18: We know that everyone who has been born of God does not keep on sinning. But the One who was born of God keeps him, and the evil one does not touch him.
62_5_19: We know that we are of God, and that the whole world lies under the sway of the evil one.
62_5_20: And we know that the Son of God has come and has given us understanding, so that we may know Him who is true. And we are in Him who is true — in His Son Jesus Christ. He is the true God and eternal life.
62_5_21: Little children, keep yourselves from idols.
56_2_1: But as for you, speak the things that are fitting for sound doctrine.
56_2_2: Older men are to be sober-minded, dignified, self-controlled — sound in faith, in love, and in steadfastness.
56_2_3: Older women likewise — that they be reverent in behavior, not slanderers, not enslaved to much wine, teachers of what is good —
56_2_4: so that they may train the younger women to love their husbands, to love their children,
56_2_5: to be self-controlled, pure, working at home, kind, submissive to their own husbands — so that the word of God will not be discredited.
56_2_6: Likewise, urge the younger men to be self-controlled.
56_2_7: In all things show yourself to be an example of good works — in your teaching showing integrity, dignity,
56_2_8: and sound speech that cannot be condemned — so that the opponent may be put to shame, having nothing evil to say about us.
56_2_9: Bondservants are to be subject to their own masters in everything, and to be well-pleasing — not arguing back,
56_2_10: not pilfering, but showing all good faith — so that in everything they may adorn the doctrine of God our Savior.
56_2_11: For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all people,
56_2_12: training us to renounce ungodliness and worldly desires, and to live sensibly, righteously, and godly in this present age,
56_2_13: looking for the blessed hope and glorious appearing of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ —
56_2_14: who gave Himself for us, to redeem us from all lawlessness and to purify for Himself a people for His own possession, zealous for good works.
56_2_15: These things speak — and exhort and rebuke with all authority. Let no one disregard you.
56_3_1: Remind them to be subject to rulers and authorities, to be obedient, to be ready for every good work,
56_3_2: to malign no one, to be peaceable and gentle, showing all humility to all people.
56_3_3: For we ourselves were once foolish, disobedient, deceived — slaves to various lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another.
56_3_4: But when the kindness and the love of God our Savior toward man appeared,
56_3_5: He saved us — not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to His mercy — through the washing of regeneration and the renewing of the Holy Spirit,
56_3_6: which He poured out on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior,
56_3_7: so that, having been justified by His grace, we should become heirs according to the hope of eternal life.
56_3_8: This saying is faithful — and concerning these things I want you to insist confidently, so that those who have believed in God may be careful to engage in good works. These things are good and profitable for people.
56_3_9: But avoid foolish controversies, genealogies, strife, and quarrels about the law — for they are useless and worthless.
56_3_10: Reject a divisive man after the first and second admonition,
56_3_11: knowing that such a one is warped and sinful — being self-condemned.
56_3_12: When I send Artemas to you, or Tychicus, make every effort to come to me at Nicopolis — for I have decided to spend the winter there.
56_3_13: Diligently send Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their way, so that nothing is lacking for them.
56_3_14: And let our people learn to engage in good works for cases of urgent need — so that they will not be unfruitful.
56_3_15: All who are with me greet you. Greet those who love us in the faith. Grace be with you all. Amen.
61_2_1: But there were also false prophets among the people, just as there will be false teachers among you — who will secretly bring in destructive heresies, even denying the Master who bought them — bringing on themselves swift destruction.
61_2_2: And many will follow their licentiousness, and because of them the way of truth will be blasphemed.
61_2_3: And in their greed they will exploit you with deceptive words. Their condemnation, from long ago, is not idle — and their destruction is not asleep.
61_2_4: For if God did not spare angels when they sinned, but cast them down to hell and committed them to chains of gloomy darkness, kept until the judgment;
61_2_5: and if He did not spare the ancient world, but preserved Noah, a herald of righteousness, with seven others, when He brought a flood upon the world of the ungodly;
61_2_6: and if He condemned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah by reducing them to ashes, making them an example of what is going to happen to the ungodly;
61_2_7: and if He rescued righteous Lot, who was distressed by the licentious behavior of lawless men —
61_2_8: for as that righteous man lived among them day after day, his righteous soul was tormented by what he saw and heard of their lawless deeds —
61_2_9: then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trial, and how to keep the unrighteous under punishment for the day of judgment;
61_2_10: and especially those who walk according to the flesh in defiling lust, and who despise authority. Bold and arrogant, they are not afraid to revile glorious beings —
61_2_11: whereas angels, though greater in might and power, do not bring a reviling judgment against them before the Lord.
61_2_12: But these, like irrational animals, born of nature to be caught and destroyed — speaking abusively about things they do not understand — will also be destroyed in their corruption,
61_2_13: suffering wrong as the wages for doing wrong. They count it pleasure to revel in broad daylight. They are spots and blemishes, reveling in their own deceptions while they feast with you.
61_2_14: Their eyes are full of adultery and never cease from sin. They entice unsteady souls. They have hearts trained in greed — accursed children!
61_2_15: Forsaking the right way, they have gone astray. They have followed the way of Balaam, son of Beor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness —
61_2_16: but he was rebuked for his own transgression: a speechless donkey spoke with a man's voice and restrained the prophet's madness.
61_2_17: These are springs without water, and mists driven by a storm. The gloom of darkness has been reserved for them.
61_2_18: For when they speak arrogant, empty words, they entice — by lusts of the flesh, by sensuality — those who are barely escaping from the ones who live in error.
61_2_19: They promise them freedom, while they themselves are slaves of corruption — for whatever overcomes a man, by that he is enslaved.
61_2_20: For if, after escaping the defilements of the world through the full knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, they are again entangled in them and overcome — the last state has become worse for them than the first.
61_2_21: It would have been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness than, having known it, to turn back from the holy commandment delivered to them.
61_2_22: For them the true proverb has come true: "A dog returns to its own vomit," and, "A washed sow returns to wallowing in the mire."
61_3_1: This is now, beloved, the second letter I am writing to you — in both of which I am stirring up your sincere mind by way of reminder,
61_3_2: that you should remember the words spoken beforehand by the holy prophets, and the commandment of the Lord and Savior given through your apostles —
61_3_3: knowing this first: that scoffers will come in the last days, walking according to their own lusts,
61_3_4: and saying, "Where is the promise of His coming? For ever since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of creation."
61_3_5: For they deliberately overlook this fact: that long ago by the word of God the heavens existed, and the earth was formed out of water and through water,
61_3_6: by which the world that then existed was destroyed by being flooded with water.
61_3_7: But by the same word, the present heavens and earth are stored up for fire — being kept until the day of judgment and the destruction of ungodly people.
61_3_8: But do not overlook this one fact, beloved: with the Lord, one day is as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.
61_3_9: The Lord is not slow concerning His promise, as some count slowness — but He is patient toward you, not wishing that any should perish, but that all should reach repentance.
61_3_10: But the day of the Lord will come like a thief — in which the heavens will pass away with a roar, and the elements will be dissolved with intense heat, and the earth and the works that are on it will be exposed.
61_3_11: Since all these things are to be dissolved in this way, what kind of people ought you to be — in holy conduct and godliness,
61_3_12: looking for and hastening the coming of the day of God, on account of which the heavens will be set on fire and dissolved, and the elements will melt with intense heat?
61_3_13: But according to His promise, we are looking for new heavens and a new earth — in which righteousness dwells.
61_3_14: Therefore, beloved — since you are looking for these things — be diligent to be found by Him in peace, spotless and blameless.
61_3_15: And consider the patience of our Lord as salvation — just as our beloved brother Paul also wrote to you, according to the wisdom given to him,
61_3_16: speaking of these things in all his letters — in which there are some things hard to understand, which the ignorant and unstable distort, as they do also the rest of the Scriptures, to their own destruction.
61_3_17: You therefore, beloved — knowing this beforehand — be on guard, so that you are not carried away by the error of the lawless and lose your own steadfastness.
61_3_18: But grow in the grace and full knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To Him be the glory both now and to the day of eternity. Amen.
18_35_2: “Do you think this is right? Do you say, ‘My righteousness is more than God’s’?
18_35_3: For you say, ‘What advantage will it be to You? What profit shall I have, more than if I had sinned?’
18_35_4: “I will answer you, And your companions with you.
18_35_5: Look to the heavens and see; And behold the clouds — They are higher than you.
18_35_6: If you sin, what do you accomplish against Him? Or, if your transgressions are multiplied, what do you do to Him?
18_35_7: If you are righteous, what do you give Him? Or what does He receive from your hand?
18_35_8: Your wickedness affects a man such as you, And your righteousness a son of man.
18_35_9: “Because of the multitude of oppressions they cry out; They cry out for help because of the arm of the mighty.
18_35_10: But no one says, ‘Where is God my Maker, Who gives songs in the night,
18_35_11: Who teaches us more than the beasts of the earth, And makes us wiser than the birds of heaven?’
18_35_12: There they cry out, but He does not answer, Because of the pride of evil men.
18_35_13: Surely God will not listen to empty talk, Nor will the Almighty regard it.
18_35_14: Although you say you do not see Him, Yet justice is before Him, and you must wait for Him.
18_35_15: And now, because He has not punished in His anger, Nor taken much notice of folly,
18_35_16: Therefore Job opens his mouth in vain; He multiplies words without knowledge.”
18_36_2: “Bear with me a little, and I will show you That there are yet words to speak on God’s behalf.
18_36_3: I will fetch my knowledge from afar; I will ascribe righteousness to my Maker.
18_36_4: For truly my words are not false; One who is perfect in knowledge is with you.
18_36_5: “Behold, God is mighty, but despises no one; He is mighty in strength of understanding.
18_36_6: He does not preserve the life of the wicked, But gives justice to the oppressed.
18_36_7: He does not withdraw His eyes from the righteous; But they are on the throne with kings, For He has seated them forever, And they are exalted.
18_36_8: And if they are bound in fetters, Held in the cords of affliction,
18_36_9: Then He tells them their work and their transgressions — That they have acted defiantly.
18_36_10: He also opens their ear to instruction, And commands that they turn from iniquity.
18_36_11: If they obey and serve Him, They shall spend their days in prosperity, And their years in pleasures.
18_36_12: But if they do not obey, They shall perish by the sword, And they shall die without knowledge.
18_36_13: “But the hypocrites in heart store up wrath; They do not cry for help when He binds them.
18_36_14: They die in youth, And their life ends among the perverted persons.
18_36_15: He delivers the poor in their affliction, And opens their ears in oppression.
18_36_16: “Indeed He would have brought you out of dire distress, Into a broad place where there is no restraint; And what is set on your table would be full of richness.
18_36_17: But you are filled with the judgment due the wicked; Judgment and justice take hold of you.
18_36_18: Because there is wrath, beware lest He take you away with one blow; For a large ransom would not help you avoid it.
18_36_19: Will your riches, Or all the mighty forces, Keep you from distress?
18_36_20: Do not desire the night, When people are cut off in their place.
18_36_21: Take heed, do not turn to iniquity, For you have chosen this rather than affliction.
18_36_22: “Behold, God is exalted by His power; Who teaches like Him?
18_36_23: Who has assigned Him His way, Or who has said, ‘You have done wrong’?
18_36_24: “Remember to magnify His work, Of which men have sung.
18_36_25: Everyone has seen it; Man looks on it from afar.
18_36_26: “Behold, God is great, and we do not know Him; Nor can the number of His years be discovered.
18_36_27: For He draws up drops of water, Which distill as rain from the mist,
18_36_28: Which the clouds drop down And pour abundantly on man.
18_36_29: Indeed, can anyone understand the spreading of clouds, The thunder from His canopy?
18_36_30: Look, He scatters His light upon it, And covers the depths of the sea.
18_36_31: For by these He judges the peoples; He gives food in abundance.
18_36_32: He covers His hands with lightning, And commands it to strike.
18_36_33: His thunder declares it, The cattle also, concerning the rising storm.
18_37_1: “At this also my heart trembles, And leaps from its place.
18_37_2: Hear attentively the thunder of His voice, And the rumbling that comes from His mouth.
18_37_3: He sends it forth under the whole heaven, His lightning to the ends of the earth.
18_37_4: After it a voice roars; He thunders with His majestic voice, And He does not restrain them when His voice is heard.
18_37_5: God thunders marvelously with His voice; He does great things which we cannot comprehend.
18_37_6: For He says to the snow, ‘Fall on the earth’; Likewise to the gentle rain and the heavy rain of His strength.
18_37_7: He seals the hand of every man, That all men may know His work.
18_37_8: The beasts go into dens, And remain in their lairs.
18_37_9: From the chamber of the south comes the whirlwind, And cold from the scattering winds of the north.
18_37_10: By the breath of God ice is given, And the broad waters are frozen.
18_37_11: Also with moisture He saturates the thick clouds; He scatters His bright clouds.
18_37_12: And they swirl about, being turned by His guidance, That they may do whatever He commands them On the face of the whole earth.
18_37_13: He causes it to come, Whether for correction, Or for His land, Or for mercy.
18_37_14: “Listen to this, O Job; Stand still and consider the wondrous works of God.
18_37_15: Do you know when God dispatches them, And causes the light of His cloud to shine?
18_37_16: Do you know how the clouds are balanced, Those wondrous works of Him who is perfect in knowledge?
18_37_17: Why are your garments hot, When He quiets the earth by the south wind?
18_37_18: With Him, have you spread out the skies, Strong as a cast metal mirror?
18_37_19: “Teach us what we should say to Him, For we can prepare nothing because of the darkness.
18_37_20: Should He be told that I wish to speak? If a man were to speak, surely he would be swallowed up.
18_37_21: Even now men cannot look at the light when it is bright in the skies, When the wind has passed and cleared them.
18_37_22: He comes from the north as golden splendor; With God is awesome majesty.
18_37_23: As for the Almighty, we cannot find Him; He is excellent in power, In judgment and abundant justice; He does not oppress.
18_37_24: Therefore men fear Him; He shows no partiality to any who are wise of heart.”
18_38_1: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said:
18_38_2: “Who is this who darkens counsel By words without knowledge?
18_38_3: Now prepare yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall answer Me.
18_38_4: “Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Tell Me, if you have understanding.
18_38_5: Who determined its measurements? Surely you know! Or who stretched the line upon it?
18_38_6: To what were its foundations fastened? Or who laid its cornerstone,
18_38_7: When the morning stars sang together, And all the sons of God shouted for joy?
18_38_8: “Or who shut in the sea with doors, When it burst forth and issued from the womb;
18_38_9: When I made the clouds its garment, And thick darkness its swaddling band;
18_38_10: When I fixed My limit for it, And set bars and doors;
18_38_11: When I said, ‘This far you may come, but no farther, And here your proud waves must stop’?
18_38_12: “Have you commanded the morning since your days began, And caused the dawn to know its place,
18_38_13: That it might take hold of the ends of the earth, And the wicked be shaken out of it?
18_38_14: It takes on form like clay under a seal, And stands out like a garment.
18_38_15: From the wicked their light is withheld, And the upraised arm is broken.
18_38_16: “Have you entered the springs of the sea? Or have you walked in search of the depths?
18_38_17: Have the gates of death been revealed to you? Or have you seen the doors of the shadow of death?
18_38_18: Have you comprehended the breadth of the earth? Tell Me, if you know all this.
18_38_19: “Where is the way to the dwelling of light? And darkness, where is its place,
18_38_20: That you may take it to its territory, That you may know the paths to its home?
18_38_21: Do you know it, because you were born then, Or because the number of your days is great?
18_38_22: “Have you entered the treasury of snow, Or have you seen the treasury of hail,
18_38_23: Which I have reserved for the time of trouble, For the day of battle and war?
18_38_24: By what way is light diffused, Or the east wind scattered over the earth?
18_38_25: “Who has divided a channel for the overflowing water, Or a path for the thunderbolt,
18_38_26: To cause it to rain on a land where there is no one, A wilderness in which there is no man;
18_38_27: To satisfy the desolate waste, And cause to spring forth the growth of tender grass?
18_38_28: Has the rain a father? Or who has begotten the drops of dew?
18_38_29: From whose womb comes the ice? And the frost of heaven, who gives it birth?
18_38_30: The waters harden like stone, And the surface of the deep is frozen.
18_38_31: “Can you bind the cluster of the Pleiades, Or loose the belt of Orion?
18_38_32: Can you bring out Mazzaroth in its season? Or can you guide the Great Bear with its cubs?
18_38_33: Do you know the ordinances of the heavens? Can you set their dominion over the earth?
18_38_34: “Can you lift up your voice to the clouds, That an abundance of water may cover you?
18_38_35: Can you send out lightnings, that they may go, And say to you, ‘Here we are!’?
18_38_36: Who has put wisdom in the mind? Or who has given understanding to the heart?
18_38_37: Who can number the clouds by wisdom? Or who can pour out the bottles of heaven,
18_38_38: When the dust hardens in clumps, And the clods cling together?
18_38_39: “Can you hunt the prey for the lion, Or satisfy the appetite of the young lions,
18_38_40: When they crouch in their dens, Or lurk in their lairs to lie in wait?
18_38_41: Who provides food for the raven, When its young ones cry to God, And wander about for lack of food?
18_39_1: “Do you know the time when the wild mountain goats bear young? Or can you mark when the deer gives birth?
18_39_2: Can you number the months that they fulfill? Or do you know the time when they bear young?
18_39_3: They bow down, They bring forth their young, They deliver their offspring.
18_39_4: Their young ones are healthy, They grow strong with grain; They depart and do not return to them.
18_39_5: “Who set the wild donkey free? Who loosed the bonds of the onager,
18_39_6: Whose home I have made the wilderness, And the barren land his dwelling?
18_39_7: He scorns the tumult of the city; He does not heed the shouts of the driver.
18_39_8: The range of the mountains is his pasture, And he searches after every green thing.
18_39_9: “Will the wild ox be willing to serve you? Will he bed by your manger?
18_39_10: Can you bind the wild ox in the furrow with ropes? Or will he plow the valleys behind you?
18_39_11: Will you trust him because his strength is great? Or will you leave your labor to him?
18_39_12: Will you trust him to bring home your grain, And gather it to your threshing floor?
18_39_13: “The wings of the ostrich wave proudly, But are her wings and pinions like the kindly stork’s?
18_39_14: For she leaves her eggs on the ground, And warms them in the dust;
18_39_15: She forgets that a foot may crush them, Or that a wild beast may break them.
18_39_16: She treats her young harshly, as though they were not hers; Her labor is in vain, without concern,
18_39_17: Because God deprived her of wisdom, And did not endow her with understanding.
18_39_18: When she lifts herself on high, She scorns the horse and its rider.
18_39_19: “Have you given the horse strength? Have you clothed his neck with thunder?
18_39_20: Can you frighten him like a locust? His majestic snorting strikes terror.
18_39_21: He paws in the valley, and rejoices in his strength; He gallops into the clash of arms.
18_39_22: He mocks at fear, and is not frightened; Nor does he turn back from the sword.
18_39_23: The quiver rattles against him, The glittering spear and javelin.
18_39_24: He devours the distance with fierceness and rage; Nor does he come to a halt because the trumpet has sounded.
18_39_25: At the blast of the trumpet he says, ‘Aha!’ He smells the battle from afar, The thunder of captains and shouting.
18_39_26: “Does the hawk fly by your wisdom, And spread its wings toward the south?
18_39_27: Does the eagle mount up at your command, And make its nest on high?
18_39_28: On the rock it dwells and resides, On the crag of the rock and the stronghold.
18_39_29: From there it spies out the prey; Its eyes observe from afar.
18_39_30: Its young ones suck up blood; And where the slain are, there it is.”
18_40_1: Moreover the LORD answered Job, and said:
18_40_2: “Shall the one who contends with the Almighty correct Him? He who rebukes God, let him answer it.”
18_40_3: Then Job answered the LORD and said:
18_40_4: “Behold, I am vile; What shall I answer You? I lay my hand over my mouth.
18_40_5: Once I have spoken, but I will not answer; Yes, twice, but I will proceed no further.”
18_40_6: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said:
18_40_7: “Now prepare yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall answer Me:
18_40_8: “Would you indeed annul My judgment? Would you condemn Me that you may be justified?
18_40_9: Have you an arm like God? Or can you thunder with a voice like His?
18_40_10: Then adorn yourself with majesty and splendor, And array yourself with glory and beauty.
18_40_11: Disperse the rage of your wrath; Look on everyone who is proud, and humble him.
18_40_12: Look on everyone who is proud, and bring him low; Tread down the wicked in their place.
18_40_13: Hide them in the dust together, Bind their faces in hidden darkness.
18_40_14: Then I will also confess to you That your own right hand can save you.
18_40_15: “Look now at the behemoth, which I made along with you; He eats grass like an ox.
18_40_16: See now, his strength is in his hips, And his power is in his stomach muscles.
18_40_17: He moves his tail like a cedar; The sinews of his thighs are tightly knit.
18_40_18: His bones are like beams of bronze, His ribs like bars of iron.
18_40_19: He is the first of the ways of God; Only He who made him can bring near His sword.
18_40_20: Surely the mountains yield food for him, And all the beasts of the field play there.
18_40_21: He lies under the lotus trees, In a covert of reeds and marsh.
18_40_22: The lotus trees cover him with their shade; The willows by the brook surround him.
18_40_23: Indeed the river may rage, Yet he is not disturbed; He is confident, though the Jordan gushes into his mouth,
18_40_24: Though he takes it in his eyes, Or one pierces his nose with a snare.
18_41_1: “Can you draw out Leviathan with a hook, Or snare his tongue with a line which you lower?
18_41_2: Can you put a reed through his nose, Or pierce his jaw with a hook?
18_41_3: Will he make many supplications to you? Will he speak softly to you?
18_41_4: Will he make a covenant with you? Will you take him as a servant forever?
18_41_5: Will you play with him as with a bird, Or will you leash him for your maidens?
18_41_6: Will your companions make a banquet of him? Will they apportion him among the merchants?
18_41_7: Can you fill his skin with harpoons, Or his head with fishing spears?
18_41_8: Lay your hand on him; Remember the battle — Never do it again!
18_41_9: Indeed, any hope of overcoming him is false; Shall one not be overwhelmed at the sight of him?
18_41_10: No one is so fierce that he would dare stir him up. Who then is able to stand against Me?
18_41_11: Who has preceded Me, that I should pay him? Everything under heaven is Mine.
18_41_12: “I will not conceal his limbs, His mighty power, or his graceful proportions.
18_41_13: Who can remove his outer coat? Who can approach him with a double bridle?
18_41_14: Who can open the doors of his face, With his terrible teeth all around?
18_41_15: His rows of scales are his pride, Shut up tightly as with a seal;
18_41_16: One is so near another That no air can come between them;
18_41_17: They are joined one to another, They stick together and cannot be parted.
18_41_18: His sneezings flash forth light, And his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.
18_41_19: Out of his mouth go burning lights; Sparks of fire shoot out.
18_41_20: Smoke goes out of his nostrils, As from a boiling pot and burning rushes.
18_41_21: His breath kindles coals, And a flame goes out of his mouth.
18_41_22: Strength dwells in his neck, And sorrow dances before him.
18_41_23: The folds of his flesh are joined together; They are firm on him and cannot be moved.
18_41_24: His heart is as hard as stone, Even as hard as the lower millstone.
18_41_25: When he raises himself up, the mighty are afraid; Because of his crashings they are beside themselves.
18_41_26: Though the sword reaches him, it cannot avail; Nor does spear, dart, or javelin.
18_41_27: He regards iron as straw, And bronze as rotten wood.
18_41_28: The arrow cannot make him flee; Slingstones become like stubble to him.
18_41_29: Darts are regarded as straw; He laughs at the threat of javelins.
18_41_30: His undersides are like sharp potsherds; He spreads pointed marks in the mire.
18_41_31: He makes the deep boil like a pot; He makes the sea like a pot of ointment.
18_41_32: He leaves a shining wake behind him; One would think the deep had white hair.
18_41_33: On earth there is nothing like him, Which is made without fear.
18_41_34: He beholds every high thing; He is king over all the children of pride.”
18_42_1: Then Job answered the LORD and said:
18_42_2: “I know that You can do everything, And that no purpose of Yours can be withheld from You.
18_42_3: You asked, ‘Who is this who hides counsel without knowledge?’ Therefore I have uttered what I did not understand, Things too wonderful for me, which I did not know.
18_42_4: Listen, please, and let me speak; You said, ‘I will question you, and you shall answer Me.’
18_42_5: “I have heard of You by the hearing of the ear, But now my eye sees You.
18_42_6: Therefore I abhor myself, And repent in dust and ashes.”
18_42_7: And so it was, after the LORD had spoken these words to Job, that the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My wrath is aroused against you and your two friends, for you have not spoken of Me what is right, as My servant Job has.
18_42_8: Now therefore, take for yourselves seven bulls and seven rams, go to My servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and My servant Job shall pray for you. For I will accept him, lest I deal with you according to your folly; because you have not spoken of Me what is right, as My servant Job has.”
18_42_9: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the LORD commanded them; for the LORD had accepted Job.
18_42_10: And the LORD restored Job’s losses when he prayed for his friends. Indeed the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.
18_42_11: Then all his brothers, all his sisters, and all those who had been his acquaintances before, came to him and ate food with him in his house; and they consoled him and comforted him for all the adversity that the LORD had brought upon him. Each one gave him a piece of silver and each a ring of gold.
18_42_12: Now the LORD blessed the latter days of Job more than his beginning; for he had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, one thousand yoke of oxen, and one thousand female donkeys.
18_42_13: He also had seven sons and three daughters.
18_42_14: And he called the name of the first Jemimah, the name of the second Keziah, and the name of the third Keren-Happuch.
18_42_15: In all the land were found no women so beautiful as the daughters of Job; and their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.
18_42_16: After this Job lived one hundred and forty years, and saw his children and grandchildren for four generations.
18_42_17: So Job died, old and full of days.
